'''Banished''' [[File:ClanBanished.png|20x20px]] is a [[clan]] in [[Monster Train 2]]. It is available at the start of the game.

Banished features the following mechanics:
* {{IconLink|Valor}} is a common buff which grants units {{Attack}} and {{IconLink|Armor}}.
* {{IconLink|Shift}} is a common trigger that activates when a unit moves. Many cards and effects move your units around to synergize with this trigger.
* {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} is a common debuff that amplifies your units' attacks.
* {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} is a common defensive buff that prevents the next instance of damage.
* '''[[:Category:Hymnist_units|Hymnist]]''' units use {{IconLink|Enchant}} to provide floorwide effects.

The clan's unique [[Merchant of Steel]] Upgrade is {{IconLink|Bravestone}}.

Friendly units gain {{IconLink|Armor}} equal to 1x Fel's {{IconLink|Valor}}.}} }} ==Strategy== Each of [[Fel]]'s paths requires a different strategy, but they can still be mixed effectively. '''Vanguardian''' wants to stay at the front of the floor, and can massively buff all units on the floor. '''Unchained''' requires moving her frequently and can allow for extremely high damage. '''Savior''' provides greater survivability, and can protect other units if fully upgraded. ===Vanguardian=== '''Vanguardian''' essentially turns '''Fel''' into a variant of [[Firebrand]], granting {{IconLink|Valor}} not only to herself but to the entire floor. This can be immensely powerful if she is placed in front of units which can take advantage of this extra damage, such as those with {{IconLink|Multistrike}} or {{IconLink|Sweep}}. Each additional level of '''Vanguardian''' doubles the {{IconLink|Valor}} applied, increasing the damage output further. The main weakness of this path is the risk of being killed before you can stack up enough {{IconLink|Valor}} to survive. Unlike [[Firebrand]], '''Fel''' cannot be upgraded with {{IconLink|Titanite}}, and even at '''Vanguardian III''' she has only {{Health|40}}. Mixing with either of the two paths can help with this. '''Unchained''' allows you to start with lots of {{IconLink|Valor}} already, and '''Savior''' lets you gain additional {{IconLink|Armor}} when you need it. ===Unchained=== When using '''Unchained''' '''Fel''', your goal is simple: move her as much as possible. [[Just Cause]] is essentially required for this, and so this path is rarely a good idea if using the [[Pyre of Dominion]]. In the early game, simply put her on the top floor next to a [[Shield Steward]], or a banner unit if you happened to start with a useful one, and swap their position over and over. Later on, your goal should be to find units with {{IconLink|Shift}} triggers such as [[Battle Dancer]] or [[Demonic Fledgling]], put them next to '''Fel''', and constantly switch their positions. [[Just Cause]] may only be a starter card, but it's actually one of the best cards you can have for this path. Adding {{IconLink|Twinstone}}, {{IconLink|Emberstone}}, or similar upgrades that will let you play it more often can be a good idea. It can even be worth making more copies with the [[Mysterious Mirror]] event or [[Lifemother's Pyre]], and putting them in the spell box from [[Wondrous Boxes]] can lead to an absurd number of {{IconLink|Shift}} triggers. [[Rising Rage]] is also useful, especially since it lets you overstack a floor with {{IconLink|Shift}} units. [[Hall of Mirrors]] can be strong as it allows for a second copy of '''Fel''' with her stored permanent {{IconLink|Valor}}, but the copy does not provide permanent {{IconLink|Valor}} to [[Fel]]'s card in your deck, despite the tooltip indicating permanent {{IconLink|Valor}} has been gained on both copies of '''Fel'''. With a good build, it's possible to start the fight against Seraph with hundreds or even thousands of {{IconLink|Valor}}. '''Unchained II''' grants a negligible benefit, adding only a few points of {{Attack}} and {{Health}}. It is only worth taking in order to get to '''Unchained III''', which adds an additional stack of {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. This technically only applies once you have {{IconLink|Valor|75}}, but by this point in the game you should be starting every battle with far more than that, so this is generally irrelevant. If mixing paths, it's best to start with one level of '''Unchained''' and then take two levels of another path, rather than pathing into '''Unchained''' later or stopping at '''Unchained II'''. The main weakness of the '''Unchained''' path is that '''Fel''' is very vulnerable until she's had a chance for her {{IconLink|Valor}} to grant {{IconLink|Armor}}. After that point, she's essentially invincible, but it may be worth going '''Unchained I/Savior II''' to make sure that she doesn't die early. That said, if you have any way to protect her, such as putting her on the middle floor and leaving another unit on the top floor as bait for flying bosses, it's usually worth it to go for the extra {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. Starting the battle against [[Ring 8|Seraph]] with a unit that deals {{Attack|1000x3}} almost guarantees a win. This path goes well with all the [[:Category:Hymnist_units|Hymnists]], which provide even greater benefits to her absurdly high damage. It is also one of the biggest beneficiaries in the game of the [[Karmic Censer]] artifact, as it doubles her scaling. Note, however, that this does '''not''' apply to [[Celestial Cascade]], which will boost her {{IconLink|Valor}} in battle but not permanently. ===Savior=== '''Savior''' allows '''Fel''' to immediately move to the front of the floor, gaining {{IconLink|Valor}} and {{IconLink|Armor}} in the process. It is especially effective when used with powerful but vulnerable units like [[Demonic Fledgling]] and [[Death's Dancer]], as '''Savior III''' applies {{IconLink|Armor}} to the entire floor. This is especially effective against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]], which would otherwise kill these units quickly. This path mixes well with either of the other two. '''Unchained''' increases the {{IconLink|Armor}} gained from each use of the '''Savior''' ability, and benefits from the additional {{IconLink|Shift}} trigger. '''Vanguardian''' is best used when '''Fel''' is at the front of the floor, and the {{IconLink|Armor}} from '''Savior''' helps her avoid being killed before she can stack up enough {{IconLink|Valor}} to survive. However, going for pure '''Savior''' allows '''Fel''' to apply {{IconLink|Armor}} to the entire floor, which is often worth giving up the benefits of the other two paths. Unlike normal {{IconLink|Valor}}, which only "refills" {{IconLink|Armor}} up to its maximum value, '''Savior''' simply applies {{IconLink|Armor}} equal to {{IconLink|Valor}} regardless of the current amount of {{IconLink|Armor}}. If you wait for '''Fel''' to gain {{IconLink|Armor}} from her {{IconLink|Valor}} normally before using '''Savior''', then she will have {{IconLink|Armor}} equal to twice her {{IconLink|Valor}}, which can make her extremely hard to kill. {{CollapsibleSection|Sounds| {{{!}} ! {{IconLink|Celebrate}}: Apply {{Attack|+10}} and {{Health|+20}} to friendly units on all floors permanently. }} ==Strategy== [[Talos]]'s '''Flight''' ability has two important benefits for the Banished: it triggers {{IconLink|Shift}} on all units on both the initial and the target floors; and it allows for free overstacking. All of [[Talos]]'s paths benefit greatly from [[Hall of Mirrors]]. '''Battle Cleric''' and '''Enchantress''' have their scaling effects doubled, and the two copies of '''Celestial Radiance''' can alternate using '''Flight''' each turn, applying {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} to all enemies every turn. Both copies can be immediately moved out of the Hall of Mirrors and onto a different floor, and if you don't need it for anything else, you can then replace the Hall of Mirrors. ===Battle Cleric=== '''Battle Cleric''' is the safest pick for a weak start, as {{IconLink|Valor|2}} per turn to the entire floor is a huge boost for Rings 1-3. This is essentially the equivalent of playing [[Inspire (spell)|Inspire]] twice per turn for free, and her '''Flight''' means that you can easily move her to the back of an already full floor to benefit as many units as possible. This quickly falls off in the late game, and the benefits offered by ranks II and III do not keep up with the scaling required for later rings. If '''Celestial Radiance''' is offered on Ring 4, it's often worth pivoting to that path. However, the higher levels can still provide some scaling in the late game, especially if the units being buffed have {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. To maximize the benefits of '''Battle Cleric''', overstack a floor with as many units as possible using cards such as [[Rising Rage]]. ===Celestial Radiance=== '''Celestial Radiance''' is a relatively simple path, giving a massive indirect boost to your damage output every other turn. Each time she moves using her ability '''Flight''', she applies {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} to all enemies, allowing your other units to deal much more damage. She is even better when you can move her by other means. Starting with [[Inspire (spell)|Inspire]] rather than [[Just Cause]] makes this path far less effective than it would otherwise be, but the Banished have many other ways to trigger {{IconLink|Shift}}. [[Imprisoned Zephyr]] can be immensely powerful, but this is extremely risky without a [[Divine Dancer]], especially given [[Talos]]'s unimpressive {{Health}}. Cards from your allied clan, such as [[Vine Grasp]] or [[It's Alive!]], can also help trigger this path's effect more frequently. Though overstacking is not as important here as it is with her other paths, it is still worth building a floor with many units to make sure that '''Talos''' can move safely without interfering with your other units. For example, if she needs to be moved from the back of the floor but you have only an [[Avenger]] with {{IconLink|Quick}} and a damage-focused unit behind him, then putting her between them could be counterproductive: the Avenger will strip [[Talos]]'s {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} from the front unit, and then '''Talos''' will remove the Avenger's {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}}, leaving none once the back unit attacks. While [[Hall of Mirrors]] is strong with all '''Talos''' paths, '''Celestial Radiance''' is easily the strongest one; the two '''Talos''' can alternate using '''Flight''' to swap positions, triggering both '''Talos'''' {{IconLink|Shift}} and applying double the {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} every turn - up to {{IconLink|Melee Weakness|6}} every turn with '''Celestial Radiance III'''! When allied with the [[Pyreborne]], [[Mind Cage]] and [[Tome of Contracts]] allows you to use '''Flight''' every turn; while this technically applies to her other paths as well, '''Celestial Radiance''' is the only one that really cares, ensuring she can apply {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} to every wave. Using the [[Tome of the Lost Path]] on an ally can provide a similar effect, allowing that unit and '''Talos''' to swap positions each turn, alternating between cooldowns. ===Enchantress=== '''Enchantress''' is a feast or famine champion path that can grant a remarkable amount of stats to your units... ''if'' they manage to survive combat. On high [[Covenant Ranks]], this certainly isn't guaranteed. In particular, '''Enchantress''''s stats on Ring 1 are pitiful for a champion, and if your initial deck is weak, you might struggle to defeat the boss at all, let alone with many surviving units. And the fewer units benefit from [[Talos]]'s {{IconLink|Celebrate}} trigger on [[Ring 1]], the harder the subsequent [[Rings]] will be. Thankfully, her '''Flight''' ability means that you'll generally benefit from her metascaling as long as the boss doesn't reach the Pyre, but if you're concerned about that, this isn't the path to take. You may want to consider skipping early [[Trial]]s to ensure you benefit, though this is a painful price to pay, and even the prospect of skipping early [[Trial]]s is a reason to consider a different path. As such, she's at her best on an otherwise strong start where she can snowball that strength into the lategame. She's particularly strong with units that care about their {{Health}} since that's the focus of her metascaling. Examples include [[Steadfast Crusader]], [[Avenger]], and [[Firebrand]] - and these units can all perform well in early rings, making this path potentially viable if you start with them. The [[Pyre of Dominion]] allows you to start with five non-[[Shield Steward]] banner units, which both makes it much easier to survive the first ring intact and gives you a lot of potential beneficiaries of her scaling. Under normal circumstances, she will provide {{AttackHealth|+38|+88}} by the ninth ring, roughly the equivalent of two {{IconLink|Largestone}}s, so any unit that takes {{IconLink|Largestone}} well will usually be a good choice with her. [[Hostguard]] will not be in your starting deck, but he is an excellent pick from banners, as his ability will do additional damage based on his {{Health}}. Even units that care less about their {{Health}} appreciate her ability to give them the chance to occasionally go to the front and benefit from their {{IconLink|Valor}}, and with enough {{Health}} any unit can use the [[Shield of Wyngh]] to kill most enemies without even needing to attack. It is also one of the very few ways to give your backline units enough {{Health}} to survive the {{IconLink|Sweep}} attacks from [[Ragewing Assassin]]s in the [[Heaven's_Maw#Champion_of_Savagery|Champion of Savagery]] combat without needing to kill or disable these enemies first; it is not a perfect solution by any means, as when enhanced with {{IconLink|Rage}} they will still deal a devastating amount of damage, but it makes it much more feasible to tank a few hits from them if your backline removal is unreliable. Like '''Battle Cleric''', this path is best when you can overstack many units onto a single floor. This makes [[Heaven's Light]] a useful pick, and cards like [[Rising Rage]] are excellent for helping move all of your units to a higher floor. When playing with clans that have units that want to die, like [[Imps]] or [[Tombs]], you may want to be careful to ensure they ''don't'' get the buffs. It is usually not worth cross-pathing into '''Enchantress''' at later Forges. Not only will she be a level behind, but you'll also miss out on the scaling you would have gotten in earlier rings. It can be a good idea to switch from '''Enchantress''' to something else if the higher levels of permascaling are not necessary, however. '''Enchantress III''' only triggers twice, once in Ring 7 and once against Seraph, so at best it is worth {{AttackHealth|+12|+20}} to your other units. It may be better to take a level in another path instead - usually '''Celestial Radiance''' for the damage boost, as '''Battle Cleric''''s {{IconLink|Valor|+2}} every turn is pathetic at this stage of the run. ==Quotes== '''Summoned''' * ''Disciple of Seraph no more.... He gives all friendly units on his floor {{IconLink|Quick}}. == Strategy == This unit is especially strong on floors that have good damage capability or with {{IconLink|Sweep}} units, as he saves upgrade slots for units that'd need {{IconLink|Quick}}, or simply provides another avenue to it if shops didn't offer it. {{IconLink|Quick}} enables you to clear entire floors of normal enemies without your units taking any damage. With a strong enough supporting cast and {{IconLink|Sweep}}, '''Upbeat Warbler''' can keep himself safe from units that would kill him and other vulnerable backliners, like [[Ragewing Assassin]]. Note that he doesn't give himself {{IconLink|Quick}}, which usually doesn't matter but does mean: * He can pick off {{Health|1}} enemies that {{IconLink|Reanimate}}d by virtue of attacking last. * He's not a good candidate for [[Iron-tongue]] - while its {{IconLink|Sweep}} works well with '''Upbeat Warbler''''s {{IconLink|Quick}}, it'll need to be applied to one of his allies. Also keep in mind that {{IconLink|Quick}} may occasionally be a disadvantage. With [[Avenger]], for example, all of your units will attack before {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} is applied, dealing massively reduced damage. As a non-banner unit, he is subject to your draw order. If you need him to keep your powerful units safe from damage, it's possible you won't have him until you've made it through your deck. While '''Upbeat Warbler''''s effect mostly only matters for your high-{{Attack}} or {{IconLink|Sweep}} units, if you're looking to overstack floors with flight abilities or [[Ascend]] or [[Descend]] cards like [[Rising Rage]], the floor '''Upbeat Warbler''' want to be on may well be full by then. Adding {{IconLink|Seekstone}} to [[Ascend]] or [[Descend]] cards isn't guaranteed to work either, making it hard to guarantee this bird will be on your main floor like he wants to be. {{IconLink|Dominating Authority}} on a unit played during the [[Deployment Phase]] along with removal of other non-banner units is one answer to this problem. [[Sketches of Salvation]] in conjunction with [[Ascend]] and [[Descend]] works as well. A deck that consistently has [[Ascend]] or [[Descend]] cards, perhaps by putting {{IconLink|Freezestone}} on one, is another. [[Departure Manifest]] is of course the most reliable option, assuming you have the {{DeploymentEmber}} necessary. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! Avenger:
{{UnitCard |name = Avenger |image = PLR_Avenger.png |clan = Banished |rarity = Uncommon |type = Angel |banner = Yes |cost = 2 |size = 2 |stats = 20/40 |ability = {{IconLink|Revenge}}: Apply {{IconLink|Melee Weakness|1}} to the attacker. |flavor = Once the keepers of Heaven's Walls, their flails now protect Fel's army from their former allies. |artist = Loy Bouttamy }} '''Avenger''' is an uncommon [[Banished]] [[banner unit]]. He possesses a {{IconLink|Revenge}} trigger that applies {{IconLink|Melee Weakness|1}} to the attacker. == Strategy == '''Avenger''' functions similarly to [[Firebrand]], both being Banished tanks with {{IconLink|Revenge}} triggers and the same {{Ember}} cost. However, Firebrand is more self-sufficient, as her {{IconLink|Valor}} lets her continue to tank whole waves without any additional support. By contrast, '''Avenger''' will require help in order to stay alive; he needs cards like [[Divinity]] to supply him with enough {{IconLink|Valor}} to continuously perform. The upside is that [[Avenger]]'s mass application of {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} can make it trivial to tear through even the most durable enemies. In particular, against flying bosses, '''Avenger''' can sometimes stack enough {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} on them over the course of several turns to eliminate them in one blow. [[Avenger]]'s damage output is also deceptively high, as whatever his {{Attack}} value is will be at least doubled when he actually strikes. Sources of {{IconLink|Valor}}, like Divinity, [[Everlasting Light]], and [[Spike of the Banished]], are excellent with '''Avenger''', as they both provide the {{IconLink|Armor}} he needs to stay alive in prolonged fights and increase his damage output further. [[Shield of Wyngh]] is extremely useful as it allows '''Avenger''' to eliminate backline units while making the tanks vulnerable due to {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}}. If using this combination, [[Bloodsoaked Arena]] will grant '''Avenger''' plenty of {{IconLink|Valor}}, as any enemies that die to Shield of Wyngh's {{IconLink|Revenge}} damage will trigger {{IconLink|Slay}}. {{IconLink|Trample}} is highly desirable alongside {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}}, as any overkill damage from {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} will spill over and kill the units behind. As such, giving '''Avenger''' or his allies {{IconLink|Trample}} should be a high priority if offered. In-clan, [[Punk Shredder]] can provide this effect; outside of the clan, you can use cards like [[Twisted Assistant]] or [[Umbra Stone]]. [[Avenger]]'s lack of natural scaling sometimes means he's better to use as a support unit, with a high {{Attack}} ally behind him or on another floor. If that's the case, giving '''Avenger''' {{IconLink|Quick}}, either through {{IconLink|Speedstone}} or [[Swiftsteel Dagger]], means that he will attack before any {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} has been applied, and therefore will not consume the {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} applied to the front enemy. Alternatively he can be stopped from attacking entirely, either through {{IconLink|Dazed}} or, if allied with the [[Railforged]], equipping [[Geared Gauntlet]] on him. As he lacks a {{IconLink|Shift}} trigger and generally always wants to remain at the front of the floor, he can be difficult to use alongside strategies or units that rely on {{IconLink|Shift}} like [[Battle Dancer]] and [[Demonic Fledgling]], though he can be given a rest from frontline duties to preserve his {{Health}} against some less tanky waves this way. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! Battle Dancer:
{{UnitCard |name = Battle Dancer |image = PLR_BattleDancer.png |clan = Banished |rarity = Uncommon |type = Angel |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 7/14 |ability = {{IconLink|Shift}}: Gain {{IconLink|Valor|3}}. |flavor = "I used to say, 'dance is for everybody.' Now, I say the same of death." |artist = Loy Bouttamy }} '''Battle Dancer''' is an uncommon [[Banished]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever it moves, it gains {{IconLink|Valor|3}}. == Strategy == The value of '''Battle Dancer''' depends heavily on whether you are playing with the [[Just Cause]] or [[Inspire (spell)|Inspire]] version of Banished. When starting with Just Cause, '''Battle Dancer''' is a premium pickup at Banished unit drafts and one of the very best units that can appear. Its {{IconLink|Valor}} scaling speed is second-to-none, quickly reaching high {{Attack}} values even if Just Cause is the only {{IconLink|Shift}} card in the deck, while also serving dual-duty on defense, if given even a single turn to gain {{IconLink|Armor}} at the front of the floor. Thus, '''Battle Dancer''' should be highly sought after and given ample investment to succeed, by giving it major [[Merchant of Steel]] upgrades as well as cost reductions and/or {{IconLink|Twinstone}} on Just Cause and other movement cards. [[Windblade]] is a strong early pickup for '''Battle Dancer''' as well, accelerating its {{IconLink|Valor}} scaling to even stronger levels. With Inspire, '''Battle Dancer''' conversely turns into one of the least desirable Banished banner units. At a weak starting statline of {{AttackHealth|7|14}}, it struggles to contribute due to the difficulty of scaling it, unless you have ample movement cards in your starters, such as [[Rising Rage]] or a starting Windblade. Even then, you must still pare down your deck aggressively to fix the density of movement cards, which is a high level of investment that may be better directed towards building another line that functions better with Inspire by default. It is still possible to make '''Battle Dancer''' work, particularly if [[Talos]] is your Champion, but more often than not, it will not be worth the heavy investment. Due to its poor {{Health|14}}, it can be difficult to give '''Battle Dancer''' an opportunity at the front of the floor to actually gain {{IconLink|Armor}}. This is especially true in [[Clash with the Titans]], where the front unit on all floors will usually take at least 25 damage every turn (due to [[Entropy]]'s {{Attack|20}} and [[Dominion]]'s {{IconLink|Corruption|5}}). {{IconLink|Damage Shield}}, from cards like [[Selfless Sacrifice]] or [[Sanctuary]], can keep '''Battle Dancer''' alive for long enough to acquire {{IconLink|Armor}}. [[Imprisoned Zephyr]] will also put a different '''Battle Dancer''' at the front of the floor after your units attack, letting it gain {{IconLink|Armor}} safely. Alternatively, if your secondary clan offers chump blocker units like [[Tombs]] or [[Assistants]], one of those can block the first attack and die while leaving '''Battle Dancer''' at the front of the floor at turn end. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! {{UnitCard |name = Demonic Fledgling |image = PLR_DemonicFledgling.png |clan = Banished |rarity = Uncommon |type = Angel |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 10/10 |ability = {{IconLink|Strike}}: Gain {{IconLink|Valor|1}}. {{IconLink|Shift}}: Gain {{IconLink|Rage|2}}. |flavor = "Is it time for a break yet?" |artist = Taylor Bray }} '''Demonic Fledgling''' is an uncommon [[Banished]] [[banner unit]]. He gains {{IconLink|Valor|1}} on {{IconLink|Strike}}, and {{IconLink|Rage|2}} on {{IconLink|Shift}}. == Strategy == '''Demonic Fledgling''' is similar to [[Battle Dancer]], but more focused on offense. He gains {{IconLink|Rage|2}} (equivalent to {{Attack|4}}) whenever he moves, compared to Battle Dancer's {{IconLink|Valor|3}} (equivalent to {{Attack|3}}), and also gains {{IconLink|Valor|1}} when he attacks. However, he lacks any meaningful defensive abilities, leaving him vulnerable if not protected behind other units. He synergizes well with [[Divine Dancer]], which can provide {{IconLink|Armor}} to protect him, as well as with [[Punk Shredder]] and [[Deathmetal Hymnist]], which let you take advantage of his enormous damage potential. He is also effective if allied with [[Hellhorned]] due to their {{IconLink|Rage}} synergies, or [[Underlegion]], since '''[[Propagate]]''' will affect both {{IconLink|Valor}} and {{IconLink|Rage}}. As with any {{IconLink|Shift}} unit, he benefits greatly from having an overstacked floor, more so than usual due to his fragility. Tools to accomplish this, like [[Rising Rage]] and [[Heavensward]], should be highly prioritized. [[Everlasting Light]] is a good option to provide him with enough {{IconLink|Valor}} and therefore {{IconLink|Armor}} to tank through some amount of chip damage, though he's still not ideal as a frontliner. [[Imprisoned Zephyr]] can be useful when using him this way as long as none of your units are {{IconLink|Quick}}, as if he is the last unit to {{IconLink|Strike}}, he will wind up at the front of the floor and gain his {{IconLink|Armor}}, in addition to triggering {{IconLink|Shift}} much more frequently. '''Savior III''' [[Fel]] can accomplish a similar effect by granting {{IconLink|Armor}} equal to her {{IconLink|Valor}} to the entire floor. The {{IconLink|Valor|1}} he gains on {{IconLink|Strike}} counteracts the {{Attack|-1}} effect of [[Cursed Twinblade]], and due to his tremendous potential damage output he greatly appreciates the {{IconLink|Multistrike}} it grants. '''Demonic Fledgling''' is most effective against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Entropic]], as his {{IconLink|Rage}} can make up for the {{IconLink|Sap}} which Seraph applies. Against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]], he tends to die to {{IconLink|Corruption}} if not properly protected, and against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]] he can quickly be killed by enemies with {{IconLink|Sweep}}. He can still be a strong choice for any of the three as long as you prepare properly. She possesses a {{IconLink|Revenge}} trigger that gives her {{IconLink|Valor|2}} whenever she takes damage. == Strategy == '''Firebrand''' is almost always a solid pick, and can be used to both protect backliners and deal damage. Because {{IconLink|Valor}} both provides damage and gives {{IconLink|Armor}} to the front unit, this unit's {{IconLink|Revenge}} trigger allows her to quickly stack up large amounts of {{IconLink|Armor}} as long as she stays at the front of the room. Since {{IconLink|Revenge}} requires her to take damage, she generally wants to stay there anyway. Likewise, she is usually best played on the bottom floor in order to maximize the number of hits she takes, and can remove the need for effects like {{IconLink|Quick}}. This unit does have a slightly awkward relationship with {{IconLink|Shift}} units, such as [[Battle Dancer]] or [[Fel]]'s '''Unchained''' upgrade path. If using {{IconLink|Shift}} units on the same floor as '''Firebrand''', you'll need to move her back to the front lines by the end of turn to take advantage of her {{IconLink|Revenge}} trigger, which can be inconvenient and slow down other units' scaling. However, '''Firebrand''' is strong enough in general to often be worth taking even in these situations, and with enough ability to {{IconLink|Shift}} this becomes less of an issue. '''Firebrand''' is especially useful if fighting [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]], as her regenerating {{IconLink|Armor}} helps counteract the effects of {{IconLink|Corruption}}, and she can even take advantage of it to gain more {{IconLink|Revenge}} triggers. It's important to be careful if you're planning to use '''Firebrand''' against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]], however, as the {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} means that she may be killed instantly before she can stack up enough {{IconLink|Valor}} to protect your other units. Weak spells like [[Torch]] can also be played on '''Firebrand''' to grant even more {{IconLink|Valor}}, as {{IconLink|Revenge}} does not need to be triggered by enemy attacks. [[Wolo's Bloodletter]] is very useful, as it activates a free {{IconLink|Revenge}} trigger every turn on top of granting a damage boost to all of your units. [[Shield of Wyngh]] is a useful piece of equipment for '''Firebrand''', as while she can stack up plenty of {{IconLink|Valor}} she does not usually have any way of dealing with backline units. However, this relies on keeping her true {{Health}} fairly high, which can be difficult before she's built up enough {{IconLink|Valor}}. {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} can prevent her from losing {{Health}} during the first few turns of combat. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! She draws an equipment card when played and gains {{IconLink|Valor|8}} whenever a friendly unit on her floor is given equipment. == Notes == Units with {{IconLink|Graft}}ed equipment entering the floor trigger [[Swordmaiden]]'s ability, as do units with the {{IconLink|Red Crown}} upgrade. == Strategy == '''Swordmaiden''' has excellent synergy with [[Lazarus League]], due to the amount of units with grafted equipment by default and units that want to be repeatedly {{IconLink|Equipped}}, like [[Pincushion]] and [[Hydra Armed Horror]]. Starting with [[Erratic Assistant]] can allow '''Swordmaiden''' to gain ridiculous amounts of {{IconLink|Valor}}. She also works very well with the [[Railforged]], who have various means of improving, generating, and replaying equipment. [[Heph]]'s '''Handy''' and '''Weaponsmith''' paths can both generate [[Crafted Equipment]] every other turn. [[Armament Drive]] can generate up to seven pieces of {{Ember|0}} equipment at once, and overstacking [[Swordmaiden]]'s floor is not difficult between native Banished cards and cards like [[Steel Pulley Claw]]. [[Magnetic Relay]] should not be played on '''Swordmaiden''' herself, as she will lose her {{IconLink|Valor}}, but it can be played on an ally with equipment so that you can play the equipment again. Outside of these clans, [[Swordmaiden]]'s utility is diminished, but not entirely. The Banished clan has several powerful pieces of equipment, such as [[Everlasting Light]], [[Shield of Wyngh]], and [[Cursed Twinblade]]. [[Swordmaiden]]'s {{IconLink|Summon}} effect allows you to draw this equipment during the Deployment phase without needing to make them Deployable. However, the cost is that this can be unreliable if you have a lot of equipment, and because '''Swordmaiden''' costs {{Ember|1}}, you will be paying slightly more than you would otherwise if you are not using the unit as a central part of your strategy. Multiple copies of '''Swordmaiden''' will draw additional equipment, and because {{IconLink|Artificer}} triggers when any unit on the floor is equipped, playing multiple '''Swordmaidens''' on the same floor can be a viable strategy, as they will all benefit from each piece of equipment. Because of how quickly '''Swordmaiden''' can amass significant amounts of {{IconLink|Valor}}, [[Cleave]] is a fantastic pairing for her, particularly when given {{IconLink|Seekstone}} and {{IconLink|Keepstone}}. '''Swordmaiden''' has a slightly awkward relationship with [[Weapons Cache]]. Although Weapons Cache is an extremely powerful room for drawing a lot of equipment, it conflicts with [[Swordmaiden]]'s {{IconLink|Summon}} trigger, and '''Swordmaiden''' may draw an expensive piece of equipment that will not have its {{Ember}} cost reduced by Weapons Cache. If you have enough banner units to make this viable, it may be worth it to play Weapons Cache on a floor that is '''not''' where you will be playing your '''Swordmaidens''', and filling it up first to cheapen as many pieces of equipment as possible. It is possible in the early rings to have a deck with no equipment at all. In that case, [[Swordmaiden]]'s poor base stats can be a detriment, as she is more or less equivalent to a [[Shield Steward]], and she will likely be a throwaway unit instead of part of your main strategy. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! {{UnitCard |name = Death’s Dancer |image = PLR_DeathsDancer.png |clan = Banished |rarity = Rare |type = Angel |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 7/14 |ability = {{IconLink|Shift}}: Apply {{Attack|+4}} to friendly units. |flavor = “Dance is a poem in which each kill is a step.” |artist = Loy Bouttamy }} The '''Death's Dancer''' is a rare [[Banished]] [[banner unit]]. It grants {{Attack|+4}} to friendly units on {{IconLink|Shift}}. == Strategy == '''Death's Dancer''' is a support unit for {{IconLink|Shift}}-based builds, similar to its counterpart, the [[Divine Dancer]]. Instead of providing {{IconLink|Armor}}, it strengthens its allies. It compares favourably to [[Battle Dancer]] and [[Demonic Fledgling]], both of which gain relatively less or equal {{Attack}} per {{IconLink|Shift}}. However, those units (as well as Divine Dancer) can be given {{IconLink|Dualism}} to boost their scaling ability, while '''Death's Dancer''' cannot, since it applies a pure stat increase. Thus, in order for '''Death's Dancer''' to be worth it, one must leverage its greatest advantage: the fact that its scaling applies to the whole floor. {{IconLink|Shift}} strategies often want to overstack their floors anyway with cards like [[Rising Rage]], which makes '''Death's Dancer''' much more appealing. When allied with {{IconLink|Shift}} units like the aforementioned Battle Dancer, it can help hit the necessary damage thresholds against units like [[Avowed Gladiator]]s sooner. In the interest of triggering {{IconLink|Shift}} as much as possible, [[Imprisoned Zephyr]] can be used, albeit with caution. '''Death's Dancer''' is quite fragile, and does not naturally build up {{IconLink|Armor}} or {{IconLink|Valor}}, so if it ends up at the front of the floor it can be highly vulnerable. However, if you can pair it with Divine Dancer, this concern is mostly irrelevant as Divine Dancer will provide plenty of {{IconLink|Armor}}. [[Windblade]] grants very little {{IconLink|Valor}} per {{IconLink|Shift}}, but it is more than nothing, and it will also trigger an extra {{IconLink|Shift}} on {{IconLink|Resolve}}. The more copies of '''Death's Dancer''' that are present on the floor, the greater its scaling effect is. As such, this card is an excellent target for duplication, especially from the [[Mysterious Mirror]] event. The [[Clipped Wings]] event is also highly beneficial, as the flight provided by {{IconLink|Discarded Wings}} or {{Icon|ArchusWings}} '''[[Archus' Wing]]''' lets '''Death's Dancer''' trigger {{IconLink|Shift}} all on its own, acting like an automatic [[Tome of the Lost Path]] with a bit of extra stats attached. Due to [[Death's Dancer]]'s powerful {{Attack}} scaling, it also pairs well with off-clan units that do not have {{IconLink|Shift}} triggers but which benefit from high damage values, such as [[Eel Gorgon]], [[Animus of Will]], and [[Plague Doctor]]. It pairs well with any path on [[Primordium]], boosting its {{Attack}} and therefore the stats it provides when {{IconLink|Eaten}}. These strategies may benefit from a way to protect the floor from damage, such as Divine Dancer or [[Fel]]'s '''Savior''' path. [[Just Cause]] is vital for '''Death's Dancer''' to function well; as with other {{IconLink|Shift}} strategies, the unit is much weaker with [[Inspire (spell)|Inspire]] or [[Pyre of Dominion]]. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! Instead of providing {{Attack}}, it gives its allies {{IconLink|Armor}}. In order for '''Divine Dancer''' to be worth it, one must leverage its greatest advantage: the fact that its scaling applies to the whole floor. {{IconLink|Shift}} strategies often want to overstack their floors anyway with cards like [[Rising Rage]], which makes '''Divine Dancer''' much more appealing. It has a cooldown of 3. == Strategy == '''Hostguard''' is a strong pick if you have enough {{DeploymentEmber}} to play him, but can be prohibitively expensive in some cases. His {{Capacity|3}} may also seem like a problem, but he can immediately move to an already full floor, meaning that as long as you have an empty floor to place him on during Deployment he is essentially {{Capacity|0}}. Effects that grant extra {{DeploymentEmber}}, like [[Herzal's Horde]] or [[Artificial Pyrestone]], make him a much stronger pick. The ability to move to an already full floor is his main benefit, and the damage dealt by his ability is usually not a huge deal. However, it allows you to do an extra bit of damage every few turns, and can be made much stronger through [[Talos]]'s {{IconLink|Celebrate}} effect. He can be an effective frontliner due to his high base {{Health}}, and can use the [[Shield of Wyngh]] very well for the same reason. However, he competes with [[Firebrand]] and [[Avenger]], both potent and slightly less expensive frontliners in the same clan, and it may be better to move him to the back of a floor if you have one of those units. {{IconLink|Valor}} is extremely valuable for '''Hostguard''', as the Banished have no way in-clan to restore raw {{Health}}, while the {{IconLink|Armor}} granted by {{IconLink|Valor}} will replenish itself each turn as long as he's at the front. Thus, cards like [[Divinity]] should be a high priority. Combined with the Shield of Wyngh, [[Bloodsoaked Arena]] is a great way to provide plenty of extra {{IconLink|Valor}}, as he will have no trouble triggering {{IconLink|Slay}} when fragile backliners attack him. Consider using {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} cards like [[Selfless Sacrifice]] or [[Sanctuary]] at the start of battle, before he's built up any {{IconLink|Armor}}, to keep his raw {{Health}} high. Since one of his biggest boons is his built-in overstacking, any effects that scale the entire floor make him far more desirable, as he can serve as an extra body. These include his fellow rare units [[Divine Dancer]] and [[Death's Dancer]], setups that make heavy use of [[Everlasting Light]], or builds revolving around [[Branded Warrior]], [[Keeper of Echoes]], or '''Living Armory''' [[Baron Grael]]. While both '''Hostguard''' and '''Hall of Mirrors''' are highly expensive, his inherent ability to move to any other floor can make this combination worthwhile, as both copies can be flown down to a different floor right away. Units in {{IconLink|Stasis}} do not count, so [[Stasis Crystal]] can only be used to gain a high-damage '''Cleave''' after breaking the unit out of {{IconLink|Stasis}}. Unlike [[Minds Of Their Own]], '''Cleave''' is a direct damage spell, and does not count as your units attacking. This means that it will not trigger {{IconLink|Strike}} or {{IconLink|Slay}}. == Strategy == '''Cleave''' provides a versatile spell in tandem with your units. Even with a frontliner with modest {{Attack}}, it will generally wipe out backline enemies on its floor with ease. With a more powerful frontliner, such as one with plenty of {{IconLink|Valor}}, this can not only clear backliners but dent and even kill tanky frontline enemies, including [[Avowed Gladiator]]! It does have a couple of downsides, though: it has a high {{Ember}} cost, and it cannot be played on floors that don't have friendly units. While it's very strong at handling waves of enemies, make sure your units are able to handle non-flying [[Bosses]] without the help of this card, though this can take a big chunk out of Flying Bosses, especially if you can clear the waves in front of them with it. {{SpellCard |name= Rising Rage |image = CRD_RisingRage.png |clan= Banished |rarity= Common |cost= 1 |effect= '''[[Ascend]]''' then '''[[Advance]]'''. |flavor= A simmering fury bubbled in the angel's throat. "You clipped my wings," they cried, their voice echoing against Heaven's high walls, "but now I fly higher than ever before!" |artist = Luke Banke }} '''Rising Rage''' is a common [[Banished]] spell. It [[Ascend]]s then [[Advance]]s a unit. == Strategy == '''Rising Rage''' is a great way to trigger {{IconLink|Shift}}. As long as the target unit is actually Ascended, this will trigger {{IconLink|Shift}} on every unit on the destination floor twice, and on every unit on the floor of origin once. As such, this works great for a floor full of {{IconLink|Shift}} units. It is also an excellent way to "break the game" in one of the most fundamental ways: overstacking units on higher floors. When a unit is Ascended, it doesn't check to see if the target floor has {{Capacity}} for the ascended unit. You can set up a full floor of units on two adjacent floors, and then Ascend each unit on the lower floor to the upper floor, creating a floor with units greatly exceeding the capacity of that floor. You can now take much fuller advantage of units and equipment like [[Death's Dancer]], [[Everlasting Light]], [[Lead Songbird]], [[Deathmetal Hymnist]], and so forth, having their effects apply to all your units. It also makes a floor that's an absolute nightmare for bosses, who only get one attack while 6-7 of your units all get turns attacking. If all goes well, you may not even need [[Heaven's Light]]. If you set up all your units on the third floor, you can then use this card to reposition your units and continue triggering {{IconLink|Shift}}; otherwise you may not want to break up your "band." This card, especially with the {{IconLink|Seekstone}} upgrade, should be strongly considered for duplication as necessary to get your kill floor together. One thing to be careful of with this card, though, is its tendency to put your units on higher floors. Monster Train 2 has many enemies and bosses that can punish you for that, such as [[Scourge]]-adding enemies and enemies and bosses with {{IconLink|Resolve}} triggers. But it's absolutely possible to get a floor so strong that that doesn't really matter this way. Just be sure to look for answers to those threats, like [[Inferno Room]] or [[Zone of Silence]] on lower floors. While you'll generally want to play this on friendly units, it also has some situational utility in use on enemies too, such as breaking up dangerous waves into smaller chunks, putting backline enemies in front to be sniped, or moving flying bosses to or from your units. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! It can apply a reasonable amount of {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}}, significantly increasing the damage taken by the target, as well as moving them down a floor. For builds which want to overstack the top floor, '''Demonize''' is one of the few cards which can move flying bosses like [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]] away from that floor. It '''[[Descend]]s''' and '''[[Advance]]s''' a friendly unit, then damages the front enemy based on that unit's {{Health}} and {{IconLink|Armor}}. == Strategy == '''Heroic Dive''' is a rare Descend option for the Banished, which immediately makes it worthwhile. The Banished benefit greatly from overstacking, and cards like [[Rising Rage]] generally encourage doing so on higher floors. However, the game can punish higher-floor setups quite heavily with enemies like [[Terrifying Amalgam]]s, [[Chosen Supplicant]]s, and [[Nourishing Cherub]]s, not to mention bosses with {{IconLink|Resolve}} effects like [[Rax the Overblessed]] and [[Athane, Last to Fall]]. This card allows you to overstack the bottom floor instead, minimizing the danger from these enemies. Compared to Rising Rage, its disadvantages are twofold. As an uncommon card, you will generally not have a chance to draft it until after Ring 4, which means building around it in the early game is risky since you may not be offered it at all. It also '''[[Consume]]s''', meaning by default you can only play it once. The damage it deals to the front unit in exchange is usually irrelevant. It is usually a worse pick overall compared to cards like [[Restoring Retreat]] and [[Dripfall]], but your secondary clan may not have those options. Within the Banished, its only direct competition is [[Demonize]], which is significantly more expensive and applies {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}}, and [[Tome of the Lost Path]], which is rare. As such, it has a definite niche, but usually relies on visiting the [[Merchant of Magic]] to perform. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! She felt a familiar warmth fill her heart. Perhaps it was her friend, not Wyngh, who answered." |artist = Aubrey Kim }} '''Wyngh's Radiance''' is a rare [[Banished]] spell. It moves its target to the front of the floor and applies X {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} to it. ==Strategy== '''Wyngh's Radiance''' can be thought of as a damage spell that does X times the damage your first attacking unit does to its target. It can be compared to a [[Forever Consumed]] that can target a unit and can do quite a bit more damage, as it's quite likely your first unit can do more than 80 damage by the time you find the card. But in the best case, this card can do even better than that. If you have a source of {{IconLink|Trample}} such as [[Punk Shredder]], the ''entire floor'' of enemies can suffer the {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} of the first unit, as the overflow damage is still subject to the multiplication that {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} applies. Couple this with a powerful, {{IconLink|Quick}} attacker, and the entire enemy floor can instantly perish before combat really begins! It's also worth noting that this card can be played on friendly units and can be played for {{Ember|0}}. You can use it to simply reposition your units and trigger {{IconLink|Shift}}, if that's what the situation calls for. This can take advantage of the {{IconLink|Twinstone}} upgrade, especially with the '''Celestial Radiance''' path of [[Talos]]. You can play one or both copies at {{Ember|0}} and often generate much more {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} than you would by playing the card normally. Finally, this card is one of a small handful that is effective against [[Dominion]]. It deals X times your Pyre's {{Attack}} to him, ignoring his {{IconLink|Spell Shield}} entirely. Note that if you have a [[Pyre Light]], you should play that first before playing '''Wyngh's Radiance'''. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! '''Penitent's Bloodsuit''' is a common [[Banished]] equipment. It deals 30 damage to its wearer on {{IconLink|Shift}}, and can be equipped on enemy units.

==Strategy==

'''Penitent's Bloodsuit''' notably triggers on enemies as they move up the train, meaning an enemy equipped with it on the bottom floor will take at least 90 damage from it before being able to reach the Pyre. This is a death sentence for enemies in early rings. It also applies to [[Flying Bosses]] as they move, meaning this does about 240 damage to [[Arkion, Scion of Savagery]] or [[Fleshweaver]] if applied on turn 1 without any further {{IconLink|Shift}} investment from the player.

There are rare reasons to equip it on friendly units - while its damage is too high to e.g. exploit {{IconLink|Revenge}} triggers, it can be used with e.g. [[Baron Grael]] or [[Swordmaiden]] or [[Hydra Armed Horror]] to cheaply trigger Artificer or {{IconLink|Equipped}} triggers.

Normally, it has no way of scaling barring additional {{IconLink|Shift}} support, and seeing as it can only be applied to a single enemy and {{IconLink|Shift}} cards are often better spent scaling your units, it will fall off later in the game. Even worse, it can become a liability if you pick up [[Attuned Whetstone]], as it could be what you draw with that artifact, and you probably don't want to equip it in the [[Deployment Phase]]. Should you receive that later, this should be Purged immediately. It can also be drawn by [[Swordmaiden]] and [[Weapons Cache]], which could be a benefit if you're triggering those abilities after [[Deployment Phase]] but a liability in the more typical case where you're activating them during Deployment. 

So it could be worth taking if you think you could use the early-game help, but it often becomes a card you want to Purge later.

When running Banished with [[Pyreborne]], it can benefit from [[Pyregel]] scaling, providing a reliable way to trigger Pyregel damage and serving as a meaningful threat even to late-game flying bosses.

'''Shield of Wyngh''' is an equipment card from the [[Banished]] clan. It deals damage equal to the equipped unit's current {{Health}} (after deducting any damage from the attack) when attacked.

==Strategy==
'''Shield of Wyngh''' is helpful for killing backline enemies with low health. Having a lot of {{IconLink|Valor}} allows the wearer to avoid losing health when hit, and keep the {{IconLink|Revenge}} damage from decreasing. This makes it useful for units like [[Firebrand]].

It generally doesn't deal enough damage to significantly hurt tougher enemies, but if allied with clans whose Champions have high max health, it can deal significant damage. It is especially effective on '''Titanchannel''' [[Solgard]] or any path on [[Sentient]], and can also be good on [[Awoken Hollow]] or [[Thorned Hollow]] if you can get them to full health. {{IconLink|Largestone}} and {{IconLink|Heartstone}} can also be used to buff the {{Health}} of any unit, as can artifacts like [[Medallion of Superiority]], [[Triboulet]], and [[Unstable Shard]].

'''Enchantress''' [[Talos]] can massively increase the {{Health}} of your other units, making the '''Shield of Wyngh''' far stronger.

'''Imprisoned Zephyr''' is an uncommon [[Banished]] room. It causes friendly units in it to [[Advance]] when they attack.

==Strategy==

'''Imprisoned Zephyr''' is a vital card for {{IconLink|Shift}}-focused strategies, allowing for absurd amounts of {{IconLink|Shift}} triggers every single turn. It is recommended that you use movement spells and abilities to overstack the room, as more units results in more {{IconLink|Shift}} triggers.

For strategies that don't utilize {{IconLink|Shift}}, this room usually doesn't do much at best and is actively harmful at worst, as the effect may expose your backliners if you don't position them correctly.

Another benefit of this room is its interaction with {{IconLink|Valor}}: usually, units must survive one combat at the front of a floor before they can gain {{IconLink|Armor}} from {{IconLink|Valor}}. But with '''Imprisoned Zephyr''', whichever unit ends up at the front after combat is the one who gets the {{IconLink|Armor}}.

'''Imprisoned Zephyr''' has a complicated effect on unit positioning depending on whether all friendly units get to attack, and whether any of them have {{IconLink|Quick}}. See the section below.

Blockers with {{Attack|0}}, like [[Prickly Puffball]], are incompatible with this room: all backline units advance in front of them, and from then on the blocker sits uselessly behind the units it was supposed to protect.

== Unit Positioning ==

Here's how '''Imprisoned Zephyr''' affects unit positioning:
* Assuming all friendly units on the floor make an attack and that either none or all of them have {{IconLink|Quick}}, then their positions are inverted every turn, and each unit gets {{IconLink|Shift}} triggers equal to the number of units behind it.
** If no units had {{IconLink|Quick}}, then the frontmost friendly unit is attacked by enemy units; if all units had {{IconLink|Quick}}, then the backmost unit is attacked.
** In either case, only the frontmost and backmost unit receive enemy attacks, alternating between one another.
* If not all friendly units get to attack because the enemy units die first, then only the order of the attacking units is inverted.
* If some but not all friendly units have {{IconLink|Quick}}, then the {{IconLink|Quick}} units attack first and invert their order first. Then the {{IconLink|Quick}} unit that was furthest back is now in front and gets attacked by the enemy units. And finally, the non-{{IconLink|Quick}} friendly units attack and have their order inverted. At the end of combat, all friendly {{IconLink|Quick}} units are at the back with their order inverted, and in front are all non-{{IconLink|Quick}} units with their order inverted.
** In this situation, only the frontmost and backmost {{IconLink|Quick}} unit receive enemy attacks, alternating between one another. The non-{{IconLink|Quick}} units are never attacked, but they are affected by [[Dominion]]'s {{IconLink|Resolve}} trigger which applies {{IconLink|Corruption}}.

'''Pyreborne''' [[File:ClanPyreborne.png|20x20px]] is a [[clan]] in [[Monster Train 2]]. It is available at the start of the game.

Pyreborne features the following mechanics:
* {{IconLink|Pyregel}} is a debuff that causes enemy units to take more damage from all sources, representing the clan's primary offensive tool.
* {{IconLink|Dragon's Hoard|png=DragonsHoard}} is a unique mechanic that can grant extra {{Gold}} and [[Artifacts]].
* {{IconLink|Avarice}} is a buff that grants {{Gold}} when your units deal damage.
* Many units make use of active {{Icon|AbilityActive}} '''[[Abilities]]''', and the clan offers multiple ways of reducing cooldowns.
* Some spells and abilities are '''[[Explosive]]''', causing them to deal additional damage to the floor when slaying an enemy.
* '''[[:Category:Whelp_units|Whelps]]''' are minor, often sacrificial units that all have unique active abilities.
The clan's unique [[Merchant of Steel]] Upgrade is {{IconLink|Greedstone}}.

=== Dragon's Hoard ===
{{Icon|DragonsHoard}} '''Dragon's Hoard''' is a resource unique to the Pyreborne clan. Several units, cards, abilities, and artifacts allow you to obtain Dragon's Hoard during combat. Dragon's Hoard's primary use is outside of combat, where it can be looted at any time to gain rewards. Rewards gained depend on how many stacks of Dragon's Hoard you have obtained. You can also choose to refrain from looting and wait for more stacks before cashing in. Dragon's Hoard is the only way to obtain [[Minor Pyreborne Artifacts]].

Dragon's Hoard also has a handful of in-combat uses that incentivize refraining from looting. It can be used to:
* Increase the {{Attack}} and {{Health}} of [[Greed Dragon]]
* Increase the {{Gold}} generation of [[Wealthy Whelp]]
* Increase the damage of [[Inequivalent Exchange]]
* Heal your Pyre using [[Pay Off]]

By default, the maximum number of Dragon's Hoard that can be stored is 8. This maximum can only be increased with two artifacts: [[Hidden Coffers]] (+2) and [[Expanded Coffers]] (+3). As Hidden Coffers is a Minor Pyreborne Artifact, you will need to loot at least once to get to the maximum of 13 stacks. If both artifacts are obtained and enough stacks are looted, Dragon's Hoard can be used to obtain extra Boss Artifacts. This is the only way to obtain more than two [[Boss Artifacts]]. Boss Artifacts obtained from Dragon's Hoard have different names than regular boss artifacts, namely [[Pyreforged Flame]], [[Pyreforged Solace]] and [[Pyreforged Light]], and one can obtain at most one copy of each. That is, the second time you get to pick a Boss Artifact from Dragon's Hoard, the one you've already picked is no longer available.

Both the pools of [[Minor Pyreborne Artifacts]] and of [[Pyreforged Boss Artifacts]] can be depleted. If a Dragon's Hoard of size 12-13 is opened a fourth time, both pools are likely depleted. In this case, the Hoard will only yield the gold reward; no artifacts will be awarded, nor an option to skip artifacts for extra gold.

When a unit gains {{IconLink|Pyregel}}, it gains '''+4''' stacks. }} == Strategy == '''Lord Fenix''' can be difficult to use due to his large size at {{Capacity|3}}, which makes it difficult to fit other units on the same floor. Despite his large size, he is relatively fragile, and his ability to apply {{IconLink|Pyregel}} means that he should usually be played on the lower floors, leaving him vulnerable. You will need some way to keep him alive, and overstacking and {{Capacity}} reduction can help stack more units on his floor. His paths all value being able to use his {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}} at key points in the fight, and generally as often as possible. Artifacts, cards, and equipment that help him use it more often, like [[Pyreborne Brainspike]], [[Taskmaster's Lash]], [[Mind Cage]], and especially [[Tome of Contracts]], are very valuable on all paths. ===Overlord=== On this path, '''Lord Fenix''' seeks to annihilate backliners and snowball into a powerhouse of a unit. Killing an enemy with '''Fenix Fire''' counts as a {{IconLink|Slay}}, and that, in turn, will increase the power of your ability (and your regular attack) permanently. If you can find an early way to reduce your [[Cooldown]] or just engineer {{IconLink|Slay}}s in the normal way, you can snowball. Your {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}} will upgrade to become [[Explosive]] at level II. This means you can target weak backliners and score multiple {{IconLink|Slay}}s to further snowball. (You could even target a weak friendly unit that wants to die, like an {{IconLink|Endless}} [[:Category:Whelp units|Whelp]], and still damage enemies, getting one more {{IconLink|Slay}} this way.) And your {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}'s power doubles at level III. These powerful payoffs usually mean you won't consider cross-pathing, unless you really didn't manage to snowball your {{Attack}} and want to use '''Lord Fenix''' for {{IconLink|Dragon's Hoard|png=DragonsHoard}} economy instead by cross-pathing into '''Golden Crown'''. The major weakness of this line is its high {{Capacity}} and low {{Health}}, a combination that makes it quite difficult to keep alive in practice. In particular, you generally can't protect it with a [[Shield Steward]] in rings 1 and 2 for {{Capacity}} reasons. The fact that the [[Pyreborne]] don't have many bulky units in general adds to this problem, so hopefully your allied clan can provide a tank for him to hide behind. If not, the [[Greed Dragon]] can protect him effectively. This also means that he isn't a great unit in {{IconLink|Relentless}} combat, as he only gets to use his ability up to once under normal circumstances. His {{Capacity}} constraints make it difficult to add other offensive units on the same floor. Additionally, while very powerful when you can use his ability, he is of limited use when you can't. This means that, even if he can wipe out a wave all on his own, you'll still need another way to wipe out 2 out of every 3 waves on the turns when his ability is on cooldown. Ideally, at some point in the run you'll become able to use his {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}} every turn, such as by using [[Tome of Contracts]] with {{IconLink|Twinstone}} and {{IconLink|Seekstone}}. When choosing this path, be aware that you are gambling heavily on seeing Cooldown reduction. With the [[Melting Remnant]], especially if starting with [[Primitive Mold]], this path can be game-breakingly powerful. '''[[Reform]]ing''' a unit resets ability cooldowns, so having '''Fenix''' target himself every time you draw a Reform card allows him to permanently gain {{Attack|1}}, gain {{Attack}} and {{Health}} for the rest of the current battle, and (once you get Level II of this path) kill whole waves of enemies. He can potentially gain {{Attack|500}} or more by the endgame, meaning that every time you draw a Reform card you can deal 1,000 damage to all enemies on the floor. This can be so powerful that it is potentially worth removing all other units and all cards that do not Reform, and the only enemy that can stop you is the [[Deafening Herald]], which you will need some other way to kill. [[Pyreball]] with a {{IconLink|Freezestone}} is a viable option available in-clan, but [[Zone of Silence]] is another option, especially because a strategy like this rarely requires many banner units to support it. ===Golden Crown=== On this path, '''Lord Fenix''' is simply looking to build your {{IconLink|Dragon's Hoard|png=DragonsHoard|}} economy, to allow you to snowball economy for later in the run. Every time you use his ability, you get some {{DragonsHoard}}, so you should try to maximize the number of times you get to use his ability. It's even worth calculating how many turns are left in the combat to do so. Sometimes, you can get an extra ability activation and extra {{DragonsHoard}} by putting '''Lord Fenix''' on a higher floor and killing the boss there. {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: center; |+ Maximizing Lord Fenix's {{DragonsHoard}} output |- ! Where to place Lord Fenix |- | '''1-2''' || 4-6 || 2 || Anywhere |- | '''3-5''' || 6-8 || 3 || 2nd or 3rd floors |- | '''6''' || 8-10 || 4 || 3rd floor |- | '''7''' || 7-9 || 3 || Anywhere |- | '''8''' || 8-10 || 4 || 3rd floor |- | '''9''' || No limit || No limit || Anywhere |} ''*'' assuming you have no way of reducing [[Lord Fenix]]'s [[Cooldown]] '''Lord Fenix''' can serve as a tank in a pinch (and with [[Crown of the Eternal]], can even be a good one), but his high {{Capacity}} means you'll often want him to be separate from your combat floor. If so, there can be times where there are no enemy targets. In the worst case, '''Lord Fenix''' can target himself with his {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}. Especially if you can find ways to reduce his [[Cooldown]], you'll get lots of benefits from {{DragonsHoard}}, and that will be [[Lord Fenix]]'s main contribution to your run. The trigger is tied to the {{IconLink|Conjure}} and not the ability itself, so a way to increase his {{DragonsHoard}} gain is to replace '''Fenix Fire''' with another ability with a shorter cooldown, such as '''Wind-Up Punch''' via [[Geared Gauntlet]] or '''Flight''' via [[Tome of the Lost Path]], but most notable is '''Evergrowth''' via [[Tome of Evergrowth]], with its 1-turn cooldown and strong support potential. You can upgrade this path for further economy bonuses, gaining {{Gold}} and eventually more {{DragonsHoard}}. You could cross-path into '''Pyremaniac''' if you're using '''Lord Fenix''' as a tank and have leaned into {{IconLink|Pyregel}} application, but it's too late for '''Overlord'''. ===Pyremaniac=== While the '''Overlord''' path takes time to build up its damage in order to become a powerful late-game threat, '''Pyremaniac''' is the most offensively potent path from the outset, thanks to [[Lord Fenix]]'s built-in {{IconLink|Pyregel}} synergies with his [[Firestarter|starter card]] and ability. '''Pyremaniac''' '''Lord Fenix''' increases the amount of {{IconLink|Pyregel}} a unit receives while they are on the same floor as the champion, similar to [[Madame Lionsmane]]'s '''Sporesinger''' path. As with that path, it is generally better to put '''Lord Fenix''' on lower floors so that the {{IconLink|Pyregel}} will have more time to damage enemies as they ascend the train. It synergizes very well with [[Magma Cultist]], which can take advantage of [[Lord Fenix]]'s passive bonus to grant additional {{IconLink|Pyregel}} with each spell played. Due to [[Lord Fenix]]'s large size, this combo can struggle defensively. A tank with {{IconLink|Smidgestone}} (or [[Heaven's Light]]) can protect him, or, with {{IconLink|Armor}} or similar effects, '''Lord Fenix''' himself can be a tank. Alternatively, if you have sufficient spell damage or [[Cursed Dragonstaff]], you can saturate the enemies with {{IconLink|Pyregel}} and wipe them out before they can strike, allowing the combo to work without tanking or sustaining. [[Pyreblooded]] can also be a strong support unit with this path, though it is generally less useful than [[Magma Cultist]] due to providing no {{IconLink|Pyregel}} itself, and it suffers from the same issue of generally requiring a source of sustain to function. As with the other paths, '''Pyremaniac''' suffers from [[Lord Fenix]]'s large cooldown, but it can be particularly troublesome with this path. Since '''Lord Fenix''' only applies its bonus on its own floor, a turn could pass where you draw no Firestarters and your ability is on cooldown, allowing a floor of enemies to pass without receiving any {{IconLink|Pyregel}} if you have no other means of generating it. {{IconLink|Pyregel}} provides an alternative to direct attack power, so it can completely disrupt your combo and allow a full floor of enemies to reach the Pyre if you allow such a lapse. Time the use of your ability appropriately to make sure the enemies can deal the least amount of damage. You can also take additional spells like [[Pyrecask]] and [[Lava Flow]] to help account for those underwhelming turns, as those will also be buffed by his effect. '''Pyremaniac''' is a powerful answer to bosses, especially flying bosses. Even if '''Lord Fenix''' does not defeat the boss itself, simply surviving to {{IconLink|Relentless}} can allow him to put enough {{IconLink|Pyregel}} on it that it turns a difficult fight into a trivial one for the higher floors. Since {{IconLink|Pyregel}} doesn't deteriorate over time, it can be especially useful at dealing early damage to flying bosses. The more sources of damage you have with this path, the better. For {{IconLink|Relentless}}, it can be a powerful strategy to stack a bunch of small units like [[Whelps]] or [[Imps]] behind a sturdy tank, so long as the enemy doesn't have {{IconLink|Spikes|}}. Even if they only deal 1 damage each, it will be dramatically increased by the amount of {{IconLink|Pyregel}} you can put on the boss. {{IconLink|Multistrike}} is also highly valued with this path, to the point that it can be worth giving it to a weak unit without much attack if encountered. ==Quotes== '''Summoned''' * ''Hmpf, angels and their feathery wings.'' * ''If you're not using your treasure, I'll take it!'' * ''It's time for this train to get a little hotter!'' * ''Someone better be paying me for this!'' * ''Success knows no rest!'' * ''These Titans are bad for business!'' * ''Time to add more gold to my hoard!'' They '''[[Retreat]]''' on {{IconLink|Summon}} and, if they survive the combat, will reward the player with {{DragonsHoard}} and on subsequent upgrades also with {{Gold}}. == Strategy == '''Lady Gilda''' is a quite meta champion that requires careful management to make the most out of, regardless of which path you pursue with her. Similarly to [[Fenix]] she takes up at least {{Capacity|3}}, but unlike Fenix does not hit hard on her own and so really needs to find a reliable beatstick by Ring 2 to succeed. Because she has the ability to continually generate resources, though, her runs tend to get stronger the longer they go on. Cards that also take advantage of {{DragonsHoard}} and {{Gold}}, like [[Greed Dragon]], [[Make It Rain]], [[Inequivalent Exchange]] and [[Soldier of Fortune]], have a strong synergy with her. ===Gildmother=== '''Gildmother''' needs to be placed on the top floor to protect her [[Gilded Egg]]. Fortunately, she has very good stats for a Champion, and can meaningfully contribute to combat anyway. With {{IconLink|Trample}} and high {{Health}}, she can both clear backline enemies, and survive Flying Bosses. In particular, her stats almost always allow her to win the Ring 1 boss fight, especially with a card like [[Pyrecask]] or [[Lava Armor]]. This path requires {{Capacity|4}} on the top floor and her [[Gilded Egg]] takes up another {{Capacity|1}}, which fully fills up a {{Capacity|5}} floor. However, if you have a [[banner unit]] with {{Capacity|1}} like [[Magma Cultist]] or [[Miser]], you can place it on the top floor during [[Deployment]]. While '''Gildmother''' becomes much better with other sources of {{DragonsHoard}}, just by herself she already earns enough to (almost) fully loot a size-{{DragonsHoard|8}} three times: * '''Gildmother I''' earns 3*2={{DragonsHoard|6}} in Rings 1-3. * '''Gildmother II''' earns 2*4={{DragonsHoard|8}} in Rings 4-5. * '''Gildmother II''' earns {{DragonsHoard|4}} in Ring 6, and '''Gildmother III''' earns another {{DragonsHoard|6}} in Ring 7. [[Greed Dragon]] and [[Inequivalent Exchange]] scale off of {{DragonsHoard}}. However, Greed Dragon can be somewhat awkward. If she is your main source of {{DragonsHoard}}, you will not gain any {{DragonsHoard}} until the end of combat. This means, unlike {{DragonsHoard}} sources like [[Alchemy]] or '''Golden Crown''' [[Lord Fenix]], you cannot both loot the hoard and increase Greed Dragon's stats mid-combat. Thus, later levels of this path generally just provide {{Gold}} if you are not looting. '''Gildmother''' synergizes ridiculously well with the rare room [[Hall of Mirrors]], provided your top floor has at least {{Capacity|6}} from [[Heaven's Light]] or [[Bogwurm's Growth]]. Once you play her, the Hall of Mirrors will spawn a second copy of her, and then both copies will summon two Gilded Eggs, for four in total. This lets you earn {{DragonsHoard|8}} every combat even with just '''Gildmother I''', and max out your hoard even with both [[Hidden Coffers]] and [[Expanded Coffers]] every fight once you get to '''Gildmother II'''. Note that while the Gilded Egg is usually relatively safe due to [[Retreat]]ing itself and Lady Gilda's good stats, some fights still pose a threat to it: *[[Arkion, Scion of Savagery]]'s '''Hard Headed''' variant will knock her back and expose the egg. If you lack cards that can move units around afterwards, or some means to apply {{IconLink|Dazed}} or otherwise prevent him from attacking, this may not be an ideal path to take if he is your boss. However, in total, this will only lose you {{DragonsHoard|2}} across the run, so it's likely still worthwhile. *On Covenant 4+, [[Qel the Corruptor]] will apply [[Corruption]] to ''all'' units as soon as he spawns, most likely killing the egg. *[[The Observatory#Savagery's Final Assault|Savagery's Final Assault]] features enemies with {{IconLink|Sweep}} which will wipe out the egg easily if they reach Lady Gilda; they should be taken out on the lower floors first. *If you're planning on fighting the Titans, two of the three Seraph battles also feature threats to the egg that can prevent you from claiming another {{DragonsHoard|6}} and {{Gold|400}}) before [[The Great Abyss#Clash with the Titans|Clash with the Titans]]; [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]] applies floor-wide [[Corruption]] which will kill the egg easily, while [[Heaven's Maw#Champion of Savagery|Champion of Savagery]] also features {{IconLink|Sweep}} enemies. ===Bloat Matron=== '''Bloat Matron''' synergizes with [[Whelp]]s, reducing their {{Ember}} cost. [[Bloated Whelp]] is the best option for this path, as it can die at will with its ability and apply floorwide {{IconLink|Pyregel}}. Also, if you activate two Bloated Whelps in a row, the second will have its damage increased by the {{IconLink|Pyregel}} applied by the first. However, [[Snotty Whelp]], [[Stuck Up Whelp]], and [[Wealthy Whelp]] can all be fine choices as well. It also works well with other small units intended to die, like [[Imps]] and [[Assistants]]; they just won't have their {{Ember}} costs reduced. Upgrading a Bloated Whelp with {{IconLink|Immortalstone}} is usually advisable, ensuring you can apply {{IconLink|Pyregel}} to all enemies every turn. This path works extremely well if allied with the [[Melting Remnant]]. Cards like [[Primitive Mold]] can '''[[Reform]]''' Bloated Whelps, and many Melting Remnant units are either intended to die quickly or have {{IconLink|Harvest}} triggers of their own. It also works very well with the [[Underlegion]], as [[Funguy]] is a fantastic source of {{IconLink|Harvest}} triggers, activating {{IconLink|Harvest}} every time it loses a {{IconLink|Troop}} stack. ===Lady Avarice=== '''Lady Avarice''' benefits from units that can trigger {{IconLink|Avarice}} multiple times, like [[Bloated Whelp]]s (their '''Indigestion''' ability damages all enemy units and earns {{Gold}} for every unblocked hit), or units with {{IconLink|Sweep}}, {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, or {{IconLink|Trample}}. It makes for a solid source of {{Gold}} in the early rings, where it is arguably most important, and can easily earn an extra {{Gold|50}} or so. Later on, aside from simply being an excellent {{Gold}} generator, she can become a powerful attacker as well. However, this path struggles in early rings due to {{Capacity}} constraints. '''Lady Gilda''' requires {{Capacity|3}}, but doesn't have {{IconLink|Avarice}} herself, and her stats are generally insufficient to survive long on the front lines; against the Ring 1 bosses, on average, she will only be able to take one more hit than a [[Shield Steward]]. Putting a {{Capacity|2}} tank in front of her, like [[Gildmonger]], doesn't make much use of her {{IconLink|Enchant}}. By contrast, putting [[Bloated Whelp]]s behind her can trigger {{IconLink|Avarice}} many times, but it means she will generally be unable to contribute much to the boss fight, as she will take a lot of damage. This can lead to an early loss, especially at high [[Covenant Rank]]s. '''Lady Avarice''' is safest in the early rings if you have [[Ascend]] or [[Descend]] cards in your starting deck, such as [[Hidden Passage]], [[Rising Rage]], and [[Gravity]]. This lets you get around {{Capacity}} problems, grants more units to benefit from {{IconLink|Avarice}}, and keeps '''Lady Gilda''' safe. The problems with {{Capacity}} persist throughout the run, though they can be mitigated with effects like [[Bogwurm's Growth]], [[Heaven's Light]], {{IconLink|Smidgestone}}, [[Exile's Diadem]], and {{Capacity|1}} units. They also become less relevant as your deck gets stronger, at which point she can simply be a strong way to boost your economy, turning every unit into a [[Miser]]. [[Underlegion]] similarly works quite well with her as an allied clan, as they can [[Propagate]] the {{IconLink|Avarice}} to further boost income, and then if/when '''Lady Gilda''' herself dies, they only lose the baseline {{IconLink|Avarice}} her {{IconLink|Enchant}} grants; this means sometimes you can even kill her deliberately to save space and somewhat mitigate her {{Capacity}} issues. ==Quotes== '''Summoned''' * ''Consider this a rare favor.'' * ''I could use a little more sparkle around here.'' * ''I expect nothing less than gold, darling.'' * ''Oh, this better be worth my time...'' * ''The boss dragon is here!'' * ''This sort of thing is normally beneath me.'' Deal '''1''' damage to enemy units.}} |flavor = "Look, I know I'm gold-intolerant, but I'm not going to stop eating coins." |artist = Loy Bouttamy }} '''Bloated Whelp''' is [[Lady Gilda]]'s starter card. Its {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}, '''Indigestion''', allows it to die instantly, dealing 1 damage to all enemies on the floor. == Strategy == '''Bloated Whelps''' are reasonably useful in most builds, essentially a [[Flicker]] which requires {{Capacity|1}}, costs {{Ember|1}} and can be saved for a later turn. However, they are not particularly strong and are a good target for removal. With Lady Gilda's '''Bloat Matron''' path, they are significantly stronger: they can be played for free on her floor, and apply {{IconLink|Pyregel}} to all enemies when they die. If using this path it may even be worth using {{IconLink|Immortalstone}} to guarantee a consistent supply of '''Bloated Whelps'''. This becomes even stronger when allied with the [[Melting Remnant]], which can '''[[Reform]]''' the '''Bloated Whelps''' to play them again, and which has many units that can take advantage of {{IconLink|Harvest}} triggers. With Lady Gilda's '''Lady Avarice''' path, '''Bloated Whelps''' can earn a bunch of {{Gold}} because she provides {{IconLink|Avarice}} to each one played on her floor, and their '''Indigestion''' ability damages all enemy units and thus earns {{Gold}} for every unblocked hit. '''Bloated Whelps''' synergize with cards like [[Lava Flow]] and artifacts like [[Flaming Talons]] that apply {{IconLink|Pyregel}} to all enemy units. They also work much better than other [[Whelp]] units for the [[Sacrificial Kris]] and [[Attuned Manacles]] artifacts, since they can use '''Indigestion''' to die immediately rather than relying on enemies or spells to kill them. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! {{UnitCard |name = Snotty Whelp |image = PLR_SnottyWhelp.png |clan = [[Pyreborne]] |rarity = Common |type = Whelp |banner = No |cost = 1 |size = 1 |stats = 4/1 |ability = {{AbilityBox|Gellysneeze|2|Deal '''1''' damage then apply {{IconLink|Pyregel|12}} to the front enemy unit.}} |flavor = The carrier whelps are excellent at delivering important materials quickly, just so long as you don't mind a little mucus. |artist = Genevieve Bega }} '''Snotty Whelp''' is a common [[Pyreborne]] unit. Its {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}, '''Gellysneeze''', deals a single point of damage and then applies {{IconLink|Pyregel|12}} to the front enemy unit. == Strategy == The '''Snotty Whelp''' is a decent unit, capable of applying a lot of {{IconLink|Pyregel}} to enemies. '''Gellysneeze''' applies the most {{IconLink|Pyregel}} of any single effect, slightly more than a [[Pyrecask]], but can only be used every other turn and has a set target. Since the front enemy unit will usually be either a boss or a tank, you will almost always be able to make good use out of it. Particularly in the early game, it can make killing bosses like [[Astrael the Lost]] and [[Elebor the Wall]] much less painful. In case the damage kills the front enemy unit, the {{IconLink|Pyregel}} will be applied to the next enemy unit. Since cooldown resets on unit death, killing and replaying '''Snotty Whelp''' helps make its {{IconLink|Pyregel}} application more consistent. This can be accomplished through '''[[Reform]]''' effects if you're partnered with the [[Melting Remnant]], or more commonly through {{IconLink|Immortalstone}} to make the unit {{IconLink|Endless}}. It can also absorb a hit for your other units this way, which is useful since the Pyreborne tend to struggle with defense. Note that since '''Gellysneeze''' technically deals damage, it will absorb a stack of {{IconLink|Spell Shield}} and all stacks of {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}}. Usually this is not ideal, and {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} should be saved for a more powerful user like [[Hot Head]]. As a [[Whelp]], it has synergies with [[Sacrificial Kris]], [[Attuned Manacles]], and [[Lady Gilda]]'s '''Bloat Matron''' path. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] !
