Hot Head:
{{UnitCard |name = Hot Head |image = PLR_HotHead.png |clan = [[Pyreborne]] |rarity = Uncommon |type = Dragon |banner = Yes |cost = {{Ember|2}} |size = {{Capacity|2}} |stats = {{AttackHealth|5|20}} |ability = {{AbilityBox|Fire Breathing|2|Deal damage equal to this unit's attack to enemy units, twice.}} |flavor = The guard dragons for Lady Gilda chew magma all day, just in case they ever have to give a special spew to a tax collector. |artist = Daniel Sarmiento Chuquisengo }} '''Hot Head''' is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] [[banner unit]]. Its {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}} is '''Fire Breathing''', which deals damage to all enemy units on the floor equal to [[Hot Head]]'s {{Attack}} twice, and has a cooldown of 2. == Strategy == '''Hot Head''' is an extremely splashable unit, providing consistent value to almost any run, provided you can manage its {{Ember|2}} cost. At the bare minimum, it sits on a lower floor, eliminating threatening backlines every other wave that could otherwise pose an issue for your higher floors, such as {{IconLink|Sweep}} enemies or [[Blight]] spawners. When provided with investment, it can consistently severely dent even the sturdiest double-heavy waves, outright ruining them and allowing your strategy much more flexibility to scale without the looming threat of any early damage to the Pyre. Due to [[Hot Head]]'s ability to reach an entire wave of backlines at once, it will naturally be killing a large quantity of units; thus, anything that provides a scaling {{IconLink|Slay}} trigger can amplify '''Hot Head''' significantly. Examples include [[Shadow's Sheath]], [[Bloodthirsty Blade]], and especially [[Bloodsoaked Arena]] if playing with the [[Banished]] clan. [[Pyre of Savagery]] also makes '''Hot Head''' a fantastic pick. '''Hot Head''' is also one of the strongest in-clan recipients of [[Mind Cage]] and [[Tome of Contracts]], as it will allow the use of its '''Fire Breathing''' ability every turn, essentially turning '''Hot Head''' into the equivalent of a {{IconLink|Quick}} {{IconLink|Sweep}}er with {{IconLink|Multistrike}} that still has an extra attack. Thus, if you are leaning on '''Hot Head''' as your dedicated backline solve, or you have the pieces to make it a central unit to your run, it is recommended to seek out these cards actively and make them as available to play as soon as possible with a '''[[Deployable]]''' or '''[[Intrinsic]]''' upgrade, respectively. Visiting the [[Merchant of Arms]] in Ring 3 may be advisable purely for the sake of finding Mind Cage and making it Deployable right away (as well as the possibility, with enough {{Gold}}, of finding Bloodthirsty Blade as well and merging the two). When starting with [[Bloated Whelp]]s, the [[Attuned Manacles]] artifact can be a sufficient substitute for either of the above methods of reducing cooldown. An {{IconLink|Endless}} Bloated Whelp can be placed down each turn to reduce its cooldown, then immediately killed so that you will see it again next turn. This becomes even stronger if you also have the [[Sacrificial Kris]] to apply {{IconLink|Pyregel}} to enemy units. '''Hot Head''' stands to benefit quite a bit from many of the minor Pyreborne artifacts. [[Medallion of Superiority]] and [[Sharpened Teeth]] both give it a small but useful {{Attack}} boost, while [[Shaleshell]] grants it a bit of {{IconLink|Armor}} whenever it uses its ability. [[Taskmaster's Lash]] can reduce its cooldown if you can damage it with a weak spell such as [[Torch]] every turn. Despite [[Hot Head]]'s overall strength, it suffers somewhat against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Entropic]]. The [[Purified Soul]]s in that fight come with {{IconLink|Spell Shield|2}}, which protects them against '''Fire Breathing''', and the [[Deafening Herald]]s will {{IconLink|Silence}} '''Hot Head''' and disable its ability entirely. If fighting this version of Seraph, it is important to find solutions for these enemies, such as [[Jackstrips]] for the Purified Souls or [[Zone of Silence]] for the Heralds. [[Make It Rain]] will kill both the Purified Souls and the Deafening Heralds without any upgrades necessary, as long as you have enough {{Gold}}, as can [[Inferno Room]]. [[Flicker]] upgraded with {{IconLink|Powerstone}} and {{IconLink|Keepstone}} will kill Deafening Heralds and remove a stack of {{IconLink|Spell Shield}} from the Purified Souls, allowing '''Hot Head''' to kill them. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! Greed Dragon:
{{UnitCard |name = Greed Dragon |image = PLR_GreedDragon.png |clan = [[Pyreborne]] |rarity = Uncommon |type = Dragon |banner = Yes |cost = 2 |size = 3 |stats = {{AttackHealth|20|35}} |ability = {{IconLink|Summon}}: {{Attack|+10}} and {{Health|+10}} for each {{DragonsHoard}}. |flavor = These Master Keepers of the Coin tend to take their job to the literal conclusion and hoard every small gold flake they can find. |artist = Daniel Sarmiento Chuquisengo }} The '''Greed Dragon''' is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] [[banner unit]]. It gains {{AttackHealth|+10|+10}} per {{DragonsHoard}} you currently have on {{IconLink|Summon}}. == Strategy == '''Greed Dragon''' has the potential to have rather high base stats, and with high {{DragonsHoard}} it's possibly the best tank available for the Pyreborne - a clan that can otherwise struggle on defense. You'll need to have {{DragonsHoard}} generation to want it, of course. It does ask you a rather interesting question at the end of each combat - do you want to loot your {{DragonsHoard}}? If you do, you get a reward, but it means that '''Greed Dragon''' will be weak next combat if you play it during the deployment phase, as you won't have any {{DragonsHoard}} then, and getting {{DragonsHoard}} later won't help during the current fight. If you are too greedy, you could doom your run this way. There's a few ways you can answer this question. One is simply to not loot your {{DragonsHoard}} at the end of each combat and let it sit at a high number. This lets you Purge your {{DragonsHoard}} generation if it isn't helping otherwise, though you are losing out on {{DragonsHoard}} rewards this way. Another is to not play '''Greed Dragon''' during the deploy phase, potentially letting you get {{DragonsHoard}} before playing it, if you can survive without it through the early turns. Or, you could have your cake and eat it too with {{IconLink|Immortalstone}}, allowing you to loot your {{DragonsHoard}}, play '''Greed Dragon''' early, and then play it again later after you've got {{DragonsHoard}}. The bonus stats obtained carry over resummons, letting you accumulate them multiple times! But you will need ways to ensure that '''Greed Dragon''' dies so that you can boost its stats enough for the boss. It'll also cost you a card and {{Ember|2}} each time - well worth it much of the time, but a cost to consider as well. [[Greed]], friendly fire from [[Lord Fenix]], or [[Sacrifice]] effects can help you do this. If you have consistent [[Sacrifice]] effects, you can get '''Greed Dragon''''s stats to huge levels this way - and even more so if you hold your {{DragonsHoard}} between combats! The [[Lazarus League]] in particular has some incredible synergies with an {{IconLink|Endless}} '''Greed Dragon'''. [[Scrap for Parts]] will instantly kill the unit, then put it back in your hand, while also reducing its cost to {{Ember|0}} and granting it an extra {{Attack|+40}}. Or you can use [[Brain Transfer]] to give its titanic {{Attack}} to a unit better suited to make use of it, such as a [[Plague Doctor]] or [[Test Subject Alpha]] with {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, before playing it again next turn, better than before. Due to its {{IconLink|Summon}} trigger, it has even greater potential than usual when used alongside the [[Hellhorned]] clan. {{UnitCard |name = Magma Cultist |image = PLR_MagmaCultist.png |clan = [[Pyreborne]] |rarity = Uncommon |type = Dragon |banner = Yes |cost = 2 |size = 1 |stats = 5/10 |ability = {{IconLink|Incant}}: Apply {{IconLink|Pyregel|1}} to enemy units. |flavor = ''"One day Fhyra will rise again. When she does, she will coat us in gold, and we will shine like magma in the gloom."'' |artist = Aaron Lovett }} '''Magma Cultist''' is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] [[banner unit]]. It applies {{IconLink|Pyregel|1}} to all enemies on {{IconLink|Incant}}. == Strategy == While not an impressive unit in terms of stats, the '''Magma Cultist''' can be deceptively powerful when focusing on its strengths. Although applying {{IconLink|Pyregel|1}} may seem weak, there are many synergies that can drastically increase its power. The most straightforward strategy when using this unit is to amplify the {{IconLink|Pyregel}} it applies. Upgrading it with {{IconLink|Dualstone}}, while useful, is less necessary than it may seem, as {{IconLink|Dualism}} will only increase its {{IconLink|Pyregel}} application per {{IconLink|Incant}} by 1. The same effect can be achieved through the minor [[Hellfire Bellows]] artifact received through redeeming {{DragonsHoard}}; this artifact is powerful in general, but is crucial in unlocking '''Magma Cultist''''s true potential due to the low amount of {{IconLink|Pyregel}} it applies per trigger. Additionally, as a minor artifact, it is much easier to acquire than others. As such, strong {{DragonsHoard}} production, especially in the early rings, should be sought after. Applying {{IconLink|Pyregel}} makes it easier to trigger {{IconLink|Slay}} with [[Golden Touch]]. [[Lord Fenix]]'s '''Pyremaniac''' path provides a huge boost to {{IconLink|Pyregel}} application, adding +4 stacks at max level. His '''Fenix Fire''' ability also applies {{IconLink|Pyregel}}, and can be used to take out irritating backline units. This path should be considered more strongly if '''Magma Cultist''' is your starting banner unit. Additionally, although Lord Fenix is a {{Capacity|3}} unit, '''Magma Cultist''' requires only {{Capacity|1}}, which means you can fit a second copy of the unit behind him without taking any {{Capacity}} upgrades. The [[Hellfurnace]] room is the second best {{IconLink|Pyregel}} amplifier if you do not have Lord Fenix or chose a different path with him, although as a Rare card it can be difficult to find. Keep in mind that with multiple '''Magma Cultists''' on the same floor, effects like Hellfurnace and Hellfire Bellows will increase the {{IconLink|Pyregel}} applied by each individual '''Magma Cultist'''. With two '''Magma Cultists''' in a Hellfurnace room, each {{IconLink|Incant}} will apply {{IconLink|Pyregel|8}} to enemy units, rather than {{IconLink|Pyregel|5}}. The [[Cursed Dragonstaff]] seems perfectly designed to synergize with '''Magma Cultist'''. Each {{IconLink|Incant}} will trigger its area of effect damage, which is then increased by the {{IconLink|Pyregel}} the unit applies. This can let '''Magma Cultist''' efficiently remove low {{Health}} enemies while also softening up the frontline tanks. Other useful artifacts for using '''Magma Cultist''' include [[Gel Transfusor]] and [[Sparkflint Catalyst]]. The damage dealt by [[Jackstrips]] will be increased by {{IconLink|Pyregel}} and can add up quickly, while [[Vola's Tuning Fork]] can make it easier to play starting spells like [[Firestarter]]. Spells like [[Flicker]] and [[Fanning the Flame]], which are normally quite weak, can become devastating with '''Magma Cultist''' supporting them. [[Make It Rain]] hits multiple times, scaling excellently with {{IconLink|Pyregel}} as long as you have {{Gold}} to spend on it, while [[Deathroar]] can devastate bosses at the cost of removing {{IconLink|Pyregel}} from other units on the floor. When partnered with the [[Stygian Guard]], '''Magma Cultist''' truly shines. It can fit on a floor behind a pair of {{Capacity|2}} units with {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers of their own, like [[Siren of the Sea]], [[Solgard the Martyr]], or [[Guard of the Unnamed]], and make enemy lines vulnerable as its allies scale. The [[Founding Seal]] artifact makes {{IconLink|Incant}} effects trigger twice, doubling the unit's effectiveness. It makes a fantastic partner for [[Eel Gorgon]], as Eel Gorgon tends to make a large number of weak attacks, and the {{IconLink|Pyregel}} applied by '''Magma Cultist''' can quickly make each of those weak attacks devastating. Due to '''Magma Cultist''''s {{Ember|2}} cost, the relatively small impact of shop upgrades on it, and the effectiveness of having multiple copies on the same floor, it can be worth leaving the unit without upgrades if you have the [[Purified Soul Shard]] for the sake of saving {{Ember}} during Deployment. Since '''Magma Cultist''' is not an especially effective attacker or tank, [[Stasis Crystal]] can be an expensive but effective way of keeping the unit safe. Notably, this can protect it against [[Qel the Corruptor]], who is otherwise very problematic to deal with when using '''Magma Cultist'''. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! {{UnitCard |name = Magma Mauler |image = PLR_MagmaMauler.png |clan = [[Pyreborne]] |rarity = Uncommon |type = Dragon |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 10/25 |ability = {{IconLink|Strike}}: Apply {{IconLink|Pyregel|8}}. |flavor = "You better pay what you owe to Lady Gilda, or I'll squash your toes!" |artist = Aaron Lovett }} '''Magma Mauler''' is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] [[banner unit]]. It applies {{IconLink|Pyregel|8}} on {{IconLink|Strike}}. == Strategy == '''Magma Mauler''' is a solid frontline bruiser for the Pyreborne, specializing in softening up tanky enemies and bosses. Its respectable {{Health|25}} allows it to take some hits and protect the vulnerable units behind it, although in the later rings it will quickly crumble if not supplemented with upgrades or defensive measures. It is a flexible unit that can also be played behind a proper tank like a [[Greed Dragon]] to keep it safe. Because {{IconLink|Pyregel}} scales with the number of hits and not the strength of those hits, '''Magma Mauler''' appreciates a backline of low-{{Capacity}} units, such as [[Miser]]s and [[Whelp]]s, hitting as many times as possible. These units are weak, but each hit from '''Magma Mauler''' effectively ups their {{Attack}} and can thus represent much more damage than one might guess. Units with great amounts of {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, such as [[Animus of Will]], [[Hydra Armed Horror]], and [[Dante the Dependable]] also complement '''Magma Mauler''' exquisitely. The [[Follower]]s received from the [[Cult of the Lamb]] event are perhaps the epitome of this; they take up only {{Capacity|1}} and have {{IconLink|Multistrike|2}}, providing a huge number of hits. Artifacts and effects that increase the amount of {{IconLink|Pyregel}} applied, such [[Hellfire Bellows]] and [[Hellfurnace]], pair well with '''Magma Mauler'''. However, unlike its counterpart, the [[Magma Cultist]], these effects are much less necessary for '''Magma Mauler''' due to the greater amount of {{IconLink|Pyregel}} it applies per trigger and the difficulty of triggering {{IconLink|Strike}} repeatedly as opposed to {{IconLink|Incant}}. [[Magma Mauler]]'s biggest weakness is its inability to do anything against backline units. Pairing it with a unit like [[Hot Head]] or [[Zealot]] is a good idea; those units can mop up low-{{Health}} enemies while '''Magma Mauler''' makes the heavies vulnerable. Failing that, spells like [[Pyreball]], [[Dragon's Breath]], and [[Fanning the Flame]] can be used to eliminate the backline instead. Alternatively, the [[Iron-tongue]] is an extremely strong choice, effectively turning the unit into a pseudo-Zealot by granting it {{IconLink|Sweep}} and letting it apply {{IconLink|Pyregel}} to all units on the floor with its attack. Equipping it with [[Lava Armor]] allows it to apply even more {{IconLink|Pyregel}} and makes it slightly tankier, though still not enough to survive full combats unassisted. '''Magma Mauler''' shines during {{IconLink|Relentless}} combats, as every hit will build up more and more {{IconLink|Pyregel}} on the boss, as long as you can keep it alive. This is a great help against highly durable enemies like [[Ajax the Unyielding]] and [[Quoto the Absolute]], but less so against [[The Undying One]]. Beware when fighting [[Seraph Aeternus-The Entropic]], as the {{IconLink|Sap|5}} he applies will reduce an unupgraded '''Magma Mauler''' to {{Attack|0}}, meaning it will not attack at all. The Titan Trial ups this further to {{IconLink|Sap|10}}, not counting any applied by playing [[Curse of Entropy]]. Equipment to increase its base damage output, such as [[Swiftsteel Dagger]], should be considered if this unit is to be a major participant in the combat. Equipment that locks its {{Attack}}, like [[Equalizing Rings]] or the aforementioned Iron-tongue, works as well. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! {{UnitCard |name = Miser |image = PLR_Miser.png |clan = [[Pyreborne]] |rarity = Uncommon |type = Dragon |banner = Yes |cost = {{Ember|1}} |size = {{Capacity|1}} |stats = {{AttackHealth|8|8}} |ability = {{IconLink|Avarice|10}}. |flavor = To be a Miser is the highest honor amongst the Pyreborne and is only given to those who have shown such love of coin that they refuse to spend it for anything. |artist = Aaron Lovett }} '''Miser''' is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] [[banner unit]]. Its stats are poor, but it generates lots of {{Gold}}. == Strategy == The '''Miser''' is an unusual unit, with very low stats and little to no benefit in the current battle. Its high {{IconLink|Avarice}}, however, allows it to stack up enormous amounts of {{Gold}} and lets you become much stronger over the course of the run. It is best used when you have a strong enough build to be confident that you can win the next ring, and want to focus more on putting together a build that can take on later rings. It is a {{Capacity|1}} banner unit, which is rare. This allows it to be an effective filler unit when the floor otherwise consists of multiple {{Capacity|2}} units, which are most common. As {{IconLink|Avarice}} gains more {{Gold}} with the amount of times the unit attacks, it can be worth debuffing or even killing other units in order to ensure '''Miser''' hits as many times as possible. If placed behind a durable unit for {{IconLink|Relentless}}, although it is unlikely to actually kill the boss, it will generate plenty of {{Gold}} before it dies. Aside from allowing you to make more purchases at shops, [[Miser]]'s generation of {{Gold}} will help power up [[Goldtooth]] and [[Lady Gilda]]'s '''Lady Avarice''' path. In later rings, when there are few shops remaining, having these units can let '''Miser''' stay relevant. Though generally a strong choice when offered at a [[Unit Banner]], '''Miser''' can be weak when it is one of your starting cards. Being able to use it from the very beginning of the run can allow you to rack up even more {{Gold}}, but if the rest of your deck cannot pick up the slack you may simply die on the first or second ring. On Ring 1, choose your [[Champion]] path and [[Herzal's Hoard]] artifact accordingly. When offered through [[Pyre of Dominion]], '''Miser''' improves significantly. You will naturally have two copies of it, as well as three other banner units which can hopefully carry you through the first ring without issue. Its low {{Capacity}} means two of them can fit behind a sturdy {{Capacity|3}} unit, like a [[Shadeguard]], [[Thorned Hollow]], or [[Hulking Mass]], and generate massive amounts of {{Gold}} for you to spend at your first shop. This can often solve money issues for the remainder of the run, and lets you be pickier about taking on [[Trial]]s. If you are offered [[Iron-tongue]] at an [[Armory]] or the [[Merchant of Arms]], consider putting it on '''Miser''', as this can keep it relevant even into the late game. {{IconLink|Sweep}} will trigger {{IconLink|Avarice}} for every unit struck, amplifying {{Gold}} production, and the equipment's {{Attack|30}} is a significant increase over the unit's default {{Attack}}. Upgrading '''Miser''' with {{IconLink|Speedstone}} and {{IconLink|Frenzystone}} can even allow it to clear out dangerous backliners like [[Chosen Assassin]]s and [[Holy Cherub]]s while occupying only {{Capacity|1}}. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! Its {{Attack}} scales with the amount of {{Gold}} you have. == Strategy == '''Goldtooth''' is an unusual unit due to how it interacts with the Pyreborne's exceptional economy. Its scaling generally takes place outside of combat rather than within it. Many Pyreborne runs are capable of generating more {{Gold}} than can reasonably be spent, and are able to completely buy out shops while purging unnecessary cards. However, '''Goldtooth''' encourages a more conservative approach, saving {{Gold}} where possible in order to increase its damage output. Thus, when using '''Goldtooth''', generating as much {{Gold}} as possible is of great importance, so that you are still able to buy the things you need while also keeping its {{Attack}} high. [[Sacrificial Chamber]] is a particularly good source of {{Gold}}, especially if most kills are exclusively on a single floor, or if played with [[Manifold Mirror]]. [[Greed]] can be useful, both for clearing out backline enemies and for earning {{Gold}}, and you can also kill off weak units like [[Whelp]]s with it. The [[Stuck Up Whelp]] and [[Wealthy Whelp]] are both decent sources of {{Gold}} themselves. The [[Golden Gloves]] grant a small but meaningful amount of {{IconLink|Avarice}} to all units, which is especially strong with {{IconLink|Multistrike}} or {{IconLink|Sweep}} units, or with [[Hot Head]] or [[Bloated Whelp]]s, who will gain {{Gold}} for each enemy damaged by their ability. [[Lady Gilda]] has good synergy with '''Goldtooth'''. The most obvious is her '''Lady Avarice''' path, which has a similar scaling effect to '''Goldtooth''' and applies {{IconLink|Avarice}} to friendly units to earn even more {{Gold}}. However, her '''Gildmother''' path should not be underestimated either, especially its synergy with [[Hall of Mirrors]]; the Gildeder Egg grants {{Gold|50}} at the end of the battle and the Gildedest Egg grants a whopping {{Gold|400}}, which is quadrupled if you can play her in a Hall of Mirrors, alongside a tremendous amount of {{DragonsHoard}}. [[Miser]] is an excellent support unit for '''Goldtooth''', particularly if placed behind a sturdy tank during {{IconLink|Relentless}} and on a floor below '''Goldtooth'''. Miser's low {{Attack}} and high {{IconLink|Avarice}} allow it to earn hundreds of {{Gold}} in a drawn-out boss fight, and it can even be worth applying {{IconLink|Sap}} or {{IconLink|Dazed}} to your other units to keep the fight going for as long as possible. '''Goldtooth''' itself will typically finish off bosses quickly. When partnered with the [[Melting Remnant]], '''Goldtooth''' is even more potent, as it can be used with [[Wickless Tycoon]], earning {{Gold}} every time a unit dies. Wickless Tycoon is also a respectable tank and can protect the relatively fragile '''Goldtooth'''. [[Memorial Fund]] is an excellent artifact as well, earning {{Gold|5}} whenever a friendly unit dies, which can be combined with Sacrificial Chamber, Greed, and even [[Hallowed Halls]] to kill and '''[[Reform]]''' weak units. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! Pyreblooded:
{{UnitCard |name = Pyreblooded |image = PLR_Pyreblooded.png |clan = [[Pyreborne]] |rarity = Rare |type = Dragon |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 1 |stats = 5/10 |ability = {{AbilityBox|Empower|3|Gain {{Attack}} equal to {{IconLink|Pyregel}} stacks on all units.}} |flavor = Some dragons take their obsession with gold to a new level. Entranced by the golden hues of the Pyre, these dragons insert pyregel directly into their veins. Somehow, they survive the process. |artist = Mary Ngai-Virgo }} '''Pyreblooded''' is a rare [[Pyreborne]] [[banner unit]]. Its {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}, '''Empower''', grants the unit {{Attack}} equal to {{IconLink|Pyregel}} stacks on all units on the floor, with a cooldown of 3. == Strategy == '''Pyreblooded''' is usually a fairly weak unit, only fitting into a few specific builds. However, it is fairly low-investment, taking only {{Ember|1}} and {{Capacity|1}}, so it is not unreasonable to speculate on it if you suspect that you may lean into {{IconLink|Pyregel}} strategies later, especially if it is up against a unit that also does not solve your immediate problems, like [[Miser]] or [[Gildmonger]]. Against a stronger unit like [[Hot Head]], it should really only be taken if it already fits into your build. Obviously, it needs a strong {{IconLink|Pyregel}} engine. Due to the natural flow of combat, it cannot really take advantage of effects that apply {{IconLink|Pyregel}} during combat, like [[Magma Mauler]] or [[Lava Armor]], unless placed on a higher floor. Instead, focus on effects that can apply {{IconLink|Pyregel}} before combat, especially in an area. [[Magma Cultist]] synergizes excellently with '''Pyreblooded''', applying {{IconLink|Pyregel}} to the whole floor in small amounts, which receives maximum benefit from flat amplifiers like [[Hellfurnace]] and '''Pyremaniac''' [[Lord Fenix]]. Additionally, since both of the units are {{Capacity|1}}, they can fit behind a {{Capacity|3}} unit with no upgrades, like [[Lady Gilda]] or a [[Greed Dragon]]. Without Magma Cultist, '''Pyreblooded''' is much harder to use. Cards like [[Lava Flow]] and [[Snotty Whelp]] can apply more {{IconLink|Pyregel}}. However, you want to avoid actually killing units for as long as possible, as any unit that dies before using '''Empower''' is lost {{Attack}} scaling. This makes the [[Cursed Dragonstaff]] worse, as you will usually end up killing most of the enemies via {{IconLink|Incant}}ing before you can apply enough total {{IconLink|Pyregel}} to make '''Empower''' worthwhile. If you need to clear enemies before combat, instead consider a card like [[Flicker]] that you can play after you have put down as much {{IconLink|Pyregel}} as possible. This unit has a notable advantage against [[Flying Bosses]], whose massive {{Health}} pools and presence throughout combat mean that they will often build up a lot of {{IconLink|Pyregel}}. Using '''Empower''' when a flying boss arrives on your floor can easily net '''Pyreblooded''' {{Attack|50+}}. This gets even better if you have [[Superheated]]. Generally, if you are applying enough {{IconLink|Pyregel}} that [[Pyreblooded]]'s {{Attack}} gain is significant, you don't really need it for the waves; '''[[Explosive]]''' spells and multi-hit spells like [[Make It Rain]] will suffice. [[Pyreblooded]]'s main advantage is against bosses, especially minibosses, whose large {{Health}} pools and limited time on the train make it difficult to apply mass amounts of {{IconLink|Pyregel}} to them. '''Pyreblooded''' can turn your {{IconLink|Pyregel}} application across the battle into direct damage against the boss, securing victory in only a few rounds of combat. Reducing '''Empower''''s cooldown through effects like [[Mind Cage]] or [[Tome of Contracts]] makes '''Pyreblooded''' more effective, as it will scale much faster. [[Gel Transfusor]] helps ensure that {{IconLink|Pyregel}} will not go to waste when enemies die, potentially allowing you to wipe out waves while still gaining lots of {{Attack}} through '''Empower'''. [[Sparkflint Catalyst]] and [[Hellfire Bellows]] both amplify {{IconLink|Pyregel}} application, and [[Flaming Talons]] automatically applies a small amount to enemies when they ascend. If you have run where '''Pyreblooded''' is a big contributor to your victory, it's often a solid duplication target due to its low {{Capacity}} and the fact that both copies will scale at an equal rate. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! Zealot:
{{UnitCard |name = Zealot |image = PLR_Zealot.png |clan = [[Pyreborne]] |rarity = Rare |type = Dragon |banner = Yes |cost = 3 |size = 2 |stats = 10/20 |ability = {{IconLink|Sweep}}.
{{IconLink|Action}}: Apply {{IconLink|Pyregel|5}} to enemy units. |flavor = Debtors to the Pyreborne imprisoned in The Pit learn that the Zealot's tongue is just as harsh as their whip. |artist = Luke Banke }} '''Zealot''' is a rare [[Pyreborne]] [[banner unit]]. It applies {{IconLink|Pyregel}} to all enemies on its floor before attacking with {{IconLink|Sweep}}. == Strategy == Although its {{Ember|3}} cost may seem prohibitive, '''Zealot''' is a very strong unit in the Pyreborne pool, and if seen, it is very often worth taking [[Hell's Flame]] to enable playing '''Zealot''' more easily during deployment. Due to its status as a {{IconLink|Sweep}} unit (and one of the most individually powerful ones at that), it is flexible and can slot into a variety of strategies. '''Zealot''' can either sit downstairs with {{IconLink|Quick}} and clear dangerous backlines for your run while softening up anything it can't kill with {{IconLink|Pyregel}}, or act as your run's main damage dealer with its {{IconLink|Sweep}} if you can support it with mass {{IconLink|Pyregel}} application from other sources or {{Attack}} buffs from your other clan. The most consistent comparable unit in the Pyreborne clan is [[Hot Head]], who is uncommon and can similarly clear out backliners. Furthermore, Hot Head's ability means that it effectively has {{IconLink|Quick}} and {{IconLink|Multistrike}} built in, whereas '''Zealot''' must find those upgrades in shops or equipment. However, '''Zealot''' still has several advantages over Hot Head. Hot Head is reliant on methods of Cooldown reduction in order to perform consistently, such as [[Tome of Contracts]], [[Attuned Manacles]], or by far the most common, [[Mind Cage]]. You are not necessarily guaranteed to see any of these cards or artifacts, and even if you are offered Mind Cage, you must then path to a [[Merchant of Arms]] to make it deployable for maximum consistency (unless you have [[Attuned Whetstone]]). Further, since Hot Head costs {{Ember|2}} and Mind Cage costs {{Ember|1}}, you are ultimately paying the same price you would to deploy '''Zealot'''. And lastly, '''Zealot''' is significantly more effective against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Entropic]], as the [[Purified Soul]]s in that fight will shrug off Hot Head's ability thanks to {{IconLink|Spell Shield|2}}, and the [[Deafening Herald]]s will disable it outright with {{IconLink|Silence}}, whereas '''Zealot''' will only lose its {{IconLink|Action}} trigger, not its {{IconLink|Sweep}} damage. '''Zealot''' is also stronger during {{IconLink|Relentless}} as it will keep stacking {{IconLink|Pyregel}} on the boss. Because '''Zealot''' is so flexible, taking it significantly diversifies your [[Merchant of Steel|Merchants of Steel]]. Most notably, {{IconLink|Speedstone}} becomes an extremely strong upgrade, which other Pyreborne banner units aside from [[Goldtooth]] do not usually want to take. However, '''Zealot''' can also make use of {{IconLink|Frenzystone}}, {{IconLink|Largestone}}, and {{IconLink|Dualstone}}, almost guaranteeing that you will see value out of Steel shops with it in your deck. As with other sweepers, '''Zealot''' synergizes well with equipment and rooms that give {{IconLink|Slay}} or {{IconLink|Strike}} triggers, making cards such as [[Bloodthirsty Blade]] suitable choices. Within the clan, [[Hellfurnace]] can bolster its {{IconLink|Pyregel}} application. If playing with the [[Lazarus League]], [[Twisted Back]] from [[Twisted Assistant]] is especially powerful as it gives {{IconLink|Trample}} alongside its {{IconLink|Rage}} scaling, which has a very favorable interaction with {{IconLink|Sweep}} as extra damage from killed backlines will wrap back around to units in the front. [[Swiftsteel Dagger]] can also suffice if you do not see {{IconLink|Speedstone}} in your shops. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! Though it is expensive for its low damage output, it generates {{DragonsHoard|1}} when it kills its target. == Strategy == '''Golden Touch''' is one of the two common Pyreborne spells which can produce {{DragonsHoard}}, the other being [[Alchemy]]. Compared to Alchemy, '''Golden Touch''' produces less {{DragonsHoard}} and requires a low-{{Health}} target, but it is cheaper and not entirely useless in the current battle. It can also be used multiple times if drawn repeatedly. It will be relatively easy to land kills in the early game, when many enemies have less than {{Health|5}}. Later on, however, its effectiveness will be limited unless you have a way to buff its damage, as even backliners will usually have enough {{Health}} to survive a hit. Thankfully, {{IconLink|Pyregel}} is abundant to boost this spell's damage. [[Pyreborne's Insignia]] is also an excellent minor artifact with '''Golden Touch''', increasing the range of viable targets. Notably, this allows it to kill [[Deafening Herald]]s with no upgrades. On its own merits, '''Golden Touch''' is quite bad, dealing only slightly more damage than [[Torch]] for twice the cost. It should only be used for its ability to create {{DragonsHoard}}. It can also be used to kill your own units, such as [[Spear Steward]] or [[Bloated Whelp]]. This will still give {{DragonsHoard}}. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! But because it costs {{Ember|3}} and has '''[[Consume]]''', it can't generate lots of {{DragonsHoard}} by itself in a single combat without upgrades. As a common [[Cards|card]], '''Alchemy''' can only be found as a draft reward in Rings 1-2, so drafting it generally comes down to a decision of whether your deck is strong enough to handle a card that provides little benefit in the short run while providing great benefit later. During early fights, playing it comes at a significant opportunity cost, as it will take an entire turn of spellcasting to do so. It is essentially a [[Calcified Ember]], taking up draw and requiring {{Ember|3}} to remove with no immediate benefit (unless you play a card like [[Greed Dragon]] which scales off of {{DragonsHoard}} later in the battle). [[Aquath's Reservation]] can help mitigate this. [[Echo of the Time Father]] can also help, freezing it in hand until you can afford to play it. That said, if you ''can'' afford to play it, '''Alchemy''' is one of the best sources of {{DragonsHoard}} in the game. With a reasonably strong start, you can use it to gain enormous amounts of {{DragonsHoard}}, potentially cashing in a full set of 8 by the end of Ring 2 if you happened to start with '''Alchemy'''. It is also a good reason to go to an early [[Merchant of Magic]] if you're confident that you can take on the next ring or two without a [[Merchant of Steel]], as a combination of {{IconLink|Eternalstone}} and {{IconLink|Smolderstone}} makes '''Alchemy''' far better. With those upgrades, it provides {{DragonsHoard|2}} for only {{Ember|1}} each time you shuffle your deck, potentially allowing you to cash in a full set of {{DragonsHoard}} after every battle. Without specific synergies like [[Pay Off]] or [[Inequivalent Exchange]], this card is generally safe to remove after Ring 7, although if you plan to fight the [[Titans]] this may prevent you from redeeming an extra {{DragonsHoard}} after [[Seraph]]. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Note that unlike [[Mind Cage]] or [[Tome of Contracts]], the '''Pyreborne Brainspike''' reduces ''current'' cooldown rather than ''maximum'' cooldown. This means that it can be used to activate an ability twice in a single turn, but unlike those cards it does not allow the ability to be used more frequently for the rest of the battle. It is the Pyreborne offering for the [[Railspikes (event)|Railspikes]] event. == Strategy == The '''Pyreborne Brainspike''' has two purposes: allowing units to use their abilities more frequently, and granting {{Gold}} by applying {{IconLink|Avarice}}. Its cooldown-reducing effect is of limited use: few units will be able to take advantage of more than one or two turns of cooldown reduction, and unlike [[Mind Cage]] or [[Tome of Contracts]] it does not actually decrease future cooldowns. However, it can be used to use an ability twice in the same turn, and can be very helpful for abilities with long cooldowns such as that of [[Hornbreaker Prince]] with one or two levels in '''Reaper'''. Its {{IconLink|Avarice}} can make it worth using even on units without abilities. With {{IconLink|Multistrike}} or {{IconLink|Sweep}}, {{IconLink|Avarice}} can trigger many times per turn, and if you're willing to spend a significant amount of {{Ember}} on '''Pyreborne Brainspike''' then it can provide absolutely massive amounts of {{Gold}} each battle. Fanning the Flame:
{{SpellCard |name = Fanning the Flame |image = CRD_FanningTheFlame.png |clan = Pyreborne |rarity = Uncommon |cost = 1 |effect = '''[[Explosive]]'''.
Deal '''3''' damage to a random enemy unit.
{{IconLink|Slay}}: Increase damage by '''3''' permanently. |flavor = "Fan the flames of war. It's good for business."
—The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #19 |artist = Luke Banke }} '''Fanning the Flame''' is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] spell. It deals 3 damage to a random enemy on the floor. It is '''[[Explosive]]''', meaning that any "leftover" damage will be dealt to all enemies on the floor. For each enemy it kills, either through its initial damage or the Explosive effect, it permanently gains an additional 3 damage. == Strategy == '''Fanning the Flame''' has the potential to be an immensely powerful spell, but it requires an enormous amount of investment and remains inconsistent even under the best circumstances. As an Explosive spell, it works best when targeting enemies with low {{Health}}, but its random targeting makes it difficult to hit them consistently. Its starting damage is the same as a mere [[Torch]], and its random targeting makes it unreliable against most enemy waves. It can easily kill early-game enemies like [[Forsaken]] and [[Savage Spearman]], and its Explosive property allows it to wipe out whole waves of weak enemies, but as {{Health}} increases over the course of the game it will quickly fall behind if not scaled properly. This means that it must get kills constantly, or its damage will be too low to get kills, meaning that it falls even further behind. {{IconLink|Pyregel}} and {{IconLink|Conduit}} can help it keep pace. Most backline enemies from Ring 4 onwards have {{Health|3}} or more, which means the first casting of this spell will only kill one enemy. The [[Pyreborne's Insignia]] artifact obtained by looting {{DragonsHoard}} can help with this; the {{IconLink|Conduit|4}} it applies will make it strong enough even on its first casting to wipe out all [[Vicious Axethrower]]s, [[Misshapen Fiend]]s, [[Sharp-Eye Sniper]]s, and [[Malevolent Hunter]]s in a given wave as long as it hits the right target. It's at its best when taken very early in the game, preferably after the first battle. The waves that help it scale are most common at or before the first boss; taking it after this point requires you to have reliable {{IconLink|Pyregel}} or {{IconLink|Conduit}} support to get it off the ground. The best case scenario is to take it from the [[Pyre of Dominion]], which allows it to start scaling instantly, especially if you luck into the Mark of Invasion [[Trial]] in the first battle. Under optimal circumstances, it can scale up to more than 150 damage by the endgame, making it essentially a non-Attuned, stronger, but randomly targeting version of [[Pyreclasm]] with a far lower cost. If scaled well, its random targeting drawback becomes less important, though it's always at risk of simply hitting a boss or [[Avowed Gladiator]]. '''[[Holdover]]''' and '''[[Intrinsic]]''' are practically required to use it effectively, allowing it to be played every turn and score as many kills as possible. The earlier you can get these upgrades, the better; if you can afford to risk a Ring 2 [[Merchant of Magic]], you can make this spell quite strong. If you are able to scale it up effectively, it is a good target for duplication in the late game. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! [[Upgrade]] !! {{SpellCard |name = Greed |image = CRD_Greed.png |clan = Pyreborne |rarity = Uncommon |cost = 1 |effect = Deal '''20''' damage to all units.
{{IconLink|Slay}}: Gain {{Gold|10}} |flavor = ''Leave the gold for the dragons or else they'll add you to their treasure pile.'' |artist = Leonardo Dionisi }} '''Greed''' is an uncommon [[Pyreborne]] spell. It deals 20 damage to '''all''' units, including friendly units. For each unit killed, enemy or friendly, you gain {{Gold|10}}. == Notes == As the Pyre is completely unaffected by spells, this and other "damage all" spells can be played in the Pyre room without damaging your Pyre. == Strategy == '''Greed''' is a moneymaker and a powerful backline killer rolled up into one card. It does ask that you leave an empty bottom floor for it, however, as few friendly units can tolerate the damage it deals to them. You can certainly feel free to throw friendly units you don't care about like [[Bloated Whelp]] or [[Spear Steward]] onto its floor for extra {{Gold}}, and {{IconLink|Endless}} units that want to die like [[Snotty Whelp]] can repeatedly give you {{Gold}} while also getting the death they seek. [[Gildmonger]] specifically is quite good with this card, as it has a strong {{IconLink|Extinguish}} effect but enough {{Health}} that it may take a few turns to die, so the damage from '''Greed''' can greatly speed up its demise. You'll want to play it on as many turns as possible, so upgrade and adjust your deck accordingly. It plays fairly similarly to [[Inferno Room]] once it has a {{IconLink|Keepstone}} - compared to that, it's less powerful (and thus unable to kill most Chosen enemies on Covenant 10) and consumes one draw per turn but in return makes {{Gold|100+}} per fight. This amount of {{Gold}} can make for a very strong run, letting you snowball for later fights. You might want to not use it against Seraph, however. [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]] will punish you with [[Terrifying Amalgam]]s that will likely hit your Pyre on the bottom floor; [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]], if you're playing on Covenant 10, will punish you with [[Chosen Supplicant]]s that can survive the damage and give you [[Discordant Toll]]s; and [[Seraph Aeternus-The Entropic]] can punish you with [[Purified Soul]]s that will survive and [[Enthralled Ardent]]s and their Chosen variants giving the floor or the train {{Attack}}. And all of these threats are present in the [[Clash with the Titans|Titans]] fight, making it less effective there too. It's comparable to [[Make It Rain]], dealing similar baseline damage to all enemies. Make It Rain costs {{Gold}} rather than earning it, which is a notable disadvantage, but in exchange it scales much better with {{IconLink|Pyregel}} and '''[[Magic Power]]''', it's safe to use on floors with friendly units, and it kills [[Purified Soul]]s and [[Deformed Duo]]s through their defensive buffs. Nevertheless, the value this card can give you in the midgame often means your deck is so strong that its relative lategame weakness hardly matters. But you need to beeline to a [[Merchant of Magic]] when you draft this card to take full advantage. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! [[Upgrade]] !! This means that if you have {{Gold|15}} or more, this spell will hit four times and cost {{Gold|15}}. == Strategy == '''Make It Rain''' is a fantastic way of dealing with backline enemies if you have the {{Gold}} to use it. This spell can dent tankier enemies and even bosses with liberal [[Pyregel]] application, as it capitalizes on it four times. Its {{Gold}} cost is an issue, especially if you're considering {{IconLink|Keepstone}} on it - {{Gold}} is really important to scale in this game! Luckily, the Pyreborne are quite good at having more money than they could ever need with mechanics like {{IconLink|Avarice}}. It heals {{PyreHealth|2}} for each {{DragonsHoard}} the player currently has. == Strategy == '''Pay Off''' is a useful but unconventional card, and provides one of the few ways to restore health to the Pyre. It is most helpful for strategies which need extra {{PyreHealth}}, which makes it effective if you want to act greedy and risk taking Pyre damage. This makes it more reasonable to take [[Trials]], focus on generating {{DragonsHoard}} or {{Gold}} rather than defending your Pyre, and pick nodes which will make you stronger rather than healing with [[Pyre Remains]]. Be aware, however, that this does not make you invincible. You will still need to be strong enough to take on bosses, which will easily kill your Pyre even at full health if you can't kill them on the way up. At higher Covenants, many enemies, such as the [[Chosen Bastion]], can tear your Pyre apart easily if not dealt with. '''Pay Off''' is especially powerful with other cards which scale based off of current Hoard, such as [[Greed Dragon]]. In some cases it may be best to never cash in your {{DragonsHoard}}, so that these cards will always be at maximum power. It can be combined with [[Devilish Details]] to make up for much or all of the {{PyreHealth}} lost. If both cards have {{IconLink|Eternalstone}}, it can be viable to play each one multiple times per battle. This provides one of the most efficient, though risky, ways to gather Hoard. It is much better if you plan to fight the [[Clash with the Titans|Titans]], allowing you to enter the battle against them with more {{PyreHealth}} and restore it during the battle. When played, it applies {{IconLink|Pyregel|10}} to all enemies, then deals 10 damage. {{IconLink|Pyregel}} is applied before the damage is dealt, and thus increases the damage the spell deals. == Strategy == '''Dragon's Breath''' is a powerful damage spell and a very potent source of {{IconLink|Pyregel}}, applying as much as a [[Pyrecask]] to every enemy. This will not only wipe out backliners all the way through the end of the game (barring Chosen variants or ones with protective measures like [[Purified Soul]]s or [[Deformed Duo]]s), but it will also make it significantly easier to take down tanks, and played repeatedly on bosses it can stack up quickly. For obvious reasons, it works excellently with other {{IconLink|Pyregel}} synergies, like [[Hellfurnace]], [[Superheated]], [[Pyreblooded]], and [[Gel Transfusor]]. The biggest hurdle in using this spell is its {{Ember|3}} cost. For best results, its price should be reduced by some means, or you should have ways to cheat {{Ember}} costs. The [[Split Anvil]] is a fantastic artifact to use in concert with '''Dragon's Breath''', and can even make it viable to apply {{IconLink|Keepstone}} to it, letting you not only use this powerful spell every turn but also making all spells that cost {{Ember|2}} or less free. [[Volatile Gauge]] effectively removes this spell's drawback by randomizing its cost whenever drawn, meaning that it will always either cost the same or be cheaper. [[Boiler Room]] is a big help, as this spell will almost always kill at least two enemies and thus refund most of its cost. '''Dragon's Breath''', [[Make It Rain]], and [[Greed]] are all roughly comparable, being area-of-effect spells that deal 20 damage overall by default, each with their own drawbacks and benefits. '''Dragon's Breath''' is much more expensive but applies {{IconLink|Pyregel}}, Make It Rain costs {{Gold}} to use but spreads its damage over four hits, and Greed damages your own units but earns significant {{Gold}}. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Draw a unit. If you have {{Gold|30}}, spend it to apply {{Attack|+30}}, {{IconLink|Avarice|15}}, and {{IconLink|Armor|15}}. |flavor = "A soldier who goes to war without the promise of pay is a fool with a sword."
—The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #22 |artist = Nicole Anna Alfonso }} '''Soldier of Fortune''' is a rare [[Pyreborne]] spell. It draws a unit and spends some {{Gold}} if available to strengthen them. == Strategy == '''Soldier of Fortune''', like most spells which draw a card, is at its best when you can draw a single unit consistently. This means that removing unwanted non-banner units, or banner units which you cannot play during [[Deployment]], should be a priority. Keep in mind that you can target a [[banner unit]] or even a [[Champion]] with this spell simply by not playing them during Deployment. This spell can only draw a unit that is not currently in your hand. This can be inconvenient if you happen to draw it alongside an important unit, but also helpful if you can get all unwanted units in hand before playing it. [[Echo of the Time Father]] helps with this in either situation, making it easier to align specific cards. The {{IconLink|Avarice}} this spell applies pays for itself very quickly, making back the initial investment in just two attacks. It is thus not necessary to draw a strong unit, as even a [[Spear Steward]] can make a reasonable amount of {{Gold}}. Drawing a [[Bloated Whelp]] and immediately killing it with '''Indigestion''' will gain {{Gold|15}} for each unit it hits, so as long as you can hit three or more units you will immediately make back the {{Gold}} you spent. Even if you don't have any {{Gold}}, this card will still draw a unit, which can sometimes be useful. Be aware that the extra stats granted may be undesirable if the unit is supposed to die (e.g. [[Imps]], [[Whelps]], [[Tombs]]). == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! {{SpellCard |name = Devilish Details |image = [[File:CRD DevilishDetails1.2.png|thumb]] |clan = Pyreborne |rarity = Rare |cost = 1 |effect = '''[[Consume]]'''.
Gain {{DragonsHoard|3}}. Your Pyre takes '''8''' damage. |flavor = Nothing is off the market, not even the Pyre itself. |artist = Daniel Sarmiento Chuquisengo }} '''Devilish Details''' is a rare [[Pyreborne]] spell. It grants {{DragonsHoard|3}} but deals 8 damage to your Pyre. == Strategy == '''Devilish Details''' grants easy {{DragonsHoard}}, but the price tag you pay for this is quite steep. When compared to e.g. [[Alchemy]], it's {{Ember|-2}} for {{PyreHealth|-8}}, which often isn't a good trade, especially since you can upgrade Alchemy or adjust your deck to its cost. It's often preferable to focus on improving the {{DragonsHoard}} generation your deck is already capable of rather than taking this card. If you're not facing the [[Titans]], you might be able to take this and simply hope to snowball with a couple of extra artifacts, since, as the old saying goes, "the only HP that matters is the last one." This is particularly true on bulkier Pyres like [[Proto Heartcage]] or [[Pyre of Entropy]]. But if you do intend to face the [[Titans]], {{PyreHealth}} is very valuable and it's hard to substitute it with more strength. There are a couple of ways to justify '''Devilish Details''' even if you ''are'' facing the Titans. * As Common cards, [[Alchemy]] and [[Golden Touch]] aren't available outside of starting with them or Rings 1-2, and sources of {{DragonsHoard}} are scarce outside of those rings. So if you took or started with a [[Greed Dragon]] as a tank but didn't find a way to build your {{DragonsHoard}}, this might be one of the few chances you get to amass a hoard for him. * [[Pay Off]] can offset the Pyre health cost of this card, as the {{DragonsHoard}} it provides means 6 more {{PyreHealth}} when you play it. * If you have both [[Hidden Coffers]] and [[Expanded Coffers]], and this boost in {{DragonsHoard}} is enough to get you extra Pyreforged [[Boss artifacts]] from opening a [[Dragon's Hoard]] of size 12+, those will also heal your Pyre more than the cost of this card. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Smelted Treasure:
{{SpellCard |image = CRD_Smelted_Treasure.png |clan = Pyreborne |rarity = Rare |cost = 1 |effect = Spend {{Gold|50}}. Apply {{IconLink|Armor|50}} to a friendly unit. |flavor = "And Fhyra's great, beloved greed demanded more from gold. The ancient dragons of the Pyre set forth to learn greater uses for their coin. It was the young whelp, Em Ber, who mixed gold with Pyregel." —Tales of Fire and Gold |artist = Genevieve Bega }} '''Smelted Treasure''' is a rare [[Pyreborne]] spell added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It applies {{IconLink|Armor|50}} to a friendly unit, but costs {{Gold|50}} when played. == Strategy == '''Smelted Treasure''' is the only defensive spell the Pyreborne can naturally access, but it is one of the most powerful defensive spells in the game, particularly by the point at which you will usually have the opportunity to draft it. By way of comparison, [[Alloy of the Ancients]], another Rare spell, applies only 60% as much {{IconLink|Armor}} as '''Smelted Treasure''', and it also '''[[Consume]]s''', so it can only be played once per battle without {{IconLink|Eternalstone}}. {{Gold|50}} is not an insignificant amount to spend, especially in the early game when {{Gold}} can be tight and a single cast of this spell can determine whether or not you can afford a major shop upgrade or a reroll. However, the Pyreborne are extremely good at generating huge amounts of {{Gold}}. Units like [[Miser]], [[Wealthy Whelp]], and [[Stuck Up Whelp]] can accelerate your economy to the point at which this card's fee is meaningless. Redeeming {{DragonsHoard}} can help with this as well, albeit less efficiently. [[Lady Gilda]]'s '''Lady Avarice''' and '''Gildmother''' paths both earn a significant amount of {{Gold}} to make casting '''Smelted Treasure''' easier. [[Sacrificial Chamber]] should be a high priority in the early-to-mid-game, as this room alone can single-handedly fund all the casts of '''Smelted Treasure''' you could want, especially if its effect is multiplied by [[Manifold Mirror]]. Applying {{IconLink|Avarice}} to units with {{IconLink|Sweep}}, such as with {{IconLink|Greedstone}} or [[Pyreborne Brainspike]], is one of the fastest ways to generate {{Gold}}. If you happen to see the [[Iron-tongue]], which grants {{IconLink|Sweep}}, you could also put that on a Miser, particularly one with {{IconLink|Quick}} and either {{IconLink|Dualism}} or {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. Once you initiate the [[Seraph]] fight in Ring 8, {{Gold}} can no longer be spent, so whatever you have left over can be funneled entirely into casting this spell (and [[Make It Rain]]), with no penalty other than a minor hit to score if you dip below {{Gold|2500}}. It is rare that this spell will be unnecessary, but it can happen. If you have powerful defensive measures from your other clan, such as [[Oldgrowth]] from the [[Awoken]], [[Enchantrelle]] from the [[Underlegion]], or [[Molten Encasement]] from the [[Melting Remnant]], the {{IconLink|Armor}} granted by this spell may be superfluous and turn it into a {{Gold}} sink. If you are tanking with an {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Greed Dragon]], it may also be irrelevant, as Greed Dragon can naturally build up a titanic {{Health}} stat after dying once or twice. However, if you do not have {{IconLink|Endless}} on Greed Dragon, it may still be worth investing in, as certain fights can cause it to crumble even with its massive {{Health}}. Should you happen to find [[Apex Imp]], '''Smelted Treasure''' is the most effective {{IconLink|Armor}} applicator in the game besides [[Fae's Blessing]] or [[Tidal Turning]] with great amounts of {{IconLink|Conduit}}. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! Any run that has a unit with an ability with a cooldown greater than 1 can benefit from this spell. While they are most common among [[Pyreborne]] units, many units from other clans new to Monster Train 2 and some units returning from Monster Train 1 have abilities that benefit as well. It moves all {{IconLink|Pyregel}} from all units on the floor to the target, then deals 5 damage to the target five times. == Strategy == '''Deathroar''' has two effects, but its sheer damage output is the more useful of the two. The multihit on this spell effectively gives it the same scaling as an '''[[Attuned]]''' card. Although more effective with {{IconLink|Pyregel}}, it acts as effective payoff for {{IconLink|Conduit}} and [[Magic Power]]. Its secondary effect - moving all {{IconLink|Pyregel}} on the floor to a single unit - tends to be less impactful. In order to benefit from it, you must apply large amounts of {{IconLink|Pyregel}} to multiple enemies, keep them alive to transfer their {{IconLink|Pyregel}}, then kill them without the help of the {{IconLink|Pyregel}}. This can sometimes be helpful - against flying bosses, for instance - but is generally less impactful than the damage. It's not worth taking this card for its {{IconLink|Pyregel}}-moving abilities. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! [[Upgrade]] !! {{SpellCard |name = Superheated |image = CRD_Superheated.png |clan = Pyreborne |rarity = Rare |cost = 3 |effect = '''[[Consume]]'''.

—Dante's Travel Guide |artist = Luke Banke }} '''Superheated''' is a rare [[Pyreborne]] spell. It doubles the amount of {{IconLink|Pyregel}} on the target. == Strategy == '''Superheated''' is a potentially powerful spell, but often difficult to use properly. It requires a significant amount of single-target {{IconLink|Pyregel}} in order to be worth using, but if you have enough {{IconLink|Pyregel}} then it's often more useful to deal damage than it is to stack up even more. Only enemies with very high {{Health}} are worth continuing to stack {{IconLink|Pyregel}} on. This makes it best used against flying bosses. With a {{IconLink|Pyregel}}-focused deck, flying bosses will usually gain a significant amount of {{IconLink|Pyregel}} passively over the course of the battle. Their extremely high {{Health}} also means that the extra {{IconLink|Pyregel}} will actually have an impact. This can make the {{IconLink|Relentless}} phase trivial, or even kill the boss early with a reasonably strong deck. '''Superheated''' can be used in conjunction with [[Deathroar]] to move all {{IconLink|Pyregel}} on a floor to a single target before doubling it. However, both spells are very expensive, meaning that it is often difficult to play them on the same turn. [[Gel Transfusor]] can have a similar effect passively, and makes '''Superheated''' much more useful. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! Pyreclasm:
{{SpellCard |name = Pyreclasm |image = CRD_Pyreclasm.png |clan = Pyreborne |rarity = Rare |cost = 4 |effect = '''[[Attuned]]'''. '''[[Explosive]]'''.
Deal '''150''' damage. |flavor = "And when you have followed my commandments and led a life devoted to gold, then your spirit will experience an explosive transformation."
—The Rules of Fhyra, Rule #1071 |artist = Taylor Bray }} '''Pyreclasm''' is a rare [[Pyreborne]] spell. It deals 150 damage to the target, and has [[Explosive]], meaning that any leftover damage is dealt to all enemies on the floor. It is also '''[[Attuned]]''', meaning that '''[[Magic Power]]''' increases its damage five times as much as normal. == Strategy == It may seem intuitive to use '''Pyreclasm''' on enemies with high {{Health}} due to its extremely high damage. However, you actually want to target the enemy with the lowest {{Health}}, as the extra damage will be dealt to the entire floor. Used on an enemy with {{Health|140}}, it will kill that enemy and deal 10 damage to the rest of the floor. If instead used on an enemy with {{Health|3}}, it will deal 147 damage to the floor, killing the {{Health|140}} enemy and dealing far more damage to whatever other enemies are present. As such, it both clears backliners and does significant damage to tanks and bosses, and {{IconLink|Pyregel}} can increase both the overflow damage by being applied to the original target and increase the damage the secondary victims take, making area-of-effect {{IconLink|Pyregel}} particularly powerful with this spell. It is one of the strongest spells in the game, held back only by its cost of {{Ember|4}}. This makes it very useful with [[Volatile Gauge]], [[Spell Sanctum]], or other ways to deal with its high cost. With sufficient {{IconLink|Conduit}}, it can be even more powerful, potentially killing every enemy but the boss. Note that it can also be used on friendly units, and the Explosive damage will still overflow to the enemies rather than your other units. This means you can use it on units that want to die, like [[Gildmonger]], [[Imps]], [[Tombs]], and [[Whelps]], while still wiping out enemy waves. If you are partnered with the [[Hellhorned]], you can use [[Pyre Chomper]] to gain the {{Ember}} to cast '''Pyreclasm''', then kill the Pyre Chomper for maximum Explosive damage. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! It grants {{Attack|+10}}, and lets its user accumulate {{IconLink|Soul}} as enemies die. It also gives its target a {{IconLink|Celebrate}} trigger that gives you {{DragonsHoard|1}} for every '''4''' {{IconLink|Soul}} if it survives the whole battle. ==Strategy== '''Soulsmelter''' can be a high-reward card, but it also requires a significant investment, and one that won't pay out unless the rest of your deck can deliver. If the unit with this equipment dies to the boss, you won't get any {{DragonsHoard}} at all. Ideally, you'd be able to start with it in play, which you can do by making it [[Deployable]]. This does require a lot of {{DeploymentEmber}} to work. Be careful - taking [[Hell's Flame]] just to equip this at the start of combat means you aren't using your boss artifact for much of anything that actually makes your run strong, and doing that may mean your unit doesn't survive combat anyway (and your run may well be over after that). If you're confident in how strong your run is, you could do this anyway. If you started with [[Herzal's Horde]] or [[Artificial Pyrestone]], taking this and making it [[Deployable]] is a more manageable idea. It's also an ideal target for [[Attuned Whetstone]] - in that case, you shouldn't give it [[Deployable]] and instead should make all other equipment [[Deployable]], and you can merge it with other equipment in that case. Its best-case scenario is being equipped at the start of combat to any unit on a dedicated kill floor where all enemies die. Here's the {{DragonsHoard}} payouts you can expect if you manage to do that: {| class="wikitable" |- ! Ring !! (**) [[The Undying One]] is a particularly good matchup here, especially if you can kill all enemies, including [[The Undying One]], on the top floor. '''Luna Coven''' [[File:ClanLunaCoven.png|20x20px]] is a [[clan]] in [[Monster Train 2]]. It is unlocked after defeating 40 enemies using spells.

Luna Coven features the following mechanics:
* The '''[[Luna Coven#Moon Phase|Moon Phase]]''' is a unique mechanic that many aspects of the clan interact with. Many effects are only active during a certain moon phase. Some units trigger {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} effects whenever the phase changes. 
* {{IconLink|Conduit}} is a common buff that increases Magic Power on the floor.
* Many units and spells can heal or grant {{IconLink|Armor}} to allied units.
* Many spells are '''[[Attuned]]''', increasing their damage and healing by amplifying the potency of Magic Power.
* {{IconLink|Mageblade}} is a status effect that weaponizes magic power, increasing a unit's {{Attack}}.
* '''[[:Category:Fae_units|Fae]]''' are minor units that interact with the Moon Phase or empower your spells.
The clan's unique [[Merchant of Steel]] Upgrade is {{IconLink|Glimmerstone}}.

=== Moon Phase ===
Moon Phase is a mechanic unique to the Luna Coven clan. At any given time during combat, the phase is either {{IconLink|Full Moon}} or {{IconLink|New Moon}}. Combat always begins in {{IconLink|New Moon}} during the Deployment Phase, and switches to the opposite phase at the start of each turn. There are many other ways to change the phase, such as the '''[[Phase]]''' keyword on spells. Each time the phase changes, {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} is triggered. The phase cannot be changed while combat is ongoing (i.e. units are actively fighting).

Thematically, [[Ekka]] and [[:Category:Selene_units|Selene]] units are more powerful during {{IconLink|Full Moon}}, while [[Arduhn]] and [[:Category:Silent_units|Silent]] units are more powerful during {{IconLink|New Moon}}.

She is best played with a secondary clan that also has access to spells, especially ones that also scale from {{IconLink|Conduit}}. ===Celestial Spellweaver=== By far her most consistent path, '''Celestial Spellweaver''' benefits from her 0-cost [[Witchweave]] starter card. Her entire strategy revolves around spamming spells on her floor, leading to massive {{IconLink|Conduit}} stacks, making even her 1-damage [[Witchweave]] hit or heal incredibly hard in later rounds. If your other starter card is a unit rather than a spell, such as [[Dreg]] or [[Queen's Impling]], then this path may not be as strong. Not being able to trigger {{IconLink|Incant}} consistently can severely limit her strength in the early game, which is often the most dangerous part of the run for '''Ekka'''. '''Celestial Spellweaver''' works excellently with {{IconLink|Mageblade}} units such as [[Selene Acolyte]] and [[Moonguard]]. [[Moonlit Glaive]] also provides {{IconLink|Mageblade|3}} to any unit, and therefore is incredibly valuable. [[Silent Sentinel]] is a good pickup for a tank thanks to its self-healing ability which also applies {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}}. '''Celestial Spellweaver''' is incredibly fragile, so a tank unit is necessary, especially in the early game. Survivability can be further improved by taking [[Tidal Turning]] and especially [[Fae's Blessing]], both of which provide massive amounts of {{IconLink|Armor}} in later rounds. Despite its late-game strength, this path is also highly vulnerable early on. It's difficult to kill early bosses with spells, and without a {{IconLink|Mageblade}} unit, her {{IconLink|Conduit}} will not help during {{IconLink|Relentless}}. If you have a weak start - for example, a [[banner unit]] like [[Squad Leader]] (without [[Spawn]] cards) or [[Miser]] - it may be necessary to take one of her other paths, or otherwise risk losing to the Ring 1 boss. By contrast, a strong early-game unit like [[Avenger]] or [[Crucible Collector]] makes this path much safer and can offer you confidence into the late game. ===Silver Empress=== '''Silver Empress''' is a difficult path to play due to a lack of moon phase control offered from [[Witchweave]], but finding a [[Lunar Priestess]] makes this path significantly more viable, allowing you to stay constantly in {{IconLink|Full Moon}}. '''Silver Empress III''''s {{IconLink|Conduit|70}} is equivalent to more than 20 {{IconLink|Incant}}s for '''Celestial Spellweaver III'''. '''Silver Empress''' has a bit more survivability than her '''Celestial Spellweaver''' line, allowing her to deal with issues such as {{IconLink|Spikes}} and {{IconLink|Corruption}} a little better, though she will still need a good tank. Much like '''Celestial Spellweaver''', [[Silent Sentinel]]'s self heal and application of {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} makes it a solid pick. Her '''Lunar Echo''' ability can be somewhat difficult to use well, as it requires a lot of forethought. To make the most use of it, you would ideally play only a single powerful spell while the ability is on cooldown, such that you have complete control of what you recur when you activate it on the subsequent turn. In an ideal situation, this would sync up with her natural {{IconLink|Full Moon}} effect - you would play a single spell during {{IconLink|New Moon}}, while spells are less powerful anyway, and then recur it during {{IconLink|Full Moon}} along with all your other spells while it can take advantage of her {{IconLink|Conduit}}. The issue with this is its inconsistency. In a spell-based deck, having to not play spells every other turn is very difficult to justify, and will almost always let enemies escape and get to the Pyre. It is also largely incompatible with Lunar Priestess, since it means there is a chance of recurring a mere [[Moon Ritual]], and it makes Witchweaves drastically worse since they really want to be spammed. Furthermore, it does not apply any effects that make the recurred spell easier to play like an {{Ember}} discount, so an expensive spell like [[Heavenfall]] or [[Tidal Turning]] might not even be playable. As such, more often than not, '''Lunar Echo''' will just be a minor boon, possibly giving a useful spell but more likely giving something relatively low-impact. It does improve when allied with the [[Pyreborne]] due to their cooldown-reducing effects, as well as having several very powerful spells of their own like [[Make It Rain]] and [[Pyreclasm]]. [[Mind Cage]] and [[Tome of Contracts]] can let her use '''Lunar Echo''' every turn. There is also an [[Infinites|Infinite]] involving '''Lunar Echo''' and a [[Pyreborne Brainspike]] with {{Ember|-2}}. This is a relatively simple infinite to execute, merely requiring you to play Pyreborne Brainspike and nothing else during a turn; once you recur the Brainspike, you can play it on '''Ekka''' to reduce her cooldown to 0 and re-activate '''Lunar Echo''' to recur the Brainspike again. However, it's difficult to translate this infinite into actual output, as under normal circumstances all it allows you to do is gain infinite {{Gold}} with the applied {{IconLink|Avarice}}. Cross-pathing into '''Celestial Spellweaver''' or allying with [[Magma Cultist]] can allow for infinite {{IconLink|Conduit}} or {{IconLink|Pyregel}} respectively, and [[Goldtooth]] can translate the {{Gold}} earned into {{Attack}} damage. ===Lunar Steward=== '''Lunar Steward''' is [[Ekka]]'s most potentially dangerous line in the early game: while {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} does trigger once per turn, this is far too slow to rely on at only {{AttackHealth|+1|+1}}, and [[Ekka]]'s starting [[Witchweave]] offers no '''[[Phase]]''' manipulation at all. Only [[Lunar Priestess]] and [[Meddler]] can offer any additional {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} triggers within your starting deck. Both of these units can also make the early game risky if you use her other paths; Lunar Priestess has no way to deal damage effectively in the first ring, and starting with Meddlers means that you have fewer spells with which to trigger {{IconLink|Incant}} or take advantage of {{IconLink|Conduit}}. This makes '''Lunar Steward''' the strongest and safest choice if starting with one or both of these units. Outside of Meddler and Lunar Priestess, the strongest synergy pieces for '''Lunar Steward''' are of uncommon rarity, so it's unlikely that you will see them until after Ring 4, which is a long time to survive with a weak Champion. [[Mooncaller]] doubles any {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} triggers, making her a high priority for this path, while [[Lunacy]] is the only available card that can trigger {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} more than once per play. As such, this path improves remarkably with the [[Pyre of Dominion]], where you can sometimes draft two copies of Mooncaller, Lunacy, or Lunar Priestess right off the bat. This Pyre also tends to make '''Celestial Spellweaver''' somewhat worse due to the lack of Witchweaves for cheap {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers, so '''Lunar Steward''' has less competition. Mooncaller, Lunar Priestess, and Meddler are all {{Size|1}} units, so having many of them on a floor with '''Ekka''' providing {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} triggers while '''Ekka''' buffs them is a good strategy. Since the individual scaling per {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} is fairly low even at '''Lunar Steward III''', this line benefits massively from extra {{Capacity}} or overstacking with cards like [[Gravity]] and [[Hexscalation]] to ensure that there are as many recipients of her scaling as possible. [[Astrologer]]'s natural {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} trigger makes it a better pick than normal, since you can scale its {{Attack}} much faster. [[Fae's Nook]] can also potentially be a strong pick. '''Silent''' units gain {{Attack|+3}}. }} == Strategy == Compared to [[Ekka]], '''Arduhn''' generally has a lower ceiling into the late game, but often has an easier early game due to his solid stats letting him win slugfests with the first few bosses. Two of his paths have built-in synergies with [[:Category:Silent units|Silent units]], which generally prefer to be in {{IconLink|New Moon}}, and his [[Moon Ritual]] starter card makes it much easier for him to enable a number of of Luna [[banner unit]]s. His built-in {{IconLink|Mageblade|2}} also provides a guaranteed payoff for {{IconLink|Conduit}} stacking, which is only otherwise available through [[Selene Acolyte]], [[Moonguard]], and [[Moonlit Glaive]]. ===Mystic Hammer=== '''Mystic Hammer''' is [[Arduhn]]'s most straightforward path, and is also by far the most powerful path in early rings. His high base {{Attack}} and {{Health}} make him a useful unit in any run, though his {{Attack}} ceiling is much lower than the '''Battleborne''' path; '''Shadowcast''' providing on-demand access to {{IconLink|New Moon}} is also helpful, guaranteeing that he can get the {{Attack}} bonus whenever wanted, although his starter [[Moon Ritual]] makes this less necessary. Note that '''Shadowcast''' triggers '''[[Phase]]''' and thus {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} even if it was already {{IconLink|New Moon}} before activation. ===Battleborne=== The main challenge with this path is feeding '''Arduhn''' enough {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers to scale his {{IconLink|Conduit}} appreciably. Equipment that provides {{IconLink|Multistrike}} can increase {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers, as can {{IconLink|Trample}} or {{IconLink|Spikes}}. Without these, he is essentially a glorified [[Spear Steward]], capable of hitting and killing one enemy per turn even in the best possible case. However, with access to some or all of these methods to kill enemies, he can become one of the strongest damage dealers in the game, dealing an additional {{Attack|6}} by endgame for each point of {{IconLink|Conduit}}. Alternatively, you can simply scale '''Arduhn''' up to a reasonable level over the first half of the game and then move away from letting him get kills and use him as a {{IconLink|Conduit}} battery if you haven't found an effective way to apply {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, {{IconLink|Spikes}}, or {{IconLink|Trample}}. Even with only 30 or so kills, he can provide a significant boost to other units with {{IconLink|Mageblade}}, or to damage spells used on his floor. If you plan to do this, it is generally better to crosspath away from '''Battleborne''' with later upgrades, as the higher levels only increase his own {{IconLink|Mageblade}}. With one or two levels in '''Hierophant''', he can provide both damage output and defense to the entire floor. ===Hierophant=== This path allows '''Arduhn''' to buff his whole floor's defenses, along with minor offensive scaling for certain units. The [[:Category:Silent units|Silent units]] that receive {{Attack}} are [[Nightingale]], [[Silent Sentinel]], [[Moonguard]], and [[Shadeguard]]. Of these four units, Nightingale is likely the biggest beneficiary due to its inherent {{IconLink|Multistrike}} and lack of built-in {{Attack}} scaling. Even when not using Silent units, the floorwide {{IconLink|Armor}} gain is quite useful, equal to upgrading all units on his floor with a {{IconLink|Runestone}} at worst and comparing favorably to [[Guardian Stone]]. This is especially helpful when starting with fragile units in the early rings, such as [[Lunar Priestess]] or [[Selene Acolyte]]. However, it can be redundant when used with [[Fae's Blessing]] or [[Tidal Turning]] and large amounts of {{IconLink|Conduit}}. The main purpose of this path is to solve your defensive problems, even against enemies with {{IconLink|Sweep}} or full-floor {{IconLink|Corruption}}. This allows the rest of your deck to focus on dealing damage, although having a few defensive cards can still be helpful. If you happen to get the [[Railhammer]] while allied with the [[Hellhorned]], however, a single level of '''Hierophant''' is enough to almost guarantee your units will never die, making that artifact one of the strongest in the game when using '''Arduhn'''. ==Quotes== '''Summoned''' * ''I have sailed the stars, but I have never ridden a train before.'' * ''It is strange to fighting alongside these creatures.'' * ''Sister, I'll protect you.'' * ''The moon has given me a mission. It gains {{IconLink|Conduit|1}} per each {{IconLink|Mooncycle}}. == Strategy == In theory, '''Aurora Weaver''' brings together the {{IconLink|Conduit}} and {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} effects of the Luna Coven and helps them synergize with each other. In practice, however, this is not really the case. Many {{IconLink|Conduit}} decks have much more efficient ways of scaling {{IconLink|Conduit}}, like [[Moon Pixie]], [[Planetarium]], or [[Ekka]]'s '''Celestial Spellweaver''' or '''Silver Empress''' paths. Decks that focus on {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} are relatively rare, as there are not many ways to trigger it rapidly and relatively few good payoffs. Furthermore, when successful {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} decks do come together, they tend to be more melee-based, using units like [[Astrologer]] and '''Lunar Steward''' Ekka rather than {{IconLink|Conduit}} for damage. Her problems are multiplied by being an uncommon non-[[banner unit]]. This means you are unlikely to see her until after Ring 4, so it is difficult to build around her in the early game, and even if you have a deck that can benefit from her, she cannot be played during the [[Deployment Phase]] without the [[Departure Manifest]] artifact, which means you may not draw her until several turns into the combat. {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} decks would also generally prefer to see [[Mooncaller]], who doubles all {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} effects on her floor, to speed up their scaling. As such, '''Aurora Weaver''' is left in a somewhat awkward position. However, there are ways to improve her and even let her contribute significantly. Consistently playing [[Moon Ritual]], either by having it as the starter clan card or generating them with [[Lunar Priestess]], can be an efficient means of scaling '''Aurora Weaver'''. This usually makes her a better pick with [[Arduhn]], in particular his '''Mystic Hammer''' and '''Hierophant''' paths, and his inherent {{IconLink|Mageblade|2}} acts as a decent payoff for her {{IconLink|Conduit}} scaling. [[Ethereal Seelie]] is another way to improve her, as its {{IconLink|Conduit|+1}} effect will trigger on every {{IconLink|Mooncycle}}. The aforementioned Mooncaller can double her scaling, but since they are both non-banner units and the Luna Coven don't often have much {{Capacity}} to spare, it can be hard to use these units together. Cards like [[Lunacy]] can also help trigger {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} more rapidly and turn her into a decent {{IconLink|Conduit}} source. Playing Lunacy on a {{IconLink|Dualism}} '''Aurora Weaver''' applies the same amount of {{IconLink|Conduit}} as [[Coven's Spike]], which is quite respectable. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade !
