Since you will usually not be offered '''Mooncaller''' until Ring 4 onwards, by the time you have a chance to draft the card you may have already settled on a different strategy. The second is that, even if you are using {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} strategies, '''Mooncaller''' is not a banner unit, so there's no guarantee that you will draw it early enough in the fight to matter. [[Pyre of Dominion]] makes '''Mooncaller''' a more appealing pick in general, but especially if Ekka is your champion. {{UnitCard |name = Astrologer |image = PLR_Astrologer.png |clan = [[Luna Coven]] |rarity = Uncommon |type = Selene |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 5/10 |ability = {{IconLink|Mooncycle}}: {{Attack|+5}}. |flavor = "Let me look at your star chart. I see you were born under the Blessed Moon? Oh dear, that's no good..." |artist = Mary Ngai-Virgo }} '''Astrologer''' is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] [[banner unit]]. She gains {{Attack|+5}} on {{IconLink|Mooncycle}}. == Strategy == By default, '''Astrologer''' only gains {{Attack}} once per round, far too slow to be useful outside of the early game. She is only worth taking if you have ways to increase her damage faster. Consistently playing [[Moon Ritual]], either as the starter clan card or with [[Lunar Priestess]], can be an efficient means of scaling '''Astrologer'''. Playing several copies of [[Meddler]] is similarly helpful. [[Mooncaller]] can also double the {{Attack}} she receives, while [[Lunacy]] can provide a burst of {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} triggers. [[Luna Cyclestaff]] is useful, as it has the same trigger as '''Astrologer'''. It can also be put an a different unit to scale both at the same time. [[Ekka]]'s '''Lunar Steward''' path also scales her floor on {{IconLink|Mooncycle}}, and grants {{Health}} to make '''Astrologer''' less squishy; however, using Ekka means you do not have access to Moon Ritual except from Lunar Priestess. '''Astrologer''' improves noticeably if used alongside the [[Pyre of Dominion]], as this allows you to potentially draft Mooncaller or Lunacy immediately. With two copies of Mooncaller on her floor, '''Astrologer''' will gain {{Attack|+15}} for every {{IconLink|Mooncycle}}, which makes her much more respectable in the early game and lets her scale dramatically later on. However, the fact of the matter remains that it is much more difficult to aggressively trigger {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} than triggers like {{IconLink|Incant}} or {{IconLink|Harvest}}, so [[Astrologer]]'s scaling will often wind up lackluster. You often will not know if a {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} build is feasible until Ring 5 or 6, since the key components are mostly uncommon cards. If you are partnered with the [[Hellhorned]] and can find [[Meddler]], '''Astrologer''' might be more viable, as Meddler '''[[Phase]]s''' on {{IconLink|Summon}}. This means [[Ashes of the Fallen]] will let it trigger {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} twice when played, which is very powerful if you can make it {{IconLink|Endless}}. It also means that pairing it with [[Transcendimp]] can result in a massive surge of {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} triggers. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! She adds a copy of [[Moon Ritual]] with [[Ephemeral]] to the player's hand at the end of each turn. ==Strategy== '''Lunar Priestess''' is able to give the player control over the moon phase as long as she remains alive. She guarantees that you will always have a [[Moon Ritual]] available, which you can either play or not depending on which phase you want to end the turn in. This allows you to always end in {{IconLink|New Moon}} if you want to take advantage of [[:Category:Silent units|Silent units]] such as [[Shadeguard]], or in {{IconLink|Full Moon}} to benefit your [[:Category:Selene units|Selene units]] and spells. She is especially useful if your starting deck includes [[Witchweave]], but even with [[Moon Ritual]] as a starter card she provides greater consistency and is often worth taking. She also lets you add {{IconLink|Conduit|1}} to a unit of your choice each turn, along with an {{IconLink|Incant}}, as long as you choose to play the Moon Ritual. Her main weakness is her absolutely terrible stats at {{AttackHealth|8|8}}. Her damage output is negligible, and she will easily be killed if left vulnerable to enemies. She can be left on an upper floor if you are consistently killing enemies on lower floors, but will still need to be protected from flying bosses, such as by putting her behind a [[Shield Steward]]. Regardless, she is a useful support unit, and usually worth the effort of keeping alive. == Recommended Upgrades== {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! Nightingale:
{{UnitCard |name = Nightingale |image = PLR_Nightingale.png |clan = Luna Coven |rarity = Uncommon |type = Silent |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 10/5 |ability = {{IconLink|Stealth|2}}. {{IconLink|New Moon}}: {{IconLink|Multistrike|2}}. |flavor = ''"I don't need magic to disappear into the night."'' |artist = Daniel Sarmiento Chuquisengo }} The '''Nightingale''' is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] [[banner unit]]. It enters with {{IconLink|Stealth}}, and gains {{IconLink|Multistrike|2}} during {{IconLink|New Moon}}. == Strategy == '''Nightingale''' is a somewhat weak unit, especially in the early rings. Innate access to {{IconLink|Multistrike}} is potent, especially {{IconLink|Multistrike|2}}, but its stats are quite poor, and its {{IconLink|Multistrike}} is conditional on having solid control of the moon phase. If you cannot '''[[Phase]]''' to {{IconLink|New Moon}} every turn, or if you have units like [[Selene Acolyte]] that require it to be {{IconLink|Full Moon}}, '''Nightingale''' can be worse than a [[Spear Steward]]. If you have no way to '''Phase''' the moon, and require it to help kill the boss, you'll want to put it on a floor such that it will have {{IconLink|Multistrike}} when it faces the boss - in other words, the boss must arrive at its floor on an even numbered turn. Here's a table to know where to put it: '''Having {{IconLink|Multistrike}} for {{IconLink|Relentless}} combat''' {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: center; |- ! Ring !! Number of turns !! Where to place '''Nightingale'''* |- | '''1-2''' || 4-6 || 1st or 3rd floors |- | '''3-5''' || 6-8 || 1st or 3rd floors |- | '''6''' || 8-10 || 1st or 3rd floors |- | '''7''' || 7-9 || 2nd floor |- | '''8''' || 8-10 || 1st or 3rd floors |- | '''9''' || No limit || N/A |} ''*'' assuming you have no [[Phase]] effects Fortunately, there are ways to make the unit not only pull its weight but excel. The [[Eclipse Chamber]] is practically a must with '''Nightingale''' if offered. Not only does it ensure that it will always have its {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, but the {{Attack|15}} Eclipse Chamber provides to [[:Category:Silent_units|Silent]] units on {{IconLink|Resolve}} is effectively tripled for it, and can quickly make it a potent attacker. It can be partnered with [[Shadeguard]] in an Eclipse Chamber to tank for it after its {{IconLink|Stealth}} has worn off. Its natural {{IconLink|Multistrike}} makes it a solid wielder of [[Moonlit Glaive]] if you have sufficient {{IconLink|Conduit}} support, as it gains thrice the benefit. Likewise, the [[Luna Cyclestaff]]'s potential enormous {{Attack}} is tripled for it during {{IconLink|New Moon}}. '''Nightingale''' tends to be a better choice with [[Arduhn]] as a Champion rather than [[Ekka]]. Arduhn's starter card is [[Moon Ritual]], which immediately gives you much greater control over the moon phase. His '''Mystic Hammer''' path can forcibly '''[[Phase]]''' to {{IconLink|New Moon}} in case of emergency, while the '''Hierophant''' path scales the {{Attack}} of Silent units like '''Nightingale''' on {{IconLink|Incant}}, providing a source of scaling that is not based on {{IconLink|Conduit}} or {{IconLink|Mageblade}}. It also provides {{IconLink|Armor}}, giving '''Nightingale''' some much-needed durability after its {{IconLink|Stealth}} wears off. Units like [[Lunar Priestess]] and [[Meddler]] can offer consistent control of the moon phase as well, even with Ekka or a different clan's Champion. In the absence of these effects or Eclipse Chamber, Nightingale is not usually worthwhile. When partnered with the [[Underlegion]], equipping '''Nightingale''' with a [[Loamcoat]] will cause it to '''[[Propagate]]''' its {{IconLink|Stealth}}, effectively making it invulnerable until {{IconLink|Relentless}} outside of effects like {{IconLink|Spikes}}. Against flying bosses, this can be used to lure the boss away from your main floors and waste its turn. It can also be used to prevent the {{IconLink|Resolve}} effects of [[Terrifying Amalgam]]s without making itself vulnerable. The [[Shadow's Sheath]] artifact grants '''Nightingale''' an extra boost to its {{Attack}} thanks to its natural {{IconLink|Stealth}}, and allows it to gain more with every {{IconLink|Slay}} trigger, removing the need for defense other than against enemies like [[Qel the Corruptor]] or [[Chosen Prayerstone]]s. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! She has {{IconLink|Mageblade|2}}, and has {{IconLink|Sweep}} during the {{IconLink|Full Moon}}. == Strategy == The '''Selene Acolyte''''s main advantage over other {{IconLink|Sweep}} units is her {{IconLink|Mageblade}}, which allows her to scale off of {{IconLink|Conduit}} on her floor. This can be useful, but it comes at the cost of a {{IconLink|Full Moon}} trigger, meaning that she can only {{IconLink|Sweep}} half the time unless you have consistent {{IconLink|Phase}} control through units like [[Lunar Priestess]]. Even if you can control the moon phase, she is ineffective if you are also using [[:Category:Silent units|Silent units]] or any card which requires a {{IconLink|New Moon}} to work effectively. An [[Eclipse Chamber]] can allow you to take advantage of both phases' effects at once. The first turn after Deployment is by default in {{IconLink|Full Moon}}, so {{IconLink|Sweep}} will be active. Active sources of '''[[Phase]]''' are needed to maintain this afterwards. This unit does not have the {{IconLink|Sweep}} effect by default; instead the effect is granted by the {{IconLink|Full Moon}} trigger. Since [[Deafening Herald]] blocks triggered abilities, '''Selene Acolyte''' loses {{IconLink|Sweep}} while it is present on her floor. This is a very powerful unit when paired with [[Ekka]]'s '''Celestial Spellweaver''' path. At '''Celestial Spellweaver III''', '''Selene Acolyte''' gains {{Attack|+6}} per {{IconLink|Incant}}. Another option is a [[Moon Pixie]] upgraded with {{IconLink|Dualstone}} and {{IconLink|Glimmerstone}}, which can provide her up to {{IconLink|Conduit|52}} ({{Attack|+104}}) on a fully stacked floor. [[Planetarium]] should be a high priority room if offered, as it has a similar effect to Moon Pixie but can be played during the Deployment phase. The [[Moonlit Glaive]] is an excellent choice of equipment as it gives her an additional 150% bonus {{Attack}} compared to her baseline. [[Swiftsteel Dagger]] can be a source of {{IconLink|Quick}} if one cannot find a {{IconLink|Speedstone}} at the [[Merchant of Steel]]. At {{Health|5}}, she is incredibly fragile, and even as a backliner she requires either health upgrades or defensive spells like [[Fae's Blessing]] to survive. Enemies with {{IconLink|Spikes}} or {{IconLink|Sweep}} will kill her quickly. If you use '''Superfood''' [[Primordium]] equipped with [[Iron-tongue]] to pass {{IconLink|Sweep}} to '''Selene Acolyte''', she will no longer lose her {{IconLink|Sweep}} when it is not {{IconLink|Full Moon}} or when afflicted with {{IconLink|Silence}}. This path can also pass on additional {{IconLink|Mageblade}} and {{IconLink|Conduit}}, sometimes allowing extremely early kills on flying bosses. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! {{UnitCard |name = Shadeguard |image = PLR_Shadeguard.png |clan = Luna Coven |rarity = Uncommon |type = Silent |banner = Yes |cost = 2 |size = 3 |stats = 15/40 |ability = {{IconLink|Resolve}}: If it is {{IconLink|New Moon}}, gain {{Attack|+10}} and {{Health|+15}}. |flavor = ''"When the fighting was done, when we had stopped falling through the skies, I lit my lantern and looked around. All of it, the temple walls, the home I called my own, it was all gone."'' |artist = Ron Kee }} '''Shadeguard''' is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] [[banner unit]]. It gains {{Attack|+10}} and {{Health|+15}} at the end of each turn if the current phase is {{IconLink|New Moon}}. ==Strategy== As the name implies, '''Shadeguard''' is effective at guarding your other units. Its damage output is respectable, but its main purpose is to tank damage and protect those behind it. Doing so effectively requires you to end each turn in {{IconLink|New Moon}} to let it gain as much {{Health}} as possible over the course of the battle, so units like [[Lunar Priestess]] or [[Meddler]] are useful. '''Shadeguard''' is most effective when your Champion is [[Arduhn]], especially with his '''Hierophant''' upgrade path. As a [[:Category:Silent units|Silent unit]], it gains extra {{Attack}} from each {{IconLink|Incant}} in addition to {{IconLink|Armor}}, which helps it output more damage. Additionally, starting with [[Moon Ritual]] allows you to more frequently end your turn in {{IconLink|New Moon}}, increasing '''Shadeguard''''s damage output and health scaling. That being said, the unit is hardly bad with [[Ekka]], and in fact is one of the best starting units you can have if she is your Champion; Ekka's greatest weakness is in the early rings, due to her overall low statline, and '''Shadeguard''' will build up enough {{Attack}} and {{Health}} even with no moon phase control to carry you through the first ring on its own. As with all Silent units, [[Eclipse Chamber]] is very effective, allowing you to gain the benefits of {{IconLink|New Moon}} regardless of the current phase and granting an additional {{Attack|+15}} each turn. It also allows you to equip the [[Dusk Mantle]] for a consistent {{IconLink|Titanskin|5}}, dramatically increasing the unit's tanking potential by lowering all damage it takes by 5. [[Nightingale]] is an extremely strong teammate for '''Shadeguard'''. Its low {{Health}} means it benefits greatly from '''Shadeguard''''s tanking ability, while its {{IconLink|Multistrike|2}} gives it tremendous damage output, especially in an Eclipse Chamber where it essentially gains three times the scaling. Both units want it to be {{IconLink|New Moon}} consistently as well. [[Selene Acolyte]] is a somewhat awkward partner, but certainly appreciates '''Shadeguard''''s bulk; however, since she requires it to be {{IconLink|Full Moon}} to have {{IconLink|Sweep}}, the units can only really work together in an Eclipse Chamber, where '''Shadeguard''' will continue to get its {{IconLink|Resolve}} effect even when the true moon phase is {{IconLink|Full Moon}}. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! {{UnitCard |name = Silent Sentinel |image = PLR_SilentSentinel.png |clan = Luna Coven |rarity = Uncommon |type = Silent |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 10/40 |ability = {{AbilityBox|Spell Slam|3|Restore to full health. His {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}, '''Spell Slam''', heals him to full {{Health}} and applies {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} to all enemies, with a cooldown of 3. == Strategy == '''Silent Sentinel''' is a respectable tank whose role is further improved by his ability to heal himself fully every three turns. Compared to [[Shadeguard]], he has much less offensive potential since his {{Attack}} doesn't scale, but he doesn't require moon phase control or [[Eclipse Chamber]] to be effective, and he is less demanding to play, since he is cheaper and takes up less {{Capacity}}. In the early rings, he is a far more effective tank than a [[Shield Steward]], with superior stats and the ability to confront the boss at full power no matter how much of a beating he took in the rest of the fight. Also, if you play a {{Capacity|2}} unit behind him, you will still have space to play a [[Moon Pixie]] or [[Meddler]]. The {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} applied by '''Spell Slam''' is usually less important than the full heal, simply because with a cooldown of 3 it's hard to take advantage of it consistently unless you're allied with the [[Pyreborne]]. Since it's tied to his heal, it's a lot harder to save it for use on strong tanks like [[Avowed Gladiator]]s, as using it in this way may result in '''Silent Sentinel''' dying before he can heal off the damage. However, if you happen to be partnered with the Pyreborne, reducing his cooldown with effects like [[Mind Cage]] and [[Tome of Contracts]] is quite powerful, not only letting him fully heal every turn but also powering up strong spells and effects like [[Make It Rain]], [[Pyreclasm]], and [[Hot Head]]'s '''Fire Breathing'''. Oddly for a [[:Category:Silent units|Silent unit]], he's often stronger with [[Ekka]] than [[Arduhn]], at least early. Ekka appreciates having an effective tank in the early game due to her fragility, and with the high amount of {{IconLink|Conduit}} she can generate with her '''Celestial Spellweaver''' or '''Silver Empress''' paths, she is more able to take advantage of {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}}. Meanwhile, [[Moon Ritual]] does not directly provide any benefit to '''Silent Sentinel''', and Arduhn's '''Hierophant''' path is not especially effective with him, since he has very low {{Attack}} and the {{IconLink|Armor}} Arduhn applies is redundant with his healing. He can be a solid lure for [[Flying Bosses]], as long as you can keep other units alive on at least two floors. By playing him on the top floor, he will distract the boss away from your other floors every third turn, and the three-turn cooldown on '''Spell Slam''' is exactly enough to fully heal right before or right after being attacked. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! {{UnitCard |name = Ethereal Seelie |image = PLR_EtherealSeelie.png |clan = Luna Coven |rarity = Rare |type = Fae |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 1 |stats = 5/5 |ability = {{IconLink|Conduit|5}}.

It applies an additional stack of {{IconLink|Conduit}} whenever {{IconLink|Conduit}} is applied. == Strategy == The '''Ethereal Seelie''' is an odd banner unit. It plays a supportive role, increasing the amount of {{IconLink|Conduit}} applied on its floor. Unfortunately, unlike similar support units like [[Deranged Brute]] and [[Lead Songbird]], a single extra stack of {{IconLink|Conduit}} is usually not terribly useful. It is best used alongside units that gain a little bit of {{IconLink|Conduit}} many times. Usually, this is either [[Ekka]]'s '''Celestial Spellweaver''' path, or the [[Aurora Weaver]]. With Ekka, '''Ethereal Seelie''' effectively makes her one level higher than she would otherwise be, which is quite strong, and at max level she gains {{IconLink|Conduit|4}} per {{IconLink|Incant}}. With Aurora Weaver, you will want to trigger {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} as often as possible, but this is somewhat unreliable since the Aurora Weaver is not a banner unit, so you are at the mercy of your draw order. With [[Arduhn]], it is usually much weaker, as it does not have strong synergy with any of his paths. His '''Battleborne''' path will gain {{IconLink|Conduit|2}} on {{IconLink|Slay}} during the battle, but he will only '''permanently''' gain {{IconLink|Conduit|1}}, so it cannot make him scale faster meaningfully. However, he starts with [[Moon Ritual]], which is free and applies {{IconLink|Conduit|1}}. '''Ethereal Seelie''' can double the effect of Moon Rituals played on her floor, either from starting with Arduhn or from [[Lunar Priestess]]; however, this effect is still quite weak. With [[Moon Pixie]] and [[Planetarium]], it will increase the {{IconLink|Conduit}} they apply to each friendly unit, but only if it has already been played before the effect activates. As with any source of {{IconLink|Conduit}}, you need a strong payoff for it to be worthwhile. {{IconLink|Mageblade}} units like [[Selene Acolyte]] are best, but [[Moonlit Glaive]] is also powerful, and '''[[Attuned]]''' spells like [[Cosmic Bolt]] can work in a pinch. If you happen to start with [[Fae's Nook]], '''Ethereal Seelie''' becomes a fairly respectable choice and a solid option for duplication, particularly alongside [[Meddler]]s to trigger {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} more frequently. It is the only [[:Category:Fae units|Fae unit]] that is also a banner unit, and if several of them are deployed on the same floor, that floor will gain a huge amount of {{IconLink|Conduit}} every {{IconLink|Mooncycle}}. This is aided by the unit's mere {{Capacity|1}}, and should be supplemented by cards like [[Fae's Blessing]] and [[Tidal Turning]] to keep them alive. [[The Clepsydranium]] is also a more potent pick with '''Ethereal Seelie''', doubling its effect on its floor. This is best alongside {{IconLink|Sweep}} units like the aforementioned Selene Acolyte. Unfortunately, '''Ethereal Seelie''' rarely does much on its own, so it may be wise to skip it for a unit with more immediate strength, like [[Shadeguard]], Selene Acolyte, or [[Nightingale]]. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! It has {{IconLink|Mageblade|3}}, which increases to a total of {{IconLink|Mageblade|6}} during {{IconLink|New Moon}}. == Strategy == '''Moonguard''' is a fairly straightforward unit in the context of [[Luna Coven]] - as you scale {{IconLink|Conduit}}, this unit's {{Attack}} will increase. It functionally has a [[Moonlit Glaive]] built in, and another conditional on {{IconLink|New Moon}}, and given how readily the [[Luna Coven]] can gain {{IconLink|Conduit}}, this unit's {{Attack}} can scale massively, letting it handle heavy units including [[Avowed Gladiator]] with relative ease. Owing to how powerful {{IconLink|Mageblade}} can be, the ability to maintain the moon phase is quite important, but it is not as necessary as it is for other Luna Coven units like [[Selene Acolyte]], [[Nightingale]], and [[Shadeguard]] as long as your {{IconLink|Conduit}} generation is strong enough. [[Eclipse Chamber]] is usable if you have no other options for keeping up {{IconLink|New Moon}}, but generally '''Moonguard''' would rather have [[Planetarium]]. However, Eclipse Chamber makes the unit compatible with allies that need {{IconLink|Full Moon}}, such as '''Silver Empress''' [[Ekka]]. [[Lunar Priestess]] is very valuable, adding a tiny bit of {{IconLink|Conduit}} per turn and keeping {{IconLink|New Moon}} active. [[Moon Pixie]] and [[Meddler]] are both valuable pickups. Moon Pixie is capable of applying a lot of {{IconLink|Conduit}}, while Meddler grants moon phase control. [[Moonlit Glaive]], while a worthwhile piece of equipment, is generally less valuable due to [[Moonguard]]'s already high {{IconLink|Mageblade}}, and may actually be better served on one of its allies in order to provide more individual high-damage hits. Conversely, any equipment that grants {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, like [[Void Armament]] and [[Cursed Twinblade]], should be highly prioritized. The [[Banished]], [[Lazarus League]], and [[Umbra]] are all capable of applying {{IconLink|Trample}} to '''Moonguard''', which is extremely effective due to the absurd amount of {{Attack}} this unit can build up. The Banished also have access to [[Cleave]], which lets you turn [[Moonguard]]'s incredible {{Attack}} into floor-wide damage, while the Lazarus League can trigger immediate attacks with [[Minds Of Their Own]] or clone the unit with [[Replicator Ray]], and Umbra can add extra stacks of {{IconLink|Multistrike}} with [[Furnace Tap]]. Its decent starting {{Health}} makes it usable as a frontliner if you don't have a better candidate for that, but it will need support from spells like [[Fae's Blessing]] to be able to survive battle in that position. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! {{UnitCard |name = Scrivener |image = PLR_Scrivener.png |clan = Luna Coven |rarity = Rare |type = Selene |banner = Yes |cost = 2 |size = 1 |stats = 15/8 |ability = {{AbilityBox|Spellweave|2|Draw a non-starter spell and apply {{Ember|-1}}.}} |flavor = "All my books, lost in the Fall. It will take me centuries to rewrite them. I just hope my memory is correct..." |artist = Genevieve Bega }} '''Scrivener''' is a rare [[Luna Coven]] [[banner unit]]. Her {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}, '''Spellweave''', draws a non-starter spell and reduces its cost by {{Ember|-1}}, with a cooldown of 2. == Strategy == [[Scrivener]]'s '''Spellweave''' ability provides a very strong effect: drawing an extra spell every other turn is equivalent to half a [[Limbo's Solace]] boss artifact. It may even be slightly better than that, since it can't draw undesirable cards like [[Blight]]s, can be activated on demand, doesn't run into the limit of 10 card draw per turn, etc. It also is unable to draw relatively low-impact [[starter card]]s, like [[Witchweave]] or [[Inspire (spell)|Inspire]]. Similarly, applying {{Ember|-1}} every other turn is equivalent to half a [[Hell's Flame]] artifact (minus the {{DeploymentEmber|1}}) unless the spell already cost {{Ember|0}}. Every time a '''Spellweave'''-discounted spell is redrawn, this {{Ember}} bonus accumulates. '''Spellweave''' is already a strong effect without any need to build around it, but it becomes even better as the average {{Ember}} cost of the spells in your deck increases, i.e. if it contains spells that tend to be powerful rather than {{Ember}}-efficient, those spells are then continually discounted over time. The strength of '''Spellweave''' is attached to the expensive and puny '''Scrivener''', however. At a cost of {{Ember|2}} and with just {{Health|8}}, she is expensive to play and hard to keep alive against effects like {{IconLink|Sweep}} or {{IconLink|Corruption}} (though a {{IconLink|Heartstone}} helps for her survivability). In particular, '''Scrivener''' declines in value if played after turn 1, but can be too expensive to play during [[Deployment]]. On the other hand, she provides a stronger turn 1, which can warrant playing her during Deployment over some other [[banner unit]]s. '''Scrivener''' can be a prime candidate to copy via [[Empyrean Well]], since she represents a lot of strength in a single card, and her {{Capacity|1}} means that there's often spare {{Capacity}} to play multiple copies of her. She is quite strong when partnered with the [[Melting Remnant]]. If she dies and is '''[[Reform]]ed''', not only will her {{Ember}} cost go down to 0, but '''Spellweave''' will immediately refresh, letting you draw another card. If you can force her to die and bring her back every turn, she can greatly accelerate the rate at which you draw through your deck. It also means you do not need to worry about her durability, as dying is encouraged. As a final aside, '''Spellweave''' applies an {{Ember}} discount throughout the battle, so if it hits the right spell(s), then it can even be used for some [[Infinite]]s which would ordinarily require spell upgrades to discount a combo spell like [[Deep Offering]] to {{Ember|0}}. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! {{SpellCard |name = Gravity |image = CRD_Gravity.png |clan = Luna Coven |rarity = Common |cost = 1 |effect = Deal '''5''' damage.
{{IconLink|New Moon}}: '''[[Descend]]'''.
{{IconLink|Full Moon}}: '''[[Ascend]]'''. |flavor = "Seraph had defeated us and left us with no choice. If we could no longer rise above Heaven and Hell, we would have to fall."
—Ardania the Forbidden |artist = Daniel Sarmiento Chuquisengo }} '''Gravity''' is a common [[Luna Coven]] spell. It deals 5 damage and either [[Ascend]]s the target if the {{IconLink|Full Moon}} is active, or [[Descend]]s it if the {{IconLink|New Moon}} is active. == Notes == In an [[Eclipse Chamber]], this will always [[Descend]], regardless of the outside moon phase. == Strategy == '''Gravity''' is capable of doing a lot of different things, though it takes a significant amount of setup to get to something reliable. It can almost always function as spot removal of weak backliners, as it will just about always damage them for 5, no matter what else is going on in your run. This is enough to hit things like [[Collector]], [[Profane Supplicant]] and [[Ragewing Assassin]]. It can also function as either situational disruption of enemy waves (e.g. by displacing a [[Celestial Bastion]] from its defense of its wave, or [[Ascend]]ing a boss to kill its accompanying enemies) or as a means of floor overstacking. But for maximum flexibility, it's at its best in a deck that generally has access to at least one [[Phase]] effect per turn, letting you choose which direction its target goes. You can play this card either before or after that Phase effect to functionally choose your direction. The fact that the [[Luna Coven]] has so much access to {{IconLink|Conduit}} is very much a double-edged sword with this card, as it improves the card's ability to hit backline enemies and damage enemies in general, but it can make it impractical to use as floor overstacking at times, as if you use it on your own units you might just end up killing them. It doesn't help that the [[Luna Coven]] has a lot of fragile backliners, and since [[Ascend]] and [[Descend]] move the unit to the back of the floor, generally you'd want to [[Ascend]] or [[Descend]] them, rather than the tanks that are meant to be in front of them. So overstacking with this card often requires additional investment, e.g. putting {{IconLink|Heartstone}} on units you're planning to have this hit. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! The moon phase will always be {{IconLink|Full Moon}} on turn 1, so even without any moon manipulation this can make this functionally a [[Hidden Passage]] with upside and downside. Having this on turn 1 also means you can play it before scaling up your {{IconLink|Conduit}}, giving you the best chance of playing it safely. |- | style="text-align:center;" | [[file:TwinStone.png|50x50px]]
[[Twinstone]] | '''Twinstone''' gives you two of these for the price of one, letting you Ascend/Descend two units together and thus put your kill floor together faster, or just generally increasing its utility. {{SpellCard |name = Moonbeam |image = CRD_Moonbeam.png |clan = Luna Coven |rarity = Uncommon |cost = X |effect = Deal '''20''' damage to the front enemy unit '''X''' times. |flavor = "As our beloved moon fell, our home had one last gift to give our coven. When it shattered, all the magic we had stored inside struck Seraph."
—Ardania, fallen guard to Lady Ekka |artist = Leonardo Dionisi }} '''Moonbeam''' is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] spell. It deals 20 damage to the front enemy unit X times. == Strategy == '''Moonbeam''' has a rather unimpressive baseline - at {{Ember|1}}, it's a worse [[Silver Strike]]; at {{Ember|2}}, it's a worse [[Helical Crystalis]]. It has two different ways to scale, however, which multiply with each other: * As an X cost spell, the number of times it hits scales with your ability to build up a large amount of {{Ember}} in a turn. * The per-hit damage can be upgraded with [[Magic Power]], such as with {{IconLink|Conduit}}, as with any other spell. If you can both have a lot of {{Ember}} when playing it and have a lot of {{IconLink|Conduit}}, its damage can scale to impressive heights, and its multi-hit nature means it can kill more than one enemy. If you can manage to give it the [[Attuned]] keyword with [[Silver Ink]], its damage can become even more explosive, as in that case it gains 5X damage per stack of [[Magic Power]]! It's probably not strong enough to be worth including if you're only able to scale one of its two scaling methods (playing it for a large X but no [[Magic Power]], or with a lot of [[Magic Power]] but only for X = 1 or 2), and taking it before the endgame can often be a case of betting on yourself being able to achieve both. {{SpellCard |name = Silver Ink |image = CRD_SilverInk.png |clan = Luna Coven |rarity = Rare |cost = 3 |effect = '''[[Consume]]'''.
Apply '''[[Attuned]]''' and '''+3 [[Magic Power]]''' to spells in your hand. |flavor = "Take stardust and mix it with oil. Cast a blessing. Only the fae shall read your words written in this ink."
—The Ritual Tome |artist = Loy Bouttamy }} '''Silver Ink''' is a rare [[Luna Coven]] spell. This is one of two Luna Coven cards that can be obtained through the [[Gremlin Looter]] event, the other being [[Glittering Draught]]. == Strategy == '''Silver Ink''' is a very expensive spell. Is applying Attuned to a spell really strong enough to warrant this {{Ember}} cost? Here's one way to think about it: for damage and healing spells with small numbers on their cards, Magic Power dominates over their card text (e.g. [[Witchweave]], [[Fae's Blessing]]). Applying Attuned to such a spell thus essentially multiplies the spell's effect by 5x, almost as if each spellcast added four free Ephemeral copies to your hand but you had to cast the extra copies on the same target. In addition, even just the +3 Magic Power from Silver Ink already turns into +15 damage or healing due to Attuned. So applying Attuned to one spell like Witchweave is already decent, but '''Silver Ink''' shines if you can apply it to multiple spells. That said, by itself this doesn't always happen due to luck of the draw or low spell density in the deck. Upgrades like {{IconLink|Freezestone}} or {{IconLink|Seekstone}} can help ensure that '''Silver Ink''' affects the spells you want it to. If your starter card was [[Moon Ritual]] instead of [[Witchweave]], '''Silver Ink''' is much worse, since the density of cheap damage spells in your deck is so much lower. In addition, if your damage spells are too expensive, then you won't be able to cast any of them on the turn you cast '''Silver Ink'''. Then '''Silver Ink''' costs an entire turn without having any immediate effect until you redraw your buffed spells, which is extremely slow. This can be a great pickup from [[Gremlin Looter]] if you have a large density of damage spells (or just one that you have a {{IconLink|Keepstone}} on), making the [[Luna Coven]] option worth picking off-clan. You might get [[Glittering Draught]] instead, however, so this is a better choice if you're also fine with that. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! '''Dusk Mantle''' is a rare [[Luna Coven]] equipment added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It grants a unit {{IconLink|Titanskin|5}} during {{IconLink|New Moon}}.

==Strategy==
The '''Dusk Mantle''' is a decently powerful defensive piece of equipment as long as you can consistently keep up {{IconLink|New Moon}}. {{IconLink|Titanskin|5}} is nothing to sneeze at, especially on a strong tank. [[Shadeguard]] is the ideal user, as a very durable frontliner that needs {{IconLink|New Moon}} already, but if you have solid phase control it works just as well on any other tank, like [[Firebrand]], [[The Sentient]], or [[Crucible Collector]]. It's best on a unit with {{IconLink|Titanite}}, as there it effectively counts as {{IconLink|Titanskin|10}}.

That said, it's still not a perfect solution, and it can falter somewhat against the final bosses. All versions of Seraph deal far too much damage for the {{IconLink|Titanskin}} to prevent. [[Seraph Aeternus-The Entropic|The Entropic]] is likely its best matchup, as lowering the damage of [[Purified Soul]]s from {{Attack|12}} to {{Attack|7}} is quite significant, and since that fight involves a lot of individual hits, the effect of {{IconLink|Titanskin}} is magnified. However, [[Deafening Herald]]s will disable '''Dusk Mantle''', and [[Enthralled Ardent]]s and their Chosen variants will essentially undo it with their {{IconLink|Incant}} effect if you play a spell on their floor. Meanwhile, [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage|the Savage]] will make every enemy deal 20-30 damage per hit, so {{IconLink|Titanskin}} prevents a much smaller fraction of incoming damage, and [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant|the Dominant's]] {{IconLink|Corruption}} will stack so high that any amount of {{IconLink|Titanskin}} will just be a drop in the bucket. As such, it should be paired with other strong defensive solutions, like [[Fae's Blessing]].

It's incompatible with {{IconLink|Full Moon}} strategies unless the unit holding it is placed in an [[Eclipse Chamber]].

Whenever the moon phase changes, it gains {{Attack|+1}} permanently. ==Strategy== The '''Luna Cyclestaff''' is a potent weapon with the right support. Like most permascaling cards, its main purpose is to solve the late game when you have a strong start, providing little immediate benefit but becoming strong enough to carry you to victory later on. On its own, its {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} trigger is too slow for it to gain significant scaling, and it will take several rings before it noticeably improves in quality. Assuming it is obtained as a Ring 3 reward and it is made Deployable as soon as possible, it will gain around 7-9 damage per Ring, so by Ring 8 it may only have around {{Attack|35}}. This is not insignificant, but it is not especially powerful. However, if you can trigger {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} more frequently than once per turn, it becomes much better. Even a single [[Lunar Priestess]] can double its {{Attack}} gain, assuming the [[Moon Ritual]] is played every turn. Starting with [[Arduhn]] also generally makes it stronger. [[Meddler]], [[Mooncaller]], and [[Lunacy]] are all good picks as well, and can help get its damage into the hundreds. Its biggest issue is likely its competition with [[Moonlit Glaive]]. {{IconLink|Mageblade|3}} is incredibly powerful with any big source of {{IconLink|Conduit}}, such as [[Moon Pixie]], [[Planetarium]], or [[Ekka]]'s '''Celestial Spellweaver''' path. The amount of damage that a Moonlit Glaive can provide can make even a very well-fed '''Luna Cyclestaff''' seem quaint. Additionally, {{IconLink|Conduit}} strategies are generally more common than {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} strategies. However, Moonlit Glaive is more expensive, costing {{Ember|2}}, and if using Luna Coven as a supporting clan rather than the primary, the slow but steady scaling of '''Luna Cyclestaff''' may be preferable, especially in clans lacking strong scaling options or equipment, such as the [[Awoken]]. ==History== ''See [[Version History]]'' {| class="wikitable" |- ! '''Moonlit Glaive''' is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] equipment. It grants {{IconLink|Mageblade|3}}.

==Strategy==
The '''Moonlit Glaive''' can be one of the strongest pieces of equipment in the entire game. {{IconLink|Mageblade}} makes for an incredible source of {{Attack}} scaling alongside any {{IconLink|Conduit}}. This card can be tossed even onto a weak support unit like a [[Moon Pixie]] and add an extra {{Attack|100+}} to the floor.

{{IconLink|Conduit}} sources are vital to this equipment's use. Alongside Moon Pixie, [[Planetarium]] is virtually always desirable; [[Enchanted Chamber]], while generally less effective, performs acceptably as well if you are not offered Planetarium. [[Ekka]]'s '''Celestial Spellweaver''' and '''Silver Empress''' paths can both be quite potent, with '''Silver Empress III''' giving this weapon {{Attack|210}} during {{IconLink|Full Moon}}. [[Arduhn]]'s '''Battleborne''' path can also stack up tons of {{IconLink|Conduit}}, and it synergizes well with his inherent {{IconLink|Mageblade}} to ensure he is always getting {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers.

Within the clan, [[Selene Acolyte]] can make the most of this equipment, enhancing her own {{IconLink|Mageblade|2}} and having {{IconLink|Sweep}} during {{IconLink|Full Moon}} to hit all enemies. After that, [[Nightingale]]'s inherent {{IconLink|Multistrike|2}} during {{IconLink|New Moon}} lets it triple the damage output of '''Moonlit Glaive'''. Outside of the clan, units with strong inherent traits but low damage output, such as [[Test Subject Alpha]] and [[Animus of Will]], are the best recipients. Note that with the [[Stygian Guard]], [[Eel Gorgon]] will lose the granted {{IconLink|Mageblade}} on {{IconLink|Resolve}}; try using [[Luna Cyclestaff]] instead.

{{SpellCard |name = Eclipse Chamber |image = CRD_EclipseChamber.png |clan = Luna Coven |rarity = Uncommon |cost = 1 |effect = {{IconLink|New Moon}} effects are always active. If they failed to bring the eclipse, we were doomed."
—Ardania the Forbidden |artist = Leonardo Dionisi }} '''Eclipse Chamber''' is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] room. It maintains {{IconLink|New Moon}} on its floor, and grants [[:Category:Silent units|Silent units]] {{Attack|+15}} each turn. == Notes == Note that {{IconLink|Full Moon}} triggers on units and spells will still be active in this room if the outside phase is {{IconLink|Full Moon}}. The only exception to this is [[Gravity]], whose {{IconLink|Full Moon}} trigger is mutually exclusive with its {{IconLink|New Moon}} trigger. == Strategy == The main purpose of '''Eclipse Chamber''' is to strengthen [[Shadeguard]] and [[Nightingale]]. Both units are far more effective during {{IconLink|New Moon}}, with Nightingale gaining {{IconLink|Multistrike}} and Shadeguard scaling its stats each turn. Both units also greatly appreciate the {{Attack|+15}} on {{IconLink|Resolve}}. The existence of this room allows these units to be more self-sufficient, as they no longer require a source of moon phase control such as [[Lunar Priestess]] to serve their purpose, nor do they rely on {{IconLink|Conduit}}. One particularly helpful feaure of '''Eclipse Chamber''' is allowing Selene units to work alongside Silent units, as the actual moon phase can be kept at {{IconLink|Full Moon}} while still keeping {{IconLink|New Moon}} effects active, opening up setups such as [[Shadeguard]] tanking for [[Selene Acolyte]]. [[Moonguard]] and [[Arduhn]]'s '''Mystic Hammer''' path also want to be in {{IconLink|New Moon}} at all times. However, the '''Mystic Hammer''' path already comes with a way to phase to {{IconLink|New Moon}}, and because he is technically not a Silent unit, Arduhn does not benefit from the {{Attack}} granted by this room. Moonguard, on the other hand, has {{IconLink|Mageblade|6}} during {{IconLink|New Moon}}; this means that it would usually prefer '''[[Planetarium]]''' as a room for the {{IconLink|Conduit}} application, and that {{Attack|+15}} is rather meaningless for it. The [[Silent Sentinel]] is also a Silent unit and thus receives {{Attack}} buffs, but the unit lacks a {{IconLink|New Moon}} trigger, and is not an attacker anyway. As such, if you are not playing with Shadeguard or Nightingale, this room is usually safe to skip, but if you are, it is a high priority. '''Eclipse Chamber''' only affects static {{IconLink|New Moon}} triggers that check if it ''is'' New Moon, but not ones that trigger when it ''becomes'' {{IconLink|New Moon}}, like in case of [[Silent Sigil]]. For example, [[Gravity]] Descends on {{IconLink|New Moon}}, and thus Descends when cast in '''Eclipse Chamber''' regardless of the moon phase. ==History== ''See [[Version History]]'' {| class="wikitable" |- ! '''Planetarium''' is an uncommon [[Luna Coven]] room. It grants {{IconLink|Conduit|5}} to all friendly units on the floor.

==Strategy==
'''Planetarium''' is best seen as an alternative to [[Enchanted Chamber]]. Both cost {{Ember|1}} and grant '''[[Magic Power]]''' on their floor. However, '''Enchanted Chamber''' grants a flat 15 '''[[Magic Power]]''', while '''Planetarium''' scales with the number of friendly units. This makes '''Planetarium''' more effective on floors with more than three friendly units. With overstacking or increased {{Capacity}}, it can grant up to {{IconLink|Conduit|35}}, more than twice that of '''Enchanted Chamber'''.

If only using three units on a floor, it may be better to stick to '''Enchanted Chamber''', which will continue to work just as well if one or more units are killed. However, there are certain synergies that can make '''Planetarium''''s {{IconLink|Conduit}} application preferable. When partnered with the [[Underlegion]], '''[[Propagate]]''' effects such as [[Proliferate]] and [[Loamcoat]] will increase {{IconLink|Conduit}} but will do nothing for '''Enchanted Chamber''', and '''[[Spawn]]''' effects also make it easier to overstack the floor. [[Moon Pixie]] also provides {{IconLink|Conduit}} based on the number of allies on the floor, so they work well together as both cards want the same condition. [[Ethereal Seelie]] causes '''Planetarium''' to grant {{IconLink|Conduit|6}} instead.

This room is especially effective with [[Primordium]]'s '''Superfood''' path, which can pass the {{IconLink|Conduit}} to another unit each turn. If equipped with [[Moonlit Glaive]], the {{IconLink|Mageblade}} will be passed on as well, creating an absolutely devastating unit.

'''Underlegion''' [[File:ClanUnderlegion.png|20x20px]] is a [[clan]] in [[Monster Train 2]]. It is unlocked after consuming 75 cards. 

Underlegion features the following mechanics:
* '''[[Funguy]]''' is a unique unit that is created and grown using the '''[[Spawn]]''' keyword. For more information, see the [[Funguy]] page.
* Many units interact with Funguy's unique mechanics via {{IconLink|Harvest}} and {{IconLink|Rally}} triggers.
* '''[[Status Effects#Buffs|Buffs]]''' and '''[[Status Effects#Debuffs|Debuffs]]''' are central to Underlegion gameplay. {{IconLink|Regen}} and {{IconLink|Sap}} are the clan's main survivability tools, while {{IconLink|Decay}} is the clan's main source of damage. Funguy's strength is represented using the {{IconLink|Troop}} buff. The '''[[Propagate]]''' keyword increases stacks of buffs on allied units and debuffs on enemy units.
* Underlegion has many '''Consume''' spells. Some spells interact with the Consume pile, and some units have {{IconLink|Etch}}  effects that trigger when a card is consumed.
* Certain spells and artifacts incentivize large deck sizes.
The clan's unique [[Merchant of Steel]] Upgrade is {{IconLink|Mossystone}}.

This makes him work well with '''[[Spawn]]''' and '''[[Propagate]]''' cards. '''Bolete''' struggles with dealing with backline enemies due to a lack of early-game {{IconLink|Decay}} application, and his {{Capacity|3}} size makes him less compatible with backline-handling units such as [[Spore Launcher]]. === Headsman === '''Headsman''' gives '''Bolete''' {{IconLink|Trample}}, relatively high damage, and the ability to '''[[Propagate]]''' on all friendly units on {{IconLink|Slay}}. At higher covenants, however, even {{Attack|160}} is not enough to take down late-game enemies, so a source of additional damage becomes necessary. This damage can be supplied either by other units or by giving '''Bolete''' {{Attack}} with '''Hive Minder''' or cards from the allied clan. As long as he has at least one stack of {{IconLink|Rage}}, Propagate will allow him to increase it with every enemy he kills, increasing his damage further and allowing for more {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers. However, '''Headsman''' is often used merely as support for another path, as it grants {{IconLink|Trample}}. A popular and very consistent strategy is to take '''Hive Minder''' first, then '''Headsman''', which will allow '''Bolete''' to stack up hundreds of {{Attack}} and wipe out whole waves of enemies in a single blow. Taking a second level in either path can be helpful, with '''Hive Minder II''' providing greater survivability and '''Headsman II''' providing faster scaling. Going all in on '''Headsman''' is generally ineffective unless you have another way to scale '''Bolete''''s damage using your allied clan, such as [[Ritual of Battle]], as his {{IconLink|Trample}} and {{IconLink|Slay}} effects are irrelevant if he cannot kill the first enemy unit. The main exception to this rule is when partnered with the [[Lazarus League]], in which case '''Headsman''' can be turned into an extremely strong path with one simple trick: {{IconLink|Spikes}}. By placing '''Bolete''' at the front and giving him some amount of {{IconLink|Spikes}}, he can trigger {{IconLink|Slay}} for every backliner that attacks him and dies, letting you Propagate to high heaven. With [[Faulty Body]] and [[Organ Harvester]], he can gain enough {{IconLink|Spikes}} to kill nearly every backliner in the game, and the {{IconLink|Fragile}} doesn't matter as Organ Harvester will give him {{IconLink|Reanimate}} which will then get Propagated. This also works with the [[Awoken]], as they can apply {{IconLink|Spikes}} as well, but they generally don't have many status effects worth Propagating, whereas the Lazarus League can make use of {{IconLink|Rage}}, {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, and {{IconLink|Damage Shield}}. ===Executioner=== With '''Executioner''', '''Bolete''' himself will be relatively weak, but his main value is his ability to produce Funguys in enormous numbers. This makes him extremely effective with any source of damage that depends on enormous Funguy stacks, such as [[Spore Launcher]] or [[Squad Leader]]. As long as you can consistently kill all enemies on a single floor (a relatively easy requirement), you can gain 2 stacks of {{IconLink|Troop}} for every enemy that enters the train, on top of whatever you're able to spawn by actually playing cards. The extra {{Health}} on Funguys is helpful for tanking damage, and while it doesn't directly increase their damage output, it does serve as a {{Health}} cushion for preventing the loss of {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks while they are attacked, leading to higher {{Attack}} in practice. You will still need another way to protect your backliners - [[Amorous Enoki]], for example - but this can make the Funguys themselves almost unkillable. Alternatively, [[Equalizing Rings]] (or [[Shield of Wyngh]], if you are partnered with the [[Banished]]) can directly translate the extra {{Health}} into damage. This path also mixes very well with '''Hive Minder''', as the constant Funguy spawns allow '''Bolete''' himself to stack up an enormous supply of {{Attack}}. It can even be worth pathing into '''Hive Minder''' at a later Forge, which is otherwise generally a bad idea. That said, doing so locks you out of '''Executioner III''', which increases the Spawn on {{IconLink|Siphon}} to 3, a 50% increase in Funguy production, or 1 Funguy per enemy - whether this tradeoff is worth it will depend on how much [[Spawn]] and/or [[Propagate]] of your own you have. [[Loamcoat]] has especially high synergy with '''Executioner''''s Funguy, since '''Executioner''' adds a {{Health}} cushion which scales with the number of {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks to make the most use out of the growing {{IconLink|Regen}} provided by Loamcoat. ===Hive Minder=== '''Hive Minder''' is entirely built around having good [[Spawn]] and [[Propagate]] on the floor to maximize {{IconLink|Troop}}, as each {{IconLink|Troop}} stack triggers his {{IconLink|Rally}}. As a result, he works well with Spawn and {{IconLink|Rally}} cards such as [[Amorous Enoki]], [[Deathcapped Prophet]], and most of all [[Cluster Colonel]], who seems almost made for this path. '''Hive Minder''' struggles with backline management on its own. It has good synergy with [[Spore Launcher]]'s {{IconLink|Decay}} on {{IconLink|Rally}}, but their size makes them incompatible without increasing a floor’s {{Capacity}} with the likes of [[Bogwurm's Growth]] or [[Heaven's Light]] or obtaining a {{IconLink|Smidgestone}} or [[Exile's Diadem]]. '''Hive Minder''' also works with a crosspath into '''Headsman''', with the full-floor Propagate on {{IconLink|Slay}} also triggering {{IconLink|Rally}} (so long as there is {{IconLink|Troop}} present). It is rarely worth taking the higher levels of '''Hive Minder''': level II only offers {{Health}} scaling, which is usually redundant if you have a strong source of Spawn (unless you lack another source of backline protection), and '''Hive Minder III''', while it offers double {{Attack}} scaling in the late game, only applies to the last two battles and will provide only a limited amount of extra {{Attack}} and {{Health}}. Cross-pathing into '''Executioner''' can provide more {{IconLink|Rally}} triggers and a tankier Funguy stack, so long as you don't need {{IconLink|Trample}}. ==Quotes== '''Summoned''' * ''I've survived countless wars, yet I have yet to decay.'' * ''If we win, first round's on me.'' * ''In the fungal front, once again.'' * ''Let's show them what fungi are made of.'' * ''Stay sharp. When a unit gains {{IconLink|Decay}}, it gains +5 stacks. }} == Strategy == '''Madame Lionsmane''' does not pack the same punch as [[Bolete]] does, but with her {{Capacity|2}} and her focus on status effects, she has a higher potential ceiling, if you can find the right cards for her. The ability to cancel out attacks and abilities is in particular extremely powerful against the trickiest enemies you'll have to face. She generally benefits from any card carrying the [[Propagate]] keyword. {{IconLink|Decay}} usage dictates putting her on the bottom floor to make the most out of it. If you are using '''Everbloom''' instead, you can more easily put her in the middle or top floor. ===Everbloom=== '''Everbloom''' is a relatively simple path at level I, simply spawning a [[Funguy]] each time a spell is played on her floor. This is an easy requirement to fulfill, and is especially helpful if your allied clan can also take advantage of {{IconLink|Incant}}. At higher levels, however, it requires constant {{IconLink|Etch}} triggers to be worth taking. If your deck has many Consume cards, this can be immensely powerful, but if not, it is usually better to cross-path, as both '''Maneating''' and '''Sporesinger''' offer distinct and potent benefits. [[Underlegion]] cards [[Contagious]] and [[Pandemic]] '''[[Consume]]''' to trigger {{IconLink|Etch}} but replicate themselves, so they can be replayed. Taking these and thinning the rest of your deck can allow you to consistently trigger {{IconLink|Etch}}. [[The Great Decay]] can also allow for an unholy number of {{IconLink|Etch}} triggers. Something that may not be immediately obvious is that any {{IconLink|Etch}} triggers will naturally also trigger {{IconLink|Incant}} (barring [[Sacrificial Resurrection]] or '''[[Smelt]]ing'''), so playing a Consume card on her floor will actually spawn 3 at level II, and 5 at level III. As the only other card in-clan with {{IconLink|Etch}}, [[Morel Mistress]] can potentially work well with this path. However, the constant {{IconLink|Rally}} triggers often make it more effective to use [[Spore Launcher]] instead. Depending on your secondary clan, you may want to partner her with [[Crucible Steward]], [[First of Kin]], or [[Bogdeep Cocoon]]. This path is exceptionally potent with [[Hall of Mirrors]]. As long as you keep the Hall of Mirrors active, every {{IconLink|Incant}} will spawn 4 - each time you spawn in a Hall of Mirrors, you spawn one more for a total of two per {{IconLink|Incant}}, and you will have two copies of her active. This can lead to truly tremendous Funguy stacks or absurd numbers of {{IconLink|Rally}} triggers, and if you have another unit with {{IconLink|Smidgestone}}, you can fit them all on the floor with no {{Capacity}} upgrades - place the {{Capacity|1}} unit first, then the Hall of Mirrors, then '''Madame Lionsmane'''. ===Maneater=== '''Maneating''' is available every turn, so it can be used to disable or kill one enemy per turn. It is effective against nearly all enemies and bosses, because {{IconLink|Sap}} reduces {{Attack}}, {{IconLink|Decay}} deals damage, and {{IconLink|Mute}} disables triggers, abilities, and enchantments. This includes effects like {{IconLink|Corruption}} on {{IconLink|Strike}} or {{IconLink|Extinguish}} as well as {{IconLink|Incant}} abilities. There is one unit '''Maneating''' cannot defeat, however: [[Deafening Herald]], whose {{IconLink|Silence}} ability prevents the use of '''Maneating'''. It can appear in [[The_Observatory#Purified_Hordes|Ring 7]] and always appears in the [[Seraph Aeternus-The Entropic]] fight. If you rely on '''Maneating''' as backline removal to take out the scariest threat in every wave, then be sure to have a different answer to Deafening Herald, such as [[Inhale]]. If you always use '''Maneating''' on flying bosses when they appear on [[Madame Lionsmane]]'s floor, then the boss will always be {{IconLink|Sap}}ped and {{IconLink|Mute}}d on the floor. If you only play on two floors while leaving the third empty, then {{IconLink|Mute|2}} from '''Maneating III''' is enough to disable [[Seraph]]'s abilities on both floors. When combined with either other sources of {{IconLink|Sap}}, or with '''[[Ascend]]'''/'''[[Descend]]''' effects, '''Maneating''' can completely disable flying bosses like [[Cael]]. In the [[Titans]] fight, it can disable both [[Savagery]] and the part of [[Entropy]] on [[Madame Lionsmane]]'s floor. Due to {{IconLink|Mute}}, this includes Entropy's ability to put [[Curse of Entropy]] into your deck. While the damage inflicted by '''Maneating''' is not the most impressive thing about it, it is not negligible, either. In addition to '''Madame Lionsmane''''s baseline {{Attack|65}}, inflicting {{IconLink|Decay|15}} per turn means dealing at least 65+45=110 overall damage to enemies on the current floor, and at most 65+45+42+39=191 damage if she debuffs enemies on the bottom floor and they survive until the top floor. Because debuffs persist against flying bosses and Titans, the damage against them is much higher. Because it applies three different debuffs, this path works extremely well with any '''[[Propagate]]''' card, and it is especially potent with [[Evolutionary Instinct]] and [[Contagious]]. ===Sporesinger=== '''Sporesinger''' requires no additional input to work effectively, automatically applying increasing amounts of {{IconLink|Decay}} to all enemies on the floor every turn. It is most powerful, however, when you can use other units or spells to apply {{IconLink|Decay}}. This is the only path which benefits significantly from [[Sporetouch]], making it somewhat less effective with the [[Pyre of Dominion]]. [[Underlegion]] units [[Cheery Deathcap]], [[Morel Mistress]], [[Prickly Puffball]], and [[Spore Launcher]] apply area-of-effect {{IconLink|Decay}}, benefiting massively from '''Sporesinger''''s increase. The Spore Launcher is especially powerful, as it frequently applies small amounts of {{IconLink|Decay}} to all enemies, with each activation gaining the extra {{IconLink|Decay}} from this path. It is often worth branching into this path if you started with '''Everbloom''' and are using it to power a Spore Launcher. With a deployable [[Stasis Crystal]], she can hold bottom floor all by herself while conveniently taking out most backline enemies, as {{IconLink|Action}} triggers still work under [[Stasis]]. This can be more efficient than committing resources to tank her floor during the waves, and also gives her some good {{Health}} to tank herself against the {{IconLink|Relentless}} boss. == Quotes == '''Summoned''' * ''It's time to make a grand entrance.'' * ''My shrooms are adorable, don't you think?'' * ''They call me the Queen of Spores. '''Funguy''' is a unique, stackable Shroom unit from the [[Underlegion]] clan. They are always {{IconLink|Cardless}}, as there is no card that explicitly represents them. Instead, any '''[[Spawn]]''' X effect will summon a Funguy to the front of the floor, regardless of the floor's {{Capacity}}, with X {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks. Additional '''Spawn''' X effects on a floor with a '''Funguy''' stack on it will cause them to gain X {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks, regardless of where they are on the floor. Their {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks can also be increased via [[Propagate]] effects, as they'll always have at least {{IconLink|Troop|1}}.

There can never be more than 1 '''Funguy''' on a floor; if '''Funguy''' is moved to a different floor with '''Funguy''', the moved '''Funguy''' is deleted and the existing '''Funguy''' gains {{IconLink|Troop}} equal to the moved [[Funguy]]'s {{IconLink|Troop}}. All other modifications, such as [[Equipment]] or other [[Buffs]] on the moved [[Funguy]], will be lost - for example, if a '''Funguy''' with [[Loamcoat]] is moved to a floor with other '''Funguy''' (that don't have [[Equipment]]), the [[Loamcoat]] will be lost.

As '''Funguy''' takes damage, their {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks will decrease. This will never cause them to lose current {{Health}}, though it will cause them to lose {{Attack}}. '''Funguy''' will lose stacks of {{IconLink|Troop}} once their {{Health}} drops to or below (# {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks - 1) * {{Health|4}}. Their number of {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks will then be set to (Funguy's {{Health}})/4, rounded up. Note that this differs from what {{IconLink|Troop}}'s tooltip describes if you give '''Funguy''' {{Health}} through means other than increasing their {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks, such as [[Amorous Enoki]].  Note also that '''Executioner''' [[Bolete the Guillotine#Executioner|Bolete]]'s effect, which buffs [[Funguy]]'s {{Health}}, does not change the base number "4" in the above formulas, hence contributing a {{Health}} cushion for preventing the loss of {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks just like other {{Health}} buffs.

For example, if '''Funguy''' has {{IconLink|Troop|5}}, corresponding to base {{AttackHealth|15|20}}, and you equip [[Stoic Platemail]] to them to bring their {{Health}} to 50, they would then not lose {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks unless their {{Health}} dropped to 16 (assuming you didn't gain more {{IconLink|Troop}} prior to that). The extra {{Health|30}} and {{Armor|60}} protect [[Funguy]]'s {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks, letting them take 90 damage before any {{IconLink|Troop}} loss. This is most relevant when using '''Funguy''' as both a tank and an attacking unit, as otherwise they will lose {{Attack}} while taking damage.

As the loss of {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks correlates with the loss of [[Funguy]]'s max {{Health}}, healing effects such as {{IconLink|Regen}} are of very little value on a '''Funguy''' without additional {{Health}} buffs, but become very valuable on a '''Funguy''' with such buffs.

== Interactions ==
* [[Squad Leader]] and [[Spotted Spore]] increase [[Funguy]]'s {{Attack}} per {{IconLink|Troop}} stack. [[Bolete the Guillotine]]'s '''Executioner''' path increases [[Funguy]]'s {{Health}} per {{IconLink|Troop}} stack.
* Whenever '''Funguy''' gains {{IconLink|Troop}}, {{IconLink|Rally}} effects are triggered a number of times equal to the stacks gained. 
* {{IconLink|Summon}} effects, such as those granted by [[Sapsuckling Spring]], [[Electricity Chamber]], or [[Shadow's Sheath]], are triggered once whenever '''Funguy''' gains any amount of {{IconLink|Troop}}.
* A '''[[Sacrifice]]''' effect fully sacrifices '''Funguy''', with the exception of [[Mushroom Cloud]], which explicitly causes '''Funguy''' to lose only one {{IconLink|Troop}} stack.
* When '''Funguy''' loses {{IconLink|Troop}}, any {{IconLink|Harvest}} ability on the floor triggers a number of times equal to the stacks lost.
** If '''Funguy''' is killed due to being [[Sacrifice]]d or an effect that directly kills a unit like [[Hallowed Halls]] or [[Crushing Demise]], {{IconLink|Harvest}} is triggered once for each {{IconLink|Troop}} stack '''Funguy''' had.
* {{IconLink|Slay}} and {{IconLink|Extinguish}} are only triggered if '''Funguy''' fully dies.

== Strategy==		

See various [[Underlegion]] cards - what '''Funguys''' do varies depending on your run, ranging from a tank to a chump blocker to an offensive threat. They are generally used either as a powerful damage dealer in their own right with units like [[Squad Leader]] or as a way to trigger {{IconLink|Rally}} and incidentally block damage with units like [[Spore Launcher]] or [[Enchantrelle]].

It applies {{IconLink|Decay|7}} to enemy units on {{IconLink|Summon}}. == Strategy == '''Cheery Deathcap''' does a respectable amount of floor-wide damage on {{IconLink|Summon}} - if applied on the first floor, enemies will take a total of 56* damage in three installments before they reach the Pyre, which will finish off backliners and soften tanks through the midgame. It also triggers {{IconLink|Rally}} on its floor, and can serve as a chump blocker. Its utility is somewhat diminished by being part of the [[Underlegion]], as there often won't be a spare {{Capacity}} for it to land, especially since [[Funguy]] will likely be on the floor by the time you're playing '''Cheery Deathcap''', owing to it being a non-banner unit. It also isn't the best candidate for ways to cheat non-banner units like [[Sketches of Salvation]] or {{IconLink|Dominating Authority}} as its effect is wasted if played during the [[Deployment Phase]]. Still, it can be considered as an extra source of damage for runs that do have plenty of {{Capacity}}, e.g. when paired with the [[Umbra]], [[Bogwurm's Growth]], or with [[Heph's Hammer]], and can be given {{IconLink|Endless}} to be used as a consistent strategy. == Math == (7 + 6 + 5 {{IconLink|Decay}}) * 3 damage / {{IconLink|Decay}} = 56 damage == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! Whenever a friendly unit is summoned, she increases the {{Health}} of all friendly units by 1 and applies {{IconLink|Regen|1}} to all friendly units. == Strategy == '''Amorous Enoki''' is an effective part of any {{IconLink|Rally}}-focused strategy, and works well alongside [[Deathcapped Prophet]], [[Spore Launcher]], and similar units. With solid [[Funguy]] production, she can provide enough {{Health}} and {{IconLink|Regen}} to keep the entire floor alive indefinitely. This makes her especially valuable against enemies and bosses which can damage backliners, such as [[Qel the Corruptor]], [[Ragewing Assassin]], and [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]]. She provides value to strategies dependent on Funguy for damage output, such as those revolving around [[Squad Leader]] or [[Spotted Spore]]. Usually, these strategies want Funguy pulling double duty as both tank and damage-dealer, but due to the mechanics of {{IconLink|Troop}}, its {{Attack}} will drop as enemies damage it. [[Amorous Enoki]]'s extra {{Health}} and {{IconLink|Regen}} will provide a cushion of max {{Health}} that will be used up before Funguy starts losing {{IconLink|Troop}}, and which can be restored with {{IconLink|Regen}} between turns, keeping its {{Attack}} intact. She may be redundant if you also have access to [[Enchantrelle]], but if you have the space and {{DeploymentEmber}} to play both they can combine to completely shut down enemies. During Deployment, she should usually be played first, so that she can give herself and other units extra {{Health}} and {{IconLink|Regen}} before the battle begins. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! Cluster Colonel:
{{UnitCard |name = Cluster Colonel |image = PLR_ClusterColonel.png |clan = Underlegion |rarity = Uncommon |type = Shroom |banner = Yes |cost = 2 |size = 2 |stats = 10/5 |ability = {{IconLink|Armor|10}}.
{{IconLink|Resolve}}: '''[[Spawn]] 4'''. |flavor = "I would be willing—no, happy—to lead these Caps to battle every day!" |artist = Daniel Sarmiento Chuquisengo }} '''Cluster Colonel''' is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] [[banner unit]]. At the end of the turn, he [[Spawn|Spawns]] 4. == Strategy == '''Cluster Colonel''' will trigger {{IconLink|Rally}} four times per turn with his ability, making him a strong supplement to any {{IconLink|Rally}}-based strategies. He pairs well with [[Spore Launcher]] to apply {{IconLink|Decay|8}} to all enemies each turn, and with [[Amorous Enoki]] he provides {{Health|+4}} and {{IconLink|Regen|4}} to allies every turn. [[Bolete the Guillotine]]'s '''Hive Minder''' path will gain a permanent {{Attack|+4}} each turn from his {{IconLink|Resolve}} effect, providing a good amount of scaling over the course of a run. He also has potent synergy with {{IconLink|Harvest}} units. Whenever a {{IconLink|Troop}} stack is lost, {{IconLink|Harvest}} triggers, which means that he can provide up to four triggers per turn if [[Funguy]] is killed each turn. The [[Cortical Connector]] artifact is the only {{IconLink|Harvest}} trigger available in-clan, but when partnered with [[Melting Remnant]], this synergy is easily exploitable. [[Wickless Baron]], [[Big Sludge]], and [[Rector Flicker]]'s '''Accumulator''' path can all scale rapidly with his support, as can [[Devourer of Death]]. [[Wickless Tycoon]] can generate absurd amounts of {{Gold}}. [[Lady Gilda]]'s '''Bloat Matron''' path can also abuse this effect to apply huge amounts of {{IconLink|Pyregel}} to the entire floor. If using this approach, it is best '''not''' to partner him with Amorous Enoki, as the {{Health}} that she provides to Funguy will prevent {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks from being lost. Even without any immediate synergies, '''Cluster Colonel''' is a worthwhile unit in the early rings, as the Funguy stack he creates has {{AttackHealth|12|16}} by default and gets {{AttackHealth|+12|+16}} every turn, creating a powerful unit by the time the boss arrives. For comparison, [[Morselmaker]] effectively provides {{AttackHealth|+9|+9}} each turn, although stats gained from [[Magma Morsel]]s and [[Antumbra Morsel]]s cannot be lowered by taking damage, unlike Funguy. When partnered with [[Squad Leader]] or with the [[Spotted Spore]] artifact, each {{IconLink|Resolve}} trigger provides {{AttackHealth|+20|+16}}. However, '''Cluster Colonel''' does have some downsides. {{IconLink|Resolve}} takes place at the end of the turn, including after {{IconLink|Decay}} would trigger, which means when partnered with Spore Launcher, enemy units will not actually take damage or die until the end of the next turn. This can be bad news when it comes to dangerous backliners such as [[Ragewing Assassin]]s or [[Discordant Heretic]]s. It also makes him less useful when partnered with [[Enchantrelle]], as she will not apply {{IconLink|Sap}} until after all enemy units have already attacked. This means he usually needs to be supplemented with other '''[[Spawn]]''' cards or effects. Also, because his value is mostly in his {{IconLink|Resolve}} effect, his performance is not meaningfully improved by most upgrades. While this can be beneficial, as it means you do not have to hunt for specific upgrades, it also means there is no way to scale his effect besides simply having multiple copies. This is easier said than done, as his {{Ember|2}} cost is quite steep, and though he is not an especially large unit himself, many of his best allies, like Bolete and Spore Launcher, are. {{Capacity}} is at a premium with the Underlegion, and without any natural ways to '''[[Ascend]]''' or '''[[Descend]]''' units, getting more than one '''Cluster Colonel''' on a floor can be tricky. The [[Purified Soul Shard]] artifact reduces the cost of unupgraded units by {{Ember|1}}. Due to the very small impact of most upgrades on '''Cluster Colonel''' and his {{Ember|2}} cost, it is often better to leave him unupgraded if you have this artifact. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! Morel Mistress:
{{UnitCard |name = Morel Mistress |image = PLR_MorelMistress.png |clan = Underlegion |rarity = Uncommon |type = Shroom |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 15/15 |ability = {{IconLink|Etch}}: Apply {{IconLink|Decay|8}} to enemy units. |flavor = "A mushroom's rotting scent tells you all you need to know about them." |artist = Genevieve Bega }} '''Morel Mistress''' is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever a card is Consumed on her floor, she applies {{IconLink|Decay|8}} to all enemies on the floor. == Strategy == '''Morel Mistress''' is not an especially exciting unit, but can still be a keystone of the right kind of deck. Her {{IconLink|Etch}} trigger requires the consistent use of '''[[Consume]]''' cards in order to provide value. Fortunately, the Underlegion has many strong Consume cards, such as [[Proliferate]], [[Gooey Flask]], and [[Spawning Pods]]. She will immediately draw comparisons to her fellow unit [[Spore Launcher]], which is generally considered to be the better of the two. Both units are designed to eliminate backline enemies with {{IconLink|Decay}}, and Spore Launcher's {{IconLink|Rally}} trigger tends to be easier to activate than {{IconLink|Etch}}, giving it synergies with units like [[Cluster Colonel]], [[Amorous Enoki]], and [[Enchantrelle]] which '''Morel Mistress''' lacks. However, '''Morel Mistress''' has some notable upsides compared to Spore Launcher. She applies four times as much {{IconLink|Decay}} per trigger as Spore Launcher, which is notable in the early game, when enemies have less {{Health}} and upgrades like {{IconLink|Dualism}} may not have been applied yet. Thus, for decks that cannot efficiently trigger {{IconLink|Rally}}, '''Morel Mistress''' may be preferable. She also costs {{Ember|1}} and takes up {{Capacity|2}} compared to Spore Launcher's {{Ember|2}} and {{Capacity|3}}, which means it is easier to put together several copies of '''Morel Mistress''' on the same floor than Spore Launcher. There are a few ways to ensure that '''Morel Mistress''' will always be able to apply {{IconLink|Decay}} when necessary. Taking lots of cards with Consume and copying them when possible is a straightforward option, and certain Underlegion cards and Artifacts reward you for having a large deck, such as [[Everchurning Soil]], [[Mulch]], and [[Ancient Roots]]. Certain Consume cards make a copy of themselves, allowing you to play them repeatedly, namely [[Contagious]] and [[Pandemic]]. These can be useful to ensure that you will never fully run out of Consume cards. Upgrading cards with {{IconLink|Surgestone}} and {{IconLink|Smolderstone}} will add Consume to cards that didn't originally have it. [[The Great Decay]] is perhaps her greatest synergy, applying Consume to all spells in your deck and making them cheaper. Not only will this rapidly and efficiently trigger {{IconLink|Etch}}, but it also means that you can quickly reduce your deck to only a few copies of Pandemic or Contagious and play them repeatedly for the rest of battle. If you have any other spells that are important to play repeatedly, upgrading them with {{IconLink|Eternalstone}} can prevent them from being Consumed and put them in your hand consistently. Some cards from other clans can interact nicely with her {{IconLink|Etch}} trigger. The [[Wurmkin]] have perhaps the most synergy, especially with [[Echowright]] as your Champion, who can either provide {{IconLink|Armor}}, summon a [[Bogdeep Cocoon]], or return Consumed cards so you can play them again. Cards like [[Chamber of Recall]], [[Broken Memories]], and [[Wurmkin Etchings]] can bring back large numbers of Consumed spells. [[First of Kin]] is a solid partner to '''Morel Mistress''', with its high {{Attack}} and {{IconLink|Etch}}-based scaling letting it take down the tanks that '''Morel Mistress''' struggles with while she eliminates the backline. The [[Railforged]] consume cards via '''[[Smelt]]''' as a central mechanic (particularly if their starter card is [[Salvage]]), and she is a strong pick if she shows up while allied with them. [[Spreading Spores]] with a {{IconLink|Smolderstone}} can provide {{Ember|0}} {{IconLink|Etch}} triggers while replacing each copy consumed. A [[Surgical Strike]] with {{IconLink|Smolderstone}} or {{IconLink|Surgestone}} can potentially trigger {{IconLink|Etch}} numerous times in one turn. [[Sacrificial Resurrection]] can consume your entire hand, providing a huge burst of {{IconLink|Etch}} triggers and removing unwanted cards like [[Vengeful Shard]]. [[Gifts for a Guard]] can apply Consume to any damage spell, quickly drawing through your deck and burning through cheap spells while triggering {{IconLink|Etch}} over and over. By using either Sacrificial Resurrection or Gifts for a Guard, you can quickly whittle your deck down to a few self-replicating Consume cards to trigger {{IconLink|Etch}} consistently for the rest of the battle. [[Unearth Treasure]] upgraded with {{IconLink|Eternalstone}} and {{IconLink|Keepstone}} will provide two Consume cards every turn, as long as there are at least five cards in your Consume pile. Similarly, a [[Small Gift Box]] filled with Consume spells and given the aforementioned upgrades will provide three Consume cards each turn. In both cases, it's advisable to ensure that the Consume spells you will be replaying cost {{Ember|0}} or close to it, so as not to drain your {{Ember}} every turn. If you have [[Lightstone Casing]], adding {{IconLink|Seekstone}} to these cards will ensure you draw them in your opening hand. [[Madame Lionsmane]]'s '''Everbloom''' path also has an {{IconLink|Etch}} trigger. However, it's not usually advised to use these units together, mostly because '''Everbloom''' synergizes significantly better with Spore Launcher and thus '''Morel Mistress''' ends up superfluous.
