Prickly Puffball:
{{UnitCard |name = Prickly Puffball |image = PLR_PricklyPuffball.png |clan = Underlegion |rarity = Uncommon |type = Shroom |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 0/35 |ability = {{IconLink|Revenge}}: Apply {{IconLink|Decay|5}} to the attacker. |flavor = Although they do not possess much dangerous strength, they are hard to defeat as the Puffballs were born and raised in the burls of the Fatal Elm itself. |artist = Leonardo Dionisi }} '''Prickly Puffball''' is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] [[banner unit]]. It applies {{IconLink|Decay|5}} to the attacker on {{IconLink|Revenge}}. == Strategy == While '''Prickly Puffball''' may seem unassuming, it serves two main purposes, and fulfills both incredibly well. The first is to act as a backline-clearing tank, similar to [[Titan Sentry]]. Applying {{IconLink|Decay|5}} on {{IconLink|Revenge}} lets '''Prickly Puffball''' deal 15 damage to backline units immediately, and 36 by the time they reach the Pyre. If upgraded with {{IconLink|Dualism}}, that instead becomes 30 damage immediately and 81 by the time they reach the Pyre, which is more than enough to kill all backline enemies that have more than {{Attack|0}}. It also exacts a heavier punishment on enemies with {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, such as [[Ravenous Zealot]]s and [[Chosen Assassin]]s, by applying {{IconLink|Decay}} multiple times. The tradeoff as compared to Titan Sentry is that Titan Sentry applies {{IconLink|Frostbite}} to '''all''' units on {{IconLink|Revenge}}, allowing it to kill enemies that don't directly attack like [[Collector]]s and the Cherubs summoned by [[Cael]]. '''Prickly Puffball''' can suffer in this regard, as it is completely unable to stop dangerous support enemies like [[Vampiric Cherub]]s. The other purpose that '''Prickly Puffball''' serves is as an answer to boss fights. Similarly to how '''Prickly Puffball''' is more effective against enemies with {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, during {{IconLink|Relentless}}, the boss will accumulate more and more {{IconLink|Decay}} every time it attacks. If '''Prickly Puffball''' is able to endure the repeated attacks, such as through accumulating {{IconLink|Regen}} or defensive upgrades like {{IconLink|Titanite}}, the boss will often die to {{IconLink|Decay}} before it can get past the bottom floor, without any support from other units. [[Loamcoat]] is the best equipment for '''Prickly Puffball''', and is almost necessary for enabling it to solo bosses. When made '''[[Deployable]]''', Loamcoat will allow the unit to amass large amounts of {{IconLink|Regen}} before the boss spawns, and it will also provide a significant amount of extra {{Health}}. That gathered {{IconLink|Regen}} will keep '''Prickly Puffball''' healthy despite being attacked over and over, and will usually let it outlast the boss. This is especially effective when upgraded with {{IconLink|Dualism}}, as '''Prickly Puffball''' will gain {{IconLink|Regen|2}} on {{IconLink|Resolve}}, and thus will quickly hit a critical mass of {{IconLink|Regen}} where it outheals all the damage dealt to it. For better or worse, '''Prickly Puffball''' has little compatibility with other Underlegion strategies. It is hard to use in conjunction with [[Funguy]] as Funguy will enter the floor in front of it, preventing enemies from triggering its {{IconLink|Revenge}} unless you have an '''[[Advance]]''' card like [[Glow Up]]. Also, applying {{IconLink|Sap}} to enemies to reduce their damage to {{Attack|0}} through cards like [[Gooey Flask]] will prevent them from attacking '''Prickly Puffball''', again thwarting its {{IconLink|Revenge}} trigger. If you are already using {{IconLink|Rally}} strategies, '''Prickly Puffball''' can be somewhat awkward; conversely, if you are leaning more into your secondary clan's strategies, [[Prickly Puffball]]'s build-agnostic nature means it can still provide plenty of value, much more so than other Underlegion banner units. When playing with [[Banished]], {{IconLink|Valor}} is useful for '''Prickly Puffball''' as it provides a bit of defense every turn. When facing [[Seraph Aeternus-The Entropic]], '''Prickly Puffball''' is generally less effective. Unless you have a [[Zone of Silence]] or another way of killing them, the [[Deafening Herald]]s in that fight will afflict it with {{IconLink|Silence}}, preventing it from doing its job and allowing the waves to walk past unscathed. Against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]], the {{IconLink|Corruption}} accumulated will eventually kill '''Prickly Puffball''' no matter how much {{IconLink|Regen}} it has, so {{IconLink|Endless}} is a more desirable upgrade than it might otherwise be. Similarly, against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]], {{IconLink|Titanite}} is practically mandatory, as otherwise the extremely high damage of the waves alongside {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} will tear '''Prickly Puffball''' to shreds. A lone '''Prickly Puffball''' with {{IconLink|Dualism}} is notable in that fight for the fact that it applies enough {{IconLink|Decay}} to [[Chosen Assassin]]s to kill them, due to their {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! It applies {{IconLink|Decay|2}} to enemy units on {{IconLink|Rally}}. == Strategy == '''Spore Launcher''' turns a good {{IconLink|Rally}} engine into massive floorwide damage. With a solid amount of {{IconLink|Rally}} on the first floor, the {{IconLink|Decay}} applied will deal plenty of damage to all enemies before they reach the Pyre, easily wiping out backliners and in the right circumstances even taking chunks out of tanks. It deals solid damage early with just [[Eager Conscript]] and its decent stats, and can scale to the endgame quite well with the right setup. As with most Underlegion units, the main source of his {{IconLink|Rally}} trigger is [[Spawn]]ing [[Funguy]]. Its main difficulty is its {{Capacity|3}}, as the Underlegion don't have ways of overstacking floors, and it really wants a lot of company. It wants to have units that are able to [[Spawn]] [[Funguy]] with it, like [[Cluster Colonel]], [[Bolete the Guillotine]]'s '''Executioner''' or '''Headsman''' paths, [[Madame Lionsmane]]'s '''Everbloom''' path, or [[Green Recruit]]. Of course, [[Funguy]] will be on the floor whether you want him to be or not. And it would love to have more copies of itself on the floor to multiply the effect as well! As such, it pairs excellently with a way of overstacking floors, such as [[Hidden Passage]], [[Cave In]], and [[Rising Rage]], with [[Descend]] effects being slightly preferable because {{IconLink|Decay}} is more effective on the bottom floor. It also appreciates ways of increasing the floor's {{Capacity}}, though its {{Ember|2}} cost can make it hard to take a [[Heaven's Light]] over a [[Hell's Flame]], as you'll often want to play it and its companions during the [[Deployment Phase]]. It's an obvious candidate for [[Exile's Diadem]] as well. Note that if you are using this unit alongside Cluster Colonel to eliminate backline enemies on the bottom floor, due to the priorities of {{IconLink|Resolve}} and {{IconLink|Decay}}, those enemies will not actually die until after combat resolves on the middle floor. As such, if you are trying to keep dangerous backliners away from your main floor, you will need to set up on the top floor or have alternate methods of triggering {{IconLink|Rally}} before the end of the turn, and you will still be affected by [[Scourge]] enemies on the bottom floor like [[Profane Supplicant]]. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! Get those gills in gear and fight!" |artist = Daniel Sarmiento Chuquisengo }} '''Squad Leader''' is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] [[banner unit]]. It buffs the {{Attack}} of the floor's [[Funguy]] and adds {{IconLink|Trample}}. == Strategy == '''Squad Leader''' increases the base {{Attack}} of Funguy by 67%. This is a noticeable damage boost, especially in the early game. But outside of decks that can create truly enormous Funguy stacks, it is very difficult to get enough {{Attack}} for Funguy to clear waves on its own. Multiple '''Squad Leaders''' will stack with each other, boosting Funguy's {{Attack}} even further, as will the [[Spotted Spore]] artifact; however, the returns are diminishing, especially because the {{IconLink|Trample}} effect cannot stack. At a certain point, it is better to fill out the floor with more [[Spawn]] sources like [[Cluster Colonel]], or units that benefit from {{IconLink|Rally}} like [[Spore Launcher]]. If relying on Funguy's {{Attack}}, consider using [[Glow Up]] or another positioning spell to move Funguy behind a dedicated tank so that it doesn't lose {{Attack}} from simply being hit. [[Loamcoat]] can also mitigate this, as can [[Amorous Enoki]], since her {{Health}} increase on {{IconLink|Rally}} will give Funguy "buffer" {{Health}} that will be lost to damage before {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks. For example, with {{IconLink|Troop|4}}, Funguy will have {{Health|20}} instead of {{Health|16}}, which means it can take 7 damage instead of 3 before losing a {{IconLink|Troop}} stack. Additionally, equipment is tremendously useful for turning Funguy into a proper offensive unit, as it cannot be upgraded at the [[Merchant of Steel]]. In particular, any source of {{IconLink|Multistrike}} is extremely important. [[Void Armament]] should be prioritized; its {{IconLink|Extinguish}} effect is irrelevant, since Funguy is not in your deck anyway. However, the [[Deployable]] upgrade does not help, since you cannot generate Funguy during the [[Deployment Phase]]. [[Weapons Cache]] is a better method in this case, since you will draw out your equipment on Spawning, and also reduce its {{Ember}} cost. [[Swiftsteel Dagger]] is a solid [[Merged Equipment|Merge]], granting {{IconLink|Quick}}, and so is [[Stoic Platemail]], since Funguy doesn't have any triggers. The {{IconLink|Trample}} effect is significant in the early game, but falls off once units like [[Avowed Gladiator]] begin to spawn in the front of the floor. {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} has a very strong interaction with the {{IconLink|Trample}} '''Squad Leader''' provides, as the multiplied damage will spill out to demolish the backline. This is mostly accessible through the [[Banished]], but [[Railbeater]] and the {{IconLink|Dominating Control}} upgrade can also provide it. '''Squad Leader''' is, obviously, quite useless without the ability to [[Spawn]]. This can make it a difficult start if it happens to be your starting banner unit, in particular if you have [[Sporetouch]] rather than [[Eager Conscript]]. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! {{UnitCard |name = Balmabello |image = PLR_Balmabello.png |clan = Underlegion |rarity = Rare |type = Shroom |banner = Yes |cost = 3 |size = 2 |stats = 15/50 |ability = {{IconLink|Regen|6}}. {{IconLink|Spikes|6}}.
{{IconLink|Extinguish}}: Apply this unit's '''[[Buff]]''' stacks to friendly units. |flavor = "On victory, you deserve a glass of my special Spore-brew. Upon defeat, you'll need it." |artist = Taylor Bray }} '''Balmabello''' is a rare [[Underlegion]] [[banner unit]]. It starts with {{IconLink|Regen|6}} and {{IconLink|Spikes|6}}, and when it dies, all of its [[Buff]] stacks are applied all friendly units on the floor. == Strategy == '''Balmabello''' is an extremely powerful unit despite its {{Ember|3}} cost, capable of scaling your entire floor. It functions similarly to '''Superfood''' [[Primordium]]; although Primordium passes on its effects multiple times and passes on status effects like {{IconLink|Multistrike}} that '''Balmabello''' does not, '''Balmabello''' has the advantage of applying its effects to all other units on the floor. Underlegion's '''[[Propagate]]''' allows it to amplify its buffs before eventually passing them on. The biggest hurdle to [[Balmabello]]'s use besides its cost is that, with {{Health|50}} and {{IconLink|Regen|6}}, it can be difficult to actually kill it off and thus activate its {{IconLink|Extinguish}} trigger. Particularly in the early Rings, you may need to target it with your own damaging spells like [[Sporetouch]] in order for it to die in a timely manner. [[Rot]] is a guaranteed kill if you can afford spending {{Ember|3}} to kill your own unit. Thankfully, it does not pass on [[Debuff]] effects, so there's little risk in doing this. It can also be fine to use it as an attacking unit in its own right initially. [[Balmabello]]'s two most synergistic clans are the [[Lazarus League]] and the [[Melting Remnant]]. Both clans have the ability to make repeated use out of [[Balmabello]]'s {{IconLink|Extinguish}}, which allows the unit to get out of control quickly, passing on obscene amounts of buffs to its allies. '''Balmabello''' is incredibly powerful with the {{IconLink|Reanimate}} that the [[Lazarus League]] can apply. Multiple '''Balmabellos''' on a floor can pass {{IconLink|Reanimate}} back and forth to each other repeatedly, and can quickly become invincible. Furthermore, '''[[Mix]]''' cards like [[Secret Ingredient]] provide a wide variety of buffs for '''Balmabello''' to take advantage of. Lazarus League also has cards with '''[[Sacrifice]]''', such as [[Scrap for Parts]] and [[Brain Transfer]], which allow you to kill '''Balmabello''' at will, rather than waiting for it to die. Meanwhile, the Melting Remnant has several distinct synergies of its own. '''Balmabello''' interacts with [[Intent on Death]] to trigger {{IconLink|Extinguish}} without actually killing the unit, and the [[Waxer Snuffer]] Artifact causes its {{IconLink|Extinguish}} ability to trigger twice. Applying {{IconLink|Stealth}} to '''Balmabello''' can protect your whole floor, as long as you have a way to kill it while it has {{IconLink|Stealth}}, though note that this anti-synergizes with the {{IconLink|Spikes}} it naturally applies. {{IconLink|Burnout}} is useful as another method of ensuring '''Balmabello''' dies, but be aware that it can be '''[[Propagate]]d''', thus prolonging [[Balmabello]]'s death. Once '''Balmabello''' finally dies, '''[[Reform]]''' cards like [[Molded]] can bring it back, while also making it free. The [[Hellhorned]], [[Banished]], and [[Luna Coven]] clans can all make good use of '''Balmabello''' as well, even if they can't trigger {{IconLink|Extinguish}} multiple times. These clans use '''Balmabello''' to provide their entire floor with {{IconLink|Rage}}, {{IconLink|Valor}}, and {{IconLink|Conduit}}, respectively. The [[Pyreborne]] can pass on {{IconLink|Avarice}} with '''Balmabello''' for extreme amounts of {{Gold}}. Lastly, though difficult to pull off, the [[Umbra]] clan can use '''Balmabello''' to pass on {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} by sacrificing it with [[Cannibalize]] or [[Glutton's Maw]]. {{IconLink|Reanimate}} can also be obtained through the [[Inscryption]] event. Should you find this event, it is almost always worth pursuing its follow-up, as both {{IconLink|Many Lives}} and {{IconLink|Worthy Sacrifice}} are hugely impactful upgrades for '''Balmabello''' and can easily break the game. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! Enchantrelle:
{{UnitCard |name = Enchantrelle |image = PLR_Enchantrelle.png |clan = Underlegion |rarity = Rare |type = Shroom |banner = Yes |cost = 3 |size = 2 |stats = 8/8 |ability = {{IconLink|Rally}}: Apply {{IconLink|Sap|1}} to enemy units. |flavor = "I know a mushroom has fallen in love with me when they fear to sleep. My lovely spores give them nightmares of their heart's greatest fear: being away from me." |artist = Hung Bui }} '''Enchantrelle''' is a rare [[Underlegion]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever a friendly unit is summoned on her floor, she applies {{IconLink|Sap|1}} to all enemy units. == Strategy == '''Enchantrelle''' is one of the strongest defensive units in the game, capable of shutting down enemy attacks entirely with a strong enough {{IconLink|Rally}} build. If you are able to summon [[Funguy|Funguys]] consistently, enemies will simply be unable to attack, allowing the rest of your deck to focus on dealing damage. Combined with a strong {{IconLink|Rally}} deck and a [[Spore Launcher]] for damage output, she can carry virtually the entire game on her own. With {{IconLink|Dualism}} and a very strong {{IconLink|Rally}} deck, it is even viable to ignore damage output entirely, simply applying so much {{IconLink|Sap}} that enemies will walk up to your Pyre and remain at {{Attack|0}} until they are killed. However, this is generally not an effective strategy against bosses, so you will need a way to take them down. Of course, summoning Funguys over the course of the battle means that you will usually have a Funguy stack capable of easily killing a heavily {{IconLink|Sap}}ped boss by the time they appear. You will need a different strategy against the [[Clash with the Titans|Titans]], however. [[Dominion]] will attack your Pyre multiple times in a row if enemy waves reach it, which can quickly whittle you down, and even if you apply {{IconLink|Sap}} to him with cards like [[Pandemic]], the multiple rounds it takes for the Pyre to kill enemies will cause it to run dry quite fast. Furthermore, [[Savagery]] and [[Entropy]] can still damage your Pyre even while {{IconLink|Sap}}ped to {{Attack|0}} (through their {{IconLink|Resolve}} effect on empty floors and [[Curse of Entropy]], respectively) and will never enter the Pyre room. For this reason, a few copies of [[Deadly Variant]] are highly valuable when running '''Enchantrelle''', to convert {{IconLink|Sap}} into {{IconLink|Decay}} and ensure these bosses die before you run out of {{PyreHealth}}. If you do not see Deadly Variant, consider upgrading some expensive cards with {{IconLink|Holystone}} instead. '''Enchantrelle''' can be difficult to use due to her high cost at {{Ember|3}}, which makes it impossible to play her and a [[Spore Launcher]] during Deployment without extra {{DeploymentEmber}}. [[Herzal's Horde]], [[Artificial Pyrestone]], [[Volatile Gauge]] or [[Ancient Pyretap]] can help with this. Note that simply playing one of these units later in the battle is generally impractical unless you have either '''[[Ascend]]''' or '''[[Descend]]''' effects or more {{Capacity}} than you need, as Funguys will take up a space once you begin to summon them. Note that '''Enchantrelle''' does not work as well with [[Cluster Colonel]] as other {{IconLink|Rally}} units do, as this combo will {{IconLink|Sap}} enemies only ''after'' they attack. She also does nothing against the {{IconLink|Corruption}} effects of [[Qel the Corruptor]] or [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]], which will quickly wipe out the entire floor. Qel is especially deadly, as many {{IconLink|Rally}} builds rely on playing spells. In these cases [[Amorous Enoki]] can provide enough {{Health}} and {{IconLink|Regen}} to make up for the {{IconLink|Corruption}}. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! It [[Propagate]]s 2 on the floor it's cast on. == Strategy == '''Proliferate''' is an incredibly easy card to draft, as it just about always finds a way to be useful in any loadout. The more different kinds of [[Buffs]] you can apply to your units, and [[Debuffs]] you can consistently and widely apply to enemies, the better this spell becomes. It's also an easy way to trigger {{IconLink|Etch}}. The Underlegion natively has access to {{IconLink|Regen}} and {{IconLink|Troop}} as buffs, and {{IconLink|Decay}} and {{IconLink|Sap}} as debuffs, both of which they love distributing on enemies. There are so many powerful buffs and debuffs that other clans apply that '''Proliferate''' hits, and the more of them you can add (and the more widely you can apply them), the better this card gets. It also means that what this card does widely varies depending on your other clan, but it's strong regardless of your partner clan. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Upgrade !! It deals 15 damage and applies {{IconLink|Decay|15}} to a target. ==Strategy== '''Rot''' can ruin just about any enemy's day - it can kill most backliners instantly, and is eventually a death sentence for just about every non-boss enemy before Ring 7 if applied on the first floor. Bosses, meanwhile, will suffer significant damage per turn. If you can stall out the {{IconLink|Decay}} it inflicts but don't inflict further {{IconLink|Decay}}, it will deal 375 total damage to bosses, fatal for Ring 1 bosses and able to leave a significant dent well after that. It gets better if you can [[Propagate]] it and add further {{IconLink|Decay}} in other ways. Notably, it deals 60 damage total on the turn it is cast, which is sufficient to kill [[Chosen Assassin]]s before they can get to your other units even if they spawn with a [[Harpist Protector]]. The issue with this card, of course, is its {{Ember}} cost of 3 - making it difficult to use as a consistent answer to bulky wave enemies. It also needs to be present at the right time in order to counter non-Flying [[Bosses]], as it's less good if your tanky units are no longer there to stall them out. Upgrades can address these issues, as can [[Hell's Flame]]. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! It applies {{IconLink|Sap}} and {{IconLink|Decay}}, and although it [[Consume]]s, it also puts a copy of itself in the discard pile when played, letting you draw it again. == Interactions == * If upgraded with {{IconLink|Twinstone}}, it will create two copies of itself in the discard pile. The second copy will work the same as normal and will not have '''[[Ephemeral]]''', but will not have '''[[Spellchain]]''' either. == Strategy == '''Pandemic''' is an excellent card that can fit into almost any deck and should virtually never be skipped. At minimum, it can greatly weaken a single important enemy whenever it's drawn; at best, it can be the cornerstone of a [[Consume]]-based strategy. The most obvious approach is to use it alongside [[Morel Mistress]] or [[Madame Lionsmane]]'s '''Everbloom''' path, as both of these units have {{IconLink|Etch}} triggers that activate when a card is Consumed. Usually these triggers are self-limiting, since you will eventually run out of cards with Consume, but '''Pandemic''' (as well as [[Contagious]]) will ensure that these builds never run out of fuel. Getting as many copies of the card as possible is ideal for this - the [[Twin Minds]] artifact is a great way to do so, but [[Empyrean Well]]s and [[Lifemother's Pyre]] are choice options as well. You will usually want to reduce '''Pandemic''''s cost before duplicating it, as its {{Ember|2}} cost is its main downside. {{IconLink|Emberstone}} is the basic and cheap way to do so, but {{IconLink|Freezestone}} and {{IconLink|Seekstone}} have the same effect and also provide some other benefits. {{IconLink|Smolderstone}} is only compatible with '''Pandemic''' if it has already been upgraded with {{IconLink|Eternalstone}}, which may not be optimal for every strategy. For example, it prevents the use of {{IconLink|Etch}} strategies, and since the copies it creates are not destroyed when played they can rapidly fill up your deck. If you do not care about {{IconLink|Etch}}, this may be a positive, since '''Pandemic''' is a fairly powerful card with which to flood your deck, especially at {{Ember|0}}. [[The Great Decay]] is an incredible synergy for it, especially with {{IconLink|Etch}} decks. Applying Consume to all other spells (except ones with {{IconLink|Eternalstone}}) means you will rapidly thin your deck down to just '''Pandemic''' and a few other cards, and cards that do not normally Consume like [[Sporetouch]] will trigger {{IconLink|Etch}} as well. It will also fill up your Consume pile with copies of itself, which is great for cards like [[Fertile Ground]] and [[Unearth Treasure]] that rely on the size of your Consume pile. This card is excellent in [[Clash with the Titans]]. The {{IconLink|Sap}} it applies will reduce [[Dominion]]'s {{Attack}} to 0 for at least one turn, and for longer if you have upgrades like {{IconLink|Stackstone}} or you can [[Propagate]] it, while the {{IconLink|Decay}} will speed up his demise. Additionally, {{IconLink|Sap}} prevents his damage, but still allows him to give you [[Pyre Light]], unlike {{IconLink|Dazed}}. Since Dominion is frequently the bottleneck in that combat, anything that can minimize his effects or kill him faster is tremendously impactful. Its {{IconLink|Sap}} application can also rein in [[Savagery]]'s ramping damage. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! The second copy will work the same as normal and will not have '''[[Ephemeral]]''', but will not have '''[[Spellchain]]''' either. == Strategy == '''Contagious''' is one of two Underlegion spells that reproduces when played despite having [[Consume]], the other being [[Pandemic]]. The latter tends to be more useful on its own, but depending on your build composition both can be very strong, and they work extremely well in tandem. Since it affects all enemy units, it is best used alongside [[Debuff]]s that are hard to apply in great amounts. Within the Underlegion, {{IconLink|Sap}} is the most prominent option. Any unit that has at least {{IconLink|Sap|1}} will immediately lose an additional {{Attack|8}}, rendering most enemies harmless and removing a lot of damage from bosses. It is also decent when Propagating small amounts of {{IconLink|Decay}}, adding an immediate 12 damage and lengthening its duration. This is why the card works quite well with Pandemic, bringing it from {{IconLink|Decay|8}} and {{IconLink|Sap|2}} to {{IconLink|Decay|12}} and {{IconLink|Sap|6}}. Depending on your secondary clan, it can get even better. The [[Stygian Guard]] can use it to Propagate {{IconLink|Mute}}, to shut down bosses for the entire fight, or {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}}, to set up extremely powerful attacks. They can also supplement {{IconLink|Sap}} application. The [[Banished]] can Propagate {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} - playing [[Challenge]] followed by '''Contagious''' results in {{IconLink|Melee Weakness|5}}, making the first unit attack against that enemy deal a whopping six times as much damage. The [[Pyreborne]] can Propagate {{IconLink|Pyregel}}, which does not decrease over time, so every use of this spell permanently increases all damage against the afflicted units by 4. Since it is a replayable [[Consume]] card, it synergizes with the {{IconLink|Etch}} triggers of [[Morel Mistress]] and '''Everbloom''' [[Madame Lionsmane]], ensuring you will never run out of ways to trigger {{IconLink|Etch}}. It is also a good card to replay in general, especially with {{IconLink|Sap}}, as you can rapidly run enemy {{Attack}} into the ground and leave them with so much {{IconLink|Sap}} that they will never be able to attack again. [[The Great Decay]] reduces its cost, and it already has Consume, so it has no downside. It is one of the most efficient ways to improve the effects of fellow rare cards [[Wracking Pain]] and [[Deadly Variant]]. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! This can help save {{PyreHealth}} against bosses like [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]] (from [[Terrifying Amalgam]]) and [[Cael, Lord of the Cherubs]] '''Nourishing Feed''' variant (from {{IconLink|Spikes}}). So on an uninjured and unbuffed Funguy, '''Funguy in a Suit''' essentially applies its current {{Health}} as {{IconLink|Armor}}, and then adds another {{Health|12}} and {{Armor|12}}. == Strategy == Although this spell does Spawn 3, it is generally a poor choice for triggering {{IconLink|Rally}} or building up a Funguy stack, as it is no more efficient at producing Funguy than [[Eager Conscript]] on a per-{{Ember}} basis. Rather, this card should be used when you are relying on a big Funguy stack for tanking and damage output. Due to the mechanics of {{IconLink|Troop}}, when Funguy is damaged, its {{Attack}} is lowered as well. A Funguy at the front of the floor will continually lose damage as enemies attack it, which is a problem if you are using [[Squad Leader]] or [[Spotted Spore]] to turn Funguy into your primary attacker. '''Funguy in a Suit''' solves this problem by applying a tremendous amount of {{IconLink|Armor}} to a large Funguy stack. Losing {{IconLink|Armor}} will '''not''' decrease {{IconLink|Troop}}, which means your Funguy will not lose out on damage just from enemies attacking it until all of its {{IconLink|Armor}} has been depleted. You will generally want to have as much {{IconLink|Troop}} as possible before casting this spell, especially if you only have one copy. It applies [[Consume]] and {{Ember|-1}} to all spells in your deck. == Strategy == '''The Great Decay''' is an immensely powerful spell, clearing out virtually all of the spells in your deck and allowing you to draw the same cards over and over. All starter cards will cost {{Ember|0}} and consume when played, allowing you to freely remove them in the first shuffle. The only cards which will not be destroyed are those with {{IconLink|Eternalstone}}, allowing you to put this upgrade on one or a few particularly strong spells, then play those spells over and over once the rest of your deck is gone. The {{Ember|-1}} will still be applied, making them easier to play. Keep in mind that a few other cards will also remain, even without {{IconLink|Eternalstone}}. {{IconLink|Endless}} units will be unaffected, and spells like [[Pandemic]], which already consume and duplicate themselves, have a kind of pseudo-Eternalstone built in. At higher Covenants, you will also need to deal with [[Vengeful Shard]]s constantly. This can be even more powerful with the '''Everbloom''' path on [[Madame Lionsmane]], who will spawn a massive stack of [[Funguy]]s in the process of consuming your deck. [[Morel Mistress]] can also easily wipe out waves of enemies, though you will need another way to finish later waves off once you run out of Consume cards. If your spells are very expensive, it may be worth acquiring two or more copies of this card, as there's no disadvantage once your spells already have Consume. Remember you don't have to play every spell you draw just to use all your {{Ember}} every turn. If all your spells now have Consume, when you play them becomes more important. Sometimes it's a better strategic move to hold back and wait for a future turn when you can get the maximum value out of your spell. It deals damage equal to 3x the total stacks of debuffs on the target. ==Strategy== '''Wracking Pain''' is a potentially powerful single-target spell. In the context of the [[Underlegion]], however, it can sometimes feel like it's hitting enemies that are already crippled to the point of not being a threat. With Underlegion cards, you will most frequently be applying {{IconLink|Decay}}, so this essentially allows you to deal the same amount of damage that {{IconLink|Decay}} will deal at end of turn again. Other effects like {{IconLink|Sap}} can add more damage, but they tend to be applied in smaller quantities, and if you have a lot of {{IconLink|Sap}} on an enemy, it probably isn't a threat anyway. It can hasten the demise of a Flying Boss that's already been debilitated to end the encounter sooner, potentially saving damage against waves. With that being said, '''Wracking Pain''' is still useful even with just the Underlegion in the lategame, where enemies like [[Avowed Gladiator]] loom. In a build where you can passively apply large amounts of debuffs to all enemies, such as with [[Cluster Colonel]] and [[Spore Launcher]], it can help finish tanky enemies off. Against the Titans, if your strategy consists of applying enormous amounts of {{IconLink|Sap}} and letting the Pyre kill enemies, you will often have a hard time killing [[Savagery]] and [[Entropy]] quickly, and it's even possible that you will slowly die to Savagery's {{IconLink|Resolve}} effect. '''Wracking Pain''' can be very useful in this case, finishing them off relatively easily. This spell can be much more powerful if your allied clan also allows you to apply debuffs, particularly those that are applied in large numbers. Examples include {{IconLink|Pyregel}}, {{IconLink|Frostbite}}, and {{IconLink|Unstable}}, which can be stacked in large quantities very easily. {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} also pairs excellently with this, both adding to its base damage and then multiplying it. '''Loamcoat''' is a common [[Underlegion]] equipment. It grants its wearer {{Health|+20}} and gives it a {{IconLink|Resolve}} trigger that first gives it {{IconLink|Regen|1}}, then '''[[Propagate]]s 2''', increasing all of its buff stacks, including {{IconLink|Regen}}, by 2.

== Notes ==

The timing of Loamcoat's effects works out such that on the turn it is equipped, the unit gets {{IconLink|Regen|3}} but regenerates no health yet. Then on subsequent turns, Regen restores health and ticks down once, then ticks up thrice, for an overall progression of Regen 3, Regen 5, etc., with restored health from these Regen values offset by one turn respectively.

== Strategy ==

'''Loamcoat''' combines defensive utility with lategame potential if you can give the equipped unit powerful buffs for it to [[Propagate]].

A very natural candidate for this equipment is [[Funguy]]. '''Loamcoat''' lets them lose {{Health|20}} without losing [[Troop]] (see [[Funguy]] for more). And the {{IconLink|Regen}} this provides helps keep that buffer intact. Finally, this will cause [[Funguy]] to gain 2 {{IconLink|Troop}} as well, growing their stats and triggering any {{IconLink|Rally}} triggers on the floor twice. If your allied clan can provide other buffs like {{IconLink|Rage}}, {{IconLink|Spikes}}, or {{IconLink|Conduit}}, those can also get a steady boost this way.

If you have a way of giving a unit at least 2 stacks of {{IconLink|Stealth}}, this can be used to keep them in {{IconLink|Stealth}} indefinitely, with some extra stacks to spare for {{IconLink|Relentless}}. It can also keep a {{IconLink|Burnout}} unit alive indefinitely.

Its {{Ember|2}} cost makes it difficult to merge and play, though with [[Attuned Whetstone]] it can be merged with just about anything if it's intended to be drawn that way. Keep in mind you usually can't equip [[Funguy]] during the [[Deployment Phase]] - this usually doesn't matter much in practice however, as the merged equipment will just be shuffled back into your deck after the [[Deployment Phase]], and the cost reduction will persist for the entire combat.

Mitosis Cap:
{{EquipmentCard		
|name = Mitosis Cap
|image = CRD_MitosisCap.png

|flavor = Death is an opportunity to make a new, better version of yourself. This is a lesson many have known for as long as the roots of the Fatal Elm are deep.
|artist = Herrick Ong
}}	

'''Mitosis Cap''' is a rare [[Underlegion]] equipment. Each time a unit equipped with '''Mitosis Cap''' survives a battle, the {{IconLink|Celebrate}} trigger adds a permanent copy of that unit to the deck.

== Notes ==

* The {{IconLink|Celebrate}} ability lets you permanently add [[Morsels]] to your deck, being the only way to do so in the game.
* Funguy are {{IconLink|Cardless}} units, and so are not eligible. This also prevents them from being equipped a merged equipment which Mitosis Cap is part of.
* Mitosis cap can be attached to an egg before hatching.  The cap will propagate to the hatched unit.  Celebrate will give a copy of the egg--not the hatched unit.
* If the {{IconLink|Red Crown}} is applied to [[Legion of Wax]], Twin of Wax and Mote of Wax can randomly obtain '''Mitosis Cap''' despite being {{IconLink|Cardless}}. It won't give you permanent copies of those units.

== Strategy ==

'''Mitosis Cap''' can be an incredible source of economy for your run, potentially giving you a free [[Empyrean Well]] every combat. It's also a cheap way of increasing the durability of a unit, and is very easy to merge with other equipment and make [[Deployable]] thanks to costing {{Ember|0}}.

The logistically difficult part of this is finding a unit that's worth duplicating. Each unit costs {{Ember}} and {{Capacity}}, and playing them during deployment costs {{Icon|DeploymentEmber}}, which are finite resources. If you generate copies you can't play, you're simply gumming up your deck, assuming the {{IconLink|Celebrate}} ability triggers.

But this equipment's utility means you should look for ways you can benefit from it.
* While the [[Underlegion]] doesn't have native ways to overstack floors, if your partner clan does, this can provide you with extra bodies on your kill floor. 
* If you have a unit with a {{IconLink|Smidgestone}} applied, you can use this to create more copies, and then take [[Heaven's Light]] to have space for them.
* If you have a 1-floor setup that doesn't require spell support to work, you can use this to duplicate your setup on multiple floors; if your setup '''does''' require spell support, this may not be worth doing, as you'd rather focus on supporting your existing setup.

It is possible to equip this to a unit and then intentionally '''not''' trigger the {{IconLink|Celebrate}} ability: 
* You could equip it that's simply designed to disrupt enemy waves and then die to the boss, or you can [[Sacrifice]] them come the end of combat.
* You could merge this with [[Stoic Platemail]] for a cheap equipment that gives excellent durability, but keep in mind '''Mitosis Cap''''s restriction on {{IconLink|Cardless}} units will prevent you from applying this to e.g. [[Funguy]].

==Trivia==
* Works on [[Champions]] with the Hivemind [[Mutator]].

'''Grow Room''' is an uncommon [[Underlegion]] room. It makes all units, including enemies and friendly units, '''[[Propagate]] 1''' at the end of combat each turn.

== Strategy ==
The '''Grow Room''' is one of the most universally useful rooms in the game, providing a small but noticeable boost to all buffs and debuffs you are able to apply. By default, it will Spawn one Funguy (assuming that a Funguy is already present), and the more status effects you are able to apply, the more effective it is. Powerful effects like {{IconLink|Sap}} and {{IconLink|Reanimate}} are especially good targets.

If allied with the [[Melting Remnant]], this room will Propagate {{IconLink|Burnout}} every turn, keeping {{IconLink|Burnout}} units alive until the {{IconLink|Relentless}} phase.

If an enemy has {{IconLink|Rooted}} applied to it in a '''Grow Room''', it will remain in place until the boss arrives.

Note that if you are using the [[Shadow's Sheath]] artifact, the {{IconLink|Stealth|1}} will wear off '''before''' being Propagated, so this is not a sufficient solution for perpetual {{IconLink|Stealth}} unless you have at least one other room-wide Propagate card like [[Proliferate]] that you can cast on the first turn (or an artifact like [[Shroomponics]]), or if your units can get a {{IconLink|Slay}} trigger to get an additional stack of {{IconLink|Stealth}}.

'''Infectory''' is a common [[Underlegion]] room. It spawns a [[Funguy]] whenever any non-Funguy unit is killed.

== Strategy ==
'''Infectory''' is an easy and powerful way to stack up Funguys quickly and power {{IconLink|Rally}} builds. If you have a single kill floor on which most enemies will die, then this room can produce a Funguy for every enemy that enters, triggering {{IconLink|Rally}} as it does so. It also produces Funguys when your own units are killed, though this is generally less useful unless you have {{IconLink|Reanimate}}.

Later in the run, it falls off somewhat, as a single Funguy per enemy death is not enormously impactful in later rings. It can still be useful, but other rooms may be better.

'''Lazarus League''' [[File:ClanLazarusLeague.png|20x20px]] is a [[clan]] in [[Monster Train 2]].

Lazarus League features the following mechanics:
* {{IconLink|Reanimate}} is a common defensive buff that allows units to repeatedly die.
* {{IconLink|Unstable}} is a common offensive debuff that deals area-of-effect damage and synergizes with {{IconLink|Reanimate}}.
* Other common buffs employed by the clan include {{IconLink|Spikes}} and {{IconLink|Lifesteal}}.
* Several cards use the '''[[Mix]]''' keyword which can create unique spell cards with a large variety of effects.
* Many mechanics incentivize heavy use of [[Equipment]].
* {{IconLink|Graft}} units carry powerful equipment that can be used once the units are sacrificed.

The clan's unique [[Merchant of Steel]] Upgrade is {{IconLink|Frankenstone}}.

Orechi:
{{UnitCard |name = Orechi |image = PLR_Orechi.png |clan = [[Lazarus League]] |rarity = Champion |type = Champion |banner = No |cost = 0 |size = 2 |stats = 0/5 |flavor = Fired from academia, Dr. Orechi returned to his family's estate in Trans-HELL-vania and set up a private laboratory. No one in Hell quite knows what he does, but many know not to set foot inside. |artist = Luke Banke }} '''Orechi''' is the primary [[Champion]] of the [[Lazarus League]] clan. Fittingly for his mad doctor persona, his paths vary wildly in effect, from turning into a living bomb to brewing infusions to help his team. His starter card is [[Secret Ingredient]]. == Light Forge Upgrades == {{ChampionPaths |baseStats=0/5 |a=Brewmaster |a1stats=20/20 |a1abilities={{AbilityBox|Small Concoction|3|'''[[Mix]]'''.}} |a2stats=45/35 |a2abilities={{AbilityBox|Medium Concoction|3|'''[[Mix]]''' twice.}} |a3stats=75/40 |a3abilities={{AbilityBox|Huge Concoction|3|'''[[Mix]]''' three times.}} |b=Reanimator |b1stats=15/6 |b1abilities={{IconLink|Resolve}}: Gain {{IconLink|Reanimate|1}} and {{IconLink|Unstable|6}}. |b2stats=20/12 |b2abilities={{IconLink|Reanimate|1}}.
{{IconLink|Resolve}}: Gain {{IconLink|Reanimate|1}} and {{IconLink|Unstable|12}}. |b3stats=20/16 |b3abilities={{IconLink|Reanimate|2}}.
{{IconLink|Resolve}}: Gain {{IconLink|Reanimate|1}} and {{IconLink|Unstable|18}}. |c=Mad Scientist |c1stats=15/25 |c1abilities={{IconLink|Incant}}: Apply {{IconLink|Unstable|4}} to enemy units. |c2stats=15/45 |c2abilities={{IconLink|Incant}}: Apply {{IconLink|Unstable|8}} to enemy units. |c3stats=15/70 |c3abilities={{IconLink|Incant}}: Apply {{IconLink|Unstable|16}} to enemy units. }} == Strategy == [[Orechi]]'s paths each require a different method of investment, and as such it is generally best to go all in on one strategy. '''Brewmaster''' is the simplest path, as your only worry is which infusions to generate with his ability. '''Reanimator''' is his most out-of-the-box path, turning him into a living bomb so long as you can apply enough {{IconLink|Unstable}} and {{IconLink|Reanimate}}. '''Mad Scientist''' is his most straightfoward path, giving him an easier offensive choice if you focus on filling your deck with useful spells. === Brewmaster === This is [[Orechi]]'s simplest path, but can be somewhat underwhelming without synergies, only providing support every 3 turns. While infusions are strong spells, you are faced with an important question when considering '''Brewmaster Orechi''': do I need my infusions to be stronger, and can '''Orechi''' afford to miss out on his other abilities for that? '''Brewmaster Orechi''' will not be your main unit in your run unless mixed with the other paths, often hiding in the top floor behind a tanky unit. His {{Attack}} and {{Health}} are respectable and make him more effective as a stat stick than his other paths, but at higher covenants it is usually not worth taking this path just for stats. His ability will make it easier for you to provide the necessary support to your other units, while sometimes helping his other paths by providing {{IconLink|Unstable}} or {{IconLink|Reanimate}}. As such, using this path is accepting [[Orechi]]'s role as a support unit. Choose it if you have strong units who can solo waves given the help from [[Orechi]]'s infusions. [[Secret Ingredient]], [[Mixology]], [[Mix-a-Lot]], and [[Potion Kit]] contribute greatly to this methodology. Having [[Pyreborne]] as the allied clan is also helpful due to their ability to reduce cooldowns with cards like [[Tome of Contracts]]. '''Medium Concoction''' and '''Huge Concoction''' do not allow you to change infusion types between mixes. As such, it is best to use a card like Secret Ingredient first to get your desired infusion type before activating his ability. [[Inga's Beaker]] is a huge boost to this path's consistency and should almost always be taken if offered. [[Hall of Mirrors]] is excellent with this path. At max level, you can mix six times on the first turn, which is a tremendous boon if you are relying on infusions to get your damage or {{IconLink|Reanimate}} engine online. Just be sure to have some way of protecting him against flying bosses and the [[Titans]], like a {{IconLink|Smidgestone}} tank or [[Spike of the League]]. === Reanimator === This is [[Orechi]]'s weirdest and most out of the box path. Novices might be confused on why you would want to apply {{IconLink|Unstable}} to your own unit. Just remember that {{IconLink|Unstable}} always deals damage to the enemy units, even if applied on friendly units. {{IconLink|Unstable}} also does not go away after exploding if the unit has {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, meaning that {{IconLink|Unstable}} stacks can reach the hundreds. '''Reanimator Orechi''' will need to be heavily protected, as he will constantly be down to {{Health|1}} and {{IconLink|Reanimate|1}}, and any accidental damage will end your run. Using this path is a constant struggle between having enough survivability and scaling '''Orechi''' enough that his {{IconLink|Unstable}} does massive damage to waves. [[Life Insurer]], [[Spike of the League]], [[Spike of the Legion]] (Legion is better than League for '''Reanimator Orechi''' as he is guaranteed to have the {{IconLink|Reanimate}} buff for '''[[Propagate]]''', giving {{IconLink|Reanimate|2}} per {{Ember}} as opposed to 1) and [[Forevermore Serum]] help with survivability, while [[Explosive Reaction]] and [[Tome of Horrors]] help with applying {{IconLink|Unstable}}. A strong frontliner like [[Hulking Mass]] is useful in order to protect him. He works best when left alone and protected on the third floor, but can be made to work on the first or second floors. In any case, you'll still need a reliably powerful floor elsewhere, either to kill stragglers on the late floors, or to soften up tanky enemies for '''Orechi''' to explode later. Though effective at taking down waves, '''Orechi''' can struggle during the {{IconLink|Relentless}} phase, as without support he will only damage the boss once before dying. Stacking {{IconLink|Reanimate}} can allow him to survive long enough to finish the battle. [[Tome of Horrors]] is an ideal card for this path, providing an immediate boost to both damage and survivability. Keep in mind that sometimes you will have to blow up '''Orechi''' with a spell yourself in order to kill a wave. Do not be afraid of losing one or two stacks of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} on him if you can replenish it later. [[Nefarious Overflow]] is incredibly powerful when using this path, doubling [[Orechi]]'s damage output. Always take it if possible. In [[Limbo]], it is generally worth checking [[Herzal's Hoard]] before choosing [[Orechi]]'s path, since if you happen to be offered Nefarious Overflow, you should always take either '''Reanimator''' or '''Mad Scientist'''. When partnered with the [[Underlegion]], his {{IconLink|Reanimate}} can be '''[[Propagate]]d''' by effects like [[Shroomponics]] and [[Grow Room]], so feeding him {{IconLink|Reanimate}} manually is much less necessary. Equipping him with {{IconLink|Loamcoat}} can let him reliably increase his {{IconLink|Reanimate}} stacks by two every turn, letting you target him with Explosive Reaction or other damage spells to trigger {{IconLink|Unstable}} at will without risk. It also lets him survive and win {{IconLink|Relentless}} fights with ease, as long as you build up enough stacks. === Mad Scientist === This path has a relatively straightforward ability. Applying {{IconLink|Unstable}} on {{IconLink|Incant}} is a decently powerful effect, and causes many chain reactions with explosions. It will stack {{IconLink|Unstable}} decently fast on enemy units, specially if you can spellchain 0-cost spells. But if you can't kill at least one enemy before they begin attacking, you will have to wait until they all attack before they start dying. A good way to counter this is to use units with {{IconLink|Quick}} on the same floor. A buffed [[Test Subject Alpha]] will trigger many explosions. {{IconLink|Spikes}} on your frontliner can also work; tanky enemies will likely still get all their attacks in, but tanks generally deal less damage than backliners. This path is most effective when you have other ways to stack {{IconLink|Unstable}}. [[Plague Doctor]] is a good supporting unit, [[Explosive Reaction]] will have its uses, and spellchaining [[Secret Ingredient]] with {{Ember|-1}} gives many {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers. To maximize {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers, use each infusion as it is created, rather than stacking them up. Keep in mind, however, that this will prevent you from consistently getting the infusions you want, or using higher-level infusion effects. Like '''Reanimator''', this path benefits massively from Nefarious Overflow. It is also effective if allied with the [[Stygian Guard]], another clan with many {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers. This clan can provide powerful artifacts as well, like [[Founding Seal]], which doubles his {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers, and [[Sigiled Seaweed]], which thwarts {{IconLink|Incant}}-based enemies like [[Enthralled Ardent]] on the bottom floor. == Quotes == '''Summoned''' * ''Ahh, my genius is needed once again.'' * ''Another chance to rewrite the laws of nature!'' * ''Let's see if this experiment yields better results!'' * ''The experiment begins... now!'' * ''What a fine laboratory!'' Gain three times their {{Attack}}.}} }} == Strategy == '''Living Armory''' and '''Learning Limb''' both benefit from having lots of space to place units on the same floor as [[Baron Grael]], which makes [[Bogwurm's Growth]] an appealing Pyre heart. ===Living Armory=== '''Living Armory''' provides a strong source of scaling for the entire floor, which provides only limited benefit to '''Baron Grael''' himself but can be extremely useful if units like [[Plague Doctor]] or [[Test Subject Alpha]] are on the same floor. Any unit with {{IconLink|Multistrike}} or {{IconLink|Sweep}} can also be a good target. This makes [[Heaven's Light]] a solid choice with this path, as he can provide his {{Attack}} boost to more units. It is not recommended to remove his [[Erratic Assistant]] starter cards, as they provide a constant source of cheap equipment to convert into floorwide buffs. This path is less effective when used alongside [[Pincushion]] or the [[Hydra Armed Horror]], both of which also want a constant supply of equipment cards. ===Learning Limb=== This path is all about permanently scaling up your equipment for use by other units, meaning that it is most impactful when used on equipment you actually care about rather than the [[Scissor Hands]] from his starter cards. This means it is often the best choice with the [[Pyre of Dominion]]. It is especially good with the [[Twisted Assistant]], whose powerful equipment provides a strong source of damage scaling and benefits greatly from the frontloaded damage '''Learning Limb''' provides. Playing a {{IconLink|Graft}} unit on the same floor after placing '''Baron Grael''' can allow their attached equipment to be scaled twice, as {{IconLink|Artificer}} will trigger once when the unit is played and equipped, and again when the unit dies and the equipment is placed on something else on the floor. Since most equipment is not reusable, you can generally expect a maximum addition of {{Attack|9}} when facing the flying boss in ring 3. For battles 6, 8 and 9, the total addition would be {{Attack|27}}, {{Attack|45}} and {{Attack|54}} respectively (double these values if the equipment is {{IconLink|Graft}}ed). However, using [[Hall of Mirrors]] and/or [[Replicator Ray]] to duplicate '''Baron Grael''' can increase this further. The [[Resin Blades]] equipment is incredibly strong with this path, as it is returned to hand when the unit holding it dies. This uniquely allows it to benefit from his permanent scaling multiple times per combat, boosting its damage tremendously on top of the {{IconLink|Multistrike}} it already grants. [[Weapons Cache]] is advisable for this approach so that you do not need to pay {{Ember|2}} each turn replaying it, though [[Frenzystesia]] can act as a semi-substitute. When partnered with the [[Railforged]], [[Magnetic Relay]] is extremely strong with this path as long as you can afford to replay both the equipment and the unit it's attached to. This can allow you to trigger {{IconLink|Artificer}} many more times than you normally would and therefore gain much more {{Attack}}. ===It Hungers=== This path is mostly about providing '''Baron Grael''' himself with an enormous amount of extra {{Attack}}, which means that he benefits massively from equipment like [[Double-Edged Arms]] or [[Twisted Back]]. Like '''Living Armory''', this path is best with a constant supply of Erratic Assistants. By stacking {{IconLink|Reanimate}} on both '''Baron Grael''' and an Assistant in front of him, you can use his ability, along with [[Brain Transfer]], to pass {{Attack}} back and forth between the two repeatedly, massively increasing their damage output. '''Baron Grael''' gains 3x the Assistant's {{Attack}}, then passes that {{Attack}} back to the Assistant, then gains 3x ''that'' {{Attack}}, and so on. This is best used with the [[Plague Doctor]], who is technically an Assistant, but whose abilities are not tied to {{IconLink|Graft}}ed equipment. Other effects that can cheaply increase {{Attack}} on Assistants are worth searching out. [[Fight Club]] and [[Reanimation Lab]] will both boost the {{Attack}} of any Assistants played in them, a [[Conductor Steward]] on the same floor can do the same thing, while [[Advanced Growth]] can build up permanent {{Attack}} over time, and [[Hair of the Hybrid]] and [[Scorching Restraints]] can both provide {{IconLink|Rage}} when played. If you have the {{Gold}} to spare, you can also put {{IconLink|Strengthstone}}s on Assistants at the [[Merchant of Steel]]. The [[Melting Remnant]] is a powerful allied clan for '''It Hungers''', as you can [[Reform]] and kill a single Assistant over and over again, to keep boosting their {{Attack}} for much faster scaling, supported by cards/artifacts such as [[Wicked Blaze]] and [[Resin Block]]. == Quotes == '''Summoned''' * ''Another chance to learn what I can do with this body.'' * ''Awakened again... for the Master's will.'' * ''I live to serve Orechi.'' * ''My existence, is it a miracle or a mistake?'' She has [[Scissor Hands]] grafted to her. == Strategy == '''Erratic Assistant''' is good as an easy-to-fit {{Ember|0}}, {{Capacity|1}} unit that can facetank or supplement damage in early waves, as well as a cheap equipment provider for [[Pincushion]], [[Hydra Armed Horror]] and Baron Grael's '''Living Armory''' and '''Learning Limb''' paths. He gets {{IconLink|Unstable|4}} on {{IconLink|Incant}}. == Strategy == Unlike most units, the '''Overworked Assistant''' relies on constantly exploding from his own {{IconLink|Unstable}} stacks. This unit is a good medium for stacking {{IconLink|Unstable}} if you don't have '''Reanimator''' [[Orechi]], but you'll have to constantly reapply {{IconLink|Reanimate}} while defending him, as he'll be constantly on {{Health|1}} and the explosions only trigger at the end of the turn or whenever he dies. [[Tome of Horrors]] and [[Spike of the League]] are ideal, but even {{IconLink|Reanimate}} sources like [[Secret Ingredient]] and [[Pseudoscience]] can get the job done. If you scale him fast enough and have high enough {{IconLink|Reanimate}} stacks, he can solo many waves and even bosses. Keep in mind that later fights require far more scaling, however. Despite his potential strength as a waveclear option, he is hampered by not being a [[banner unit]]. Thus, under normal circumstances, he cannot be placed during the [[Deployment Phase]] and you will be subject to your draw order when trying to place him down, meaning you may not find him until several waves have already passed, or you will draw your {{IconLink|Reanimate}} cards before you can get him on the field. The [[Departure Manifest]] solves this problem by making '''Overworked Assistant''' [[Deployable]] (though beware of overfilling your hand if you start with [[Erratic Assistant]]s), and duplicating the unit at [[Empyrean Well]]s can decrease the risk of bottom-decking. Several copies of the unit tend to work well bunched up on the same floor regardless, so there is self-synergy there. If allied with the [[Stygian Guard]], he can be stronger than normal, as he works effectively with their {{IconLink|Incant}} units. They also provide access to [[Founding Seal]] to double {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers. Even if '''Overworked Assistant''' doesn't form a core part of your run, he is still effective in clearing lower-{{Health}} backliners if you toss him a few {{IconLink|Incant}}s, and his {{Ember|0}} cost and {{Capacity|1}} make him easy to fit on a floor. ==Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! {{UnitCard |name = Hulking Mass |image = PLR_HulkingMass.png |clan = Lazarus League |rarity = Uncommon |type = Monstrosity |banner = Yes |cost = 2 |size = 3 |stats = 15/20 |ability = {{IconLink|Armor|40}}.

Literally." |artist = Ron Kee }} '''Hulking Mass''' is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] [[banner unit]]. It starts with {{IconLink|Armor|40}} and gains another {{IconLink|Armor|40}} when {{IconLink|Reanimated}}. == Strategy == '''Hulking Mass''' stands out among the Lazarus League banner units due to a very unique benefit. Instead of reviving from {{IconLink|Reanimate}} with {{Health|1}} like all other units, it essentially revives with {{Health|41}} - 1 point of actual {{Health}} and 40 points of {{IconLink|Armor}}. This allows it to survive multiple attacks for each stack of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} it has, instead of losing a stack each time it takes damage. This makes '''Hulking Mass''' an effective tank, as long as you can keep it "fed" with plenty of {{IconLink|Reanimate}}. Cards such as the default starter [[Secret Ingredient]], as well as [[Forevermore Serum]] or [[Spike of the League]], can help with this. Because '''Hulking Mass''' gains {{IconLink|Armor}}, it is a particularly strong user of [[Faulty Body]], as damage to {{IconLink|Armor}} does not trigger {{IconLink|Fragile}}. One particularly effective strategy is to combine Faulty Body with [[Organ Harvester]] to kill all attacking enemies with less than {{Health|40}} while also stacking {{IconLink|Reanimate}} with each enemy killed. Its {{IconLink|Armor}} allows it to survive multiple attacks for each stack of {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, allowing it to outpace enemy waves and making it incredibly self-sufficient. In theory, using multiple copies of Faulty Body to stack up over {{IconLink|Spikes|500}} can allow it to kill every enemy with a nonzero {{Attack}} value (except those with {{IconLink|Reanimate}} or {{IconLink|Damage Shield}}) while gaining dozens of stacks of {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, letting it solo every battle except the [[Clash with the Titans|Titans]] even with no other support. However, this is generally impractical unless you either get very lucky with events like [[Wondrous Boxes]] and [[Mysterious Mirror]], or use the [[Lifemother's Pyre]]. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! {{UnitCard |name = Makeshift Golem |image = [[File:MakeshiftGolemPLR.png|thumb]] |clan = Lazarus League |rarity = Uncommon |type = Monstrosity |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 12/12 |ability = {{IconLink|Armor|12}}.
{{IconLink|Extinguish}}: Apply {{IconLink|Armor|12}} to friendly units. |flavor = "I am made of mud but I have a heart of gold." |artist = Loy Bouttamy }} The '''Makeshift Golem''' is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] [[banner unit]]. It grants {{IconLink|Armor|12}} to friendly units on {{IconLink|Extinguish}}. == Strategy == '''Makeshift Golem''' is a solid defensive unit, as {{IconLink|Extinguish}} abilities trigger every time the unit is {{IconLink|Reanimate}}d, and note that it will give itself {{IconLink|Armor}} in that case. It functions similarly to [[Hulking Mass]], as both are defensive units that want stacks of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} and work well with broadly the same cards. Hulking Mass has the advantage in numbers, having significantly more {{IconLink|Armor}} to start and better {{Attack}} and {{Health}} for the early rings, but '''Makeshift Golem''''s advantages are twofold: it's easier to play, costing {{Ember|1}} and {{Capacity|2}} compared to the {{Ember|2}} and {{Capacity|3}} of Hulking Mass, and it provides {{IconLink|Armor}} to all units on its floor instead of just itself. This makes '''Makeshift Golem''' very useful in preparing for {{IconLink|Relentless}}, as it will contribute tons of {{IconLink|Armor}} to the units behind it. As such, if using '''Makeshift Golem''' over Hulking Mass, it's best to provide it with strong but fragile teammates that it can buff, such as [[Test Subject Alpha]], [[Plague Doctor]], and [[Hydra Armed Horror]]. All of these units greatly appreciate the additional durability granted against bosses. Plague Doctor in particular works wonderfully in tandem with '''Makeshift Golem''' due to her small size, allowing her to fit on its floor more easily while still having room for another ally. Outside of the clan, it can be used alongside glass cannon units like [[Selene Acolyte]] and [[Nameless Siren]]. [[Apex Imp]] is one of its best partners, as each {{IconLink|Extinguish}} will provide Apex Imp with both {{IconLink|Armor}} and {{IconLink|Rage}}. Because '''Makeshift Golem''' protects your backline effectively, it does well against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]] and {{IconLink|Sweep}} units like [[Ragewing Assassin]]s, and should be considered more strongly if you will struggle with these enemies otherwise. [[Faulty Body]] and [[Tome of Horrors]] are high quality cards for '''Makeshift Golem''', as long as you can provide it with plenty of {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, and will allow it to clear out backline enemies by itself. Faulty Body can be combined with [[Organ Harvester]] to gain {{IconLink|Reanimate}} whenever a unit dies to {{IconLink|Spikes}}, but this is less effective than with Hulking Mass due to Hulking Mass's greater {{IconLink|Armor}}. Tome of Horrors will deal huge amounts of damage to all enemies every turn, especially when upgraded with {{IconLink|Stackstone}}, but can result in '''Makeshift Golem''' burning through stacks of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} faster than they can be replenished. [[Spike of the League]] provides '''Makeshift Golem''' with a big starting stack of {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, while [[Electricity Chamber]] can provide {{IconLink|Spikes}} every time '''Makeshift Golem''' is {{IconLink|Reanimated}}. It can also make good use of the [[Spiky Skin]] equipment dropped by [[Pufferflesh]]. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! Once every two turns, he can pull a unit forward and apply {{IconLink|Dazed}}. == Strategy == '''Meathook''' is a solid supportive unit, boasting decent stats and a strong activated ability. {{IconLink|Dazed}} is one of the strongest status effects in ''Monster Train'', completely preventing an enemy from acting until it wears off, and '''Meathook''' gives the Lazarus League access to this powerful effect while also potentially rearranging a floor to the player's favor. This simple ability has a myriad of applications. The most intuitive is to use '''Meathook''' on your main floor, stunning high-priority enemies on tough waves, and potentially preventing harmful status effects such as {{IconLink|Corruption}} from entering your floor. While with your other units, '''Meathook''' can daze flying bosses each time they return to your floor, preventing them from pushing damage onto your frontline or activating their dangerous abilities. His ability also notably completely shuts down [[Athane, Last to Fall]], as it will bring her to the front of the room without an {{IconLink|Incant}} and thus nullify her {{Attack}} gain for that floor or the threat of {{IconLink|Spikes}} on her [[Chosen Prayerstone]]. With his below-average survivability and lack of offensive efficiency, you cannot always afford to play '''Meathook''' with your main floor. If you can find a {{IconLink|Dualstone}} in a [[Merchant of Steel]], however, he can still be worth keeping in your run, being completely serviceable as a standalone unit on a higher floor. Here, '''Meathook''' can act as cleanup in normal combats while still completely locking down flying bosses. Because bosses will always target the highest floor with units first, '''Meathook''' can "bait" them on the first turn, immediately apply {{IconLink|Dazed|2}} to them, then repeat the process every time the boss returns to his floor. With a two-floor setup, the boss will not attack '''Meathook''''s floor nor your main floor, once again completely nullifying them for the entire fight until {{IconLink|Relentless}}. '''Meathook''' is especially effective if used with the [[Pyreborne]], who have various ways to decrease ability cooldowns, such as [[Mind Cage]] and [[Tome of Contracts]]. If he can use his ability every turn, he becomes significantly more powerful. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! She scales her {{Attack}} and {{Health}} permanently when {{IconLink|Equipped}}. == Strategy == '''Pincushion''' is a very slow scaling card. Her dependency on [[Equipment]] is also a problem if you don't start with [[Erratic Assistant]]. Because equipment effects are overwritten when a new equipment is applied, committing to scaling '''Pincushion''' means that you can't fully take advantage of your equipment's effects. When used alongside [[Baron Grael]], she actually synergizes best with his '''It Hungers''' path. The '''Devour''' ability allows you to kill off [[Assistants]] faster, granting you equipment which you can use to scale '''Pincushion'''. '''Learning Limb''' works decently, as {{IconLink|Artificer}} triggers when '''Pincushion''' is equipped, but the permanent {{Attack}} buffs to equipment will sometimes be wasted due to being constantly replaced. '''Living Armory''' is in direct conflict with '''Pincushion''' for {{IconLink|Equipped}} triggers and should be avoided. (If forced to pick between the two, '''Living Armory''' is generally stronger than leaning into '''Pincushion'''.) While she can reach high {{Attack}} values and does benefit from {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, she is often best as a tank who also happens to have high base {{Attack}}. If you intend to use her as a damage unit, you will need many copies of her, ideally after she has been sufficiently scaled; this can be difficult to accomplish without [[Lifemother's Pyre]] to provide duplication services at will. If you have multiple copies of '''Pincushion''', it is better to focus your resources on scaling one. [[Replicator Ray]] and [[Weaponized Prosthetic]] are both usable with '''Pincushion''', as you will be constantly overwriting equipment anyway. The [[Weapons Cache]] is an excellent way of drawing a lot of equipment quickly, as well as making it easier to play. If you have a lot of units you can play on the floor to trigger its effect repeatedly, you can add a ton of equipment cards to your deck without really slowing down your pacing. When partnered with the [[Underlegion]], [[Truffles]] can provide a constant supply of cheap equipment to speed up her scaling. With the [[Banished]], her high potential {{Health}} can be exploited offensively by equipping her with [[Shield of Wyngh]] after she has been sufficiently scaled. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! It is the only unit in the game which naturally has both {{IconLink|Quick}} and {{IconLink|Sweep}}. == Strategy == '''Test Subject Alpha''' has two very simple strengths: it has {{IconLink|Quick}}, and it has {{IconLink|Sweep}}, which is one of the most powerful combinations in all of ''Monster Train''. This allows it to hit every enemy on the floor before they can attack, meaning that any enemy with less than {{Health|5}} might as well not exist. This is balanced out by its pathetically low stats at {{AttackHealth|5|10}} and high {{Ember|3}} cost, significantly worse than almost every other sweeper. Your goal when using this unit should be to increase its damage output and survivability enough to take advantage of its incredible innate role compression. As with other sweepers, '''Test Subject Alpha''' is flexible - it can be a low-investment waveclear machine on a lower floor with a {{IconLink|Largestone}} to keep it alive and bolster damage, or act as your main carry unit with {{IconLink|Frenzystone}} to kill an entire floor at once. [[Secret Ingredient]] or other '''[[Mix]]''' cards can help give it useful effects like {{IconLink|Rage}}, {{IconLink|Lifesteal}}, and {{IconLink|Reanimate}}. '''Test Subject Alpha''' is also an excellent recipient of in-clan {{Attack}} buffs such as [[It's Alive!]] and [[Risky Operation]], with the latter having its risk almost completely eliminated as '''Test Subject Alpha''' will gain all its {{Health}} back before any enemies are able to strike. '''Test Subject Alpha''' benefits massively from the [[Twisted Back]], and is a great pick if you happened to start with [[Twisted Assistant]]s. {{IconLink|Sweep}} allows it to gain additional {{IconLink|Strike}} triggers, and {{IconLink|Quick}} guarantees that it will be able to attack before your other units and hit all enemies. {{IconLink|Trample}} also has a powerful interaction with {{IconLink|Sweep}}, as overkill damage from backline units will loop back around to hit the frontmost unit, potentially allowing you to kill it as well. [[Bloodthirsty Blade]] is an excellent piece of equipment for '''Test Subject Alpha''', as it will trigger {{IconLink|Slay}} frequently and thus scale its damage. Similarly, [[Organ Harvester]] will provide plenty of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} and offers a great amount of survivability even if you do not upgrade its low base {{Health}}. The two can be merged to benefit from both effects simultaneously, though playing them all during the [[Deployment Phase]] will cost a hefty {{DeploymentEmber|6}}. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! He gains a stack of {{IconLink|Multistrike}} whenever he is {{IconLink|Equipped}}, but the equipment is instantly removed and the '''Hydra Armed Horror''' does not gain any of its stat boosts or effects. == Strategy == '''Hydra Armed Horror''' is potentially a very strong unit, but entirely reliant on having a solid supply of equipment. This makes him far more effective in a deck which starts with [[Erratic Assistant]] rather than [[Secret Ingredient]]. Even without Erratic Assistant, however, he can still be relatively strong, as even a few stacks of {{IconLink|Multistrike}} make for a very powerful unit. He is somewhat similar to [[Eel Gorgon]], as both have the ability to stack up absurd amounts of {{IconLink|Multistrike}} in return for a downside: Eel Gorgon clears status effects between turns, while '''Hydra Armed Horror''' cannot use the powerful abilities of Lazarus League equipment. He is less useful alongside [[Pincushion]] or the '''Living Armory''' path on [[Baron Grael]], as all three want to be given as much equipment as possible. If used alongside Pincushion, you can use equipment to permascale Pincushion in early battles until you require '''Hydra Armed Horror''''s {{IconLink|Multistrike}} to win, then switch over and just use Pincushion as a high-{{Health}} tank in the late game. It may be worth saving powerful equipment like [[Double-Edged Arms]] for other units. '''Hydra Armed Horror''' doesn't care how strong a piece of equipment is, so weak equipment like [[Scissor Hands]] works just as well as anything else. When using '''Hydra Armed Horror''', the [[Merchant of Arms]] should be a high priority. Buying as much cheap equipment as possible makes the unit very viable even without Erratic Assistant (and in fact using [[Goliath Infusion]]s to scale '''Hydra Armed Horror''' is arguably even stronger). [[Weapons Cache]] is the gold mine, allowing you to immediately pull several pieces of equipment from your deck and reduce their {{Ember}} costs if you can make it Deployable, while also thinning out your deck. [[Equalizing Rings]] is a good choice of equipment to make Deployable, if offered, since it costs {{Ember|0}} already. When paired with [[Underlegion]], an {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Truffles]] can be a worthwhile investment to provide you with a continuous stream of equipment to put on your '''Hydra Armed Horror'''. With the [[Hellhorned]], '''Hydra Armed Horror''' makes fantastic use of [[Rage Room]] due to the high number of {{IconLink|Strike}} triggers it will get per turn (as well as from {{IconLink|Rage}} application in general), and [[Fortified Pauldrons]] can be exploited for cheap {{IconLink|Equipped}} triggers. Its best partner however, is easily [[Heph]], particularly her '''Weaponsmith''' path; in addition to generating free [[Crafted Equipment]]s with her ability, she will also apply {{Attack}} and {{Armor}} on the '''Hydra Armed Horror''' every time it is equipped, giving it ludicrous damage and helping its survivability. [[Stoic Platemail]] applies {{IconLink|Silence}} '''before''' the unit's {{IconLink|Equipped}} trigger can remove it, which means the equipment will not be removed and it will not gain {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! {{UnitCard |name = Nine-Lived Nightmare |image = PLR_NineLivedNightmare.png |clan = Lazarus League |rarity = Rare |type = Monstrosity |banner = Yes |cost = 2 |size = 1 |stats = 1/1 |ability = {{IconLink|Reanimate|8}}. |flavor = "Inga's cat still looks for her in the lab. She keeps looking at Dr. Orechi with feline hate. I think she knows something."
—Baron Grael |artist = Ishmael E. Hoover }} The '''Nine-Lived Nightmare''' is a rare [[Lazarus League]] [[banner unit]]. She enters combat with a huge amount of {{IconLink|Reanimate}}. == Strategy == '''Nine-Lived Nightmare''' is a very odd unit that seems unassuming at first glance due to her low stats. Her strength lies in her inherent {{IconLink|Reanimate|8}}, meaning she can take exactly nine hits before she dies, true to her name. Unlike other tank units, this is true no matter how strong the incoming hits are, making her extremely effective against bosses that can reach high {{Attack}} values, like the '''Furious Frenzy''' variant of [[Arkion]], or [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]]. However, this also makes her more vulnerable to combats that involve a great number of small hits than other tanks. The Lazarus League has several cards to support '''Nine-Lived Nightmare''' as a tank. [[Reanimation Lab]] and [[Electricity Chamber]] are two of her most obvious synergies. The stat boosts from Reanimation Lab persist after the unit dies, so an {{IconLink|Endless}} '''Nine-Lived Nightmare''' in a Reanimation Lab will have a much more respectable statline of {{AttackHealth|64|64}} the second time she's played. Meanwhile, Electricity Chamber will supply her with an ungodly amount of {{IconLink|Spikes}}, allowing her to easily wipe out backline units and even take large chunks out of heavies after enough deaths. [[Faulty Body]] serves a similar purpose to Electricity Chamber, providing a lot of {{IconLink|Spikes}} immediately. The {{IconLink|Fragile}} applied is irrelevant due to '''Nine-Lived Nightmare''' only having {{Health|1}} to begin with. If equipped with [[Organ Harvester]], she will also regain {{IconLink|Reanimate}} whenever a unit dies to her {{IconLink|Spikes}}. Putting {{IconLink|Unstable}} on '''Nine-Lived Nightmare''' is another effective way to let her clear out backline units. Each time she dies, she deals damage to enemy units equal to her {{IconLink|Unstable}} stacks, potentially allowing her to kill backline enemies before they have a chance to hit her and waste more of her {{IconLink|Reanimate}}. [[Tome of Horrors]] is the ideal card for this, supplying both {{IconLink|Unstable}} and {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, but in its absence you can use [[Explosive Reaction]] or [[Blast Infusion]]s. This is even more effective with the [[Nefarious Overflow]] artifact. Note however that kills from {{IconLink|Unstable}} explosions do '''not''' count towards {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers, so Organ Harvester will not help rebuild her lost {{IconLink|Reanimate}}. [[Brain Transfer]] will transfer all of '''Nine-Lived Nightmare''''s {{IconLink|Reanimate}} stacks to your front unit, which can result in some truly unkillable tanks. Especially if she can be killed and bought back via {{IconLink|Endless}} or [[Reform]], this can build up obscene amounts of {{IconLink|Reanimate}}. [[Scrap for Parts]] can be used with very little consequence in order to draw units from your deck and give them a big {{Attack}} boost, which can be helpful when using [[Baron Grael]]'s '''It Hungers''' path, allowing you to draw and power up [[Assistants]] for him to devour. When paired with [[Underlegion]], '''[[Propagate]]''' will help keep '''Nine-Lived Nightmare''''s {{IconLink|Reanimate}} stacks high. [[Loamcoat]] will provide her with two stacks of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} each turn. The [[Life Insurer]] artifact provides a bit of {{IconLink|Armor}} whenever '''Nine-Lived Nightmare''' dies, making her slightly more resilient against waves with lots of small, low-damage enemies. With [[Advanced Growth]], she can rapidly and permanently scale the {{Attack}} of a piece of equipment, which can then be put on another unit in later combats. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade !
