—Baron Grael |artist = Genevieve Bega }} '''Reforming Ooze''' is a rare [[Lazarus League]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever it is {{IconLink|Reanimated}}, it permanently gains {{Attack|+6}}. == Strategy == '''Reforming Ooze''' is best taken if found early in the game. This allows you plenty of time to scale up its damage, as well as giving you an opportunity to draft {{IconLink|Reanimate}} cards to trigger its ability as often as possible. With a good build, this unit can easily get over {{Attack|500}}, allowing it to instantly kill any non-boss enemy, and can be worth building your entire strategy around. [[Organ Harvester]] can take advantage of its high damage to gain additional stacks of {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, and any spell which provides {{IconLink|Reanimate}} can help stack it up faster. [[Spike of the League]], especially upgraded with a {{IconLink|Seekstone}}, can provide a large amount of immediate {{IconLink|Reanimate}} and makes the unit safe to put on the front lines. [[Faulty Body]] is a strong synergy if using Organ Harvester. By making '''Reforming Ooze''' {{IconLink|Fragile}}, it guarantees that every hit it takes will kill it and trigger {{IconLink|Reanimated}}, and small, low-health enemies that die to its {{IconLink|Spikes}} count as {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers for Organ Harvester, providing it with more {{IconLink|Reanimate}}. This is especially effective if '''Reforming Ooze''' has {{IconLink|Dualism}}, as it will gain {{IconLink|Reanimate|2}} for every {{IconLink|Slay}} trigger, which can make it entirely self-sufficient; it will gain more {{IconLink|Reanimate}} from backline enemies dying than it will lose from being hit. If you can produce more {{IconLink|Reanimate}} than you need, then {{IconLink|Unstable}} cards like [[Tome of Horrors]] can provide further {{IconLink|Reanimated}} triggers while also wiping out smaller enemies, letting '''Reforming Ooze''' function simultaneously as a tank slayer and backline clear. However, be aware that {{IconLink|Unstable}} explosions do not trigger {{IconLink|Slay}}, so this is slightly anti-synergistic with Organ Harvester. [[Surgical Strike]] with {{IconLink|Freezestone}} can be held until the end of each battle, then used to repeatedly kill '''Reforming Ooze'''. This allows it to {{IconLink|Reanimate}} as many times as possible, and as long as you are careful to leave it with just enough stacks of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} to kill the boss it is entirely safe. With [[Life Insurer]], you can simply burn through all of its stacks of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} and block damage from the boss using {{IconLink|Armor}}, as Piercing damage leaves {{IconLink|Armor}} intact and allows you to stack enormous amounts. Keep in mind that without a frozen Surgical Strike, Life Insurer may be harmful; it makes '''Reforming Ooze''' a much more effective tank, but also limits its {{Attack}} scaling. '''Reforming Ooze''' should only be duplicated in Rings 7 or 8, to ensure that the copied cards have as much {{Attack}} as possible. After reaching those rings, however, it is a very strong target for [[Empyrean Well]]s or [[Lifemother's Pyre]]. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! When played on a unit with {{Health|5}} or less, they gain {{IconLink|Unstable|25}} and then take lethal damage, immediately triggering the {{IconLink|Unstable}} explosion, and the whole floor of enemies takes 25 damage immediately, killing most backliners. This provides a lot of early-game value, letting you keep key units like [[Shield Steward]] and [[Hulking Mass]] healthy throughout a combat while also allowing them to hit for relevant damage. It can also help you set up a {{IconLink|Reanimate}}-based tank by setting it up behind another unit, then moving it to the front when you've given it the {{IconLink|Reanimate}} it needs. If allied with the [[Banished]], it can trigger {{IconLink|Shift}}, giving it nice synergy with that clan. It isn't an ideal late-game {{Attack}} scaling card, as e.g. [[Risky Operation]] does more, but it can still chip in lategame, and {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} remains relevant lategame too, especially for {{IconLink|Quick}} units. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! {{SpellCard |name = Pseudoscience |image = CRD_Pseudoscience.png |clan = Lazarus League |rarity = Common |cost = 1 |effect = Randomly apply either {{IconLink|Lifesteal|2}}, {{IconLink|Reanimate|1}} or {{IconLink|Spikes|6}}. |flavor = "I'm not sure how it works but I do know that, for some reason, shaking a bottle and making baby noises at my specimens makes them heal faster." |artist = Michaela Nienaber }} '''Pseudoscience''' is a common [[Lazarus League]] spell. It applies either {{IconLink|Lifesteal|2}}, {{IconLink|Reanimate|1}} or {{IconLink|Spikes|6}}. == Strategy == '''Psuedoscience''' is a unique card in the sense that it does 3 different things at random. None of the three things that it does are exceptionally strong: * {{IconLink|Reanimate|1}} is [[Forevermore Serum]], albeit without [[Consume]] * {{IconLink|Spikes|6}} is part of [[Sharpen]] * {{IconLink|Lifesteal|2}} is part of [[Insatiable Hunger]] So it doesn't look great from this perspective - it's a random roll between 3 effects that are decent but not amazing, and the randomness between 3 doesn't help its case, as randomness doesn't benefit the player (e.g. you might not get {{IconLink|Reanimate}} from it when you need it). But all 3 of its modes are effective on tanks. The fact that what it does overlaps significantly with what [[Infusion]]s can do also means that you can adapt your future Infusion choices in your turn based on what this does, and in general, given enough random choices, the result starts to look the same. A unit with {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, {{IconLink|Spikes}}, and {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} is a strong foundation for a Reanimating tank, and [[Organ Harvester]] is excellent to apply to such a unit. This odd card can be more consistent than it seems with Infusions and more copies of itself. It's never an exciting card even so, but with a tank that appreciates Reanimate and [[Secret Ingredient]] it can be worth the pickup. == Interactions == When this spell's area of effect is extended with [[Abyssal Prism]], the random effect is picked individually for each affected unit. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! {{SpellCard |name = Acid Shower |image = CRD_AcidShower.png |clan = Lazarus League |rarity = Uncommon |cost = 1 |effect = Apply {{IconLink|Unstable|10}} and deal '''1''' damage to enemy units. |flavor = "If water gets in your eyes, rinse them out immediately with acid."

It applies {{IconLink|Unstable|10}} to all enemies, then deals 1 damage to them. ==Strategy== '''Acid Shower''' kills backline enemies by the end of the turn, and is particularly effective against enemies with {{IconLink|Reanimate}} like [[Undying Wretch]] or [[Deformed Duo]], as they explode when they die, damaging their fellow enemies, and causing them to die again. They'll even put a good dent into the tankier enemies of the wave as they explode! It also punches through [[Purified Soul]]'s {{IconLink|Spell Shield}}, at least once the turn ends and {{IconLink|Unstable}} explosions happen. It's stronger on Covenant 2+ because of the more crowded enemy waves this gets to exploit. These make it effective against several lategame fights, with the caveat that it doesn't work until end of turn, so you'll need to play it on an unoccupied lower floor or on a floor that can handle tanking a hit from those backliners. However, in many fights, you can make '''Acid Shower''' work much faster by giving it Magic Power to allow its damage to kill an enemy immediately, letting it chain-react the moment you play it. Its best Seraph matchup is [[Heaven's Maw#Chosen of Dominion|Chosen of Dominion]], as with a {{IconLink|Powerstone}}, it can wipe out [[Misshapen Fiend]], [[Deformed Duo]], [[Discordant Heretic]], and on Covenant 10, [[Chosen Supplicant]] immediately with the power of its chain reactions, as every wave has an enemy susceptible to its initial damage. It's also reasonably effective in the other Seraph fights, though on Covenant 10 it usually isn't able to threaten [[Chosen Assassin]] on its own. ==Recommended Upgrades== {| class="wikitable" ! {{SpellCard |name = Insatiable Hunger |image = CRD_InsatiableHunger.png |clan = Lazarus League |rarity = Uncommon |cost = 1 |effect = Friendly units gain {{IconLink|Lifesteal|2}}. |flavor = "Some return from the Reanimation Lab with a peculiar hunger that consumes their minds. —from Dr. Orechi’s notebooks |artist = Daniel Sarmiento Chuquisengo }} '''Insatiable Hunger''' is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] spell. It gives {{IconLink|Lifesteal|2}} to your units. == Strategy == '''Insatiable Hunger''' provides reliable {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} to units, and on the [[Lazarus League]] this can be used for units with {{IconLink|Reanimate}} to heal to full health. Mixology:
{{SpellCard |name = Mixology |image = CRD_Mixology.png |clan = Lazarus League |rarity = Uncommon |cost = 2 |effect = '''[[Mix]]''' twice. |flavor = "I must admit, I do find myself sometimes getting a little whimsical with my concoctions. Just look at my Hair-Lifting Blueberry Fizzes!"
—from Dr. Orechi’s notebook |artist = Leonardo Dionisi }} '''Mixology''' is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] spell. It [[Mix]]es twice, granting the player an [[Infusion]] or upgrading their existing one, and then upgrades the resulting infusion. See the [[Infusion]] page for more details. == Strategy == See [[Infusion#Strategy|Infusion]]. '''Mixology''' can be a solid addition for decks looking to invest more in their Infusion, letting you get stacks of {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, {{IconLink|Damage Shield}}, {{IconLink|Sap}}, and more. This spell is often not worth using if you don't already have [[Secret Ingredient]], as Mix cards are best when you can play them consistently. It is also not a direct upgrade to Secret Ingredient: it provides twice as many uses of Mix, but has twice the {{Ember}} cost. This makes '''Mixology''' best for decks which have plenty of {{Ember}} but relatively little draw, as this spell costs only one draw for the equivalent of two Secret Ingredients. It also doesn't allow you to use the first Infusion before creating the second, meaning that if you get an Infusion you don't want the first time, the second will often be wasted. This makes it better at upgrading an Infusion you already have rather than creating a new one, meaning if you don't have an Infusion but have a different way of [[Mix]]ing, it's often best to use that before playing this. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Risky Operation:
{{SpellCard |name = Risky Operation |image = CRD_RiskyOperation.png |clan = Lazarus League |rarity = Uncommon |cost = 1 |effect = Reduce friendly unit to '''1''' health. Apply {{Attack|+10}} and {{IconLink|Lifesteal|2}}. |flavor = "Fascinating! The subject barely survived but look how strong they are!"
—from Dr. Orechi’s notebook |artist = Daniel Sarmiento Chuquisengo }} '''Risky Operation''' is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] spell. It reduces the target friendly unit to 1 health, but gives it {{Attack|+10}} and {{IconLink|Lifesteal|2}}. ==Strategy== '''Risky Operation''', as the name implies, makes your units strong in the long term, if they can survive their immediate vulnerability. The {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} this provides means that as long as the unit you apply this to gets to attack, they'll get their {{Health}} back - for many units, this will fully heal them. Since enemies attack first most of the time, you usually can't play this on frontline units as they'll die before getting their {{Health}} back, but it's usually safe to play this on backline units. That being said, this spell can be even better if you '''can''' play it on frontliners, as {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} is very helpful in keeping them alive. And there are ways you can do just that. A {{IconLink|Quick}} frontliner attacks before enemies, and with enough {{Attack}} they make this spell's downside moot. This makes it particularly strong on [[Test Subject Alpha]], who also greatly appreciates the extra {{Attack}}. A {{IconLink|Reanimate}} tank that's often on {{Health|1}} anyway can also use this for solid defensive benefit, especially with the extra {{Health}} from [[Reanimation Lab]]. {{IconLink|Armor}} or {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} can also allow you to use this on frontliners to scale them by protecting their last {{Health|1}}. While most units that primarily use {{IconLink|Armor}} or {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} to defend don't get much benefit from {{IconLink|Lifesteal}}, [[Hulking Mass]] can use this to recover his {{Health}} after being {{IconLink|Reanimated}} while protected by his {{IconLink|Armor}}. You could also use a [[Goliath Infusion]] to apply just enough {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} to survive until your unit gets to attack and heal up to full. Regardless, this is a spell that you'll want to play often if you have it, as it synergizes with itself - {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} and {{Attack}} are both things you want to stack, and there's no added penalty from playing it on the same unit more than once in a turn. It also has some niche uses with units that want to die but often have too much {{Health}} to kill off quickly. Examples include [[Balmabello]], an {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Greed Dragon]], or a {{IconLink|Largestone}} [[Legion of Wax]]. This can be used similarly to a '''[[Sacrifice]]''' effect, but '''Risky Operation''' is more accessible than the [[Brain Transfer|other]] [[Scrap for Parts|options]], as it is uncommon rather than rare. ==Recommended Upgrades== {| class="wikitable" ! Replicator Ray:
{{SpellCard |name = Replicator Ray |image = CRD_ReplicatorRay.png |clan = Lazarus League |rarity = Uncommon |cost = 3 |effect = '''[[Consume]]'''.
Remove equipment from a friendly unit. Copy the unit. |flavor = "I found that I was burning, sometimes quite literally, through assistants faster than I liked. I made this little contraption to turn one assistant into two!"
—Dr. Orechi |artist = Loy Bouttamy }} '''Replicator Ray''' is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] spell. It creates a {{IconLink|Cardless}} copy of a targeted friendly unit with an [[Equipment]] attached, and removes that equipment. == Notes == * The copy is placed directly behind the original. * The copy has all status changes applied to the unit, not just the card. {{Capacity}} limits are ignored in creating this unit, but the 7 unit limit is not. == Strategy == '''Replicator Ray''' can create a copy of your strongest unit and ignore {{Capacity}} as it does so, though at a high cost - {{Ember|3}} and an [[Equipment]]. This is at its best in an environment full of cheap [[Equipment]], such as [[Scissor Hands]] from [[Erratic Assistant]]. On the other hand, it doesn't usually work with units that want to have a particular [[Equipment]] attached to them, such as a [[Test Subject Alpha]] with [[Twisted Back]], as that tends to make your setup have too many steps. Duplicating units can scale multiplicatively with other sources, like {{IconLink|Rage}}, [[Risky Operation]], and so on, letting your damage investments multiply. That being said, using this with in-battle scaling tends to be too slow to be practical in many fights, as your setup will have too many steps and be dependent on draw order, and leak early waves. But it does work quite well on well-scaled metascaling units, as they can be strong from the onset of a battle. A notable in-clan target is a well-scaled [[Pincushion]], as they typically will come equipped with something they don't care about, and with enough base stats, they're well worth the investment. Plus, for metascaling units, using '''Replicator Ray''' to duplicate them is better than copying them with e.g. [[Empyrean Well]], as it gets around the problem of the copy fighting for metascaling resoures, e.g. in [[Pincushion]]'s case, spare [[Equipment]], whereas duplicating them with this spell ensures the copy will be relatively up-to-date on their stats. It can also allow you to duplicate [[Champion]]s, which is normally not possible, and is especially potent for champions that metascale other units or cards, like '''Learning Limb''' [[Baron Grael]] or '''Enchantress''' [[Talos]]. When used on an activated '''Titanchannel''' [[Solgard]], '''Replicator Ray''' will copy his current {{IconLink|Shard}} stacks and stats, and it will also make '''Resurgence''' available for use again without putting him into {{IconLink|Stasis}}. This can allow you to effectively double the copy's stats immediately by using '''Resurgence''' again, or scale him up further by continuing to {{IconLink|Incant}} while also letting him participate in the combat with his current stats. [[Funguy]] cannot be usefully duplicated; if used on one, it will add only a single stack of Troop, regardless of how many they had. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Upgrade !! Description |- | style="text-align:center;" | [[file:FreezeStone.png|50x50px]]

[[Seekstone]] | On the other hand, if you have a good target at the start of battle, such as a well-scaled [[Pincushion]], and a plan to have them equipped by then, '''Seekstone''' also gives an {{Ember}} discount and lets you duplicate on turn 1 to avoid leaking early waves. |- | style="text-align:center;" | [[file:EternalStone.png|50x50px]]

{{SpellCard |name = Surgical Strike |image = CRD_SurgicalStrike.png |clan = Lazarus League |rarity = Uncommon |cost = 1 |effect = '''[[Piercing]]'''.
Deal '''4''' damage.
{{IconLink|Slay}}: Add a copy of this card with '''[[Ephemeral]]''' to your hand. |flavor = "I've found that the scalpel is mightier than the sword. It can cut with more deadly precision."
—from Dr. Orechi’s notebook |artist = Seika Nakai }} '''Surgical Strike''' is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] spell. It deals 4 damage, and creates an [[Ephemeral]] copy of itself if it kills any unit. The copy can in turn make another copy if it kills a unit, and this can continue indefinitely. ==Strategy== '''Surgical Strike''' is a deceptively strong answer to a large variety of threats in this game, and one that should be strongly considered if you don't already have something that can do its job. You will need to upgrade it for its potential to be realized, but with two common [[Upgrades]] (or just one, if you have {{IconLink|Conduit}}), it's already a powerhouse throughout the game. Once upgraded to {{Ember|0}} and above 5 damage, its power becomes apparent. [[Deformed Duo]] dies to repeated use of this spell. [[Purified Soul]] dies to this spell's [[Piercing]]. You can do this on all 3 floors as needed, making this spell arguably more of an area-of-effect spell than most actual area-of-effect spells! If you've got {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers, either [[Orechi]]'s '''Mad Scientist''' line, or from allied [[Stygian Guard]] or [[Luna Coven]], this spell gives you several of them. One weakness of '''Surgical Strike''' if you're playing on Covenant 10, however, is that unless you have a lot of {{IconLink|Conduit}}, you won't be able to kill Chosen variants of enemies with it. A build that's able to stack {{IconLink|Unstable}}, such as one with the aforementioned Orechi path, solves this quite nicely by blowing up smaller units. It also has utility in killing your own units, like [[Assistants]] and [[Imps]], without needing to wait for them to be killed by enemies - you can do this and kill enemies all in the same turn. If you've built up a unit with a large amount of {{IconLink|Unstable}} and {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, you can even use this to spend as many {{IconLink|Reanimate}} stacks as you need to deal with the current wave. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Weaponized Prosthetic:
{{SpellCard |name = Weaponized Prosthetic |image = CRD_WeaponizedProsthetic.png |clan = Lazarus League |rarity = Uncommon |cost = 1 |effect = Remove equipment from a unit. Apply {{Attack|+30}}. |flavor = "Look, Mom! Isn’t my new arm cool?" |artist = Ishmael E. Hoover }} '''Weaponized Prosthetic''' is an uncommon [[Lazarus League]] spell. It removes a unit's equipment but applies {{Attack|+30}}. The removed equipment does not return to the player hand nor to the discard pile. == Strategy == '''Weaponized Prosthetic''' is one of the strongest sources of raw {{Attack}} scaling in the game, but comes with a fairly steep cost. For the Lazarus League in particular, the strength of equipment like [[Twisted Back]] and [[Organ Harvester]] can make it difficult to justify this card, since the {{Attack|+30}} granted is often not worth the loss of other utility granted by equipment. Additionally, even cheap and weak equipment can provide {{Attack}} on its own, so the net {{Attack}} gain from this spell is diminished somewhat. For example, a unit with [[Scissor Hands]], perhaps the most accessible and weakest equipment in the game, only gains a net total of {{Attack|+21}} from this card compared to not giving the unit any equipment in the first place. That is still significant, of course, but unlike other {{Attack}}-boosting cards like [[Risky Operation]], this card is difficult to upgrade with {{IconLink|Twinstone}} since that would require two separate pieces of equipment to remove within the same turn, so there is not much potential for increasing its output. It is also largely incompatible with what would otherwise be its best in-clan recipient, the [[Hydra Armed Horror]], as the unit will automatically remove any equipment given and thus cannot have equipment removed by '''Weaponized Prosthetic'''. The only exceptions are giving it [[Stoic Platemail]], whose {{IconLink|Silence}} will suppress its automatic equipment removal, or equipping it while a [[Deafening Herald]] is active. Even so, this is difficult to line up. That being said, it still has its uses for units that benefit strongly from raw {{Attack}} boosts. [[Legion of Wax]] is notable as the bonuses it gets from equipment are lost when it dies and do not get passed down, but the {{Attack}} boost from '''Weaponized Prosthetic''' ''will'' be inherited by the units it spawns. [[Eel Gorgon]] cannot benefit from most utility granted by equipment, and with its tremendous potential {{IconLink|Multistrike}} it makes excellent use of the {{Attack}} boost. It is also usually a net gain when starting with [[Erratic Assistant]]s, outside of '''Learning Limb''' [[Baron Grael]]. [[Pincushion]] has its equipment replaced constantly anyway to scale, so using '''Weaponized Prosthetic''' just before giving it a new piece of equipment is pure upside. Baron Grael's '''It Hungers''' path can also benefit from it on certain [[Assistants]], in particular Erratic Assistants and [[Pufferflesh]], where the loss of their {{IconLink|Graft}}ed equipment is not a big deal and the {{Attack|+30}} will be multiplied when Grael eats them. Avoid using it on [[Double-Edged Bearer]] and [[Twisted Assistant]], as their native equipment is often strongly desirable. Having the {{IconLink|Red Crown}} upgrade on your units can be a valid reason to take this spell, so that unfavorable equipment like [[Equalizing Rings]], [[Stoic Platemail]], or [[Glass Cannon]] can be removed without needing to kill the unit and replay it. Additionally, since the unit is {{IconLink|Endless}}, if it dies anyway, the {{Attack|+30}} will be preserved when replayed. If partnered with the [[Underlegion]], an {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Truffles]] can supply new equipment every turn, so you can continually scale with '''Weaponized Prosthetic''' as long as the recipient unit doesn't actually need any permanent equipment. When partnered with [[Railforged]], '''Weaponsmith''' [[Heph]] or an [[Armament Drive]] with {{IconLink|Eternalstone}} can also provide a regular supply of [[Crafted Equipment]] to use. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! '''Smolderstone''' therefore pulls double duty, making it free to play and giving it [[Consume]], so it is removed from your deck once used and you will not keep drawing it. If you have enough equipment in your deck that you will be able to benefit from repeated plays of this spell, '''Emberstone''' still improves your {{Ember}} economy. |- | style="text-align:center;" | [[file:SeekStone.png|50x50px]]

{{SpellCard |name = Brain Transfer |image = CRD_BrainTransfer.png |clan = Lazarus League |rarity = Rare |cost = 2 |effect = '''[[Sacrifice]]'''.
Transfer {{Attack}} and all '''[[Buff]]''' and '''[[Debuff]]''' effects to front friendly unit. |flavor = "While a body can still be usable if preserved correctly, brain matter must be transferred to a host within hours."
—from Dr. Orechi’s notebook |artist = Hannah Lim }} '''Brain Transfer''' is a rare [[Lazarus League]] spell. It [[Sacrifice]]s its target, grants the front friendly unit the target's {{Attack}}, and moves all [[Buff]] and [[Debuff]] effects to the front friendly unit. ==Notes== * If the target has {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, it will lose 1 stack of {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, ''then'' transfer its {{Attack}}, [[Buff]]s and [[Debuff]]s to the front friendly unit. ** The target will lose all its [[Buff]]s and [[Debuff]]s, including its remaining {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, but will keep its {{Attack}}. * {{IconLink|Dualism}} on either the target or the front friendly unit does not affect this spell. * If this is cast on the front friendly unit and that unit has {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, that unit will simply lose a stack of {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, and it will transfer its Buffs and Debuffs to itself (doing nothing in practice). It will ''not'' gain any {{Attack}} in this case. ==Strategy== '''Brain Transfer''' is a powerful and versatile card, but can be somewhat difficult to use. Its most basic use is to "combine" two units, for example by sacrificing a [[Nine-Lived Nightmare]] to put its stacks of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} onto an important tank unit like [[Hulking Mass]]. You can also move stats from a unit with high base stats onto one with {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, {{IconLink|Sweep}}, or other useful effects. With [[Baron Grael]]'s '''Devour''' ability, it is possible to pass stats back and forth between him and a frontline Assistant, multiplying them each time. As long as you can consistently apply {{IconLink|Reanimate}} to the Baron, he will gain up to three times the assistant's {{Attack}}, then pass it back to them, then gain three times that {{Attack}} and so on. This allows both units to potentially gain some of the highest stats possible on any unit, orders of magnitude higher than would be needed to win any fight in the game. This spell can also be used effectively with other clans, either when allied with the Lazarus League or if you happen to get it from the [[Wreckage Remains]] event. The ability to kill units on command is incredibly strong with many [[Melting Remnant]] strategies, but the best target for this spell is from the [[Pyreborne]]: an {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Greed Dragon]] will gain extra stats every time he is killed and resummoned, and can repeatedly transfer his enormous {{Attack}} onto a unit of your choice. When used on '''Silver Empress''' [[Ekka]] during {{IconLink|Full Moon}}, she will transfer her {{IconLink|Conduit|70}} to the front unit. That {{IconLink|Conduit}} will no longer be lost during {{IconLink|New Moon}}, and if you can bring her back e.g. with {{IconLink|Reanimate}} / {{IconLink|Endless}} / [[Reform]], once you phase back to {{IconLink|Full Moon}} she will gain another {{IconLink|Conduit|70}}. Done repeatedly, this can quickly add a ridiculous amount of {{IconLink|Conduit}} to the floor. Note that the effects are transferred, not copied. Even if the sacrificed unit is saved by {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, all effects on it will still be taken away to give to the recipient. Its {{Attack}}, however, will not change. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! Description |- | style="text-align:center;" | [[File:SeekStone.png|50x50px]]
[[Seekstone]] | '''Seekstone''' guarantees that you will see this spell immediately, which is particularly important if you want to use it to instantly shift buffs from one unit to another. This makes it especially good with Nine-Lived Nightmare. |- | style="text-align:center;" | [[File:KeepStone.png|50x50px]]
[[Keepstone]] | '''Keepstone''' allows you to play this spell every turn, making it particularly good if you plan to pass stats back and forth or use it repeatedly on an endless unit. |} ==History== ''See [[Version History]]'' {| class="wikitable" |- ! He froze. The hand he had just collected was gone! |artist = Merilliza Chan }} '''Minds Of Their Own''' is a rare [[Lazarus League]] spell. It causes all friendly units on the floor to attack immediately, as long as they have equipment. ==Strategy== '''Minds Of Their Own''' can be an extremely powerful card, allowing all units on the floor to attack an additional time. This can let you finish off tough enemies like [[Avowed Gladiator]] even if your units cannot kill them under normal circumstances, or even wipe out enemies before they can attack. The requirement to have equipment does make it slightly harder to benefit from, but putting Deployable equipment on your important units can allow you to begin playing it even on the first turn. Cheap {{IconLink|Graft}} units like [[Erratic Assistant]] can also help make sure all of your units are equipped after a turn or two, even if you don't have any stronger equipment to use. It is rare for a Lazarus League run to not use equipment on important units. Unlike most spells, the damage here is actually dealt by your units, and so it can trigger {{IconLink|Strike}} and {{IconLink|Slay}}. This spell's main problem is its relatively high cost, but any way of dealing with this - cost reduction upgrades, [[Hell's Flame]], [[Volatile Gauge]], or anything else - can make it much easier to use. ==Recommended Upgrades== {| class="wikitable" ! It requires the [[Sacrifice]] of a friendly unit but draws a friendly unit and applies {{Attack|+40}}. == Notes == This spell draws from the top of your draw pile, and then your discard pile if there are no units in your draw pile. * This means that an {{IconLink|Endless}} unit [[Sacrifice]]d using this card is guaranteed to be re-drawn. * Naturally, it cannot draw a unit already in your hand. == Strategy == '''Scrap for Parts''' is a very useful spell, though like all "draw a unit" spells it's hard to have it give the bonus to the unit you want. From the player's perspective, the unit it draws is a random unit you haven't played yet. Without upgrades, its effectiveness is limited, but it is essentially draw-neutral as long as you have a unit for it to draw. It gives a significant offensive stat boost to any unit. Initially, it can often draw units in your starting deck, like [[Spear Steward]]s or [[Shield Steward]]s that were unplayed during the [[Deployment Phase]], which benefit somewhat but are usually not ideal targets. [[:Category:Assistant units|Assistants]] can also be drawn, and they aren't the best targets for the buff either. Purging these can allow you to more effectively choose your target. Note that if you intend to draw a banner unit, that unit must not be played during the [[Deployment Phase]]. Good units to target with this spell: * Units that take advantage of extra {{Attack}} effectively. The [[Lazarus League]] have [[Test Subject Alpha]], and [[Plague Doctor]]. [[Hydra Armed Horror]] also enjoys {{Attack}}, but it usually wants there to be a lot of [[:Category:Assistant units|Assistants]] in the deck, which this card doesn't want. * While they're not great targets for the buff, you can use this to get [[:Category:Assistant units|Assistants]] early if you need their equipment, or it can grab other non-banner units you need early. ** The exception to this is when running [[Baron Grael]]'s '''It Hungers''' path, in which case even drawing an [[Erratic Assistant]] and granting it {{Attack|+40}} will give Grael {{Attack|+147}} at max level. * Units with high {{Ember}} costs that have their cost set to 0 by this spell, such as [[Test Subject Alpha]] and [[Plague Doctor]]. This can allow you to, in practice, improve your {{DeploymentEmber}}. * Units with {{IconLink|Endless}}, as the {{Ember|0}} buff persists through death, allowing you to save {{Ember}} multiple times. This spell is especially effective used this way, as if you [[Sacrifice]] a unit with {{IconLink|Endless}} (that doesn't have {{IconLink|Reanimate}}), you're guaranteed to draw it and apply the buffs. This is also a great way to farm {{IconLink|Summon}} and {{IconLink|Extinguish}} triggers - [[Makeshift Golem]] is one in-clan example. Generally, you'll want to play the unit as soon as possible, making a {{IconLink|Seekstone}} essential, as well as a unit that doesn't mind dying on turn 1. An exception is if you're using it to scale an {{IconLink|Endless}} unit, in which case you'll probably prefer an {{IconLink|Eternalstone}} and something else. This can even be used to draw your [[Champion]], which can be immensely powerful for certain champions like Brawler [[Hornbreaker Prince]] or any path on [[Primordium]]. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! {{EquipmentCard |name = Organ Harvester |image = CRD_OrganHarvester.png |clan = Lazarus League |rarity = Uncommon |cost = 2 |effect = {{IconLink|Slay}}: Gain {{IconLink|Reanimate|1}}. |stats = {{Attack|10}} |flavor = "My experiments tend to take a toll on the bodies of my assistants. I made this contraption so I could collect new parts with more efficiency."
—from Dr. Orechi's notebook |artist = Seika Nakai }} '''Organ Harvester''' is an equipment from the [[Lazarus League]]. It grants the equipped unit {{Attack|+10}} and gives it a {{IconLink|Slay}} ability that gives it {{IconLink|Reanimate|1}}. == Strategy == '''Organ Harvester''' can be used to give incidental survivability to powerful units that are able to {{IconLink|Slay}}, such as powerful frontline tanks, or to units in your backline as an answer to {{IconLink|Corruption}}. [[Life Insurer]], [[Reanimation Lab]], or the abilities of [[Hulking Mass]] and [[Makeshift Golem]] can increase this survivability bonus, as can adding {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} to get your {{Health}} back after a near-death experience. Note that you will need to be able to kill enemies in order to get this equipment's bonus, which can be hard for defensive units, though {{IconLink|Spikes}} can help with this. But this equipment can do much more than that if you lean into the idea that your unit is going to repeatedly die, leaving them on {{Health|1}}, and repeatedly {{IconLink|Slay}} to stay alive, using this equipment to gather enough {{IconLink|Reanimate}} stacks to stay alive. In order to do this, you will need the equipped unit to either have a lot of {{Attack}} and {{IconLink|Multistrike}} to plough through front enemies, and/or {{IconLink|Sweep}} or {{IconLink|Spikes}} to be able to {{IconLink|Slay}} backliners, and {{IconLink|Trample}} is nice in any case. (Sadly, you can't merge this with [[Twisted Back]], meaning you'd need to find {{IconLink|Trample}} off-clan.) {{IconLink|Quick}} is also helpful, especially with {{IconLink|Sweep}}. This will allow you to scale using {{IconLink|Reanimated}} triggers, {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers, {{IconLink|Extinguish}} triggers, and more. Examples of great candidates for this include [[Reforming Ooze]] which can amass a ton of {{Attack}} this way, and [[Test Subject Alpha]] who easily racks up stacks of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} to be a tank. [[Reanimation Lab]] and [[Electricity Chamber]] are great to put in the room with such a unit. You can also apply [[Faulty Body]] to give you needed {{IconLink|Spikes}}, and merge this equipment with [[Glass Cannon]], with little downside, all while being impervious to a wide variety of threats, including {{IconLink|Corruption}} as long as you get enough stacks of {{IconLink|Reanimate}}. You will need a source of initial {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, or a way to protect your unit with this equipment early, in order to amass a good initial cache of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} for this to work. If you're protecting your unit early, you'll need to ensure the protecting unit will eventually die, or use e.g. [[It's Alive!]] to advance your {{IconLink|Reanimate}} tank to the front when it's time. You'll also need to be aware that in the [[Titans]] fight, you'll have nothing to kill one out of 3 waves, and [[Savagery]] will take some of your {{IconLink|Reanimate}} stacks then, making this strategy more perilous in that fight than in others. If your Champion happens to be the [[Shardtail Queen]] on the '''Imperialist''' path, then she can easily stack up {{IconLink|Reanimate}} by using her ability to kill Imps. This can make her into an almost invincible tank, though the {{Capacity}} required to fit Imps alongside her can make it difficult for her to protect your other units. ==Merges== {| class="wikitable" ! {{EquipmentCard |name = Potion Kit |image = CRD_PotionKit.png |clan = Lazarus League |rarity = Common |cost = 1 |effect = {{AbilityBox|Brew|3|'''[[Mix]]'''.}} |stats = 8/4 |flavor = "An essential collection of tools that every lab technician needs: powdered Titan bone, a beaker, a faulty burner, and chili, of course."
—OHELL Safety Regulations and Guidelines |artist = Herrick Ong }} '''Potion Kit''' is an equipment from the [[Lazarus League]]. Its Ability lets the unit it's equipped on to '''[[Mix]]''' once every 3 turns. == Strategy == While the Ability's cooldown is just too long for it to be a consistent equipment, and it's not the most exciting choice for combining with other equipment, being able to mix for free is a very good effect, and you can use it whenever you're able to get a strong infusion. With [[Progress Pacemaker]], you can save the ability for a turn when you otherwise can't [[Mix]] to ensure you get your double Mix for that turn. It usually should be put on a unit that otherwise doesn't need equipment, and can be combined with something else if you have the {{DeploymentEmber}}. '''Potion Kit''' can also be solid for units that simply want to spam equipment, like [[Baron Grael]]'s Living Armory path or [[Pincushion]], as they can use the ability once and then just replace it with something else. ([[Hydra Armed Horror]] doesn't get any extra utility from this than other equipment, though.) Don't go haywire on the number of '''Potion Kits''' you get - one or two will be more than enough to help you [[Mix]] when you need to. It isn't the greatest economic value, but if you can use it without paying too much of an opportunity cost it's a solid value add. It gets noticeably better if allied with the [[Pyreborne]], as they have cooldown-reducing effects like [[Tome of Contracts]] and [[Attuned Manacles]] that can allow you to Mix every turn rather than every third turn, essentially turning this equipment into a free [[Secret Ingredient]] each turn. ==History== ''See [[Version History]]'' {| class="wikitable" |- ! '''Reanimation Lab''' is a room from the [[Lazarus League]] clan. It gives units {{AttackHealth|+7|+7}} on {{IconLink|Summon}} and {{IconLink|Reanimate}}.

== Notes ==

Despite using the {{IconLink|Summon}} keyword, this room does not interact with [[Ashes of the Fallen]].

== Strategy ==

By making '''Reanimation Lab''' [[Deployable]], you can use it to get a flat {{AttackHealth|+7|+7}} on all of your units on the floor. This is comparable to [[Fight Club]] but with a more balanced offensive and defensive benefit. Used this way, you can even play a different room afterwards.

'''Reanimation Lab''' can be even better if you have a unit that is primarily defending with {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, as they will get the {{AttackHealth|+7|+7}} boost every time they do so. The {{Health|+7}} can be a nice way to limit how much {{IconLink|Reanimate}} you're losing, and the {{Attack|+7}} provides some offensive scaling over time. Applying {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} to your tank after they've gotten some boosts can allow them to put their extra {{Health}} to good use. [[Nine-Lived Nightmare]] in particular can become quite tanky with this room in play. 

This room combined with a reanimating tank with {{IconLink|Savage Spirit}} provides {{Attack|+21}} per {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, giving that upgrade a niche.

Its {{Health}} buff makes it incompatible with most {{IconLink|Endless}} resummoning builds as it makes it harder for {{IconLink|Endless}} units to die, but it can be quite strong with the [[Melting Remnant]], as they are good at killing their units and resummoning them. With [[Hallowed Halls]] in particular, this room more than doubles the scaling it provides.

{{IconLink|Revenge}}: Gain {{IconLink|Rage|6}}. }} ==Strategy== A glass cannon of a champion, the '''Hornbreaker Prince''' lives on the razor's edge of balance, able to deliver massive amounts of damage but never more than a few hits away from destruction. Even his tank line requires him to consistently get kills every round in order for it to be effective, making targeted support essential. With the right equipment and support though he can become an extremely potent beatstick. ===Brawler=== [[Hornbreaker Prince]]'s '''Brawler''' line gets a lot of {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, giving it high damage potential. It's up to your deck to take advantage of this. The most immediate problem with the '''Brawler''' line is its lack of initial power and lack of ability to scale that power on its own - its damage is the lowest of the three upgrade lines, even with {{IconLink|Multistrike}} taken into account, and while its inital {{IconLink|Armor}} is nice, it isn't sturdy enough to serve as a great tank. However, it is a lot easier for [[Hellhorned]] cards to scale {{Attack}} than it is for them to scale {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, which gives this line a lot of potential. Cards that give {{IconLink|Rage}} such as [[Fledgling Imp]], [[Rage Serum]], [[Ritual of Battle]], and effects that amplify {{IconLink|Rage}} like [[Resonant Shard]], [[Collection of Tails]], or [[Deranged Brute]] are what you are looking for. Taking this upgrade line in Limbo on high [[Covenant Ranks]] is dangerous unless you either already have some ways to scale its {{Attack}} or have a strong start in general, but it is capable of getting strong. Taking upgrades in either the '''Reaper''' or the '''Wrathful''' line later may be worth it if you haven't found great ways to scale its {{Attack}} or find yourself really needing the roles those lines fill, but given how strong {{IconLink|Multistrike|4}} can be with the right support, this can feel like a missed opportunity. ===Reaper=== [[Hornbreaker Prince]]'s '''Reaper''' line focuses on amassing {{Attack}} through kills. In order to help with this, '''Hornbreaker Prince''' gains an ability, '''Culling''', which allows him to immediately perform an attack. That said, it also requires a lot of support. As with all of [[Hornbreaker Prince]]'s lines, you'll need to keep him protected. The '''Reaper''' line also needs kill support, specifically a way to set up kills for him. While '''Hornbreaker Prince''' has solid {{Attack}}, it's not enough to kill most front line units at the start of the fight. If it fails to get early kills, it won't be able to snowball its {{Attack}} over the course of the fight. This can be fixed by softening up enemies with spells, lower floors, or the unit in front of '''Hornbreaker Prince'''. Boosting [[Hornbreaker Prince]]'s {{Attack}} early with {{IconLink|Rage}} can work too. '''Culling''' allows '''Hornbreaker Prince''' to more easily get kills, but while it is a powerful ability, its level 1 iteration has a massive cooldown of 6. This means that it is essentially a once per battle ability, so it is best used to get an early kill and start his scaling. Placed behind a [[Shield Steward]], he can kill a frontline [[Fallen Champion]] between '''Culling''', the Steward's attack, and his own attack. With the [[Melting Remnant]], [[Reform]]ing him can reset the cooldown, and the [[Pyreborne]] have several cooldown-reducing cards, but with other clans he will have difficulty using his ability more than once each battle. '''Culling''' becomes more reliable at '''Reaper II''', lowering its cooldown to 3 turns. At '''Reaper III''', it becomes a 1 turn cooldown, allowing '''Hornbreaker Prince''' to make use of it every turn. This makes it a very powerful ability, allowing '''Hornbreaker Prince''' to essentially make twice as much use out of offensive buffs, like {{IconLink|Rage}} or {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. It can be thought of as an alternative to {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}} where one of the two hits has {{IconLink|Quick}}. {{IconLink|Multistrike}} is extremely desirable if not necessary for this upgrade path - both because of his high base {{Attack}} and because this will allow him to kill multiple enemies per turn, scaling his {{Attack}} to tremendous levels. At '''Reaper III''', every stack of {{IconLink|Multistrike}} is effectively doubled, since he will make his full attack twice every turn; for example, with {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}}, he will make four attacks each turn. You can consider crosspathing into '''Brawler''' for {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}}, but he really benefits from the one-turn cooldown on '''Culling''', so it's usually better to seek out other sources like [[Void Armament]] unless you have access to cooldown reduction or other ways to use '''Culling''' every turn. He makes good use of [[Onehorn's Tome]], since this upgrade path is already very fragile and needs protection. If you can make him {{IconLink|Endless}}, such as via [[Memorial for the Melted]] or [[Votive Key]], he's also a fantastic user of [[Resin Blades]], as when he dies to {{IconLink|Burnout}} and gets replayed, '''Culling''' will be available for use again. Mixing the '''Reaper''' line and the '''Wrathful''' line is not recommended, as '''Wrathful''' is intended to be a front line unit while '''Reaper''' is not. Its {{IconLink|Armor}} gain won't be enough, and its {{IconLink|Rage}} gain doesn't mean much compared to {{IconLink|Slay}} boosts. ===Wrathful=== [[Hornbreaker Prince]]'s '''Wrathful''' line serves as a tank for its team, snowballing into both an offensive and defensive threat by the end of the fight while providing space to tuck offensive back line units. Unlike the '''Reaper''' line, the '''Wrathful''' line does not need to get early kills to scale, as he gains {{Attack}} by being hit. Instead, its longevity is very dependent on getting kills. It has solid initial longevity and can reliably serve as a tank in early rings, though it is prudent to look for kill opportunities to keep him healthy for the boss fight. In later rings, it can be a good idea to have additional sources of {{IconLink|Armor}} to keep it alive longer and other sources of {{IconLink|Rage}} to accelerate it early in the fight. You can use spells such as [[Torch]] and Imps to block in a pinch also help control how much damage '''Hornbreaker Prince''' takes over the course of a match, though it may be better to let '''Hornbreaker Prince''' take hits if it is able to. [[Torch]] can even be used on '''Hornbreaker Prince''' to trigger his {{IconLink|Revenge}} ability. [[Branding Rite]] can also be used to this effect. {{IconLink|Rage}} boosters like [[Deranged Brute]], [[Resonant Shard]], and [[Collection of Tails]] help too. The biggest issue with this line is its reliance on getting {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers in order to not die. This can become almost impossible in the late game due to [[Avowed Gladiator]]s leading waves. It improves tremendously with a source of {{IconLink|Spikes}}, either from the [[Awoken]] or [[Lazarus League]], as now it can kill weak backliners that attack it and gain significantly more {{IconLink|Armor}}. The [[Shield of Wyngh]] from the [[Banished]] can work as well, as his {{Health}} is decent at high levels. [[Onehorn's Tome]] can be powerful for this line if you manage to get it going. While the {{IconLink|Fragile}} debuff essentially reduces [[Hornbreaker Prince]]'s {{Health}} to 1, if you can generate enough {{IconLink|Armor}} from his {{IconLink|Slay}} effect, this won't matter too much, and the {{IconLink|Multistrike}} can mean you'll get more kills to replace that. Mixing the '''Reaper''' line and the '''Wrathful''' line is very much not recommended, as '''Wrathful''' is intended to be a front line unit while '''Reaper''' is not. Mixing in a '''Brawler''' upgrade is worth strongly considering, especially without other sources of {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, as '''Wrathful III''' only gains 1 more {{IconLink|Rage}} on {{IconLink|Revenge}}, so '''Wrathful II''' with {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}} actually scales much faster offensively, and it can help '''Wrathful''' '''Hornbreaker Prince''' scale quickly defensively if it can get multiple kills without sacrificing too much initial longevity. == Quotes == '''Summoned''' * ''For Grrrg!'' * ''For the Hellhorned!'' * ''Hellhorned, rally to me!'' * ''I could always use another trophy!'' * ''It's gonna be a bumpy ride!'' * ''You will fear the Hellhorned!'' All of her paths revolve around [[Imps]], either producing them, killing them, or becoming stronger when they're played. Her starter card is [[Queen's Impling]]. == Light Forge Upgrades == {{ChampionPaths |baseStats=10/10 |a=Imp Parade |a1stats=30/15 |a1abilities={{IconLink|Resolve}}: Add a '''[[Queen's Impling]]''' to your hand.

Deal 60 damage per [[:Category:Imp_units|Imp]] to enemy units.}} }} == Strategy== '''Shardtail Queen''' focuses heavily on [[Imp]] spamming and management. She generally synergizes well with clans that also use chump cards, such as the [[Melting Remnant]] and [[Lazarus League]], as well as {{Capacity}} increase and card copying tech to get as many Imps into her deck as possible. Ultimately, she's an extremely situational Champion that requires both set-up and specific cards to show up to make good use out of. Particularly at higher Covenants, [[Hornbreaker Prince]] is a much more reliable choice. ===Imp Parade=== This path gives you a way to put a steady stream of Imps on the battlefield. This can have a decent amount of utility in chump blocking enemies. In early Rings, you can dent enemy units with [[Queen's Impling]], and in later waves you can scale the floor with {{IconLink|Rage}} from [[Fledgling Imp]]. If you go all the way into III, you add [[Welder Helper]]s, who can either tank enemy fire better directly in e.g. the [[Clash with the Titans|Titans]] fight, or, if you have ways of killing them yourself, bulk up your frontline with {{IconLink|Armor}}. Unfortunately, all of this takes quite a bit of setup, and it can be difficult to justify. You'll need to be careful to make sure that you have space to play your Imps and that they die. [[Imp-portant Work]] and [[Imp-pressive]] can be very helpful for this purpose. And [[Imp-olate]] is a decent payoff, scaling as the fight goes on. It can be quite difficult to play [[Fledgling Imp]] on a floor with enough beneficiaries, and it requires that you actually have {{Capacity}} to play them, ruling out floor overstacking in particular. If you aren't able to play your Imps, they'll gum up your deck. You will probably need to take [[Heaven's Light]] to make sure you have room. Especially given how difficult it can be to take advantage of [[Welder Helper]] at times, you can consider cross-pathing into either '''Royalty''' or '''Imperialist''', the latter being a particular help in clearing your own imps, though the stat gain of III is particularly nice. ===Royalty=== This is a difficult path to use. The idea is to put your Imps and other expendable bodies in front of her to build up her power and protect her, then unleash her at the end. But ultimately, she's not going to perform very well against bosses unless she has defense, and it's hard to put both a tank and several cheap bodies in front of her. This variant is especially vulnerable in Ring 1, as you often just won't have a way to address this in that fight. Like '''Imp Parade''', you'll need {{Capacity}} to do this well, though you might be able to use [[Hidden Passage]] to move '''Shardtail Queen''' herself to a more protected floor once the boss is coming. You'll need the cheap bodies too - while she starts with [[Queen's Impling]], you'll want more powerful Imps / other expendable units from your partner clan. It's a good idea to find good units to apply {{IconLink|Endless}} to, either by imps or from your partner clan, and means of sacrificing them, such as [[Imp-portant Work]] and [[Imp-pressive]]. The imps' own {{IconLink|Summon}} abilities can add utility here too. [[Shardtail Queen]]'s {{Attack}} can get quite high if you do this right - you'll also want sources of {{IconLink|Multistrike}} like [[Onehorn's Tome]] or from equipment to really make the most of this. It's worth mentioning that this line is crazy strong with the the [[Underlegion]]'s [[Spawn]] mechanic, as they trigger {{IconLink|Rally}} easily without need to worry about {{Capacity}}. However, she needs {{IconLink|Multistrike}} to make the most of this, and the only sources naturally available in that clan combination are the aforementioned Onehorn's Tome and [[Void Armament]], so keep an eye out for those cards. It is also strong with lots of [[Morsels|Morsel]] generation, and unlike the Underlegion the [[Umbra]] can give her both {{IconLink|Multistrike}} and {{IconLink|Trample}} via [[Furnace Tap]] and [[Umbra Stone]]. You can cross-path either into '''Imp Parade''' (if you need more imps) or '''Imperialist''' (if you need a way to clear imps and backliners). ===Imperialist=== One way to think about '''Imperialist''' is that, as long as you have Imps to play, it's as if '''Shardtail Queen''' has an attack with {{IconLink|Quick}} and {{IconLink|Sweep}} which also kills your own imps. '''Imperialist''' is probably the easiest line to get into, as it doesn't make as many demands on your {{Capacity}}, and gives you a built-in way to clear your imps while also clearing out backliners - no need for [[Imp-pressive]] or [[Imp-portant Work]]. It also gives '''Shardtail Queen''' respectable stats - she can take hits and with her ability deals respectable damage. The issue with this line is that it ultimately has no route to being able to do much of anything against bosses (or the [[Avowed Gladiator]]s you'll eventually face), and like the other lines, requires you to be constantly playing imps for it to function. So again, you're not overstacking floors. As with '''Royalty''', you'll need a source of Imps to use this ability consistently; adding {{IconLink|Endless}} to one that supplements your build is a nice way to do this, and can add some utility (e.g. with [[Molting Imp]]) and/or bulk ([[Welder Helper]]) to the floor. Welder Helper is a particularly good card for '''Imperialist''', as it can keep '''Shardtail Queen''' alive, and you can kill it off every turn guaranteed, which can otherwise be difficult. Ultimately, the floor with '''Shardtail Queen''' usually has to be a supplementary floor that clears backliners for your true boss-killing floor, and it can be difficult to build two good floors. Still, it does clear nasty backliners like [[Ragewing Assassin]], [[Discordant Heretic]], and [[Chosen Assassin]] in the lategame, lessening the need for defense on your upper floors. However, [[Deafening Herald]]s will disable '''Imp Toss''', and [[Deformed Duo]]s will survive thanks to {{IconLink|Reanimate}} regardless of how many Imps you kill, as the damage is all done at once. Setting up this ability to work well often ends up being harder than simply playing an [[Inferno Room]], though unlike that room it does prevent [[Terrifying Amalgam]] from hitting your Pyre. This champion line can cross with the other two lines, with this line largely serving as a way of clearing out imps and giving supplementary utility to the other line. '''Queen's Impling''' is [[Shardtail Queen]]'s starter card. When played, it deals 16 damage to the front enemy.

== Strategy == 
'''Queen's Impling''' can both provide some solid chip damage and chump blocking early in the game if played correctly. It also has plenty of synergy with all of Shardtail Queen's paths, though its limitations are what make Shardtail Queen hard to play a lot of the time. Its 16 damage is best used as additional support for other damage sources, rather than as a damage solution on its own. Like all Imps, it can "charge up" [[Transcendimp]], though its effect is generally not very strong by the time you're likely to see such a rare card.

Even early in the game, it can be unwieldy at times, since it isn't always going to die. While having a couple of these in front of your unit can protect you from standard enemies in the early game, it won't provide enough protection against bosses most of the time, and having these on the floor can prevent you from being able to place a tankier unit like a [[Shield Steward]] or a more damage-dealing unit like a [[Spear Steward]]. You'll often want to refrain from playing these as early as ring 2 or 3.

How much of a purge priority these are depends on your ability to kill them and manage {{Capacity}}. A chump blocker can be useful into the lategame (e.g. against the [[Titans]]), and Shardtail Queen can still interact with them. If you have Imp sacrifice effects you've leaned into like [[Imp-portant Work]] they can remain moderately useful, but their ability to take up {{Capacity}} without doing much else is hard to tolerate then. Ideally, you've found Imps that have more of an impact later in the game.

== Recommended Upgrades ==
None, as ideally this unit isn't sticking around in a fight (and possibly not in your deck, either).

* Queen's Impling in Monster Train 1 had the same stats, but a weaker {{IconLink|Summon}} effect, dealing only 10 damage to the front enemy unit.

While [[Alpha Fiend]]'s {{Health|25}} looks respectable on first glance, he's quite fragile in practice. As he has {{Capacity|3}}, it's hard to place units defend him - in particular, if you start with him, you can't defend him with a [[Shield Steward]] - and you'll want to upgrade his offense given his abilities. Thankfully, the [[Hellhorned]] are good at floor overstacking with cards like [[Hidden Passage]], and '''Alpha Fiend''' very much appreciates a floor full of company. On a well-defended floor, '''Alpha Fiend''' scales without need for specific spell help from the player. This can make it a reasonable duplication target as well, provided you can manage its {{DeploymentEmber}} and {{Capacity}} costs. It can sometimes compete with other units and possibly its copies for targets to {{IconLink|Strike}}, but in key lategame fights like [[Seraph]] and the [[Titans]], there's plenty of enemies to hit, including bosses. The biggest issue in using '''Alpha Fiend''' is that it takes time to ramp up, and there is not very much you can do to accelerate his damage output. As a result, early waves may escape relatively unscathed, and in certain fights this can be extremely dangerous. For example, it is quite difficult to get '''Alpha Fiend''' strong enough to handle Wave 2 of [[Cael, Lord of the Cherubs#Vampiric_Feed|Vampiric Feed]], which features a [[Scarred Sentinel]], a [[Chosen Bastion]], and a [[Vampiric Cherub]]; if Cael himself buffs the bottom floor that turn, that wave can reach your Pyre at full health and with upwards of {{Attack|70}}, which is usually an immediate game over. As such, it is of utmost importance to have some method of defeating or minimizing the effects of early waves, such as [[Tiresome Climb]] to apply {{IconLink|Dazed}}. Effects that allow '''Alpha Fiend''' to attack before its normal turn, like [[Eagleheart]] or [[Minds Of Their Own]], should be upgraded with {{IconLink|Seekstone}} if at all possible to get its scaling off the ground. [[Iron-tongue]] has an interesting interaction with '''Alpha Fiend'''. The {{IconLink|Sweep}} it grants allows '''Alpha Fiend''' to get many more {{IconLink|Strike}} triggers than it would otherwise in most combats - but it locks its damage to a pedestrian {{Attack|30}}, so the {{IconLink|Strike}} trigger is irrelevant. However, if you then '''remove''' Iron-tongue, [[Alpha Fiend]]'s {{Attack}} will skyrocket, since all of those {{IconLink|Strike}} triggers did functionally apply. This means it can sometimes be worthwhile to equip Iron-tongue to '''Alpha Fiend''' during the Deployment phase and aim to remove it by turn 2. However, for this to be reliable, you either need a lot of replacement equipment (perhaps from [[Erratic Assistant]]s) or a thin deck; otherwise '''Alpha Fiend''' may be stuck at {{Attack|30}} for far longer than you are comfortable with. If you happen to have '''Superfood''' [[Primordium]] as your champion, Iron-tongue is the absolute jackpot; Primordium can transfer {{IconLink|Sweep}} to '''Alpha Fiend''' without the damage cap, creating one of the most broken units in the game. Even failing that, transferring additional {{IconLink|Multistrike}} stacks through a card like [[Void Armament]] can be nearly as powerful. One specific matchup to beware is [[Seraph Aeternus-The Entropic]] - if '''Alpha Fiend''' is {{IconLink|Sap}}ped to {{Attack|0}}, it will stop scaling, and potentially get stuck there. This can really be a problem if you take his Titan Trial and play [[Curse of Entropy]]. If that's your Seraph, it might not be a bad idea to pack a little bit of initial {{Attack}} support like a [[Ritual of Battle]] to make sure you can get your first few {{IconLink|Strike}} triggers. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! {{UnitCard |name = Branded Warrior |image = PLR BrandedWarrior.png |clan = Hellhorned |rarity = Uncommon |type = Demon |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = {{AttackHealth|20|8}} |ability = {{IconLink|Rage|5}}.

Though I can't say I'm seeking out that opportunity... |artist = Loy Bouttamy }} '''Branded Warrior''' is an uncommon [[Hellhorned]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever it kills an enemy, it grants {{IconLink|Rage|5}} to all friendly units on the floor, including itself. == Strategy == '''Branded Warrior''' is a classic feast or famine card: its effect is exceptionally powerful, but it can be difficult to trigger {{IconLink|Slay}} consistently on the higher [[Rings]], and missing a {{IconLink|Slay}} trigger can be disastrous if you are relying on the provided {{IconLink|Rage}} to scale, as it can lead to a snowball effect. As such, when building around '''Branded Warrior''', effectively managing enemy {{Health}} is vital - you must ensure that you are picking up as many {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers as possible, especially on the first turns of combat. There are a few ways to accomplish this. The most obvious is through {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, either from {{IconLink|Frenzystone}}, cards like [[Onehorn's Tome]], or [[Grrrg's Goad]]. Even a single stack of {{IconLink|Multistrike}} dramatically increases '''Branded Warrior''''s effectiveness, giving it twice as much damage for killing heavy units, or letting it kill two units in one attack. {{IconLink|Rage}} applicators, like [[Ritual of Battle]] and [[Dark Deal]], should be focused on '''Branded Warrior''', as it needs as much {{Attack}} as possible to guarantee {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers; the rest of your units can get their {{IconLink|Rage}} from it. [[Last Stand]] works exceptionally well with '''Branded Warrior''' - it doubles its natural {{IconLink|Rage}} as well as the {{IconLink|Rage}} on all allies, making it easier to get kills. Another way to ensure that '''Branded Warrior''' gets its {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers is by having multiple copies on the same floor. This is easier than usual with the Hellhorned due to their access to '''[[Ascend]]''' cards like [[Hidden Passage]]. This strategy can also be used to overstack the floor and thus increase the number of recipients of its {{IconLink|Rage}}, or to isolate weak backline units that '''Branded Warrior''' can pick off, especially when made {{IconLink|Quick}}. The [[Resonant Shard]] artifact makes '''Branded Warrior''' quite a bit stronger and helps it more easily reach the breakpoints necessary to trigger {{IconLink|Slay}}. Similarly, having [[Deranged Brute]] as an ally makes {{IconLink|Rage}} much more potent, increasing the unit's potential tremendously. Although an unorthodox strategy, with certain clans, '''Branded Warrior''' can trigger {{IconLink|Slay}} even more efficiently: with {{IconLink|Spikes}}. Units that die to {{IconLink|Spikes}} count towards {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers, so when playing with the [[Awoken]] or the [[Lazarus League]], '''Branded Warrior''' can kill off backline units without even attacking and apply huge amounts of {{IconLink|Rage}} to your floor. The obvious problem, of course, is that '''Branded Warrior''' has only {{Health|8}}. With the Awoken, you can increase its {{Health}} with artifacts like [[Emblem of the Exiles]] and cards like [[Awakening Thicket]] while applying {{IconLink|Spikes}} with cards like [[Pyre Shards]]. With Lazarus League, you can rely on {{IconLink|Reanimate}} stacks to keep it alive instead, and pair it with [[Organ Harvester]] and [[Faulty Body]] or [[Madman Infusion]]s. In either case, you can also supplement its defenses with {{IconLink|Armor}} cards like [[Alloy of the Ancients]] and [[Enflame]]. Lastly, while technically not {{IconLink|Spikes}}, the [[Shield of Wyngh]] from the [[Banished]] clan provides essentially the same effect, and you can use {{IconLink|Valor}}, [[Martyr's Signet]], and [[Talos]]'s '''Enchantress''' path to improve its durability. Certain equipment is extremely helpful in letting '''Branded Warrior''' get its {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers. [[Iron-tongue]] is extremely strong thanks to granting {{IconLink|Sweep}}, especially when combined with {{IconLink|Quick}} and either {{IconLink|Multistrike}} (to kill [[Chosen Assassin]]s and get extra kills on [[Deformed Duo]]s) or {{IconLink|Dualism}} (if the increased {{IconLink|Rage}} application is more important). However, because Iron-tongue locks the unit's damage to {{Attack|30}}, using '''Branded Warrior''' in this way relegates it entirely to backline clear and support, and it must have at least one but preferably two powerful allies to take advantage of its {{IconLink|Rage}}. With the [[Umbra]], [[Glutton's Maw]] also allows '''Branded Warrior''' to trigger {{IconLink|Slay}} once per turn by killing non-Morsel units like [[Imps]], while simultaneously boosting its poor {{Health}}. With the [[Pyreborne]], the [[Cursed Dragonstaff]]'s area of effect damage will count as a {{IconLink|Slay}} trigger for anything that it kills. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! {{UnitCard |name = Demon Fiend |image = PLR DemonFiend.png |clan = Hellhorned |rarity = Uncommon |type = Demon |banner = Yes |cost = 4 |size = 3 |stats = 60/60 |ability = {{IconLink|Trample}}. |flavor = These demons, rumored to be the most ancient among the Hellhorned, do not speak in any known tongue. Thankfully, they have a natural proclivity for fighting making communication unnecessary. |artist = Daniel Sarmiento Chuquisengo }} The '''Demon Fiend''' is an uncommon [[Hellhorned]] [[banner unit]]. Though highly expensive, it has excellent stats and the coveted {{IconLink|Trample}}. == Strategy == Despite '''Demon Fiend''' being one of the most expensive units in the game (tied with [[Shadowsiege]], [[Consumer of Crowns]], and [[Deathmetal Hymnist]]), the difficulty of playing it is often well worth the reward. As the only unit in the game to inherently possess {{IconLink|Trample}}, none of its damage output is wasted on overkill, allowing it to crush the fragile backliners that often lurk behind heavy enemies. {{Attack|60}} may seem unimpressive in later rings, but the Hellhorned have the best {{IconLink|Rage}} generation of any clan, and can quickly rocket its damage up. Cards like [[Ritual of Battle]], [[Fledgling Imp]], and [[Dark Deal]] are never wasted on '''Demon Fiend''', and it is the best recipient in the clan of {{IconLink|Rage}} amplifiers like [[Deranged Brute]] and [[Last Stand]]. Any source of {{IconLink|Multistrike}} is valuable on '''Demon Fiend''', as doubling its damage output makes it much more realistic for it to take down enemies like [[Avowed Gladiator]]s. {{IconLink|Frenzystone}} is the most common method, but [[Grrrg's Goad]], [[Void Armament]], and [[Onehorn's Tome]] are all viable as well. Having more hits also makes '''Demon Fiend''' safer against units with {{IconLink|Reanimate}} like [[Undying Wretch]]es and [[Deformed Duo]]s. {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} is extremely desirable for units with {{IconLink|Trample}}, as the multiplicative damage results in lots of overkill that then spreads to the units behind. This makes [[Railbeater]] a fantastic support unit for '''Demon Fiend'''. Upgrading Railbeater with {{IconLink|Dualstone}} and {{IconLink|Titanstone}} makes it a very durable tank, with {{IconLink|Titanite}} and {{IconLink|Armor|60}}, and further causes it to apply {{IconLink|Melee Weakness|2}} on {{IconLink|Strike}}, tripling [[Demon Fiend]]'s damage. Outside of Railbeater, the only sources of {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} are the [[Banished]] clan, [[Enfeebling Infusion]]s, and the {{IconLink|Dominating Control}} upgrade. [[Talos]]'s '''Celestial Radiance''' path can apply absurd amounts of {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} to enemy units, as can [[Wyngh's Radiance]]. [[Avenger]] can fulfill the role of tank instead of Railbeater, but note that Avenger is more expensive and must be made {{IconLink|Quick}} by some means, as otherwise its own attack will consume the {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} meant for '''Demon Fiend'''. Effects that trigger on {{IconLink|Slay}} are worthwhile on '''Demon Fiend''' due to its ability to kill whole waves alone when sufficiently supported. [[Bloodsoaked Arena]] lets '''Demon Fiend''' accumulate lots of {{IconLink|Valor}}, which both scales up its damage and provides it with free {{IconLink|Armor}}, making it far more durable. [[Organ Harvester]] does not bolster its damage, but does grant it stacks of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} to ensure it doesn't die. Both the [[Bloodthirsty Blade]] and [[Pyre of Savagery]] grant a permanent {{Attack|+1}} on {{IconLink|Slay}}, giving it a method to snowball from earlier combats; [[Blood of the Apex]] is the same, but works with any Equipment and grants {{Attack|+2}}. The [[Consumed Crown]] and [[Shadow's Sheath]] both effectively grant {{Attack|+3}} per {{IconLink|Slay}}, and Shadow's Sheath also grants {{IconLink|Stealth}} as a defensive measure, which is especially useful against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]]. [[Volatile Gauge]] is usually a terrific pick with '''Demon Fiend'''. Not only will it always reduce the unit's cost, it also benefits several of its most synergistic cards, like the aforementioned Ritual of Battle and Last Stand. For obvious reasons, it also benefits greatly from sources of extra {{DeploymentEmber}}, like [[Artificial Pyrestone]], [[Herzal's Horde]], or [[Pyre Chomper]] with [[Departure Manifest]]. These can let you play both '''Demon Fiend''' and its supporting units or equipment. [[Demon Fiend]]'s extremely high base stats make [[Cavendish]] unusually powerful (so long as it does not self-destruct!), as it will start at {{Attack|180}}, enough to instantly kill a [[Celestial Bastion]] or a [[Ravenous Zealot]]. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! Its main draw is its natural {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. == Strategy == '''Horned Warrior''' is a simple backline damage dealer that has solid up-front early game damage while also having innate {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}}, making your damage scaling twice as effective. It can be compared to [[Animus of Will]]; '''Horned Warrior''' has slightly higher base {{Attack}}, but Animus of Will has an extra {{IconLink|Multistrike}} stack. This usually makes Animus of Will the better choice in a vacuum, but practically speaking, Animus of Will's best in-clan {{Attack}} scaling comes from [[Razorsharp Edge]], while the Hellhorned have lots of access to {{IconLink|Rage}}, including potent cards like [[Ritual of Battle]] and [[Fledgling Imp]]. It's great as part of a floor overstacking strategy with cards like [[Hidden Passage]]. Its low {{Health}} means it should be in the back, and you should have a plan for how to keep it alive against enemies with {{IconLink|Sweep}} or backline {{IconLink|Corruption}}. {{IconLink|Spikes}} are also an issue, especially against [[Penitent Prayerstone]]s. While it doesn't have the blowout potential of units like [[Demon Fiend]], [[Alpha Fiend]], or [[Branded Warrior]], it's much less unwieldy. It only costs {{Ember|1}} to play and takes up only {{Capacity|2}}, and it is not reliant on getting {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers to have value like Branded Warrior. This makes it a solid survival pick in the early game, and a good recipient of cheap or otherwise undesirable shop upgrades like {{IconLink|Largestone}} and {{IconLink|Furystone}}. In Ring 1, it can do decent damage to the boss if you can place it behind a relatively healthy [[Shield Steward]], even if your [[Champion]] is weak. Its [[:Category:Demon_units|Demon]] typing can give it an additional stack of {{IconLink|Multistrike}} with [[Grrrg's Goad]]. {{UnitCard |name = Railbeater |image = PLR Railbeater.png |clan = Hellhorned |rarity = Uncommon |type = Demon |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 10/10 |ability = {{IconLink|Armor|30}}.

Not to mention, they're a fantastic help in the construction of our Rail. |artist = Gary Laib }} The '''Railbeater''' is an uncommon [[Hellhorned]] [[banner unit]]. It enters with {{IconLink|Armor|30}} and applies {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} on {{IconLink|Strike}}. == Strategy == '''Railbeater''' is a flexible unit that can serve a number of roles within the Hellhorned clan. {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} is a potent debuff, making the unit a viable carry despite its low {{Attack}}, or letting it be one of the most useful supporting tanks in the game, similar to [[Avenger]]. There are two main ways to take advantage of '''Railbeater''' - it can use its own {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} to multiply its damage output with {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, or it can provide a single hit and set up the unit behind it for a devastating blow. Which option you pick may depend on your other banner units, the artifacts you have, or the upgrades you are offered in shops. '''Railbeater''' takes almost every major upgrade at the [[Merchant of Steel]] extremely well, making those shops overall more valuable. Due to its {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} application, every stack of {{IconLink|Multistrike}} on the unit is equivalent to {{IconLink|Multistrike|2}} (or '''3''' if you have {{IconLink|Dualism}}), which makes stacking {{IconLink|Rage}} on it through cards like [[Ritual of Battle]] an effective way of scaling your damage output. [[Grrrg's Goad]] is an incredible artifact for virtually any Hellhorned unit, and '''Railbeater''' may be rivalled only by [[Alpha Fiend]] for the greatest beneficiary of it among the Uncommon units. Similarly, [[Onehorn's Tome]] is more effective on '''Railbeater''' than other units due to its natural {{IconLink|Armor}} protecting it from {{IconLink|Fragile}}. However, be aware that this only applies when '''Railbeater''' is striking the same unit over and over; its damage output drops sharply each time it gets a kill, as it must then apply {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} to its next target with its subsequent attack. As such, the unit falters somewhat against waves where low {{Health}} units like [[Misshapen Fiend]]s block the way to the tank units behind them. Conversely, it is tremendously effective during {{IconLink|Relentless}}, rapidly chewing through even the sturdiest bosses. However, certain units can take advantage of {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} more than '''Railbeater''' itself. [[Demon Fiend]] is the prime example due to its natural {{IconLink|Trample}}. Unlike other units, the increased damage output it gets from {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} will never be wasted on overkill and instead spill out to crush the enemies behind. While not as effective as Demon Fiend, [[Branded Warrior]] and [[Hornbreaker Prince]]'s '''Reaper''' path can both benefit from {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} as a way to ensure they get their {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers. In these cases, '''Railbeater''' serves as a solid tank that sets its more offensively-inclined allies up for success. Because '''Railbeater''' effectively has {{Health|40}}, it is quite durable for a Hellhorned unit. Further, unlike units with raw health totals, the {{IconLink|Armor}} it starts with can be doubled by {{IconLink|Dualism}} or [[Reinforce]], and it can more safely be made {{IconLink|Fragile}}, enabling it to take advantage of [[Glass Cannon]] and the aforementioned Onehorn's Tome. '''Railbeater''' is a very good user of [[Iron-tongue]]. Aside from granting {{IconLink|Sweep}} and thus letting the unit pull double-duty as backline clear, it also causes '''Railbeater''' to apply {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} to all enemy units instead of just the frontmost one, which helps a lot when clearing waves with multiple tanks. It also has a specific use against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Entropic]], as the {{IconLink|Sap}} applied will normally reduce [[Railbeater]]'s {{Attack}} to 0, preventing it from attacking and applying {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} at all. Since Iron-tongue locks the unit to {{Attack|30}}, it grants immunity to {{IconLink|Sap}} and ensures '''Railbeater''' can always apply {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}}. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade !
