{{UnitCard |name = Transcendimp |image = PLR Transcendimp.png |clan = Hellhorned |rarity = Rare |type = Imp |banner = No |cost = {{Ember|2}} |size = {{Capacity|1}} |stats = {{AttackHealth|1|1}} |ability = When played, repeat all {{IconLink|Summon}} effects triggered so far this battle. |flavor = ''When a demon dies under the weight of their horns, they are reborn as impish infants, restarting their molting cycle. These imps are quite possibly the most powerful Hellhorned in existence - seeing all that has come before and all that will come after. While this power is lost upon their first molting, they've been crucial in my research of their Ring.'' |artist = Loy Bouttamy }} The '''Transcendimp''' is a rare [[Hellhorned]] unit. When played, it repeats all {{IconLink|Summon}} effects triggered so far in the battle. Although it interacts with {{IconLink|Summon}} triggers, unlike other [[Imp]]s, its ability occurs "when played", and is not a {{IconLink|Summon}} trigger itself. This prevents '''Transcendimp''' from exponentially scaling with its own trigger. == Strategy == '''Transcendimp''' is one of the strongest cards in the game for any build based around Imps, repeating all previously played Imp units when played. This allows it to be one of the most powerful cards in the game once "charged up" properly, potentially wiping out backliners, applying {{IconLink|Rage}} and {{IconLink|Armor}} to other units, and supplying more {{Ember}} than you can ever need with a single card play. Due to its power, {{IconLink|Endless}} is an extremely high priority, alongside a way to quickly kill it such as [[Imp-portant Work]] or '''Imperialist''' [[Shardtail Queen]]. It is often worth playing Imps on empty floors if they cannot fit elsewhere, simply to add their effects to future plays of '''Transcendimp'''. It can become even stronger with units from allied clans which have {{IconLink|Summon}} triggers, as it is not limited to copying Imps. See below for more notes on its interactions. It is also extremely strong with [[Melting Remnant]], due to the relative ease of killing and resummoning it. Combining {{IconLink|Immortalstone}} and {{IconLink|Wickstone}} allows it to die and return to the top of the deck every turn. An {{IconLink|Endless}} '''Transcendimp''' alongside another {{IconLink|Endless}} {{IconLink|Summon}} unit, with both dying every turn, can scale the Imp up over the course of the battle. Each time they are played, '''Transcendimp''' will trigger the other unit's effect an additional time. [[Transcendimp]]'s ability isn't stopped by {{IconLink|Silence}}. Playing it on the same floor as a [[Deafening Herald]] will still trigger its ability. ==Interactions== * '''Transcendimp''' will copy other clans' {{IconLink|Summon}} effects, and can gain large amounts of stats by doing so (e.g. [[Awoken Hollow]], [[Greed Dragon]]). ** [[Greed Dragon]]'s {{IconLink|Summon}} effect can be especially powerful, as the stats will be added to the unit and are retained when it is killed. '''[[Sacrifice|Sacrificing]]''' an {{IconLink|Endless}} '''Transcendimp''' can allow it to repeatedly gain the bonus stats based on [[Dragon's Hoard]]. ** '''Architect''' [[Penumbra]] adds {{Capacity}} to a room, making it easy to massively increase the size of a floor (or even all floors) by repeatedly playing '''Transcendimp'''. ** [[Lady Gilda]]'s '''Gildmother''' path will cause '''Transcendimp''' to summon a [[Gilded Egg]] and then '''[[Retreat]]'''. ** [[Dante the Dependable]] will cause '''Transcendimp''' to add another [[Dante's Candle]] to the deck, then gain {{IconLink|Multistrike}} stacks. * {{IconLink|Summon}} effects from rooms like [[Electricity Chamber]] and [[Reanimation Lab]] will also be applied, once for each time a unit has been played in that room. * Artifacts with {{IconLink|Summon}} effects, such as [[Sapsuckling Spring]], will trigger once for each previous activation. * If a copy of '''Transcendimp''' is created, such as with [[Hall of Mirrors]], it will '''not''' copy previous triggers, as it is not technically played. * '''Transcendimp''' is unaffected by {{IconLink|Silence}}, since its effect isn't technically a trigger. * A unit like [[Welder Helper]] or [[Fledgling Imp]] with {{IconLink|Dualism}} will not cause '''Transcendimp''' to apply double status effects. ** However, a '''Transcendimp''' with {{IconLink|Dualism}} ''will'' apply double status effects, whether or not the original {{IconLink|Summon}} effect did so. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! {{UnitCard |name = Apex Imp |image = PLR_ApexImp.png |clan = Hellhorned |rarity = Rare |type = Demon Imp |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 10/10 |ability = {{IconLink|Armored}}: Gain {{IconLink|Rage}} equal to gained {{IconLink|Armor}}.

Their existence in a sort of “transition state,” however, is rarely seen. These Imps, almost Demons, exhibit reserved behavior and a sort of misplaced confidence that I’ve only seen in human adolescents on their way to adulthood. I can understand the Hellhorned’s hesitance to make these Imps known... |artist = Jordan Thomas }} '''Apex Imp''' is a rare [[Hellhorned]] [[banner unit]]. He has a triggered ability upon being {{IconLink|Armored}} - he gains an equal amount of {{IconLink|Rage}}. == Strategy == The '''Apex Imp''' is one of the strongest units in the game due to his ability to convert defense to offense. With any reasonably strong source of {{IconLink|Armor}}, he can gain massive amounts of {{IconLink|Rage}}, allowing him to act as both a tank and a damage dealer. {{IconLink|Armor}} is generally applied in greater amounts than {{IconLink|Rage}}, which is what makes him such a strong scaler - compare the effect of [[Fledgling Imp]] to [[Welder Helper]], for example. Once you have an '''Apex Imp''', your main priority should be giving him as much {{IconLink|Armor}} as possible through cards like Welder Helper, [[Alloy of the Ancients]], [[Steelworker]], and especially [[Reinforce]]. Applying {{IconLink|Multistrike}} and/or {{IconLink|Trample}} is also important. Due to the ludicrous amounts of {{IconLink|Armor}} he will ideally receive, he makes a fantastic target for [[Onehorn's Tome]], since the {{IconLink|Fragile}} effect will be irrelevant; however, this means you cannot target him with [[Branding Rite]] anymore, so keep that in mind. With a strong enough supporting deck, '''Apex Imp''' can win the entire game, wiping out entire waves while remaining virtually invincible. He works especially well with clans like [[Banished]] and [[Luna Coven]] which have ways to apply even more {{IconLink|Armor}}. With the [[Pyreborne]], [[Smelted Treasure]] is an extremely powerful {{IconLink|Armor}} application, especially when upgraded with {{IconLink|Stackstone}}, just so long as you have the {{Gold}} to fund it. He is often worthwhile as a speculative pick even if you have not been offered any {{IconLink|Armor}} cards, but be wary of investing too heavily into him in that case. His {{IconLink|Summon}} effect does not provide enough {{IconLink|Armor}} on its own for him to be relevant, essentially making him a {{AttackHealth|20|15}} unit that degrades over time. If you were not offered Welder Helper or [[Fortified Pauldrons]] in your common drafts or Steelworker from a unit banner, he may not be able to participate much against the first boss fight. If you spent all your {{Gold}} upgrading him and do not have other paths to victory, this can lead to an early loss. If he is partnered with Steelworker, or another floorwide {{IconLink|Armor}} source like [[Divine Dancer]] or [[Makeshift Golem]], he is an excellent duplication target at [[Empyrean Well]]s. But if you are relying on single-target sources of {{IconLink|Armor}} like [[March of Shields]] or Reinforce, this becomes less effective as an option, and you may be better off duplicating your {{IconLink|Armor}} applicators instead. One detail you could overlook: as he is an [[:Category:Imp_units|Imp]], the '''Imperialist''' path on [[Shardtail Queen]] will treat him like any other Imp and kill him instantly. Even with {{IconLink|Endless}} or another way to bring him back, he'll lose the {{IconLink|Rage}} and {{IconLink|Armor}} that he's stacked up, which means it's rarely worth it just for a small amount of extra damage to the floor. Place him on a different floor if you want him to survive. He'll also affect the strength of [[Imp-olate]]. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! However, it also has {{Capacity|3}} and {{Ember|4}}, meaning it'll be hard to play other units with it, and while {{Health|40}} isn't terrible, it isn't able to tank on its own. However, its ability is where it shines the most, allowing it to attack over and over again provided you have [[Imps]] to give it. One way to think about its ability is to treat it as if it has {{IconLink|Quick}} and gains {{IconLink|Burst|1}} whenever you play an Imp on its floor. So having steady access to [[Imps]], such as by starting with [[Queen's Impling]], having an {{IconLink|Endless}} Imp, or finding a way of generating Imps like [[Imp-cicle]] or [[Shardtail Queen]]'s '''Imp Parade''' line, is ideal if you want to draft this high-investment unit. [[Welder Helper]] is a noteworthy companion to this unit, as it helps '''Consumer of Crowns''' tank while '''Consumer of Crowns''' helps Welder Helper die. The [[Melting Remnant]] is a particularly powerful partner for '''Consumer of Crowns''', as it can kill an [[Imp]] to use its ability, and then that Imp can immediately be brought back with [[Reform]] to let it attack again thanks to the ability's 0-turn cooldown - as many times as you can [[Reform]]! Similarly the [[Lazarus League]] is a strong partner, as {{IconLink|Reanimate}} allows you to use that ability multiple times on the same Imp. As a [[:Category:Demon units|Demon]] with high {{Attack}} and an ability that allows it to attack more often, [[Grrrg's Goad]] looms as a way to give it additional {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, and it is an ideal target for [[Onehorn's Tome]] if you can find it and manage the {{IconLink|Fragile}} it applies. Alternatively, the enormous base {{Attack}} of the '''Consumer of Crowns''' can make it worth using if you have a way to play it easily. [[Herzal's Horde]] or [[Volatile Gauge]], along with any method of overstacking, can allow you to slot it into the back of the floor relatively easily as an extra stat stick. {{UnitCard |name = Deranged Brute |image = PLR_DerangedBrute.png |clan = Hellhorned |rarity = Rare |type = Demon |banner = Yes |cost ={{Ember|1}} |size ={{Capacity|2}} |stats ={{AttackHealth|10|25}} |ability = {{IconLink|Rage}} on friendly units adds {{Attack|+3}} per stack. |flavor = For a race that is bred on violence, even the Hellhorned have limits to the amount of aggression that is acceptable. But desperate times have forced the Hellhorned to agree to release their most dangerous prisoners. |artist = Daniel Sarmiento Chuquisengo }} The '''Deranged Brute''' is a rare [[Hellhorned]] [[banner unit]]. It amplifies the effect of {{IconLink|Rage}} on friendly units. == Strategy == '''Deranged Brute''' is one of the strongest supporting units available to the Hellhorned, and can also function as a primary damage unit as well, as long as you're able to apply {{IconLink|Rage}}. It causes cards like [[Ritual of Battle]] to provide the equivalent of {{Attack|60}}, rather than {{Attack|24}}, over double the initial effect. {{IconLink|Rage}} is the usual Hellhorned solution to damage scaling, and '''Deranged Brute''' makes this damage plan far more efficient. There are myriad synergies with '''Deranged Brute''', both in and out of clan. In-clan, it's a fantastic partner for [[Branded Warrior]], spiking its initial damage output and making it easier to achieve the {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers it requires. [[Fledgling Imp]] provides {{IconLink|Rage}} to the whole floor, and is an excellent method of scaling, especially if upgraded with {{IconLink|Dualism}} and {{IconLink|Endless}}. {{IconLink|Rage}} applicators like [[Enflame]], [[Rage Serum]], and [[Dark Deal]] should be prioritized; [[Last Stand]] is a particularly effective option and can quickly scale out of control. All of these {{IconLink|Rage}} sources fit well on [[Horned Warrior]] or [[Hornbreaker Prince]]'s '''Brawler''' path, as the damage from {{IconLink|Rage}} is multiplied with each stack of {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. [[Demon Fiend]]'s inherent {{IconLink|Trample}} makes it a potent target for the exponential scaling offered by Last Stand upgraded with {{IconLink|Eternalstone}} and {{IconLink|Keepstone}}, allowing it to wipe out whole waves. Outside of the Hellhorned, it's a strong partner for any unit that relies on {{IconLink|Rage}}, such as [[Nameless Siren]], [[Paraffin Enforcer]], [[Demonic Fledgling]], and [[Big Sludge]]. When partnered with the [[Lazarus League]], it makes good use of [[Goliath Infusion]]s, and the [[Twisted Back]] equipment provides {{IconLink|Rage}} on {{IconLink|Strike}}, along with {{IconLink|Trample}}, which is useful when your damage becomes exceptionally high. [[Replicator Ray]] can also be used to duplicate '''Deranged Brute''' and multiply its effect. More broadly, any unit that benefits greatly from an injection of raw damage works well, as long as you have other Hellhorned cards to apply {{IconLink|Rage}}. Units like [[Hot Head]], [[Animus of Will]], [[Husk Hermit]], [[Plague Doctor]], and [[Dante the Dependable]] can quickly reach enough damage to take out [[Avowed Gladiator]]s this way. Because its effect is not a trigger, it is not suppressed by {{IconLink|Silence}}. Therefore, it's a decent recipient of [[Stoic Platemail]] if you are concerned about its survivability. However, it means that putting the unit in {{IconLink|Stasis}} via [[Stasis Crystal]] will prevent its effect from working, so this is unfortunately not an option for keeping it alive against backline-targeting enemies. '''Deranged Brute''' stacks with itself, so having multiple copies on the floor is viable in order to accelerate your damage output. Note, however, that each additional copy of the unit after the first provides diminishing returns; the first '''Deranged Brute''' increases the output of {{IconLink|Rage}} by 150% ({{Attack|2}} → {{Attack|5}} per stack), while the second one only increases output by 60% ({{Attack|5}} → {{Attack|8}} per stack). If using many copies of the unit, consider putting them in a [[Rage Room]] for a bit of extra damage. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! '''Vent''' is an X cost spell, but you'll usually be playing this for only {{Ember|1}}, or {{Ember|0}} with a damage upgrade. The first few points of damage are by far the most important. I sealed many of them off to all but those who are willing to tear through steel and squeeze through the shreds. |artist = Andrew Vera }} '''Hidden Passage''' is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It [[Ascend]]s a chosen unit. ==Strategy== '''Hidden Passage''' is a simple card, but it represents one of the simplest ways to "break the game" in one of the most fundamental ways: overstacking units on higher floors. When a unit is Ascended, it doesn't check to see if the target floor has {{Capacity}} for the ascended unit. See [[Rising Rage]] for more on this strategy. While this could be considered a "worse" version of [[Rising Rage]], as it doesn't have as much {{IconLink|Shift}} synergy, it's just as good for getting your kill floor together. In some cases, it may actually be better; the lack of an [[Advance]] effect means you can safely add low-{{Health}} support units or glass cannons like [[Horned Warrior]] to the floor without exposing them to danger. Hellhorned units that make particularly good use of a stacked floor include [[Deranged Brute]], [[Steelworker]], and [[Branded Warrior]]. It's also a great way to keep Hellhorned's fragile backliners well-protected. However, using this sort of strategy will lock you out of using [[Imps]], as you will have no {{Capacity}} to play them. While the primary purpose of this card is to move your own units for overstacking purposes, it can also be used to break up particularly troublesome enemy groups by ascending one member to a different floor, potentially exposing enemy backliners. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! It adds 2 random [[:Category:Imp units|Imp units]] to your hand that last for the combat. It is one of three [[Hellhorned]] spells offered by the [[Gremlin Looter]] event. ==Notes== See the [[:Category:Imp units|Imp]] category page for the chance of receiving each type of imp. ==Strategy== '''Imp-in-a-Box''' packs two cards in one, but asks you to adapt to whatever it gives you. Remember that each [[:Category:Imp units|Imp]] will cost {{Capacity|1}} and {{Ember|1}} (with the exception of [[Transcendimp]] costing {{Ember|2}}). So even though this costs {{Ember|0}}, keep this cost in mind; if you don't play both imps it gives you, it no longer has any advantage over a plain Imp in your deck while still having the downside of being random. Ultimately, your deck has to be able to benefit from each of [[Welder Helper]], [[Fledgling Imp]], [[Molting Imp]], and [[Pyre Chomper]], as each imp your receive has a higher than 80% chance of being one of those. Since you'll get [[Welder Helper]] sometimes, a way to kill your own imps, such as [[Imp-pressive]], is important to have with this card. You'll also want to be able to capitalize on [[Pyre Chomper]]'s {{Ember}} surges when you get them, making [[The Unbroken Horn]] valuable with this card. It's particularly good with interactions with {{IconLink|Summon}} triggers and {{IconLink|Rally}} triggers, like [[Ashes of the Fallen]] and [[Transcendimp]]. Each of [[Shardtail Queen]]'s paths interact well with this card as well. '''Imp-in-a-Box''' has little use outside of [[Hellhorned]], as you won't have the imp synergies to make it worthwhile. It is only through dying that Imps can teach Horned.” -excerpt from Hell's Horns by Grrrg Onehorn on the posthumous transfer of knowledge in Hellhorned society. |artist = Loy Bouttamy }} '''Imp-portant Work''' is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It [[Sacrifice]]s the target [[Imp]], and upon doing so draws a card and provides {{Ember|1}}. == Notes == Because of how {{IconLink|Endless}} works, if this is played on an {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Imp]] (and nothing stops it from properly dying like {{IconLink|Reanimate}}), you will immediately draw that Imp from this card's effect. ==Strategy== Because [[Imps]] generally provide a benefit when played but then just take up space on your train, Sacrificing them is usually a benefit, clearing up space for more units to be played. The main downside of this card is that you may draw it with no [[Imps]] in play, making it impossible to play and wasting a draw. If you consistently ''do'' have an [[Imp]] to sacrifice, perhaps because you have [[Imp-cicle]] or [[Shardtail Queen]]'s '''Imp Parade''' path, this is draw-neutral, {{Ember}}-positive, and helps control the [[Imp]] population on the train. It can do more with a single {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Imp]], as it will draw that [[Imp]] and give you the {{Ember}} to play it (with the exception of [[Transcendimp]]), allowing you to immediately replay that [[Imp]], re-activating its {{IconLink|Summon}} trigger. As you upgrade and duplicate this card, you'll be able to further multiply the effects of that {{IconLink|Summon}} trigger, empowering a lot of simple and powerful per-turn strategies, such as empowering your floor with {{IconLink|Rage}} with [[Fledgling Imp]]. It is possible to consistently draw and replay an {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Transcendimp]], allowing you to activate every {{IconLink|Summon}} you've ever triggered each time you play this card, but because [[Transcendimp]] costs {{Ember|2}} this will cost you a net of {{Ember|1}} per use unless you have a way to reduce its cost or produce {{Ember}}. [[Boiler Room]], [[Pyre Chomper]] and [[Shardtail Queen]]'s '''Imp Parade''' path can all be used to either gain {{Ember}} or reduce [[Transcendimp]]'s cost, making this interaction {{Ember}}-neutral or {{Ember}}-positive. There's even an [[Infinite]] that is possible with {{IconLink|Smolderstone}} and [[Impish Scholar]] (or [[Transcendimp]] after playing an [[Impish Scholar]]) - see upgrades for more. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! It targets an [[Imp]] and [[Sacrifice]]s it, then deals 50 damage to the front enemy unit. It has [[Attuned]], gaining 5x damage from [[Magic Power]]. ==Strategy== '''Imp-pressive''' is a reasonably strong spell which benefits significantly from [[Magic Power]], but it is usually not worth taking unless its [[Imp]]-sacrificing effect is a benefit rather than a cost. For decks where Imps are a limited resource, it will have trouble pulling its weight. But in a run where [[Imps]] are plentiful, such as those with [[Imp-cicle]] or [[Shardtail Queen]]'s '''Imp Parade''', clearing them out to make space can be helpful rather than harmful. It can also be used to help recur [[Imps]] you may have applied {{IconLink|Endless}} to. It's not as good as [[Imp-portant Work]] at recurring them, but can be used alongside it as a decent damage spell. It'll dent frontliners like [[Fallen Champion]] and [[Fallen Executioner]], especially with a Magic Power upgrade. As it has the [[Attuned]] keyword, it's particularly strong with {{IconLink|Conduit}}, making it potentially strong in the lategame if allied with the [[Luna Coven]]. Otherwise, its damage becomes less significant in the lategame, and if used as a per-turn strategy with an {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Imp]], it costs you 2 draws per turn, both its own draw and the need to re-draw the [[Imp]], significantly slowing your ability to get through your deck. [[Imp-portant Work]] is therefore much more suited for this purpose, and that can also allow you to replay the {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Imp]] multiple times per turn. Still, it can be used alongside [[Imp-portant Work]] and in runs featuring many [[Imps]] its ability to clear them remains valuable. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Upgrade !! It deals 3 piercing damage to any target, and then, if it survives, grants it {{IconLink|Armor|20}}. ==Strategy== '''Branding Rite''' combines two different effects - inflicting damage and providing {{IconLink|Armor|20}} - in a way that isn't usually synergistic, and it isn't efficient at {{Ember|2}}, either as a buff spell or as a damage spell. It can have some awkward interactions, too: {{IconLink|Fragile}} units can't be buffed by it, and {{IconLink|Conduit}} or other Magic Power buffs can also render it unusable as a buff. It also limits how many times you can use it on your units based on their {{Health}}, as the {{IconLink|Armor}} they get won't save them from the damage of future plays. It makes up for this with its versatility and role compression. It can give your units surivability with {{IconLink|Armor}} or pick off backliners, including [[Purified Soul]] thanks to its [[Piercing]]. It can also pick off your own [[:Category:Imp units|Imps]] that you need to kill. It even has some synergy with healing effects in other clans, giving them something to do in an otherwise {{IconLink|Armor}}-based survivability plan. And in a few cases, you can get value out of both sides of this card. {{IconLink|Revenge}} triggers exemplify this best, and [[Hornbreaker Prince]]'s '''Wrathful''' line is an in-clan example of a great target for this spell. Units with {{IconLink|Reanimate}} that provide a benefit on {{IconLink|Extinguish}} can be another example of how to take advantage of both sides of the card. Ultimately, '''Branding Rite''' provides some role compression, even if the roles it takes are both fairly accessible on the [[Hellhorned]], and it's not the cheapest {{Ember}}-wise. If you can handle its high {{Ember}} cost, either with upgrades or simply by having a lot of {{Ember}}, it can provide solid utility. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Upgrade !! It [[Ascend]]s a unit and applies {{IconLink|Dazed|2}}. ==Strategy== '''Tiresome Climb''' combines two powerful effects into one card. It can end up being less than the sum of its parts at times, but it is very often a good choice. One use that few other cards can replicate is safely [[Ascend]]ing enemies on the third floor to the Pyre room. The {{IconLink|Dazed|2}} means the enemy will take two hits from the Pyre before it gets to do anything - a death sentence for all but the bulkiest of enemies. It can be used as a more-expensive [[Hidden Passage]] with the downside of applying {{IconLink|Dazed}} if used on your units. Although it is by and large worse than Hidden Passage when used this way, if it's what you have and you need floor overstacking, it'll do. See [[Rising Rage]] for ideas. It can also be used as an answer to flying bosses' powerful effects - most notably [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]], but it's strong against all three Seraph variants, as well as [[Cael]] and [[Arkion]]. With {{IconLink|Keepstone}}, it can keep a flying boss on lockdown for the entire fight and buy you several free turns during {{IconLink|Relentless}}. The same can somewhat apply to non-flying bosses, though only if you're mostly set up on higher floors, as they will clear floors they're ascended from. This (along with other [[Ascend]] effects) can be useful as a way of short-circuting {{IconLink|Resolve}} effects on enemies like [[Rax the Overblessed]], and the {{IconLink|Dazed}} it applies prevents even more. Finally, it has the same situational utility as any [[Ascend]] card does for dealing with enemies, with the added benefit of stunning them. This is particularly nice for dealing with enemies that add [[Scourge]]s on upper-floor setups, moving them closer to their death while disabling their meddling simultaneously. It's also a great way to answer specific dangerous enemies - [[Deafening Herald]]s can fly right to the Pyre almost harmlessly, [[Chosen Assassin]]s are much easier to deal with while {{IconLink|Dazed}}, and it can prevent [[Enthralled Ardent]]s (but not [[Chosen Ardent]]s) from triggering {{IconLink|Incant}} on a floor that matters. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! {{SpellCard |name = Battering Ram |image = CRD_BatteringRam.png |clan = [[Hellhorned]] |rarity = Uncommon |cost = 3 |effect = Deal damage to the front enemy unit equal to '''4x''' {{IconLink|Armor}} on friendly units. |flavor = Working with the Railbeaters, I was able to devise a series of interlocking shields that turn the Hellhorned into a mobile battering ram. |artist = Luke Banke }} '''Battering Ram''' is a [[Hellhorned]] spell. It deals a single hit of damage to the front enemy unit equal to four times the total {{IconLink|Armor}} on all friendly units on the floor. ==Strategy== There may be certain runs where '''Battering Ram''' looks like a strong choice for the lategame - for some [[Hellhorned]] builds, you might amass hundreds or even thousands of {{IconLink|Armor}} on a floor, giving it a gaudy damage number. Unfortunately, it's hard to find a situation where it's worth drafting. First of all, it's obviously a poor card in most runs. For any build which cannot stack up enormous quantities of {{IconLink|Armor}}, it is essentially useless, dealing little or no damage. Even if your run seems to be generating decent {{IconLink|Armor}} now, remember that in key fights like [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]], your {{IconLink|Armor}} will be depleted more. It also cannot be used effectively on any floor without heavily armored units, meaning that even in the best possible case, it can only target enemies on a specific floor. The nail in this card's coffin is that even on the builds it does look good on - ones where you have plenty of {{IconLink|Armor}} and the enemies are on the same floor as your armored units - '''Battering Ram''' is still not very good. It only targets the front enemy, meaning that it will often be wasted on a weak enemy rather than targeting the ones you want to hit like [[Avowed Gladiator]]. Even in the perfect situation where it does strike a powerful enemy and you have enough {{IconLink|Armor}} to instantly kill it, it doesn't justify the hoops you had to jump through to get to that situation. Its cost of {{Ember|3}} adds to the difficulty of finding a niche, and unlike most expensive spells, [[Volatile Gauge]] isn't sufficient to save it. One thing this spell can do that is quite impressive is allow some runs to kill bosses in one hit, such as those that have managed to put {{IconLink|Keepstone}} on [[Reinforce]] - there, you can achieve thousands of {{IconLink|Armor}} on a unit. Even if you can do this, you'll need to be able to clear the other enemies to be able to actually hit the boss. This can be immensely satisfying if you can pull it off, putting the exclamation point on a run (that was probably already going to win). == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Upgrade !! It deals 120 [[Piercing]] damage to all units on the floor, including both enemies and friendly units. == Notes == As the Pyre is completely unaffected by spells, this and other "damage all" spells can be played in the Pyre room without damaging your Pyre. ==Strategy== '''Inferno''' is an immensely powerful spell capable of wiping out backliners, dealing massive damage to frontliners, and ignoring effects like {{IconLink|Armor}} and {{IconLink|Spell Shield}} which would stop other spells. Note that the [[Piercing]] effect applies to your units as well. No amount of {{IconLink|Armor}} or {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} will protect them. However, {{IconLink|Reanimate}} can revive a unit killed by '''Inferno''', which allows both your units and certain enemy units, like [[Deformed Duo]], to survive. Its main downside is that it also kills your own units, which in practice requires you to leave an open floor for it, preferably on the bottom floor to pick off backliners (though it can also be used to pick off weakened tanks that escape a bottom-floor setup, especially before Ring 7). The [[Hellhorned]] often leave an empty bottom floor anyway if they're using [[Hidden Passage]] to overstack an upper floor, so for some runs this isn't too much of a cost. Because of the investment of a floor that it requires and its powerful effect, it's good to have a plan to play it just about every turn, either with a small deck or a {{IconLink|Keepstone}}. Once you can use it consistently, it's similar to [[Inferno Room]] in concept, but requires a per-turn investment of a card, {{Ember}}, and likely upgrades. In exchange, it gives you more damage and Piercing, and the ability to play another room on the floor you play it on. The increased damage and Piercing is notable against [[Heaven's Maw#Harbinger of Entropy|Harbinger of Entropy]], which is by far this card's best Seraph matchup. It'll kill [[Purified Soul]], [[Celestial Bastion]], [[Chosen Bastion]], [[Enthralled Ardent]], and even [[Chosen Ardent]] who normally is outside the range of backline removal, leaving only [[Avowed Gladiator]] and maybe low-health [[Scarred Sentinel]]s for your units to deal with. The ability to play another room on its floor notably lets you play [[Boiler Room]] to more-than-offset this card's {{Ember}} cost as you kill enemies. You can also play [[Zone of Silence]] on its floor against [[Heaven's Maw#Champion of Savagery|Champion of Savagery]] to negate the Pyre damage that [[Terrifying Amalgam]] otherwise punishes you with. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! This card is at its strongest when you can play it repeatedly for exponential scaling. Unfortunately, this is easier said than done, due to its '''[[Consume]]''' and high cost. But if you have strong {{Ember}} generation, such as from [[Boiler Room]] or [[Pyre Chomper]], then you might be able to pull it off. Should that be the case, [[Demon Fiend]] is the best in-clan target, as {{IconLink|Trample}} ensures that none of its damage will be wasted on overkill, and if you can play this card repeatedly you will quickly get to the threshold at which you are dealing far more damage per hit than necessary to deal with a single enemy. '''Rage Room''' is a rare [[Hellhorned]] room added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It grants friendly units {{IconLink|Rage|2}} on {{IconLink|Strike}} and {{IconLink|Revenge}}.

==Strategy==

'''Rage Room''' provides a steady amount of scaling over the course of a fight regardless of your build - you can expect your units to gain {{Attack|2}} per round they fight in the backline (because {{IconLink|Rage}} decays before you get to use it), and {{Attack|6-10}} in the frontline. As with all things {{IconLink|Rage}}, these numbers are slightly better in builds that have other ways of applying {{IconLink|Rage}}. In comparison to the similar [[Fight Club]] it doesn't provide as much {{Attack}} initially, so you'll need to make up for this with its interactions. 

There's two ways to really capitalize on this card's triggers:

* a strong tank that intends on soaking up every hit in the lategame, perhaps with a {{IconLink|Revenge}} ability of their own, such as [[Hornbreaker Prince]]'s '''Wrathful''' line, ideally with an {{IconLink|Armor}} engine and some ways to manually trigger {{IconLink|Revenge}} with spells. [[Wolo's Bloodletter]] is worth a special mention here, scaling all your units in the room passively on top of its intrinsic boost.
* an offensive unit that triggers {{IconLink|Strike}} often. {{IconLink|Multistrike}} more than doubles this room's scaling, and {{IconLink|Trample}} and {{IconLink|Sweep}} are even better. (And having both of these keywords is even better still if you can manage it - see [[Trample]] for more on that interaction.)

In addition, {{IconLink|Rage}} synergies like [[Resonant Shard]], [[Deranged Brute]], and [[Last Stand]] can multiply its impact, as with any card that gives {{IconLink|Rage}}.

'''Awoken''' [[File:ClanAwoken.png|20x20px]] is a [[clan]] in [[Monster Train 2]], returning from [[Monster Train 1]].  It is unlocked after unlocking [[Hellhorned]] first and then healing 300 lost health.

Awoken features the following mechanics:
* Healing and {{IconLink|Regen}} feature prominently in the clan. Many units have {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} triggers that activate when healed.
* Many effects directly buff {{Attack}} and {{Health}}. '''[[Cultivate]]''' is a common keyword that buffs the stats of the lowest-health unit on the floor.
* {{IconLink|Spikes}} is a common buff that synergizes with the high health pools of many units.
* {{IconLink|Rooted}} is a common debuff that prevents enemies from ascending.
* Many units have {{IconLink|Quick}} or {{IconLink|Sweep}}.
* Many spells and units increase the number of cards you draw. [[Sting]] is a {{Ember|0}} damage spell that increases card draw which can be obtained in several ways.

The clan's unique [[Merchant of Steel]] Upgrade is {{IconLink|Thornstone}}.

{{UnitCard |name = The Sentient |image = PLR_TheSentient.png |clan = Awoken |rarity = Champion |type = Champion |banner = No |cost = 0 |size = 2 |stats = 0/10 |flavor = This Hollow was able to sever her connection to the Wildwood, slowly awakening to the prison her soul was trapped in, but still agreeing to champion our Covenant. She is intended as a tanky frontliner who can block large amounts of damage due to her high {{Health}} and access to healing, while also dealing damage to enemies, drawing extra cards and buffing your other units. Her starter card is [[Restore]]. == Light Forge Upgrades == {{ChampionPaths |baseStats=0/10 |a=Explosive |a1stats=0/30 |a1abilities={{IconLink|Rejuvenate}}: Deal 30 damage to front enemy unit. |a2stats=0/60 |a2abilities={{IconLink|Rejuvenate}}: Deal 60 damage to front enemy unit. |a3stats=0/120 |a3abilities={{IconLink|Rejuvenate}}: Deal 120 damage to front enemy unit. |b=Cultivating |b1stats=0/40 |b1abilities={{IconLink|Revenge}}: '''[[Cultivate]] 2'''.
Draw +1 each turn. |b2stats=0/80 |b2abilities={{IconLink|Revenge}}: '''[[Cultivate]] 3'''.
Draw +1 each turn. |b3stats=0/160 |b3abilities={{IconLink|Revenge}}: '''[[Cultivate]] 4'''.
Draw +1 each turn. |c=Bristling |c1stats=0/40 |c1abilities={{IconLink|Spikes|15}}. |c2stats=0/80 |c2abilities={{IconLink|Spikes|25}}. |c3stats=0/150 |c3abilities={{IconLink|Spikes|50}}. }} == Strategy== Regardless of which path you choose, the '''Sentient''' is intended to be on the front lines, blocking hits and potentially providing other benefits depending on the path. While her {{Health}} is impressive, it won't be enough to survive the whole game at higher Covenants, and so status effects like {{IconLink|Armor}}, {{IconLink|Valor}} or {{IconLink|Reanimate}} can help her tank even more if your allied clan can provide them. Artifacts like [[Crown of the Eternal]] or [[Emblem of the Exiles]] are also incredibly useful. ===Explosive=== '''Explosive Sentient''' deals damage to the front enemy whenever she is healed. If using her to kill enemy waves, it is best to focus on direct healing spells like [[Restore]] rather than stacking {{IconLink|Regen}}, as {{IconLink|Regen}} will only trigger once per turn. When fighting the boss, however, {{IconLink|Regen}} is more effective, as it will trigger every turn during {{IconLink|Relentless}}. This path generally does not deal enough damage to clear out enemy waves on its own. However, it is a fantastic supplement to your damage output and allows you a lot of leeway if your engine needs time to ramp up. The Awoken tend to excel at backline removal due to {{IconLink|Spikes}} and {{IconLink|Sweep}}, but can struggle with frontloaded damage output. '''Explosive''' addresses this weakness neatly; she can easily output bursts of 120 damage three or four times during a turn, letting her chip away at tanks enough for your damage dealers to kill them, mop up enemies that escaped your attackers, or clear out small frontliners like [[Fleshling]]s or [[Misshapen Fiend]]s so your main units do not waste their attacks on them. Because the '''Explosive''' path is dependent on healing, it is the only path which really requires Restore. This means that it is generally a poor choice with the [[Pyre of Dominion]], and you should usually not remove Restore unless you have better options for healing. [[Focused Growth]] is notable for triggering {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} twice. This path also has the lowest overall {{Health}}. When fighting against the [[Titans]] or [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]], the '''Sentient''' is likely to die to a combination of {{IconLink|Corruption}} and enemy attacks in a single turn, rendering healing and {{IconLink|Regen}} irrelevant. Either find another way to keep her alive or a way to still win once she's dead. It is usually inadvisable to cross-path in or out of '''Explosive''', as she really needs the damage offered at each level in order to keep up the pace with the tanks found in each ring. She will not accomplish much dealing 60 damage per heal against [[Avowed Gladiator]]s. [[Oldgrowth]] is good with all three of her paths, but deserves special mention for '''Explosive''' both because it already has a {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} trigger and because it has the least {{Health}} total. ===Cultivating=== The '''Cultivating''' path has three benefits, none of which are great on their own, but which add together to form a very strong path. It gives '''Sentient''' the highest {{Health}} of any path, draws an additional card each turn, and slowly scales the unit behind her. The extra draw and {{Health}} can be thought of as a simple buff which doesn't require you to change your strategy significantly, but the '''[[Cultivate]]''' effect does demand a particular playstyle to be used effectively. You will want to have a single unit behind the '''Sentient''' which can consistently take advantage of the stat buffs, making effects like {{IconLink|Multistrike}} and {{IconLink|Sweep}} very useful. Conveniently, the Awoken have access to units with both. The [[Animus of Will]] triples the effect of each point of {{Attack}}, while the [[Husk Hermit]] and [[Shattered Shell]] can deal that additional damage to all enemies. A {{IconLink|Sweep}} unit with {{IconLink|Frenzystone}} makes a particularly strong Cultivate target. Keep in mind that Cultivate always targets the unit with the lowest current {{Health}}. This makes units like [[Edge Prior]] actively harmful on the '''Sentient''''s floor, as they will steal stats from your other, better units. (Excluding [[Morsels]], which are no longer targeted by Cultivate as of the [[Lost Arsenal]] update.) In addition, the '''Sentient''' will begin targeting herself if she takes enough damage, or if she buffs the other unit enough that its maximum {{Health}} exceeds her own. After this point, she will alternate between the two, giving herself minor and generally borderline useless stat buffs while only scaling the other unit half as often. This also makes certain upgrades or units worse. {{IconLink|Quick}} will let your backliner kill enemies before they can attack the '''Sentient''', limiting the stat boosts she can apply with her {{IconLink|Revenge}} trigger. {{IconLink|Heartstone}} and {{IconLink|Largestone}} are also usually poor choices, as they mean that your backliner will reach or exceed the '''Sentient''''s {{Health}} faster, limiting how much you can buff their {{Attack}}. This arguably makes Shattered Shell's low {{Health}} an advantage, as long as you can keep it alive. Spells like [[Vine Grasp]] can trigger the '''Sentient''''s {{IconLink|Revenge}} trigger to buff the back unit manually. If you only care about the extra card draw, it can be worth taking one level in this path and two in another. ===Bristling=== '''Bristling''' is probably the simplest path, giving the '''Sentient''' plenty of {{IconLink|Spikes}} and letting her kill backliners without help. As with the other paths, it is a good idea to find some way to keep her alive beyond simply healing her. By placing her on the bottom floor and your other units on a higher floor, you can even kill a [[Ragewing Assassin]] before it has a chance to hit your other units. Doing this also blocks the Pyre damage from the [[Terrifying Amalgam]]. At the highest level, this path can deal reasonable damage even to tanky frontliners, but it may be worth mixing with other paths if you only care about taking out the backliners. '''Bristling II''' deals just enough damage to kill a [[Chosen Assassin]] as long as it has no {{IconLink|Titanskin}}. Keep in mind the usual pitfalls of using {{IconLink|Spikes}} as backline clear - they won't help against enemies that don't attack, like [[Vampiric Cherub]]s or [[Enthralled Ardent]]s. == Quotes == '''Summoned''' * ''Awoken at last.'' * ''I can...feel?'' * ''Move quickly so I can be finished with this.'' * ''No longer trapped...'' * ''The Wildwood lives!'' {{IconLink|Enchant}}: Grant {{IconLink|Quick}}. }} == Strategy== By far the simplest and strongest build for '''Wyldenten''' is to take '''Strangler''' at the first [[Light Forge]], then '''Predator''' at the next two. (Taking '''Predator''' first and '''Strangler''' later is also effective, though not quite as much so due to the lack of {{IconLink|Sweep}} in the early game.) This will give him {{IconLink|Quick}}, {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, and {{IconLink|Sweep}}, making him extremely powerful and massively increasing the effect of any kind of stat buff, whether that's [[Razorsharp Edge]] or out-of-clan options like [[Ritual of Battle]]. The [[Pyre of Savagery]] can make him far stronger, as his {{IconLink|Sweep}} allows him to start racking up kills from the very beginning of the run, although the Pyre's effect will be weaker in the 1/3 of runs in which you don't get '''Strangler''' at your first [[Light Forge]]. '''Strangler''''s {{IconLink|Rooted}} effect, while useful, is a nice bonus rather than the main purpose of the build, keeping tankier enemies in place so that '''Wyldenten''' can hit them again on the next turn. There is very little reason to ever ''not'' use this particular combo. This also turns '''Wyldenten''' into an excellent target for any kind of {{Attack}} boost. While the Awoken are severely lacking in scaling to defeat [[Avowed Gladiator]]s and [[Terrifying Amalgam]]s on high [[Covenant Rank]]s, with their best option being the mediocre [[Razorsharp Edge]], your allied clan is likely to offer a strong source of scaling, whether that involves {{IconLink|Rage}}, {{IconLink|Valor}} or direct {{Attack}}. If your clan combination is lacking in scaling options, several [[Clanless]] [[Equipment]]s from a [[Merchant of Arms]] can help '''Wyldenten''' and the Awoken with scaling, like [[Glass Cannon]], [[Bloodthirsty Blade]] (with '''Strangler''''s {{IconLink|Sweep}}), or [[Void Armament]]. If you don't get '''Predator''' for {{IconLink|Quick}}, [[Swiftsteel Dagger]] can substitute for that, too. Finally, the combo of '''Strangler''' plus '''Predator''' will not always be offered, or you may simply want to mix things up and try other path combinations. Each of '''Wyldenten''''s paths has its own benefits, and should be considered separately. ===Thornlord=== '''Thornlord''' can gain a lot of {{Attack}} via {{IconLink|Incant}}, but this Champion path lacks keywords like {{IconLink|Sweep}} and {{IconLink|Quick}} which are available in the other paths. For this reason, it can be preferable to branch out into one of the other paths: * '''Thornlord II''' + '''Strangler I''': gives up {{IconLink|Incant}}: {{Attack|+1}} and {{AttackHealth|+5/+20}} in exchange for {{IconLink|Sweep}} and {{IconLink|Strike}}: {{IconLink|Rooted}}. Whether or not this is worth it depends on if you already have strong backline clearing, as it gives up some single-target damage in exchange for {{IconLink|Sweep}}. * '''Thornlord I''' + '''Predator II''': gives up {{IconLink|Incant}}: {{Attack|+2}} and {{Health|+60}} in exchange for {{IconLink|Quick}}, {{IconLink|Enchant}}: {{IconLink|Quick}}, and {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}}. This is usually worth it, as the {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}} means you actually don't lose any damage - you just get {{IconLink|Incant}}: {{Attack|+2x2}} instead of {{IconLink|Incant}}: {{Attack|+4}} - so the only tradeoff is the lower {{Health}}, but the floor-wide {{IconLink|Quick}} means you'll take less damage to begin with anyways. In any case, '''Thornlord''' is best used on a floor with other {{IconLink|Incant}} units, making it particularly good with the [[Stygian Guard]]. Stygian's lack of direct damage scaling is another good reason to take this path, as it will give '''Wyldenten''' the {{Attack}} he otherwise lacks. If you use '''Needlebloom''' whenever it is available and play all the [[Sting]]s it generates, '''Thornlord''' effectively provides +1 draw per turn (more precisely, +3 draw every three turns), which is another reason to take this path. That said, producing a lot of Stings does have caveats, so after a certain point it may not be wise to keep producing them; see [[Sting]] for more. ===Strangler=== '''Strangler I''' is one of the strongest Champion paths in the game, allowing '''Wyldenten''' to wipe out backliners and applying any {{Attack}} boost to all enemies instead of only the front one. The {{IconLink|Rooted}} effect makes it even stronger, keeping enemies on a single floor to get hit again. If it is offered, you should almost always take it. '''Strangler II''' and '''III''', meanwhile, are some of the weakest upgrades available, giving no benefit outside of mediocre boosts to {{Attack}} and {{Health}}. It is generally better to crosspath into something else for later upgrades, unless you truly have no way to increase his {{Attack}} otherwise. Keep in mind that the {{IconLink|Rooted}} effect will keep enemies on the floor, and if there are already 7 enemies present, then future enemies will move directly to the floor above. This means that you will need to actually deal enough damage to kill enemies rather than simply holding them in place. This can be especially bad against bosses, which will skip over '''Wyldenten''''s floor, killing him and any other units on the floor instantly. This path is also mildly less useful - though still worth consideration - if you started with another {{IconLink|Sweep}} unit like [[Husk Hermit]] or [[Shattered Shell]]. While these units do not apply {{IconLink|Rooted}} and are therefore somewhat more susceptible to letting high-{{Health}} units escape, they take up less {{Capacity}} and can be upgraded at the [[Merchant of Steel]] and duplicated at [[Empyrean Well]]s. In particular, if you start with one of these units, taking '''Predator''' instead of '''Strangler''' can guarantee that your {{IconLink|Sweep}} unit will have {{IconLink|Quick}} even if you are never offered {{IconLink|Speedstone}}. If you desperately need the {{IconLink|Rooted}} effect later, you can always crosspath. ===Predator=== '''Predator''' makes '''Wyldenten''' and his allies {{IconLink|Quick}}. This allows them to take out enemies before they can attack. At higher levels, it also grants {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, turning '''Wyldenten''' into something like an [[Animus of Will]] upgraded with {{IconLink|Speedstone}} and {{IconLink|Largestone}}. However, it is almost never worth taking '''Predator III'''. '''Strangler I''''s {{IconLink|Sweep}} is much stronger than another stack of {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, and even '''Thornlord I''' can provide a damage boost which is often worth it if you have no effective way to buff '''Predator''''s low {{Attack}}, as well as improving your draw. == Quotes == '''Summoned''' * ''For my forest!'' * ''Let this serve as my redemption.'' * ''My roots run deep!'' * ''Such a strange contraption we're on.'' Upon our completion of the Rail, they agreed to extend this practice to other Hellborne in need. |artist = Loy Bouttamy }} '''Restore''' is [[The Sentient]]'s starter card. It restores {{Health|4}} and applies {{IconLink|Regen|2}}. ==Strategy== '''Restore''' returns to ''Monster Train 2'' with significant buffs that help shore up its usability throughout the game. Although healing for {{Health|4}} will generally not suffice for very long, it does keep your units healthy in the early-game to shore up early {{IconLink|Relentless}} phases. Since it now provides {{IconLink|Regen|2}}, {{IconLink|Regen}} is also easier to stack and maintain with it. In later rings, however, base '''Restore''' cards cannot be your only plan to keep units alive, as the output will simply not be enough. However, what makes '''Restore''' useful is its ability to trigger and maintain {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} abilities. It will often do so twice on the first turn, since it also gives {{IconLink|Regen}}, and as mentioned previously, it is much easier to keep {{IconLink|Regen}} up now that it provides 2 stacks instead of just 1, often allowing a unit to {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} every turn passively even if you cannot consistently draw back into {{IconLink|Regen}} cards. Having '''Restore''' thus strengthens your [[Awoken]] banners as it makes {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} units, such as [[Awoken Hollow]], [[Thorned Hollow]], and [[Steelsinger]], significantly better. It also makes [[Oldgrowth]] much more consistent; with '''Restore''' in your deck, your heal density will be very high, often allowing you to stack hundreds of {{Health}} over the course of a combat. In these instances, '''Restore''' can be an extremely useful card, and will be worth keeping in your deck. If your run does not use {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} strategies, '''Restore''' falls off quickly, and should be a removal target going into the late-game, or given upgrades that make it '''Consume'''. However, because it is such a core component of these strategies, starting with '''Restores''' keeps your run flexible from the outset, even if you do not end up needing it later. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! His final gift before his Exile. |artist = Brian Mutschler }} '''Rootseeds''' is [[Wyldenten]]'s starter card. It applies {{Attack|+3}} and draws 1 next turn. ==Strategy== '''Rootseeds''' has fallen off since the original ''Monster Train'', where it was one of the best starters in the game. It was mostly unchanged in the transition to ''Monster Train 2'', which works against it, as {{Attack|+3}} is simply not enough even as a supplementary source of scaling against the much more resilient enemies of Heaven. Additionally, for runs that want to keep '''Rootseeds''', the [[Merchant of Magic]] no longer stocks two guaranteed {{IconLink|Emberstone}} upgrades, meaning that it is much harder to discount all of them. The biggest limitation of '''Rootseeds''' in ''Monster Train 2'', however, is that starting with it makes {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} strategies much harder to play, often shutting them off altogether. [[Awoken]] banners become much less reliable when your run cannot make as good use out of [[Awoken Hollow]], [[Thorned Hollow]], and [[Steelsinger]]. The [[Lost Arsenal]] update also added [[Oldgrowth]], a powerful rare Equipment card that has helped the Awoken catch up in power level to other clans, which '''Rootseeds''' has no synergy with at all. Nonetheless, it remains a solid card by [[starter card]] standards, and many strategies still appreciate what it can enable. If played, it's draw neutral, and while the {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} units can't make use of it, several other Awoken units (and many in other clans) take the {{Attack}} buff reasonably well early on, like [[Animus of Will]], [[Husk Hermit]], and [[Shattered Shell]]. Because it replaces itself and often creates large hands, '''Rootseeds''' is a great way to spam {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers, whether for [[Wyldenten]]'s '''Thornlord''' path or various {{IconLink|Incant}} units from other clans, most notably the [[Stygian Guard]]. The meta of ''Monster Train 2'' also tends to lean towards taking at least one [[Hell's Flame]] for the extra {{Ember|2}} during [[Deployment]], which happens to offset the limitation of not being able to reliably discount all of your '''Rootseeds'''. Note that '''Rootseeds''' stops being card-neutral if you have too much card draw and too many other "draw next turn" effects (e.g. [[Sting]]), to the point that your draw next turn goes higher than 10; if it gets to this point, you may want to consider purging some of them. This is also another reason to lean towards taking {{Ember}}. It improves significantly with [[Vola's Tuning Fork]], reducing all copies of '''Rootseeds''' to {{Ember|0}} and making them take up no resources at all, allowing them to act as just a tiny bit of free scaling. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! As a non-[[banner unit]], it can only be drafted from post-combat card rewards. It reduces the costs of [[:Category:Healing cards|healing spells]] and spells that directly apply {{IconLink|Regen}} played on its floor. == Strategy== '''Edge Prior''' is one of the least useful units in the game, and is almost never worth taking. Its niche from the original ''Monster Train'' of being a reasonably useful midgame infusion into a Hollow no longer exists, thus removing almost all of its already very situational utility. With its extremely low stats, '''Edge Prior''' is essentially worthless for any combat purpose beyond decreasing the cost of healing and {{IconLink|Regen}} spells. Even this ability, which sounds good on paper, only affects a small number of spells, and {{Ember|-1}} is not a particularly significant benefit. This is exacerbated by the fact that Awoken has [[Pyre-Gro]] in the uncommon pool and also often wants [[Hell's Flame]] anyway to capitalize on the clan's plentiful card draw, and will usually already have the {{Ember}} needed to play the necessary healing cards. As a non-banner unit, it also takes up draw and can be bottom-decked, limiting its effectiveness further. While the '''Edge Prior''' could theoretically be used with a unit like [[The Sentient]] or [[Awoken Hollow]] which wants to be healed frequently, its low {{Health}} means that it will almost always be targeted by '''[[Cultivate]]''', wasting impactful scaling on an essentially useless unit rather than adding stats to something stronger on the floor like an [[Animus of Will]]. This makes it actively harmful alongside '''Cultivating''' Sentient or Awoken Hollow. That isn't to say that '''Edge Prior''' does not have use cases. It can be somewhat useful with '''Explosive''' Sentient, as long as you don't intend to crosspath into '''Cultivating''' at any point. It is also decent with the other two {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} banner units in the clan, [[Thorned Hollow]] and [[Steelsinger]], who appreciate being able to play lower-impact healing cards like [[Restore]]s for {{Ember|0}}. Being allied with the [[Luna Coven]] also makes '''Edge Prior''' slightly more useful, due to their powerful healing spells. Even under optimal conditions, however, it is still not generally worth drafting, as you will often be able to find alternative {{Ember}} solutions for your run. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! It grants +1 draw per turn while on the train. == Strategy== '''Wildwood Custodian''' provides a useful, passive benefit of an extra card per turn, which is useful for almost any build. However, its generic, universal benefit also means that it rarely has any synergies. It grants an extra card draw on all turns after it is played, but does nothing before that, and costs a draw and {{Ember|1}} on the turn that you draw and play it. Compared to [[Rootseeds]], a starter card (and not a particularly great one), it provides no {{Attack}}, takes up {{Capacity|1}}, and provides extra draw starting two turns from when it is played. (Rootseeds is +1 draw next turn, while '''Wildwood Custodian''' is +1 draw on all future turns.) This is not a particularly great value proposition. As its effect doesn't interact with allies or enemies in any way, it can be placed on a floor higher than your main floor and left to simply exist and draw you more cards, or if you have an extra {{Capacity}} on a floor with allies, you can put it behind them to keep it safer. If leaving it on higher floors, you'll need to have a way to protect it against enemies that slip through, flying bosses, and the [[Clash with the Titans|Titans]] if you go there. Note that [[Stoic Platemail]] doesn't shut off its ability, making that a great way to keep it alive. It can even serve as a {{Capacity|1}} tank itself with that and some upgrades. Like any non-[[banner unit]], it is subject to your draw order. If you can manage to draw it out with {{IconLink|Dominating Authority}}, [[Sketches of Salvation]], or [[Departure Manifest]], that is very helpful, since it means you'll benefit from its draw starting on turn 1. If you can afford to play it in a [[Hall of Mirrors]], its extra draw will be doubled. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! {{UnitCard |name = Animus of Speed |image = PLR_AnimusOfWill.png |clan = Awoken |rarity = Uncommon |type = Animus |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 35/8 |ability = {{IconLink|Quick}}.

It is possessed by the soul of the Wildwood and the Channelers who guard it, often making my conversations with it obtuse and pointless. |artist = Taylor Bray }} '''Animus of Speed''' is an uncommon [[Awoken]] [[banner unit]]. It has high {{Attack}}, {{IconLink|Quick}}, and its '''Swiftshot''' ability allows it to immediately attack any unit on the floor. == Strategy== The '''Animus of Speed''' is a potent unit in Awoken's kit, primarily thanks to its '''Swiftshot''' ability. This ability is highly flexible depending on your needs, and can allow '''Animus of Speed''' to serve as a way of clearing out important backline enemies, or to provide some extra juice to take down tough units like [[Avowed Gladiator]]s and [[Celestial Bastion]]s. This flexibility is key to '''Animus of Speed'''. [[Husk Hermit]] and [[Shattered Shell]] are available within the same clan, and thanks to {{IconLink|Sweep}} are more reliable as backline removal units. Similarly, [[Animus of Will]] and its {{IconLink|Multistrike|2}} will generally be a stronger payoff for damage-scaling effects; without any upgrades, across two turns, '''Animus of Speed''' will attack three times, while Animus of Will will attack six times. But '''Animus of Speed''' widens your margin of error on these effects. If a higher-{{Health}} backliner like a [[Chosen Ardent]] escapes your {{IconLink|Sweep}} unit, '''Animus of Speed''' can remove it before you need to start casting spells. If your damage scaling is off to a slow start, it can output some burst damage to prevent leaks. And in the early game, it can snipe a [[Collector]] or a [[Savage Spearman]] while still having high enough {{Attack}} to kill a [[Fallen Champion]] in two hits. Any source of {{IconLink|Multistrike}} is huge for '''Animus of Speed'''. Because '''Swiftshot''' is a full attack, it will take {{IconLink|Multistrike}} into account and deliver the appropriate number of extra hits. To return to the earlier comparison, an '''Animus of Speed''' with {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}} will attack the same number of times over two turns as an Animus of Will, while having a much greater default {{Attack}}. Additionally, if the original target dies, extra strikes will loop around to hit the front enemy unit. The greatest drawback to '''Swiftshot''' is its '''Cooldown 2'''. This means it can normally only be used every other turn, which is a massive blow to consistency, especially because wave design will frequently threaten you every turn. However, this problem is not insurmountable, depending on your resources. Allying with the [[Pyreborne]] is the most obvious route, as reducing '''Cooldown''' is one of their strengths. [[Mind Cage]] is a great piece of equipment for it, and it is cheaper to deploy than the similar [[Hot Head]] (and frequently better during {{IconLink|Relentless}} as well). You can also use [[Tome of Contracts]], ideally with {{IconLink|Seekstone}}, or failing that you might be able to pull off a success with [[Taskmaster's Lash]], [[Attuned Manacles]], or [[Pyreborne Brainspike]] with {{IconLink|Eternalstone}} and {{IconLink|Keepstone}}. Another way to reset its '''Cooldown''' is to kill it. If '''Animus of Speed''' dies and is replayed, '''Swiftshot''' will be available for use again, which makes the unit exemplary with the [[Melting Remnant]]. It can be '''[[Reform]]ed''' with cards like [[Molded]] and [[Wicked Blaze]], or you can use [[Hallowed Halls]] to kill it and bring it back stronger in the same turn. Its very low {{Health|8}} is actually a boon here, especially in tandem with {{IconLink|Quick}}, as it will always get to make its full attack before enemies can kill it. Additionally, Melting Remnant can sometimes struggle with taking out backline units, so they complement each other quite well. If you are not partnered with Melting Remnant, you can still reset its '''Cooldown''' via death; it just needs {{IconLink|Immortalstone}}. Alternatively, you can duplicate it and alternate between using each copy's ability; while one is on '''Cooldown''', you can attack with the other. Note that if it is given {{IconLink|Trample}}, any leftover damage after killing a backliner with '''Swiftshot''' will be directed to the front enemy unit instead of the one behind the backliner, despite its description; this means that you cannot kill a row of backliners by targeting the front one. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! [[Immortalstone]] | '''Immortalstone''' makes '''Animus of Speed''' {{IconLink|Endless}}, which lets you play it on the bottom floor, take out an important backliner or two, attack the front unit, die, and then be available to do it all again next turn. |- | style="text-align:center;" | [[File:BurstStone.png|50x50px]]

Animus of Will:
{{UnitCard |name = Animus of Will |image = PLR_AnimusOfSpeed.png |clan = Awoken |rarity = Uncommon |type = Animus |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 3/8 |ability = {{IconLink|Multistrike|2}}. |flavor = These Animus have grown to see beyond their Ring. I've learned that they are rarely created by Channelers since their gift of sight can expose them to the reality of their imprisonment. |artist = Taylor Bray }} The '''Animus of Will''' is an uncommon [[Awoken]] [[banner unit]]. It has low stats but starts with {{IconLink|Multistrike|2}}. == Strategy == '''Animus of Will''' is one of the strongest units in the Awoken clan, and one of the most consistently useful units in the entire game. As the only banner unit which starts with {{IconLink|Multistrike|2}} by default, it triples the effect of {{IconLink|Rage}}, {{IconLink|Valor}}, or any other {{Attack}} increase. Almost any build can take advantage of this, regardless of the allied clan. Cards that increase {{Attack}} such as [[Razorsharp Edge]], [[Steel Enhancer]], and [[Sharpen]] are effective on '''Animus of Will''' as their effects are essentially tripled. In this vein, [[Rootseeds]] is usually a better starter card for it than [[Restore]]. However, all of these stat increases are quite small and tend to fall off after the early rings, so try to look for more impactful buff cards from your secondary clan. When using the [[Sentient]] and her '''Cultivating''' path, the '''Animus of Will''' is one of the strongest targets for the '''[[Cultivate]]''' effect. With a strong deck to support them, '''Cultivating''' Sentient and a single '''Animus of Will''' can potentially win the entire game with no other units required. [[Awoken Hollow]] can provide a similar effect, but requires frequent {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} triggers to do so. If '''Animus of Will''' is being scaled through a buff like {{IconLink|Rage}} or {{IconLink|Valor}} rather than true stat increases, then [[Adaptive Mutation]] can be a solid pickup. Adaptive Mutation will swap its buffed {{Attack}} with its {{Health}}, while the buffs that got its {{Attack}} so high in the first place will remain in place, essentially giving it both tremendous {{Attack}} and {{Health}}. Equipment is a huge boon to '''Animus of Will''', making up for its poor stats. [[Glass Cannon]] provides a massive {{Attack}} boost, but you must be able to protect the unit from effects like {{IconLink|Spikes}} and {{IconLink|Sweep}}. [[Swiftsteel Dagger]] buffs its {{Attack}} and grants it {{IconLink|Quick}}, so it can potentially take out enemy units before they can hit. The [[Overgrowth Carapace]] grants it a large boost to its stats at the end of each turn as long as you have free space on the floor, and if upgraded with {{IconLink|Smidgestone}} it will never grow beyond {{Capacity|1}}. [[Bloodthirsty Blade]] has great potential if obtained early, though it is usually better served on a {{IconLink|Sweep}} unit like [[Husk Hermit]] or [[Shattered Shell]]. If you can use those units to scale its damage up, you can duplicate it and put the second copy on '''Animus of Will'''. [[Everlasting Light]] provides {{IconLink|Valor|6}} to your whole floor due to {{IconLink|Multistrike|2}}, and is highly effective with several copies of the unit. [[Herzal's Hammer]] is more expensive, but applies {{Attack|+9}} and {{IconLink|Armor|9}}, so it's even better. Both [[Luna Cyclestaff]] and [[Moonlit Glaive]] have the potential to give '''Animus of Will''' absurdly high {{Attack}}, while [[Combustion Suit]] can turn it into a pseudo-{{IconLink|Sweep}} unit by applying large amounts of {{IconLink|Unstable}} to all units. [[Brain Transfer]] is an easy way to provide '''Animus of Will''' with damage, as long as you have another unit with high {{Attack}} to '''[[Sacrifice]]'''. It's an excellent recipient of [[Primordium]]'s scaling, and all three of its paths are valuable; even full '''Stalwart Snack''' can be worthwhile if Primordium is given {{Attack}}-boosting equipment like Glass Cannon. [[Talos]]'s '''Enchantress''' path provides permanent stat increases after each combat as long as '''Animus of Will''' survives. [[Baron Grael]]'s '''Living Armory''' path can skyrocket its {{Attack}}, while '''Learning Limb''' can permanently scale equipment applied to it. If you can trigger {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} frequently, [[Ekka]]'s '''Lunar Steward''' can bolster both its {{Attack}} and {{Health}}. [[Little Fade]]'s '''Fire Light''' path can buff a whole floor of '''Animus of Will''' at once, especially with [[Waxer Snuffer]] or [[Intent on Death]]. All of these paths are strong options anyway, but should be considered even more so if you are starting with '''Animus of Will''' in your deck. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! Description |- | style="text-align:center;" | [[File:LargeStone.png|50x50px]]

However, if you are scaling '''Animus of Will''' via '''[[Cultivate]]''', the huge boost to {{Health}} can be a detriment, as eventually its {{Health}} will be greater than the unit with '''[[Cultivate]]''' and its scaling will slow. |- | style="text-align:center;" | [[File:SmidgeStone.png|50x50px]]
[[Smidgestone]] | '''Smidgestone''' decreases its size, making it easier to fit on a floor with other units. It can be combined with '''Largestone''' to grant the benefits of both, turning the '''Animus of Will''' into an extremely powerful unit with {{Capacity|1}}, {{Attack|18x3}} and {{Health|58}}. I had no idea of this until the Channelers told me. It took me some time to trust them again after that revelation. |artist = Evan Yovaisis }} '''Awoken Hollow''' is an uncommon [[Awoken]] [[banner unit]]. It gains 60 max {{Health}} on {{IconLink|Summon}} (which is unfilled), and has a {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} trigger that [[Cultivate]]s '''3''', letting it strengthen the frailest unit on the floor whenever it is healed. == Notes == Like all ''max health'' buffs, its {{IconLink|Summon}} effect is applied to the '''unit''', not the '''card''', unlike normal {{Health}} buffs. This means the extra max health will not stay if '''Awoken Hollow''' dies and is replayed, e.g. due to {{IconLink|Endless}} or [[Reform]]. It will get the same buff next time it's played on {{IconLink|Summon}} - it just won't accumulate. == Strategy == '''Awoken Hollow''' can serve as an excellent tank for its team with healing support, as it starts with 60 health to fill, and when filled it sports an impressive {{Health|85}} base. It can keep units behind it safe, and allow the healing you invest into keeping it alive also work as a [[Steel Enhancer]] kind of effect. It's better with [[Restore]] as a starter card, as that can heal it, trigger its {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} immediately, and then trigger it again when {{IconLink|Regen}} triggers. [[Cultivate]] effects can be tricky to use effectively, as they target the unit with the lowest current {{Health}}. Ideally, {{Attack}} buffs should go to units that capitalize on them well, like [[Animus of Will]], but even if she receives the Cultivate buffs initially, if another unit, like a [[Edge Prior]], is on the floor, that doesn't capitalize on the {{Attack}} as well is also on the floor, her {{Health}} will eventually surpass that unit's, and it will start taking buffs you'd rather have had on the [[Animus of Will]]. '''Awoken Hollow''' can start taking its own buffs if its health is low for the same reason, which may not be what you want. You can deal with this by being careful only to place unit(s) that benefit well from the {{Attack}}, which might mean just one super-focused unit. [[Razorsharp Edge]] gets a special mention here, as not only is it a desirable spell for the units '''Awoken Hollow''' wants to Cultivate, it also decreases their {{Health}}, making them more likely to be Cultivated (and the Cultivate trigger, in turn, lets you keep playing [[Razorsharp Edge]]). Alternately, even if the {{Attack}} isn't well placed, you can just think of [[Awoken Hollow]]'s [[Cultivate]] activations as a way to ensure your floor doesn't die to things like {{IconLink|Spikes}} or {{IconLink|Sweep}}, though its {{Health}} scaling is probably too slow to adequately protect against [[Chosen Assassin]] on Covenant 10. [[Morsels]] are excepted as targets for Cultivate, making them safe to play on [[Awoken Hollow]]'s floor, either to buff '''Awoken Hollow''' or as chump blockers. '''Awoken Hollow''' is usually a passive unit, as you'll usually want to invest in its bulk and let the units behind it do the damage-dealing. That said, there are a few situations where it can become an offensive powerhouse of its own. [[Equalizing Rings]] can give it a solid amount of {{Attack}} power, and if you can merge that with [[Oldgrowth]], '''Awoken Hollow''' can scale to great heights. [[Adaptive Mutation]] can also be strong on [[Awoken Hollow]], especially with the aforementioned [[Oldgrowth]], though it may not be a suitable frontline unit after that is used. '''Awoken Hollow''' works splendidly with [[Primordium]], as you can Cultivate Primordium to boost its stats, which '''Awoken Hollow''' will then receive many times over when it eats Primordium. This can scale '''Awoken Hollow''' enough to actually become your primary damage unit, and makes {{IconLink|Frenzystone}} a safer pick. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! She has {{IconLink|Sweep}} and gets {{Attack|+3}} on {{IconLink|Revenge}}. == Strategy == '''Husk Hermit''' is an unusual {{IconLink|Sweep}} unit. Usually, {{IconLink|Sweep}} units like her close relative [[Shattered Shell]] are backliners, and must be protected by a sturdy tank on the bottom floor. '''Husk Hermit''' instead serves as both tank and sweeper, fulfilling a role somewhat similar to [[Thorned Hollow]]. Her {{IconLink|Revenge}} trigger means that attempting to keep her behind another unit will deprive her of her damage output. {{Health|35}} is respectable, especially in the early game and with the many healing options available to the Awoken. Because she will be taking lots of damage to scale her {{Attack}}, durability is of great importance. Shop upgrades like {{IconLink|Titanstone}} and {{IconLink|Largestone}} are paramount. Curiously, while {{IconLink|Speedstone}} is vital to the success of most other sweepers for its ability to kill weaker enemies before they can move, it is significantly less necessary on '''Husk Hermit''' because killing those enemies means she will get fewer {{IconLink|Revenge}} triggers. It may even be detrimental if you are relying on that scaling to kill really dangerous enemies like [[Chosen Supplicant]]s or [[Chosen Assassin]]s. Cards like [[Wildwood Tome]] can be upgraded with {{IconLink|Freezestone}} so that '''Husk Hermit''' only gains {{IconLink|Quick}} after her {{Attack}} has gone up sufficiently, striking a balance between scaling and survival. However, if you already have another powerful scaling method available, such as [[Pyre of Savagery]], [[Bloodsoaked Arena]], or [[Primordium]], {{IconLink|Quick}} may be the better choice again. Aside from shop upgrades, '''Husk Hermit''' can be sustained through healing. She will generally need to increase her max {{Health}} by some means, as {{Health|35}} is not enough in later rings, even with {{IconLink|Titanite}}. [[Awakening Thicket]] is a solid choice, despite her lack of a natural {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} trigger, as it will continually heal her every turn. [[Oldgrowth]] is a fantastic piece of equipment that can continually raise her max {{Health}} each time she is healed, and goes best with a card like [[Unleash the Wildwood]] for a full heal, or [[Focused Growth]] for two large heals. Other defensive equipment should also be considered, depending on your partnered clan, such as [[Dusk Mantle]], [[Meat Shield]], and [[Loamcoat]]. Alternatively, you can use equipment to increase her immediate damage output without waiting for {{IconLink|Revenge}} triggers, such as [[Everlasting Light]], [[Luna Cyclestaff]], and [[Bloodthirsty Blade]]. [[Rage Room]], from the [[Hellhorned]] clan, is always a worthwhile pick with {{IconLink|Sweep}} units, but it is especially good with '''Husk Hermit''' because she can also benefit from the {{IconLink|Rage|2}} on {{IconLink|Revenge}} instead of just on {{IconLink|Strike}}. The aforementioned Bloodsoaked Arena is also superb, as the {{IconLink|Valor}} it accumulates will provide '''Husk Hermit''' with lots of {{IconLink|Armor}}. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! {{UnitCard |name = Shattered Shell |image = PLR_ShatteredShell.png |clan = Awoken |rarity = Uncommon |type = Animus |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 3/10 |ability = {{IconLink|Sweep}}.
