Against my wishes, the Channelers have hoarded Pyre shards to further enhance the power of these creatures. |artist = Brian Mutschler }} '''Shattered Shell''' is an uncommon [[Awoken]] [[banner unit]]. She has low starting stats, but has {{IconLink|Sweep}} and gains {{Attack|+3}} whenever she kills an enemy. == Strategy== The '''Shattered Shell''' is very similar to the [[Husk Hermit]] from the same clan, and often performs a similar role. The main differences are her much lower {{Health}} and her ability to gain {{Attack}} on {{IconLink|Slay}}, while Husk Hermit gains {{Attack}} on {{IconLink|Revenge}} instead. This cements her firmly as a backliner, rather than a frontline tank, and generally a more offensive option. The choice between Husk Hermit and '''Shattered Shell''' often comes down to a matter of available upgrades or current deck composition. For example, if {{IconLink|Speedstone}} is available in the shop or you already have a tanky unit like [[Thorned Hollow]], then '''Shattered Shell''' may be the better choice than her sister, whereas if the shop instead offers {{IconLink|Largestone}} or {{IconLink|Titanstone}}, or you have a powerful but fragile attacker like [[Animus of Speed]], then Husk Hermit may be more advisable. It may also depend on which form of [[Seraph]] you are facing; [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage|The Savage]] might overwhelm Husk Hermit with damage before she can kill the backline enemies, while [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant|The Dominant]] could threaten [[Shattered Shell]]'s low {{Health}}. Although she will build {{Attack}} relatively quickly thanks to killing several units per turn, this extra damage is not enough to carry you through the late game. By later rings, that additional damage will usually be a minor boost compared to whatever other damage scaling you are using. Within the Awoken, [[Razorsharp Edge]] is usually the best option, but depending on your secondary clan you can use {{IconLink|Rage}}, {{IconLink|Valor}}, {{IconLink|Mageblade}}, or other effects, which are generally more impactful. Like other {{IconLink|Sweep}} units, she is also extremely effective with a source of permanent scaling like [[Bloodthirsty Blade]] or [[Pyre of Savagery]]. When using '''Shattered Shell''' as a damage carry without a source of permanent scaling or an extremely powerful scaling engine, it is likely that early waves will leak, especially in the late game. If your other floors cannot handle this, consider drafting cards like [[Restoring Retreat]] or [[Ensnare]] to force enemies back onto [[Shattered Shell]]'s floor. '''Strangler''' [[Wyldenten]] can be useful as a supplement; although it may seem redundant to have two {{IconLink|Sweep}} units on the same floor, he can ensure enemies cannot escape from '''Shattered Shell''' and get to your Pyre. Just beware that this may be less effective in [[Clash with the Titans]] as [[Savagery]] cannot be {{IconLink|Rooted}}, and the overall lower enemy density in that combat means '''Shattered Shell''' will have a harder time triggering {{IconLink|Slay}} and scaling, especially with [[Curse of Entropy]] factored in. [[Shattered Shell]]'s low {{Health}} can actually be an advantage in certain situations, as she will be targeted more by [[Cultivate]] effects. She is an excellent target for '''Cultivating''' [[Sentient]], but note that since the Sentient Cultivates on {{IconLink|Revenge}}, it is less advisable to apply {{IconLink|Quick}} to '''Shattered Shell''' (since killing enemies before they can attack denies {{IconLink|Revenge}} triggers). [[Awoken Hollow]] may be a better choice for this approach, as {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} is entirely compatible with a {{IconLink|Quick}} '''Shattered Shell'''. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! {{UnitCard |name = Thorned Hollow |image = PLR_ThornedHollow.png |clan = Awoken |rarity = Uncommon |type = Hollow |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 3 |stats = 15/25 |ability = {{IconLink|Summon}}: Gain 60 max {{Health}}.

While impossible for me to visit, I've heard that the Hollows that root there are afflicted with a similar transformation. |artist = Evan Yovaisis }} '''Thorned Hollow''' is an uncommon [[Awoken]] [[banner unit]]. It has a large amount of {{Health}} and builds {{IconLink|Spikes}} whenever it is healed. == Notes == Like all ''max health'' buffs, its {{IconLink|Summon}} effect is applied to the '''unit''', not the '''card''', unlike normal {{Health}} buffs. This means the extra max health will not stay if '''Thorned Hollow''' dies and is replayed, e.g. due to {{IconLink|Endless}} or [[Reform]]. It will get the same buff next time it's played on {{IconLink|Summon}} - it just won't accumulate. == Strategy == '''Thorned Hollow''' has a very high ceiling but a somewhat low floor. At its best, it can build up hundreds of {{IconLink|Spikes}} and devastate enemy lines all on its own. At its worst, it can be no better than a [[Shield Steward]]. Its effectiveness varies greatly depending on whether your deck contains [[Rootseeds]] or [[Restore]]s (or neither, if using [[Pyre of Dominion]]). With Restores, its {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} effect is far easier to trigger; without them, you must rely on drafting healing cards, and these will naturally be less frequently drawn than Restores. [[Witchweave]]s can also trigger {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} and do so without costing any {{Ember}}, but do not provide any {{IconLink|Regen}} the way Restores do. Overall, if you do not have Restores in your starting deck, it's typically advisable not to draft '''Thorned Hollow''' (as well as [[Awoken Hollow]] and [[Steelsinger]]). If you do have Restores, and you want to lean into '''Thorned Hollow''' as your main carry, then your next priority should be drafting additional healing cards. Cards like [[Glimmer]] and [[Engraft]] are cheap ways of building up {{IconLink|Spikes}}. [[Restoration Detonation]] provides a respectable heal and helps fill out the additional {{Health|60}} that '''Thorned Hollow''' gains when played, while also heavily damaging an enemy. [[Focused Growth]] is somewhat expensive, but it heals a tremendous {{Health|40}} and triggers {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} twice. It is also an excellent recipient of {{IconLink|Keepstone}} because it actually increases your draw each turn, unlike most other Holdover cards. [[Restoring Retreat]] is solid because '''Thorned Hollow''' usually prefers to be played on the bottom floor, and the '''[[Descend]]''' effect is useful for breaking up enemy lines, overstacking floors, and keeping flying bosses off your main floor. [[Spreading Spores]] triggers {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} and grants additional {{IconLink|Regen}} and {{IconLink|Spikes}} while also filling your deck with copies of itself. [[Wildwood Sap]] does not immediately trigger {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}}, but helps build up {{IconLink|Regen}} for {{IconLink|Relentless}} and increases its max {{Health}}. [[Bramble Lash]] is usually [[Thorned Hollow]]'s best way of killing heavy units due to its powerful scaling, and can even destroy flying bosses early if you can get a clear shot at them. [[Edge Prior]] reduces the {{Ember}} cost of healing cards, while [[Shard Channeler]] increases the damage dealt by {{IconLink|Spikes}}, and multiple copies combined with aggressive healing can even let '''Thorned Hollow''' kill [[Avowed Gladiator]]s on its own. [[Petrified Crucible]] has the same effect as Shard Channeler but is always active, so it should be highly prioritized if offered. [[Gnarled Root]] can increase [[Thorned Hollow]]'s {{Attack}}, and is another method by which it can take down high {{Health}} enemies. Most of the time, though, '''Thorned Hollow''' will simply be a very durable tank that can clear out backline enemies and chip down heavy units for its high {{Attack}} allies, rather than killing them itself. [[Awakening Thicket]] is a useful room for '''Thorned Hollow''', increasing its max {{Health}} and healing it a significant amount on {{IconLink|Resolve}}. [[Oldgrowth]] is an immensely powerful equipment for [[Thorned Hollow]]'s durability, letting it easily build up over {{Health|400}} with rapid {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} triggers. [[Unleash the Wildwood]] should be a high priority with this equipment, as it is otherwise quite difficult to fully heal '''Thorned Hollow'''. {{IconLink|Corruption}} is difficult for '''Thorned Hollow''' to deal with if you lack Oldgrowth, especially the exponential {{IconLink|Corruption}} applied by [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]]. Effects that can prevent {{IconLink|Corruption}} from being applied, like {{IconLink|Silence}}, {{IconLink|Mute}}, and {{IconLink|Dazed}} are practically necessary in these cases; {{IconLink|Endless}} is not a sufficient solution because if '''Thorned Hollow''' dies and is replayed, it will lose all of its {{IconLink|Spikes}}. When playing with [[Underlegion]], [[Loamcoat]] is an incredibly powerful equipment for '''Thorned Hollow''', especially if merged with Oldgrowth. It allows its {{IconLink|Regen}} stacks to grow extremely high, and '''[[Propagate]]s''' both its {{IconLink|Regen}} and its {{IconLink|Spikes}}. If not playing with Underlegion, [[Meat Shield]] is another way of restoring {{Health}}. [[Equalizing Rings]] is quite worth taking if you can merge it with Oldgrowth as well, turning its immense {{Health}} into damage output. Keep in mind that {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} triggers {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}}, so ways of applying {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} like [[Morsel Excavator]]s and [[Insatiable Hunger]] can be quite useful. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! Description |- | style="text-align:center;" | [[File:DualStone.png|50x50px]]
[[Dualstone]] | '''Dualstone''' grants {{IconLink|Dualism}}, doubling the {{IconLink|Spikes}} gained per heal. This upgrade is vital if using '''Thorned Hollow''' as a carry, as it is extremely difficult to garner enough {{IconLink|Spikes}} to kill later ring enemies without it, but less necessary (though still useful) if only using it as a backline-eliminating tank. |- | style="text-align:center;" | [[File:TitanStone.png|50x50px]]
[[Titanstone]] | '''Titanstone''' grants {{IconLink|Titanite}}, halving all incoming damage. It causes {{IconLink|Spikes}} on friendly units to deal +1 damage per stack on its floor, doubling the damage taken by attackers. Multiple copies will each add an extra point of damage for each stack of {{IconLink|Spikes}}. == Strategy == '''Shard Channeler''' is a very niche unit, generally only worth taking if {{IconLink|Spikes}} is central to your run. But if {{IconLink|Spikes}} ''is'' central to your run, the '''Shard Channeler''' can be a good addition as long as you can keep it alive behind your primary {{IconLink|Spikes}} unit. Keep in mind that most sources of {{IconLink|Spikes}} in the Awoken aren't enough to deal with units like [[Avowed Gladiator]] even with [[Shard Channeler]]'s help, so its effect mostly helps against backliners. Keeping it alive is extremely difficult, though, as two out of three versions of Seraph will kill it easily. A single [[Ragewing Assassin]] in the [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]] fight can destroy it, as {{IconLink|Sweep}} attacks hit the entire floor even if {{IconLink|Spikes}} on the front unit kill the sweeper. Its low {{Health}} means that [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]] will quickly kill it with {{IconLink|Corruption}}. If you have some way to deal with these problems, it can be an effective pick. Keep in mind that, even if the final boss is [[Seraph Aeternus-The Entropic]], the '''Shard Channeler''' can still die in other battles, including the fight against [[Qel the Corruptor]] and [[Savagery's Final Assault]]. Within the Awoken, '''Shard Channeler''' is best paired with [[Thorned Hollow]] or '''Bristling''' [[Sentient]]. It's also strong with {{IconLink|Spikes}} strategies from other clans, such as runs featuring [[Faulty Body]] or [[Little Fade]]'s '''Little Icarus''' path. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Steelsinger:
{{UnitCard |name = Steelsinger |image = PLR_Steelsinger.png |clan = Awoken |rarity = Rare |type = Hollow |banner = Yes |cost = 3 |size = 4 |stats = 20/40 |ability = {{IconLink|Summon}}: Gain 80 max {{Health}}.
{{IconLink|Rejuvenate}}: {{Attack|+3}} permanently. |flavor = “Not of us, but of the Mother,” as the Edge Priory says of Steelsingers. I often just nod at their rambling words, accepting them for the insanity they are, but their strange mention of the Mother — a Divinity no doubt — adds an air of validity to this crazy claim. |artist = Adam Lee }} '''Steelsinger''' is a rare [[Awoken]] [[banner unit]]. It has one of the highest maximum {{Health}} values in the game, and gains {{Attack}} permanently whenever it is healed. == Notes == Like all ''max health'' buffs, its {{IconLink|Summon}} effect is applied to the '''unit''', not the '''card''', unlike normal {{Health}} buffs. This means the extra max health will not stay if '''Steelsinger''' dies and is replayed, e.g. due to {{IconLink|Endless}} or [[Reform]]. It will get the same buff next time it's played on {{IconLink|Summon}} - it just won't accumulate. == Strategy== With the buff it received in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update, '''Steelsinger''' is once again a tremendously powerful unit, albeit still with some drawbacks that can limit its usage. Gaining a permanent {{Attack|+3}} on {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} means that healing is the name of the game when running '''Steelsinger'''. You want to heal it aggressively and often, getting as many triggers in as many times as possible in the limited number of turns and combats that you have. It also means you want to avoid healing your other units as much as possible, since with very few exceptions, healing other units means you are not healing '''Steelsinger'''. This makes it generally incompatible with [[Awoken Hollow]], [[Thorned Hollow]], and '''Explosive''' [[Sentient]]. The unit is fairly demanding in terms of getting it into play; it's not quite on the level of [[Shadowsiege]], but at {{Ember|3}} and {{Capacity|4}}, it is a steep investment. As such, if you do not believe you will be able to scale its {{Attack}} output significantly with lots and lots of healing, it is usually not worth taking. In particular, starting with [[Rootseeds]] rather than [[Restore]] makes it extremely difficult to scale '''Steelsinger''' to the levels that are required to justify its cost and space. If you have Restores, you will still want to draft plenty of healing cards, as although '''Steelsinger''' has a mighty {{Health|120}} at maximum, it enters combat at only {{Health|40}}. Cards like [[Restoration Detonation]], [[Glimmer]], [[Engraft]], and [[Spreading Spores]] will both keep it alive and scale its {{Attack}}. [[Unleash the Wildwood]] is an especially good one, immediately bringing '''Steelsinger''' to full for a paltry {{Ember|1}}. It is also the most efficient way to heal other units if you need to, as it fully heals an entire floor for just a single card. [[Focused Growth]] is somewhat expensive, but grants a tremendous heal, uniquely triggers {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} twice, and increases your draw next turn. [[Restoring Retreat]] can help get around [[Steelsinger]]'s {{Capacity}} problem due to its '''[[Descend]]''' effect. {{IconLink|Regen}} is useful, but is rather inefficient at buffing '''Steelsinger''' since it will only ever trigger once per turn outside of {{IconLink|Relentless}}, so it is typically not worthwhile to invest in {{IconLink|Regen}} cards like [[Wildwood Sap]]. The [[Edge Prior]] is usually a rather bad unit, but it has a niche with '''Steelsinger'''. It is small enough that it can fit on a floor behind '''Steelsinger''', and reducing the {{Ember}} cost of all healing cards in hand, combined with the Awoken's natural access to card draw, can let you trigger {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} rapidly. At the [[Merchant of Arms]], [[Meat Shield]] and [[Exile's Diadem]] are worth grabbing - the former grants extra healing, while the latter reduces [[Steelsinger]]'s {{Capacity}} without needing {{IconLink|Smidgestone}}, letting you fit other units behind it. [[Awakening Thicket]] grants another heal every turn - with Meat Shield, Awakening Thicket, and {{IconLink|Regen}}, '''Steelsinger''' can gain {{Attack|+9}} every turn even with no other healing cards. [[Enchanted Chamber]] increases the healing granted by spells like Restore and Glimmer, which can help bring '''Steelsinger''' up to max {{Health}} even without Unleash the Wildwood. Although [[Void Armament]] is extremely pricey, it grants a precious stack of {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, and '''Steelsinger''' is pretty unlikely to die anyway. Note that in certain battles, especially [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]] and [[The Great Abyss]], '''Steelsinger''' can still be killed even if healed constantly. This makes [[Oldgrowth]] an extremely strong pick, as your deck will likely be focused on triggering {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} as frequently as possible already, and the extra {{Health}} can make '''Steelsinger''' virtually invincible. Keep in mind that although [[Equalizing Rings]] is one of the best combos with Oldgrowth under normal circumstances, it is generally bad with '''Steelsinger''', as its permascaling {{Attack}} can easily outpace its {{Health}}. This frees you up to merge Oldgrowth with another piece of equipment instead. Regardless of what else your deck includes, '''Steelsinger''' absolutely requires a {{IconLink|Multistrike}} source to pull its weight. Even if you can upgrade it with {{IconLink|Smidgestone}} and duplicate it, or give it {{IconLink|Fecundity}}, its steep {{Ember}} cost makes it impractical to play many copies of the unit. {{IconLink|Frenzystone}} should be priority number one at shops, and you should strongly consider fishing for a second unless you absolutely need {{IconLink|Smidgestone}} or {{IconLink|Titanstone}}, or another unit desperately needs {{IconLink|Multistrike}} as well. '''Steelsinger''' benefits massively from support to clear out backline units and soften up tanks. {{IconLink|Sweep}} units like [[Husk Hermit]] and [[Shattered Shell]] are excellent choices, and Shattered Shell in particular greatly appreciates being able to hide behind a beefy unit like '''Steelsinger''', though you will need extra {{Capacity}}, {{Capacity}} reduction effects, or cards like Restoring Retreat to actually set this up. Failing that, you can use {{IconLink|Spikes}} instead. '''Bristling''' Sentient is a solid option, but you can also put {{IconLink|Spikes}} on '''Steelsinger''' directly with cards like [[Pyre Shards]]. [[Inferno Room]] can be hard to play alongside '''Steelsinger''' as they are both on the expensive side, but it does a great job at destroying units that {{IconLink|Spikes}} would miss, like [[Vampiric Cherub]]s and [[Enthralled Ardent]]s. Your secondary clan will usually not offer much in the quest to heal '''Steelsinger''', but there are some exceptions. The [[Luna Coven]] has a decent number of healing cards, like [[Fae's Blessing]], [[Glittering Draught]], and [[Duality]], as well as artifacts like [[Kingdom's Tears]] and [[Circle of Cycles]]. Most importantly, if you start with [[Witchweave]]s, that adds another five cards to your deck that can heal '''Steelsinger''', and for {{Ember|0}} too. The [[Umbra]] and [[Lazarus League]] both have access to {{IconLink|Lifesteal}}, which '''Steelsinger''' adores, letting it scale its damage whenever it attacks and easily keeping it at maximum {{Health}}. [[Morsel Excavator]], [[Immortal Trade]], [[It's Alive!]], and [[Insatiable Hunger]] all grant {{IconLink|Lifesteal}}, as do [[Refined Void]], [[Vampire's Tooth]], and [[Goliath Infusion]]s. Both clans also offer the ever-useful {{IconLink|Trample}}, either from [[Umbra Stone]] or [[Twisted Assistant]]. Aim to get a minimum of {{Attack|250}} on '''Steelsinger''' by the time you reach Ring 7. With {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}}, this allows it to kill an [[Avowed Gladiator]] from full health. This is on the lower end of [[Steelsinger]]'s potential damage output by this point, and should be relatively easy to accomplish, albeit somewhat underwhelming for its price tag. Other key breakpoints include {{Attack|425}}, to kill a full-health [[Terrifying Amalgam]] in one hit, and {{Attack|500}}, to do the same to Avowed Gladiators; these are on the upper end of the spectrum and usually very tough to accomplish unless you have a lot of synergies, but are somewhat more feasible by Ring 8 or 9. If you pick up '''Steelsinger''' early and focus on taking healing spells, however, it is potentially possible to reach {{Attack|700}} or more, easily taking care of your damage output in the last few battles. '''Steelsinger''' should only be duplicated at an [[Empyrean Well]] by Ring 7 or 8; any earlier, and the copy will lose out on a huge amount of damage, or you will have to split your resources healing both and therefore make both less effective. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! {{UnitCard |name = Vinemother |image = PLR_Vinemother.png |clan = Awoken |rarity = Rare |type = Hollow |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 0/35 |ability = {{IconLink|End of Turn|png=EndOfTurn}}: '''[[Sting]]''' spells in your deck gain '''+4 [[Magic Power]]'''.
{{AbilityBox|Vinewrath|2|Add 2 [[Sting]] spells to hand.}} |flavor = These Awoken focus solely on the reproduction of the Wildwood, shedding their steel armor to further spread their thorns with each new surge of life. The Mothers are quite small in stature, but the shell around them provides immense natural protection. Along with the Channelers, they've been indispensable guides during my time in the Wildwood. |artist = Tammy Chang }} '''Vinemother''' is a rare [[Awoken]] [[banner unit]]. For every turn she is on the field, she makes [[Sting]]s in your deck stronger. Her {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}, '''Vinewrath''', provides two Stings every other turn. == Strategy == Assuming you use '''Vinewrath''' whenever it is available and play the [[Sting]]s it produces, '''Vinemother''' grants +2 draw every other turn, which makes her overall equivalent to a [[Limbo's Solace]], averaging out to +1 draw per turn. The fact that it comes in the form of [[Sting]]s is a blessing and a curse, as Sting is a rather useful spell overall, but does have some drawbacks (see [[Sting]] for more). She also boosts the strength of Stings in your deck every turn. While this isn't nothing, it still doesn't make Stings tremendously useful for damage past Ring 3 or so; she will add around +20-30 '''[[Magic Power]]''' total, which is okay but not enough to make a dent in later-game enemies. This can be improved by having multiple copies of '''Vinemother''', and is more useful if you have [[Channelheart]] or [[Thorn Casing]] for a head start or '''[[Piercing]]'''. However, it should be mentioned that her {{IconLink|End of Turn|png=EndOfTurn}} trigger '''only applies to Sting spells that currently exist in your deck'''. Since most sources of Sting like [[Thornfruit]], [[Preserved Thorns]], and '''Vinemother''' herself add Stings in the middle of combat, they will be completely unenhanced. Thus, even if you have an army of '''Vinemothers''', continually producing Stings during combat will still result in most of them being extremely weak. As such, '''Vinemother''' should generally be used as a tank that increases your draw, somewhat like '''Cultivating''' [[Sentient]], but in exchange for not scaling units behind her, she provides a bit of frontline damage and offers easy {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers (which makes her much more useful with the [[Stygian Guard]] in particular, as they greatly appreciate both {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers and extra draw). Considering that the other Awoken tanks, like [[Awoken Hollow]] and [[Thorned Hollow]], take up {{Capacity|3}} or more, her {{Capacity|2}} is an advantage. She can also be placed on a higher floor alone just for her draw effect. This way, she can perhaps guard a [[Wildwood Custodian]] or a similar support unit like [[Bone Dog]]. As discussed on the [[Sting]] page, Stings only increase your "real" draw if you are drawing non-Sting spells. As such, depending on your deck size and especially if you have multiple copies of '''Vinemother''', it may not be wise to use '''Vinewrath''' every time it is available. Even if you are trying to build a deck that Stings its way through every ring and have a bunch of '''Vinemothers''' to support this, due to the aforementioned issue with her {{IconLink|End of Turn|png=EndOfTurn}} effect, it is more advisable to use '''Vinewrath''' many times on the first turn and then never touch it again, as that way the huge number of Stings you produce will gain maximum power. Using it further will only dilute your draw with weaker Stings. Her prospects improve somewhat if you happen to be partnered with the [[Luna Coven]] or can obtain [[Silver Ink]] through an event like [[Gremlin Looter]] or [[Wreckage Remains]]. Making Stings '''[[Attuned]]''' dramatically increases the effect of her {{IconLink|End of Turn|png=EndOfTurn}} trigger, especially if you can redraw the same Stings several times with {{IconLink|Keepstone}} or by having a small deck. {{IconLink|Conduit}} in general can also power them up significantly, and she pairs very well with '''Celestial Spellweaver''' [[Ekka]]. Overall, when offered '''Vinemother''', she is usually better than a skip as long as you can afford to place her during Deployment, but she is very unlikely to be the centerpiece of your deck. Take her as a support unit, but do not prioritize her over a unit that actually solves problems for you. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! Wilting Sapwood:
{{UnitCard |name = Wilting Sapwood |image = PLR_WiltingSapwood.png |clan = Awoken |rarity = Rare |type = Hollow |banner = Yes |cost = 2 |size = 3 |stats = 5/50 |ability = {{IconLink|Revenge}}: Gain {{Ember|1}}. |flavor = As an Awoken prepares to leave its physical being to become a custodian of the Wildwood, they harden their bark for ensured protection. I've observed that they also put down more roots with each step towards death, strengthening the entire Wildwood in the process. |artist = Evan Yovaisis }} The '''Wilting Sapwood''' is a rare [[Awoken]] [[banner unit]]. It has high {{Health}} and provides {{Ember|1}} whenever it takes damage. == Strategy == '''Wilting Sapwood''' benefited greatly from the changes made in ''Monster Train 2''. Pure tank units have risen in value, and excess {{Ember}} is generally more useful as well. The Deployment phase also makes it far easier to get into play. Compared to other tanks in the Awoken clan, like [[Thorned Hollow]] and [[Awoken Hollow]], '''Wilting Sapwood''' requires much less maintenance and attention to perform, at the price of having a lower ceiling due to its lack of innate scaling. Its {{Health|50}} makes it one of the most durable units available, and unlike the other Hollow units, it does not need to be healed up to its max {{Health}}. This makes it effective at protecting fragile units like [[Animus of Will]] and [[Shattered Shell]]. '''Wilting Sapwood''' should be paired with decks that can make use of the glut of {{Ember}} it will provide. For the Awoken, this usually involves card draw effects, in order to maximize your hand size each turn and play as many cards as possible. Cards that provide extra draw, such as [[Rootseeds]], [[Invigorating Solution]], and [[Focused Growth]], should be prioritized. [[Awoken's Rail Spike]] can easily draw a full hand of cards with '''Wilting Sapwood''' supporting it. This draw, in turn, makes cards such as [[Spreading Spores]] better, as you will redraw them faster and can play them more often. In the worst case, you can use the {{Ember}} to play expensive cards like [[Cycle of Life]]. Depending on your partnered clan, there are other ways to benefit from large amounts of {{Ember}}. The respective [[Railspike]]s, being [[X-cost cards]], are almost always a solid option. The [[Spike of the Hellhorned]] and [[Spike of the Banished]] can provide a huge boost to {{Attack}} and {{IconLink|Armor}} on a unit, while [[Spike of the League]] can make a unit practically invincible by applying {{IconLink|Reanimate}}. [[Spike of the Legion]] '''[[Propagate]]'''s extant buffs on the unit and can send them through the roof. [[Shroud Spike]] is perhaps the strongest synergy, especially when combined with [[Kindle]], as a single [[Morsel Miner]] can easily be made to provide hundreds of {{Attack}} and {{Health}} to the frontmost unit, as well as triggering {{IconLink|Gorge}} many times over. Barring X-cost cards, you can also use '''Wilting Sapwood''' to play cards that would otherwise be too expensive to rely on, such as [[Heavenfall]], [[Pyreclasm]], [[Shadowsiege]], or [[Onehorn's Tome]]. These cards are much stronger when you don't need to worry about their staggering costs. {{Ember}} generated by '''Wilting Sapwood''' will be reduced by {{IconLink|Emberdrain}}, so it does not work well when frequently playing cards like [[Perils of Production]] and [[Void Binding]], but if you are not applying it in huge amounts - for example, if you are playing just a single copy of [[Furnace Tap]] - then the next few turns before it wears off will be much easier to stomach with '''Wilting Sapwood'''. Weak {{Ember|0}} damaging spells, such as [[Vine Grasp]], can be played on '''Wilting Sapwood''' to trigger {{IconLink|Revenge}} during your turn, potentially giving you enough {{Ember}} to play something else. It deals 12 damage to the front enemy unit, and draws 1 extra card on the next turn. ==Strategy== '''Sting''' is a mostly "free" card - it costs no {{Ember}}, and the draw it takes it makes up for by drawing one extra card next turn. Its damage is moderately useful early (and sometimes can pick off things like [[Misshapen Fiend]], or kill backliners with [[Vine Grasp]]'s help), and it's a low-cost {{IconLink|Incant}} activation. Owing to its low opportunity cost to play, it also scales quite well with {{IconLink|Conduit}} and other sources of Magic Power. Thankfully, you don't need a target to play it, so even if your train is flooded with enemies with {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers like in [[Heaven%27s_Maw#Harbinger of Entropy|Harbinger of Entropy]], you can play it in the Pyre room in the worst case to still get the draw next turn. There are several ways to add copies of this card to your deck, in mostly temporary ways. One hazard common to all of them is overfilling your deck with this card. While it's "free" up to a point, you can only draw up to 10 cards per turn, meaning if you're already drawing 10 cards next turn, this card actually is costing you a "real" draw. If half of them are '''Stings''', you may very well be actually losing "actual" (meaning non-'''Sting''') card draw to this card. (And if you have [[Rootseeds]], they also contribute to this limit.) What that limit is depends on your deck size; this can become a problem if you trim down your deck at the end of a run. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Upgrade !! {{SpellCard |name = Glimmer |image = CRD_Glimmer.png |clan = [[Awoken]] |rarity = Common |cost = 1 |effect = Restore '''3''' health to friendly units and deal '''3''' damage to enemy units. |flavor = If struck by a surge of electricity, a Sapwood will crystallize into glass. The sap within will become preserved as a supercharged healing solvent. But I can't seem to break the glass without losing much of this sap in the process. |artist = Cameron Archer }} '''Glimmer''' is an [[Awoken]] spell. It deals 3 damage to enemies and restores {{Health|3}} to friendly units. ==Strategy== '''Glimmer''' has fallen off significantly since the original ''Monster Train''. In ''The Last Divinity'' DLC, powerful temple upgrades such as '''Extremestone''' and '''Truestone''' allowed it to keep up with the increased stats and distribution of {{IconLink|Spell Shield}} on enemies, letting it solve waves deep into the lategame and making it a strong duplication target. Enemies since then have only gotten more resilient, while these upgrades have not been brought back for ''Monster Train 2'', nor has '''Glimmer''' seen a notable buff that would allow it to address its newfound weaknesses. This leaves '''Glimmer''' and other similar AoE cards such as [[Vent]] in an awkward position. Nonetheless, it remains a decent pickup, especially early on, where it can wipe out squishy waves such as [[Forsaken]] rushes as well as access other threatening backlines. With a {{IconLink|Powerstone}} upgrade, it can defeat most backliners up to Ring 6, and with two of them or a single {{IconLink|Surgestone}}, it can defeat [[Discordant Heretic]]s and [[Enthralled Ardent]]s even afterward. However, its usefulness as an offensive spell in the lategame is otherwise limited; it struggles to kill Chosen enemies and fails to address [[Deformed Duo]] and [[Purified Soul]] by itself, forcing you to find other solutions to them. The healing from '''Glimmer''' will often be more relevant for your run at that point, especially if you are leaning into {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} triggers. '''Glimmer''' also synergizes well with the [[Luna Coven]], which can provide {{IconLink|Conduit}} to increase spell damage significantly. Any sources of scaling {{IconLink|Conduit}}, such as [[Ekka]]'s '''Celestial Spellweaver''' path, can quickly pump up this card's numbers back to what they need to be to punch through the lategame waves it would otherwise struggle with. Such a strategy also appreciates Glimmer being only {{Ember|1}} baseline, as the Luna Coven's options for area damage all tend to be expensive. [[Enchanted Chamber]] can also provide more Magic Power to help '''Glimmer''' muscle through lategame backliners that it normally can't reach. Overall, '''Glimmer''' is a viable option and remains strong early in the run. However, barring highrolls or specific synergies, it can't be relied on as much anymore for all-purpose waveclearing against the powercreep of the ''Monster Train 2'' lategame. ==Recommended Upgrades== {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! It increases the target's {{Attack}} by 6 and applies {{IconLink|Spikes|6}}. ==Strategy== '''Sharpen''' allows any frontline unit to be able to efficiently wipe out early- and mid-game backliners on contact through the {{IconLink|Spikes}} it grants, assuming it can take their hits. With backline clear being of utmost importance in ''Monster Train 2'', '''Sharpen''' has improved slightly from the original ''Monster Train'', especially with its buff to {{IconLink|Spikes|6}}, increasing its reach further into the game. The lack of Pact Shard-enhanced enemies also helps '''Sharpen''' considerably, as you will no longer have to worry about early-game backliners in regular combats randomly gaining {{Health}} and being out of reach of a single '''Sharpen''' application. Furthermore, the new [[Merchant of Magic]] upgrade {{IconLink|Smolderstone}} also fixes several of this card's problems, allowing it to add {{IconLink|Spikes}} for free and then get out of the way for your deck's faster forms of scaling later on. Another factor that improves '''Sharpen''' is that frontline bruisers with high {{Attack}} are more common, and also stronger, than in the original ''Monster Train''. The [[Awoken]] themselves have no shortage of such units, such as the newly-buffed [[Husk Hermit]] or [[Awoken Hollow]], but cross-clan, new tanks such as [[Firebrand]] and [[Shadeguard]] frequently both take damage and dish it back out, to the point where you may even consider {{IconLink|Frenzystone}} on them on occasion. Thus, it is no longer as paradoxical for '''Sharpen''' to be providing a {{Attack}} buff to a frontline tank, as they will often be able to use that buff well. That being said, '''Sharpen''' still tends to be overcosted for the stat boosts it applies. If you are using other forms of backline removal, such as a unit with {{IconLink|Quick}} and {{IconLink|Sweep}}, it usually isn't economical to use '''Sharpen''' as a source of long-term damage scaling, unless you have [[Gnarled Root]]. For example, [[Steel Enhancer]] gives half as much offensive scaling, plus defensive scaling for {{Ember|2}} less, while [[Razorsharp Edge]] gives twice as much offensive scaling at once. The {{IconLink|Spikes}} that it grants will also fall off into the lategame unless you can find a way to play '''Sharpen''' consistently or upgrade its output, and only the most resilient of tanks will be able to survive long-term to make those {{IconLink|Spikes}} work against lategame waves, especially against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]]. On Covenant 10, Chosen variants of enemies during flying boss fights are essentially '''Sharpen''''s ghosts from ''Monster Train'' past, as they have far too much {{Health}} to reach even with repeated applications of '''Sharpen'''. Nonetheless, '''Sharpen''' still fares quite a bit better in ''Monster Train 2'' compared to its original incarnation, and can be a worthy early addition to your run. ==Recommended Upgrades== {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! It applies {{IconLink|Rooted}} to the target, holding them in place for a turn. ==Strategy== '''Ensnare''' is one of the strongest cards available to the Awoken, and should almost never be skipped. It costs no {{Ember}}, refunds its draw on the next turn, and has an extremely strong effect, able to stop an enemy of your choice in place for a turn. This is almost always useful, and even when you have no enemies you want to root, you can usually find one that's going to die anyway and play this card for the +1 draw next turn. {{SpellCard |name = Awoken's Rail Spike |image = CRD_AwokensRailSpike.png |clan = Awoken |rarity = Rare |cost = X |effect = '''[[Consume]]'''.

Cannot draw additional cards this turn. |flavor = Though reluctant at first to allow the Rail to come through the Wildwood, the Edge Priory eventually agreed with me to let it pass and uphold the Covenant with Seraph. |artist = Brian Mutschler }} '''Awoken's Rail Spike''' is an [[Awoken]] spell. It draws X cards and applies {{Ember|-1}} to each of them for the rest of combat, but prohibits you from drawing more cards this turn. It is the Awoken offering for the [[Railspikes (event)|Railspikes]] event. ==Notes== * As with all card draw effects in Monster Train 2, this card cannot directly draw itself, even if it has an {{IconLink|Eternalstone}}. ==Strategy== '''Awoken's Rail Spike''' is a rare and powerful source of immediate card draw, making it uniquely powerful. It can let you access cards faster and spam them more easily, and is one of the most breakable cards in the game. As it's offered in the [[Railspikes (event)|Railspikes]] event, you'll sometimes get the chance with clan combos that don't include the [[Awoken]], and it can shine with any clan combination. '''Awoken's Rail Spike''' will mostly refund you what you paid for it immediately in {{Ember}} discounts, as well as progressing you through your deck faster. It will leave you on {{Ember|0}} after playing it, like any X cost card, though. If it discounts 1-cost cards, you can then play them immediately, and regardless of whether you can play them or not, the cards will stay discounted through the rest of the battle. It can be less good if you hit cards that cost more than 1, as you won't be able to play them immediately. It can be troublesome if there's a key spell that costs {{Ember|2+}} that you draw with '''Awoken's Rail Spike''', as you might have to wait until the second cycle of your deck to play it. It can also be a bit difficult to decide when to use it on a particular turn, as you're choosing between the known power in your hand and the less known power of the next few cards of your deck - usually, you won't be able to play cards that were already in your hand after playing this if they don't cost {{Ember|0}}. The aforementioned problem of being unable to play cards that still cost 1 after drawing them with this card can be mitigated with ways to gain {{Ember}} mid-turn, such as [[Aquath's Reservation]], [[Engraft]] with {{IconLink|Emberstone}}, or [[Excavated Ember]], making them excellent to pair with this card. [[Ancient Pyretap]] can help with this situation too if you have a little bit of {{PyreHealth}} to spare. Alternatively, [[Split Anvil]] can be used to amazing effect with this card. If given enough {{Ember}} [[Split Anvil]] will discount all spells currently in hand while this card discounts all incoming cards. It's usually hard for you to control what this spell discounts - [[Keepstone|Holdover]] cards that you've already played this turn won't be drawn unless you can draw everything else, though they are desirable targets for the discount. {{IconLink|Endless}} units can be discounted reliably enough, though, if you kill them right before playing this card, as they are put on top, and this can be very useful. It draws a unit, reduces its cost to {{Ember|0}}, and applies {{Attack|+20}} and {{Health|+20}}. ==Notes== This spell draws from the top of your draw pile, and then your discard pile if there are no units in your draw pile. * This means that if an {{IconLink|Endless}} unit died and hasn't been re-drawn yet, this is guaranteed to draw them. * Naturally, it cannot draw a unit already in your hand. ==Strategy== '''Channelsong''' is a very useful spell, though like all "draw a unit" spells it's hard to have it give the bonus to the unit you want. From the player's perspective, the unit it draws is a random unit you haven't played yet. Without upgrades, its effectiveness is limited, but it is essentially draw-neutral as long as you have a unit for it to draw. It also provides an appreciable stat boost to any unit, improving both damage output and survivability. Initially, it can often draw units in your starting deck, like [[Spear Steward]]s or [[Shield Steward]]s that were unplayed during the [[Deployment Phase]], which benefit somewhat but are usually not ideal targets. Purging these can allow you to more effectively choose your target. Note that if you intend to draw a banner unit, that unit must not be played during the [[Deployment Phase]]. Good units to target with this spell: * Units with {{IconLink|Sweep}} or {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, which can take advantage of extra {{Attack}} effectively. Conveniently, the Awoken have [[Animus of Will]], [[Husk Hermit]] and [[Shattered Shell]], all excellent targets. * Non-banner units like [[Shard Channeler]] or [[Wildwood Custodian]] that want to be in play early and appreciate the extra {{Health}} this gives. * Units with high {{Ember}} costs that have their cost set to 0 by this spell, such as [[Wilting Sapwood]]. This can allow you to, in practice, improve your {{DeploymentEmber}}. * Units with {{IconLink|Endless}}, as the {{Ember|0}} buff persists through death, allowing you to save {{Ember}} multiple times. If you have a way of killing them mid-turn, you can even use this spell after they have died to be guaranteed to re-draw them and apply {{Ember|0}}, meaning you don't even need to refrain from playing them in the [[Deployment Phase]]. Generally, you'll want to play the unit as soon as possible, making a {{IconLink|Seekstone}} essential. When these stores are tapped into, the energy provides a surge of new life and power to the host. |artist = Loy Bouttamy }} '''Unleash the Wildwood''' is an [[Awoken]] spell. It fully heals all friendly units on the floor. ==Strategy== '''Unleash the Wildwood''' is undoubtedly the best healing card in the game (not counting "healing" cards which are valuable for other reasons, such as [[Fae's Blessing]]). It affects all friendly units on the floor, provides an unlimited amount of healing, and comes at a very low cost. That said, it is still not always worth taking. Healing can only restore {{Health}} up to its maximum value, unlike cards which apply {{IconLink|Armor}} or {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} on top, like [[Alloy of the Ancients]] or [[Void Binding]], or those which increase {{Health}} directly like [[Cycle of Life]]. This means that '''Unleash the Wildwood''' is useful only if your units are frequently at low health, but are not actually dying. It works best with units which have extremely high {{Health}}, or with {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, which can keep a unit alive at {{Health|1}} until they can be healed. '''Unleash the Wildwood''' is worth taking for any healing-focused build. The main question is whether a healing-focused build is worth investing in in the first place. [[Oldgrowth]] immediately justifies taking '''Unleash the Wildwood''', as it will cause units to gain far, far more max {{Health}} than other healing spells can reasonably fill. With Oldgrowth, '''Unleash the Wildwood''' can instantly heal a unit for over {{Health|300}}. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Upgrade !! Adaptive Mutation:
{{SpellCard |name = Adaptive Mutation |image = CRD_AdaptiveMutation.png |clan = Awoken |rarity = Rare |cost = 2 |effect = '''[[Consume]]'''.
Restore a friendly unit to full health then swap {{Attack}} and {{Health}}. |flavor = After the soul within has succumbed to the will of the Wildwood, a Hollow is free to evolve into something more suitable for its eventual purpose, growing new vines or sloughing them off as necessary. |artist = Evan Yoviasis }} '''Adaptive Mutation''' is an [[Awoken]] spell. It fully heals a friendly unit, then sets its maximum {{Health}} equal to its current {{Attack}} and its base {{Attack}} equal to its {{Health}}. ==Notes== You can mouse over a unit to see what its "base" {{Attack}} is and its maximum health - if the unit has [[Buffs]]/[[Debuffs]] that increase/decrease its {{Attack}}, the base {{Attack}} is shown on the bottom, and the value with the boost on top. For {{Health}}, the bottom number is the maximum. The top number for {{Attack}} will become the unit's new maximum {{Health}} value, which will also be their current {{Health}}. The bottom number for {{Health}} (the maximum {{Health}}) will become the ''bottom'' number for {{Attack}}. Since [[Buffs]] are not affected by this card, the difference between the bottom and top numbers for {{Attack}} will remain the same. So the top number for {{Attack}} will then be their previous maximum {{Health}} ''plus'' {{Attack}} granted by their buffs. ==Strategy== '''Adaptive Mutation''' is an odd spell, with an effect which can be either negative or positive. On its own, it is generally not very effective; it decreases either {{Attack}} or {{Health}} in return for increasing the other, and the benefit is not particularly significant in most cases. In its regular best-case scenario, '''Adaptive Mutation''' can turn Awoken's high-health units ([[Awoken Hollow]], [[Thorned Hollow]], [[Steelsinger]], and [[Wyldenten]] as '''Thornlord''' or '''Strangler''') into damage dealers, especially if the banner units have been upgraded with {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. For example, an Awoken Hollow upgraded with {{IconLink|Heartstone}} is summoned as a {{AttackHealth|15/45}} with an extra 60 max {{Health}}, which '''Adaptive Mutation''' immediately turns into {{AttackHealth|105/15}}. Unfortunately, this scenario is hard to plan for, since {{IconLink|Multistrike}} is not good on these units (barring Steelsinger) without '''Adaptive Mutation''', and you're not guaranteed to see any particular rare card in your run. This also leaves these units vulnerable due to their low {{Health}}, and still does not make them strong enough to deal effectively with late-game enemies. However, the spell becomes enormously useful if you have an effective source of {{IconLink|Rage}} or {{IconLink|Valor}}. This will set the unit's {{Health}} equal to ''total'' {{Attack}}, including that from buffs, while only setting the ''base'' {{Attack}} equal to {{Health}}. This can massively increase the unit's health for little or no cost. For example, a unit with base {{Attack|10}}, {{IconLink|Rage|5}} (and therefore an effective {{Attack|+20}}), and {{Health|10}} will end up with base {{Attack|10}}, {{IconLink|Rage|5}}, and {{Health|20}}. This can be even more effective if you have a way to play '''Adaptive Mutation''' multiple times, converting {{IconLink|Rage}} to {{Health}} and then converting it back to {{Attack}}, which the {{IconLink|Rage}} will stack on top of, meaning that you will gain even more {{Health}} the next time you play the spell. This can be used to scale up both {{Health}} and {{Attack}} on a unit to ludicrous levels if you have a way to play this spell frequently. A similar synergy can be achieved with the [[Gnarled Root]] artifact, effectively stacking {{IconLink|Spikes}} on units to increase {{Attack}}. It is extremely useful with [[Little Fade]]'s '''Little Icarus''' path, as she will build up a ludicrous amount of {{Attack}} and {{IconLink|Spikes}}, but her {{Health}} will remain pitifully low, forcing her to be constantly '''[[Reform]]ed'''. With '''Adaptive Mutation''', you can instead turn her directly into a tank with hundreds of {{Health}} and let entire combats simply kill themselves on her {{IconLink|Spikes}}. Units equipped with [[Oldgrowth]] are another solid target for this spell, as long as you have the ability to rapidly trigger {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} and thereby increase their max {{Health}}. This ends up working somewhat similarly to merging it with [[Equalizing Rings]]. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Upgrade !! {{SpellCard |name = Spreading Spores |image = CRD_SpreadingSpores.png |clan = Awoken |rarity = Rare |cost = 1 |effect = Restore '''3''' health. Apply {{IconLink|Regen|3}} and {{IconLink|Spikes|3}}. Add a copy of this card to your discard pile. |flavor = When thorns find their mark, they release spores into the air to incapacitate unsuspecting victims. These poor souls soon transform into Awoken and feed the vines that first spread the spores. On the embarrassingly frequent occasions that I'm stung by these thorns, I remove them before any real damage occurs. |artist = Loy Bouttamy }} '''Spreading Spores''' is an [[Awoken]] spell. It heals 3 health, applies {{IconLink|Regen|3}} and {{IconLink|Spikes|3}}, and creates a copy of itself each time it is played. The copies are identical, and will also create copies, but are not permanently added to the deck and will be removed at the end of the battle. ==Interactions== * If '''Spreading Spores''' has {{IconLink|Twinstone}}, then the '''[[Ephemeral]]''' copy will also duplicate itself, albeit without Ephemeral. Since each Spellchain copy creates two copies of itself (one with {{IconLink|Twinstone}} and one without), and each Ephemeral copy creates another non-Spellchain copy, this allows you to fill your deck up with '''Spreading Spores''' much faster, at the cost of most copies not having Spellchain. ==Strategy== '''Spreading Spores''' is a powerful card, having been significantly buffed in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It has the potential to fill your entire deck with copies of itself, but this is only desirable if your deck is capable of using them effectively. Because any upgrades applied will affect all copies, filling out upgrade slots is a high priority. It is best to use '''Spreading Spores''' when you have plenty of draw, making it better with [[Rootseeds]] than [[Restore]] and encouraging [[Limbo's Solace]] over other boss artifacts. It is also best with a small deck, so that you can shuffle and replay '''Spreading Spores''' as often as possible. Each time you shuffle the deck, assuming you play all copies of '''Spreading Spores''', you will double the number of copies on the next shuffle. This can quickly turn your deck into a massive pile of '''Spreading Spores''' with occasional other cards mixed in. This makes cost reduction upgrades especially important, as not being able to play out all of the '''Spreading Spores''' in your hand will defeat the purpose of taking it in the first place. It is particularly good with the [[Pyre of Entropy]], which provides plenty of draw and which benefits from large numbers of cheap but useful spells which can flood your deck. In the right situation, '''Spreading Spores''' can stack up an enormous amount of {{IconLink|Regen}} and {{IconLink|Spikes}} on a unit, making it virtually unkillable by the time the boss arrives. In addition, even a single copy will apply {{IconLink|Spikes|3}} (or {{IconLink|Spikes|6}} with Doublestack), easily wiping out most backliners as soon as you can play it. Because a strong '''Spreading Spores'''-focused deck solves defense, backline damage, and boss fights, the rest of your deck should be focused on killing tanky frontliners like [[Avowed Gladiator]]. Fortunately, '''Spreading Spores''' has synergies with several other Awoken cards which can take those enemies down effectively. [[Steelsinger]] benefits from constant {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} triggers and can stack up enough {{Attack}} to kill most enemies in a single hit, while [[Bramble Lash]] scales off of your {{IconLink|Spikes}}, becoming stronger each time '''Spreading Spores''' is played. With {{IconLink|Smolderstone}}, it can consistently trigger {{IconLink|Etch}}, similar to [[Pandemic]]. However, this prevents it from fulfilling its normal functions unless it also has {{IconLink|Twinstone}}, as you will only have one copy in your deck at any time. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Oldgrowth:
{{EquipmentCard |image = CRD_Oldgrowth.png |clan = Awoken |rarity = Rare |cost = 1 |effect = {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}}: Gain '''10''' max health.
'''+10''' max health. |flavor = Where the Hollow leave behind their husks, there are vines that refuse to die. They grow and grow, forestalling their inevitable decay. The Channelers say this is because "She" still lives. Few know what they could mean and even fewer find comfort in their words. |artist = Genevieve Bega }} '''Oldgrowth''' is a rare [[Awoken]] equipment added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It grants a unit 10 max {{Health}} immediately and an additional 10 max {{Health}} on {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}}. The added {{Health}} is only ''maximum'' {{Health}}, so a unit with {{Health|10/10}} which is healed for {{Health|1}} will be left at {{Health|11/20}}. ==Notes== Like all ''max health'' buffs, these buffs go on the '''unit''', not the '''card''', unlike normal {{Health}} buffs. This means the extra max health will not stay if the unit dies and is replayed, e.g. due to {{IconLink|Endless}} or [[Reform]]. ==Strategy== '''Oldgrowth''' is an extremely powerful card, potentially allowing you to stack up hundreds of {{Health}} and making a unit virtually invincible. It is better with [[Restore]], but even if you start with [[Rootseeds]] it can be extremely effective. Any source of {{IconLink|Regen}} will provide {{Health|+10}} every turn, and the Awoken have access to many spells which are useful for activating constant {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} triggers, especially [[Engraft]] and [[Spreading Spores]]. You will need to fill the unit's empty {{Health}}, so stronger healing cards like [[Unleash the Wildwood]] are also effective. The [[Luna Coven]] is an effective allied clan when using '''Oldgrowth'''; if you happen to start with [[Witchweave]], it can provide cheap {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} triggers, and {{IconLink|Conduit}} improves the effectiveness of healing spells. '''Oldgrowth''' can be merged effectively with many other pieces of equipment. [[Equalizing Rings]] becomes one of the strongest sources of {{Attack}} in the game when merged with '''Oldgrowth''', granting {{Attack|+10}} every time the unit is healed and still only costing {{Ember|1}}, and also making the unit immune to {{IconLink|Sap}}. [[Meat Shield]] will provide a {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} trigger every turn. If allied with the [[Banished]], the [[Shield of Wyngh]] allows a unit to easily wipe out backliners and deal massive damage even to units like [[Avowed Gladiator]]. Because '''Oldgrowth''' merged with Equalizing Rings solves both offense and defense (assuming that you can continuously heal the unit), it can make a fragile damage dealer strong enough to win with no support. Units with {{IconLink|Multistrike}} or {{IconLink|Sweep}} are excellent targets, and several are available in the Awoken. '''Awakening Thicket''' is an uncommon [[Awoken]] room added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update, replacing [[Awake]]. It grants friendly units '''+20''' max health and restores '''10''' health on {{IconLink|Resolve}}.

==Strategy==

'''Awakening Thicket''' gives another {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} and '''Cultivate''' activation to all your units on the floor, in addition to your spells. The health recovery helps your units survive longer. The max health increase makes your units harder to kill if you are able to restore them to max health consistently, especially when you are fighting a [[Boss]] unit with {{IconLink|Relentless}}.

Don't forget the effects apply to all your units on the floor, which means it can also help your backline units stay alive in certain situations. For example, it can help them survive {{IconLink|Spikes}}, enemy units with {{IconLink|Sweep}}, or minor amounts of {{IconLink|Corruption}}.

'''Stygian Guard''' [[File:ClanStygian.png|20x20px]] is a [[clan]] in [[Monster Train 2]], returning from [[Monster Train 1]]. It is unlocked after unlocking [[Hellhorned]] first and then casting 5 spells in a turn. 

Stygian Guard features the following mechanics:
* Many units have {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers, encouraging lots of spells to be played.
* Many spells and units draw or discard other cards during your turn. '''[[Offering]]''' cards can be played for free by discarding them.
* The clan features many high-damage spells, often with '''[[Attuned]]'''. {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} is a common debuff that increases spell damage, and the clan offers other ways to increase '''[[Magic Power]]'''.
* Some spells have '''[[Permafrost]]''', and certain mechanics allow other cards to be '''[[Frozen]]'''.
* {{IconLink|Frostbite}} is a common debuff which deals damage to enemies over time.
* {{IconLink|Sap}} and {{IconLink|Armor}} are both used to mitigate incoming damage.

The clan's unique [[Merchant of Steel]] Upgrade is {{IconLink|Runestone}}.

{{AbilityBox|Runespeak III|3|Draw a damage spell and apply '''+20 [[Magic Power]]'''.}} }} ==Strategy== '''Tethys''' was widely considered the worst Champion in the first Monster Train (at least after the release of the Last Divinity DLC), but in Monster Train 2 she is far stronger. For the most part, this is not due to direct changes to '''Tethys''' herself, but rather indirect buffs resulting from changes to enemies. With {{IconLink|Spikes}} and {{IconLink|Sweep}} being far less common on enemies, her low {{Health}} is much less of a liability. However, it is still important to put effort into keeping her alive regardless of path, especially against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]] or [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]]. This makes cards which can apply effects like {{IconLink|Armor}}, {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} or raw {{Health}} very useful to mitigate her very low base {{Health}}. Regardless of path, '''Tethys''' should almost always be placed in the back. Being only {{Capacity|1}} helps with this, allowing her to fit behind two {{Capacity|2}} units on a {{Capacity|5}} floor. ===Chillwind=== This is [[Tethys Titansbane|Tethys]]'s simplest path, applying {{IconLink|Frostbite}} to a single enemy. With this path, she is essentially just a glass cannon who deals high damage to a single target, and requires little planning or support to be effective. {{IconLink|Frostbite}} damage is delayed until after enemies attack regardless of when she attacks, meaning that she does not benefit as much from {{IconLink|Quick}} as other damage dealers would. However, this also means that her damage hits again on future turns. It also makes her exceptional at {{IconLink|Relentless}} combat, as her damage effectively scales with each hit. It is usually worth taking a level in '''Handheld Totem''' to let her hit the entire row of enemies and add {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}}. However, '''Chillwind III''' increases her damage significantly, and if you already have another unit with {{IconLink|Sweep}} to deal with backliners (or [[Iron-tongue]], for the best of both worlds) it may be worth going all in on this path. ===Conduit=== '''Conduit''' allows you to play expensive damage spells at lower costs, or even for free. Even one level of '''Conduit''' is enough to make her starter card, [[Frozen Lance]], cost {{Ember|0}}. At level III, almost every damage spell in the game will cost {{Ember|0}}. This makes [[Limbo's Solace]] much more useful, and [[Hell's Flame]] much less so. You will also want to pick up as many expensive damage spells as possible to take advantage of the cost reduction. Her {{IconLink|Conduit}} can add a reasonable amount of extra damage, which becomes much more important on Attuned or multihitting spells. Note that spells which do not deal direct damage, such as [[Hoarfrost Effigy]], are not discounted. This path works extremely well with {{IconLink|Incant}} units, of which there are many in the Stygian Guard. However, in the early game, it is by far the weakest of her paths, having very low stats and contributing little against {{IconLink|Relentless}} bosses. Thus, it's safest to take this path when you already have a solid {{IconLink|Incant}} unit that can carry you against the first boss, like [[Siren of the Sea]]. While it may be worth mixing this path with others if you do not need to fully discount {{Ember|3}} spells, it is somewhat awkward when mixed with '''Handheld Totem'''. '''Conduit''' wants you to play damaging spells on the same floor as Tethys, while '''Handheld Totem''' works best while playing them on the floor above. This combo can still be worth using, however, as both paths are very powerful even at level I. ===Handheld Totem=== '''Handheld Totem''' gives Tethys {{IconLink|Sweep}}, a very strong status effect, along with {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} on {{IconLink|Strike}}. This means that all enemies will leave combat ready to be instantly destroyed by a powerful damage spell. When using this path, '''Tethys''' should usually be played on the middle or bottom floor, so that you can play damage spells against enemies on the floor above her. Against bosses, '''Tethys''' is less effective due to her low damage output and the irrelevance of {{IconLink|Sweep}} against single targets. However, even if her floor fails to kill the boss, she can stack up enough {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} that a spell on the next floor can finish them off. She also wipes out any other enemies that might get in the way of the spell. Like '''Conduit''', '''Handheld Totem''' works best when you have many damage spells in your deck. However, even without that, {{IconLink|Sweep}} makes her a powerful unit for clearing backliners. If you don't care about {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}}, it can be worth taking one or two levels in '''Chillwind''' for higher damage output. Her '''Runespeak''' ability can provide extra draw, as well as gradually buffing the average spell damage of your deck over the course of a battle. However, it is difficult to use effectively, as the spell drawn is random and will often be a basic [[Frozen Lance]]. This should be seen as a minor boost to her power rather than the main reason to use this path. If you can remove cards until all those which are left are good targets for Magic Power (either due to full-floor damage, Attuned, or multiple hits), this ability can buff them significantly. == Trivia == Tethys loosely resembles an [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axolotl axolotl], and her internal name is AcksoLotal. == Quotes == '''Summoned''' * ''Does the Titan still sleep?'' * ''The Covenant was necessary. Removes ability on use.}} }} == Strategy== All of '''Solgard''''s upgrade paths require {{IconLink|Shard}} which is gained on {{IconLink|Incant}} to function. As such, they all want to be paired with other {{IconLink|Incant}} units for you to make the most of your spells. All of these paths, as they rely on {{IconLink|Shard}}, struggle early in fights (though '''Titanchannel''''s being in {{IconLink|Stasis}} can sometimes be an advantage) and tend to prefer higher-floor setups to give you time to build up your {{IconLink|Shard}}. ===Direchannel=== '''Direchannel''' uses {{IconLink|Shard}} to deal damage to the front enemy unit - this is fairly similar to giving '''Solgard''' {{Attack}}. This allows it to be put behind a tank and contribute what can add up to a fairly large hit, especially as the fight goes on. With a good tank, it can do well in {{IconLink|Relentless}} combat. Unfortunately, the issue for this path is that there are very few ways for you to build on it. Since the damage is an {{IconLink|Action}} rather than a standard attack, you can't even use {{IconLink|Multistrike}} to multiply it. He's stuck being able to do this once per turn, and in many cases he might just be picking off a weakened enemy or removing a stack of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} from an enemy, as you have few ways of reliably controlling when '''Solgard''''s {{IconLink|Action}} trigger goes off unless you can give him {{IconLink|Quick}} from [[Swiftsteel Dagger]] or a few clan cards. The upsides of this being an {{IconLink|Action}} rather than a standard attack, such as bypassing {{IconLink|Spikes}} and {{IconLink|Sap}}, are not generally relevant. You could take this path if you need a boss answer early in the game, weren't offered '''Titanchannel''', and can't satisfy '''Coldchannel''''s need for health support. You could consider it pseudo-{{IconLink|Multistrike}} if combined with the other paths, but it really struggles to make much of an impact on a run - which is not a position you want your [[Champion]] to be in. ===Coldchannel=== '''Coldchannel''' gives '''Solgard''' the ability to apply {{IconLink|Frostbite}} in large quantities to entire floors, clearing backline enemies, significantly denting sturdy enemies later in fights, and taking on {{IconLink|Relentless}} bosses very well while also accumulating {{IconLink|Frostbite}} on flying bosses, but only with enough support to keep it alive. The immediate problem with this line is that he needs to be in front and take hits to be able to use its ability, but his {{Health}} isn't great, and the [[Stygian Guard]] don't have a lot of ways to help him with this. Furthermore, {{IconLink|Frostbite}} is more effective if applied on lower floors, but '''Solgard''' tends to want time to build up {{IconLink|Shard}}, and Monster Train 2's lategame is full of enemies that can bring plenty of offensive pressure to bear on your units. But if your allied clan has ways of keeping him alive - {{IconLink|Armor}}, {{IconLink|Regen}}, {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, [[Reform]], etc. - he can be the centerpiece of your strategy. However, note that [[Reform]] specifically will entirely reset his {{IconLink|Shard}} count, making it less than ideal. Drafting spells that can snipe backliners can still be a good idea on this line, even though it already deals with them, simply as a way to control how much pressure '''Solgard''' is under. Depending on how many {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers you can consistently proc on the first turn of battle, it may be wise to take a level or two of '''Titanchannel''', although note that you will miss out on '''Coldchannel III''' which doubles the {{IconLink|Frostbite}} application. If you can {{IconLink|Incant}} at least four times on turn 1 (or by the first turn enemies reach '''Solgard'''), '''Titanchannel I''' will give '''Solgard''' more {{Health}} than '''Coldchannel II''' or '''Coldchannel III'''. If you have '''Titanchannel I / Coldchannel I''', you must be able to {{IconLink|Incant}} seven or more times on the first turn for '''Titanchannel II''' to give more {{Health}} than '''Coldchannel II'''. ===Titanchannel=== '''Titanchannel''' is a very potent path for '''Solgard''', capable of accumulating absolutely tremendous stats, but he requires quite a bit of setup time to be effective. As such, this path can be slightly awkward. The biggest issue with using '''Titanchannel''' is that you effectively don't have a Champion for the first several turns of battle, which is problematic against flying bosses and the Titans. '''Titanchannel''' can make '''Solgard''' an incredible tank, easily building over {{Health|300+}}, but he cannot effectively protect fragile allies like [[Nameless Siren]] for the first few turns, necessitating an alternate means of defense, like [[Guardian Stone]] or [[Lodestone Totem]]. Despite this, he still occupies {{Capacity}} on his floor, which means that until you activate '''Resurgence''', your floor essentially has {{Capacity|-2}}. This can be a problem for {{IconLink|Incant}} builds, which typically want as many units as possible on their floors, and {{Capacity}} is often at a premium. In general, if you have a decent {{IconLink|Incant}} floor that involves '''Solgard''' and you can wait to activate '''Resurgence''' until the boss arrives, '''Titanchannel''' will be strong enough to secure {{IconLink|Relentless}}, as he will likely have built up {{IconLink|Shard|40+}} and gain truly colossal stats. It is usually a good idea not to trigger '''Resurgence''' until it is absolutely necessary - for example if an important unit is about to die. With sufficient defensive measures (for example, a Holdover [[Frenzied Swarm]]), it is possible that you will not need to pop '''Solgard''' until the very end of the fight, or even that you will win without him. Note, however, that this is somewhat more difficult in [[Clash with the Titans]], as [[Entropy]] will be attacking your frontmost unit (other than '''Solgard''') for {{Attack|20}} every turn unless you can apply {{IconLink|Sap}}, which will generally severely limit your setup time. If your build is strong enough to survive without '''Solgard''', you can consider placing him alone on an empty floor, perhaps even in an [[Inferno Room]]. {{IconLink|Stasis}} prevents him from being damaged, but he counts as a unit on the floor for the purposes of [[Terrifying Amalgam]]s' and [[Savagery]]'s Pyre damage on {{IconLink|Resolve}}. When partnered with the [[Melting Remnant]], '''Titanchannel''' should almost always be the first choice, simply because it is the only path '''Solgard''' has that is compatible with dying and being [[Reform]]ed, or being made {{IconLink|Endless}}. {{IconLink|Shard}} resets on unit death, but the stats gained from '''Resurgence''' will stick. In fact, if he is killed and brought back, he will retain his boosted stats but also regain '''Resurgence''', giving another opportunity to build up his stats. Copying '''Solgard''' through a card like [[Replicator Ray]] will also grant the copy '''Resurgence''', and the {{IconLink|Shard}} total will even carry over, letting you nearly double the copy's stats with no effort. '''Titanchannel''' can also be very effective in builds which rely mostly on spell damage to clear waves. If you can consistently put out enough spell damage to kill each wave of enemies, then '''Solgard''' can gain {{Attack}} and {{Health}} while you do so. The flaw of a deck which relies on magic damage is that bosses are almost impossible to kill with only spells, but '''Solgard''''s high stats allow him to easily defeat any boss in the game as long as you've built up lots of {{IconLink|Shard}}. By the later rings, he can easily rack up 500 or more {{Attack}} and {{Health}} with a strong spell deck. Keep in mind that this requires a very strong and consistent set of damage spells, or a set of other units which can take out waves before '''Solgard''' enters play. It may be worth dipping into '''Coldchannel''' if you are in need of backline clear. However, this generally runs counter to the way '''Titanchannel''' wants to be played, as it requires you to activate '''Solgard''' as soon as possible. {{CollapsibleSection|Quotes| '''Summoned''' * ''Aqath Be Praised!'' * ''My mind has not rotted!'' * ''The Sea has not forgotten me!'' * ''Your soul is mine!'' And even though it's not the most impressive spell, it still triggers {{IconLink|Incant}} and can even do so when no enemies are on the floor, unlike some other damage spells. With Tethys' '''Conduit''' upgrade tree, this spell costs {{Ember|0}}. Discard a card at random. |flavor= The Martyr speaks of the power a name has over the soul, that the Titan released its name for the good of Heaven, Hell, and Humans. Perhaps the same practice observed by the Stygian Guard is an evolution of this and grants them some minimal power as well. |artist = Andrew Vera }} '''Forgone Power''' is [[Solgard the Martyr]]'s starter card. It applies {{IconLink|Frostbite|8}} to the front enemy unit and discards a card at random. == Strategy == '''Forgone Power''' is not a particularly good card, and should usually be a high priority for removal. It can be decent at whittling down frontline enemies and bosses early in the game, and is a fairly easy way to trigger {{IconLink|Incant}}. It can also sometimes help you use powerful [[Offering]] cards if its discard effect hits them, which makes it easier to pick them from card rewards before you've seen other discard options like [[Offering Token]]. Later in the game, it loses potency, but it can still work with Offering and {{IconLink|Incant}} effects, especially with good card draw. You can usually avoid discarding important cards by simply playing them first, but spells like [[Frenzied Swarm]] or [[Deep Offering]], which must be played last, may require you to simply not play '''Forgone Power''' if you draw them together. Its random targeting means that drawing multiples of this card in the same hand isn't desirable (as it can discard the other copies instead of what you wanted it to discard), and so it isn't a reliable way to use [[Offering]]. As a result, you'll usually want to purge at least some of these. Ironically, it also has significant anti-synergy with card freeze effects most of the time, since it can discard [[Frozen]] cards. If you're making a lot of use of Frozen cards, unless they have Offering, you'll want these cards out of your deck as soon as possible. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! Its {{IconLink|Ability|png=AbilityActive}}, '''Freeze Ray''', applies [[Frozen]] to a card of your choice in your hand, similar to [[Preserve]]. == Strategy== '''Cuttlehex''' is a relatively harmless but not particularly impactful card. If you happen to start with it, it can provide a small but appreciable damage boost in the first ring if it can fit behind two other units (for example, [[Tethys Titansbane]] and a [[Shield Steward]]). However, its actual stats are almost irrelevant after the first battle; it will instantly die to [[Legion]] after attacking once, and in later battles its {{Attack|5}} rarely has much of an impact. Its main benefit is its ability to freeze a card every other turn, which can either hold an important card until you need it or "remove" a card by holding it in hand to keep it from being shuffled back into the deck. This is a helpful ability, but not an enormously strong one, and unless you have some specific reason - for example, a particular spell that you want to play against the boss, or expensive cards like [[Alchemy]] that you want to ensure you can play - '''Cuttlehex''' may not be worth taking. If allied with the [[Railforged]], the ability to freeze cards is much stronger, since you can keep a unit or equipment card in hand until you have enough [[Forge Points]]. '''Cuttlehex''' is much more effective with the [[Titan's Claws]], which allow it to reduce any card's cost to {{Ember|0}}. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! {{UnitCard |name = Molluscmage |image = PLR_Molluscmage.png |clan = Stygian Guard |rarity = Common |type = Mage |banner = No |cost = 1 |size = 1 |stats = 5/3 |ability = {{IconLink|Conduit|10}}. |flavor = These dark mages have made themselves known through their control of the power that radiates from the Titan. Though small in nature, these mages have a striking resemblance to the Titan itself, which has resulted in the spread of many unproven theories of their origin. |artist = Aaron Lovett }} '''Molluscmage''' is a common [[Stygian Guard]] unit. It has {{IconLink|Conduit|10}}, strengthening spells on its floor. == Strategy== '''Molluscmage''' is one of only two {{IconLink|Conduit}} sources available to the Stygian Guard, the other being [[Tethys Titansbane]]'s '''Conduit''' path. However, it is somewhat difficult to take advantage of. The only way to increase its {{IconLink|Conduit}} beyond its original 10 is by upgrading it with {{IconLink|Dualstone}}, but it competes with many other Stygian Guard units for this upgrade, like [[Nameless Siren]], [[Titan Sentry]], [[Guard of the Unnamed]], and [[Lodestone Totem]]. Additionally, since it is not a banner unit, you have no guarantee of drawing it early. Due to its {{Capacity|1}}, it isn't too difficult to fit many '''Molluscmages''' on a floor and increase the impact of {{IconLink|Conduit}} that way, but this runs into another issue. {{IconLink|Incant}} builds often want as many other {{IconLink|Incant}} units on the floor as possible, which means {{Capacity}} is at a premium, and you may not be able to justify '''Molluscmage''' occupying space on your floor. And since '''Molluscmage''' itself has very poor stats, it can be dangerous to put it on a higher floor, as it won't survive long against flying bosses. Compared to the similar [[Moon Pixie]], '''Molluscmage''' provides more {{IconLink|Conduit}} when the floor has three or less units, while Moon Pixie provides more {{IconLink|Conduit}} when the floor has four or more units. However, Moon Pixie has a lot more {{IconLink|Conduit}} support within its own clan, including {{IconLink|Mageblade}}, which provides a strong payoff for stacking {{IconLink|Conduit}} that the Stygian Guard generally cannot match. (Of course, if you are using both clans together, '''Molluscmage''' becomes very useful indeed.) Likely the best way to use '''Molluscmage''' is alongside powerful '''[[Attuned]]''' spells like [[Crypt Builder]] and [[Ice and Pyre]], as well as a source of {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}}, generally from [[Icy Cilophyte]] or Tethys's '''Handheld Totem''' path. These units can make even the strongest tanks highly vulnerable to spell damage, and '''Molluscmage''' can boost your spells enough to blow them away. If you can apply lots of {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}}, you may even be able to get an early kill on flying bosses this way. But this may not be enough against certain minibosses like [[Rax the Overblessed]] (who has {{IconLink|Spell Shield}}) or [[The Undying One]] (who has {{IconLink|Reanimate}}), so make sure you have a decent answer to {{IconLink|Relentless}} as well. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] !
