When the Sea froze, ice formed around each bolt, prying it loose to drift through the open water. |artist = Jordan Thomas }} '''Glacial Seal''' is an uncommon [[Stygian Guard]] unit. Whenever a spell is played on its floor, it applies {{IconLink|Frostbite|2}} to all enemies on the floor. == Strategy== '''Glacial Seal''' is a somewhat awkward unit, and may not be useful in many decks. As an {{IconLink|Incant}} unit, it is best used on the same floor as other units like [[Siren of the Sea]] or [[Nameless Siren]], and unlike those units, it is good at finishing off backliners. However, its damage is dealt only after enemies attack, and the same backliners it is meant to kill, especially [[Ragewing Assassin]], will finish it off easily. A [[Guardian Stone]] or [[Lodestone Totem]] can help with this. Like the Lodestone Totem, but unlike most other {{IconLink|Incant}} units in the Stygian Guard, the '''Glacial Seal''' only affects enemies, and does not scale in any way over the course of the battle. This means that it requires many {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers every turn in order to function. Unless you have [[Sigiled Seaweed]] or another way to {{IconLink|Mute}} enemies, a '''Glacial Seal'''-based strategy will struggle massively against enemies with their own {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers. You must choose between gaining no benefit from '''Glacial Seal''' or suffering the effects of enemy {{IconLink|Incant}}s. An [[Adamant Shieldbearer]] can shut down your other damage dealers (though it has no impact on '''Glacial Seal''' itself), and [[Enthralled Ardent]] will allow enemies to tear through your units before [[Glacial Seal]]'s {{IconLink|Frostbite}} has any effect. One last weakness of '''Glacial Seal''' is that it is not a banner unit, meaning that you will need to draw and play it before it has any effect. That is not to say that the '''Glacial Seal''' is never useful. If you have ways to get around its weaknesses, it can deal an impressive amount of damage to the entire floor. It works well with '''Coldchannel''' [[Solgard]], doubling down on the {{IconLink|Frostbite}} via {{IconLink|Incant}} strategy, and [[Cuttlebeard]], which affects every {{IconLink|Incant}} trigger. However, it requires a very specific deck to work effectively. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! They have been etched by its various members, marking the only true record of each Stygian who has been inducted. |artist = Daniel Sarmiento Chiquisengo }} '''Guardian Stone''' is a uncommon [[Stygian Guard]] unit. It has an {{IconLink|Incant}} ability that applies {{IconLink|Armor|1}} to all friendly units on the floor. == Strategy == '''Guardian Stone''' provides floor-wide protection in the form of {{IconLink|Armor}}, helping protect weak backliners like [[Nameless Siren]], [[Lodestone Totem]], and [[Offering Monument]] from some incidental damage. It also helps your frontliner take damage, but this is relatively minor, often providing a benefit similar to [[Fortified Pauldrons]]. It is a non-[[banner unit]], which is a problem because the main thing that it does - backline protection - is most required at the ''start'' of fights for the most part, as threats like [[Penitent Prayerstone]], [[Ragewing Assassin]], and [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]] will attack your backline immediately. Its protection also isn't usually adequate for frontline tanks, and so it should only be considered a supplement to an existing strategy to keep them alive. There are a few bosses that threaten backliners (and also happen to be problematic for decks that like {{IconLink|Incant}}ing) that show up later in fights, and '''Guardian Stone''' is fairly effective against them, such as [[Qel the Corruptor]] and [[Athane, Last to Fall]]. As such, using it to help frail backliners generally requires a deck you can cycle through quickly, or some way of getting it early like {{IconLink|Dominating Authority}}, [[Departure Manifest]], or a unit retrieval spell. If you do so, it can help you keep your floor alive against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]] and unboosted [[Ragewing Assassin]]s, but its {{IconLink|Armor}} application probably isn't enough against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]]-boosted [[Ragewing Assassin]]s or [[Chosen Assassin]]s. If allied with the [[Hellhorned]], '''Guardian Stone''' works exceptionally well with [[Railhammer]], as it will multiply the power of its {{IconLink|Incant}} ability by 5, making your floor exceptionally durable quite quickly. Its {{IconLink|Armor}} application has additional synergies when paired with them as well. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! {{UnitCard |name = Coldcaelia |image = PLR_Coldcaelia.png |clan = Stygian Guard |rarity = Uncommon |type = Siren |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 3/15 |ability = {{IconLink|Sweep}}.

They lack formal training in classical combat, but make up for it in their magical prowess. |artist = Jordan Thomas }} '''Coldcaelia''' is an uncommon [[Stygian Guard]] [[banner unit]]. She possesses {{IconLink|Sweep}} as well as a {{IconLink|Strike}} trigger that applies {{IconLink|Frostbite|6}} to enemies on hit. == Strategy == '''Coldcaelia''' returns to ''Monster Train 2'' with improved stats, more {{IconLink|Frostbite}} application on {{IconLink|Strike}} to increase the scope of enemies she can defeat, and most importantly, a Deployment phase where she can be placed down immediately before the start of combat. The ability to set up multiple units immediately allows '''Coldcaelia''' to act as support even if you have no source of damage scaling for her. Being able to place all units down before the combat starts allows you to use {{IconLink|Sweep}} units as low-investment, low-opportunity cost waveclear machines that can solve backlines for the run. Because you will no longer need to draw into units to set them up over several turns, there is little remaining opportunity cost in grabbing '''Coldcaelia''' to diversify your [[Merchant of Steel]] shops, opening {{IconLink|Speedstone}} and {{IconLink|Largestone}} as valuable major upgrades. You can then drop her on a lower floor to clear waves while fully assembling your main floor at the same time. Her ability to deal damage multiple times, with both her direct attack and the {{IconLink|Frostbite}} she applies, is useful for clearing out {{IconLink|Reanimate}} enemies like [[Undying Wretch]]es and [[Deformed Duo]]s. As a sweeper, '''Coldcaelia''' appreciates any source of {{IconLink|Quick}}, such as from the aforementioned {{IconLink|Speedstone}} or a [[Swiftsteel Dagger]] from a [[Merchant of Arms]] or Armory. {{IconLink|Multistrike}} is also uniquely strong with '''Coldcaelia''' due to her {{IconLink|Strike}} trigger, allowing her to apply {{IconLink|Frostbite}} to enemies multiple times, and can increase the scope of backline enemies she can kill. Any equipment with {{IconLink|Strike}} or {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers can also be strong, such as [[Everlasting Light]] or [[Organ Harvester]]. Rooms with these triggers are potent as well, depending on your secondary clan, like [[Bloodsoaked Arena]] and [[Rage Room]]. '''Coldcaelia''' can also slot into your main floor as your damage dealer, as her {{IconLink|Sweep}} makes her an excellent recipient of {{Attack}} buffs and {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. However, using her this way without the help of your other clan is generally not viable, as Stygian Guard has no such buffs in its card pool. [[Pyre of Savagery]] and [[Bloodthirsty Blade]] make this a much more appealing option, both allowing her to permanently scale her {{Attack}} whenever she gets a kill. However, be aware that enemies which die to her {{IconLink|Frostbite}} will not trigger these effects. Any source of {{Attack}}, {{IconLink|Rage}}, {{IconLink|Valor}}, or {{IconLink|Mageblade}} from the allied clan can turn her into your main damage dealer, but even if you have no access to any of these, she can still act as support to clear backliners. [[Cuttlebeard]] is a minor but worthwhile synergy, increasing the {{IconLink|Frostbite}} she applies and preventing it from decaying. This is mostly useful against high-{{Health}} enemies that would be out of her range otherwise, and during {{IconLink|Relentless}}. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! Guard of the Unnamed:
{{UnitCard |name = Guard of the Unnamed |image = PLR_GuardOfTheUnnamed.png |clan = Stygian Guard |rarity = Uncommon |type = Siren |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 5/25 |ability = {{IconLink|Incant}}: Gain {{IconLink|Armor|3}}. |flavor = Original captors and protectors of the titan, these Sirens have existed almost since the creation of the sea itself. They were the first to follow Tethys in recognizing the importance of the Titan's survival and that its imprisonment would be the only way to ensure it. |artist = Luke Banke }} '''Guard of the Unnamed''' is an uncommon [[Stygian Guard]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever a spell is played on his floor, he gains {{IconLink|Armor|3}}. == Strategy == '''Guard of the Unnamed''' is part of a set of three closely related units, along with [[Siren of the Sea]] and [[Nameless Siren]]. All three become stronger on {{IconLink|Incant}}: Nameless Siren deals more damage, '''Guard of the Unnamed''' gets more defense, and Siren of the Sea gets some of each. Unfortunately, '''Guard of the Unnamed''' tends to be the weakest of the three, and is generally one of the weakest Stygian Guard units overall. While he is a perfectly functional unit on his own merits and can serve his role as a frontlinke tank well into the lategame in a spell-based strategy, he suffers from heavy opportunity cost, as he is almost completely outclassed by Siren of the Sea. Siren of the Sea gains {{Health|3}} per {{IconLink|Incant}}, which is essentially equivalent to the defensive scaling of '''Guard of the Unnamed''', but also gains {{Attack|+3}} as well, meaning that you are often giving up {{Attack}} per {{IconLink|Incant}} for no direct benefit. Each, of course, still has their own advantages as a tank. '''Guard of the Unnamed''' has slightly more initial survivability than Siren of the Sea, making a {{IconLink|Heartstone}} or {{IconLink|Largestone}} upgrade less likely to be necessary. [[Guard of the Unnamed]]'s {{IconLink|Armor}} can be doubled by a {{IconLink|Dualism}} upgrade, while {{Health}} cannot. {{IconLink|Armor}} also has synergies with the [[Hellhorned]] clan that simple {{Health}} gain doesn't - it works with [[Reinforce]], [[Railhammer]], and [[Battering Ram]]. Losing {{IconLink|Armor}} will not kill a {{IconLink|Fragile}} unit, allowing '''Guard of the Unnamed''' to theoretically use [[Glass Cannon]], [[Onehorn's Tome]] and [[Faulty Body]] with little downside. However, the only one of these that it can actually use effectively is [[Faulty Body]], and if you are allied with the [[Lazarus League]], that spell is better used on Lazarus tanks such as [[Hulking Mass]], which have {{IconLink|Reanimate}} synergies to keep them alive in case an enemy can break through their {{IconLink|Armor}}. On the other hand, '''Guard of the Unnamed''' actually has ''worse'' defensive scaling than Siren of the Sea if allied with the [[Awoken]] or [[Banished]] clans. Healing spells (with the exception of those used by the [[Luna Coven]]) cannot restore {{IconLink|Armor}}, and {{IconLink|Valor}} will not grant {{IconLink|Armor}} if the unit already has it. Additionally, Siren of the Sea's increased {{Health}} will be maintained if the unit is killed and brought back through {{IconLink|Endless}} or '''[[Reform]]''', while [[Guard of the Unnamed]]'s {{IconLink|Armor}} will not. This leads me to believe that the Stygian may be the only clan that has benefited from the Freeze. |artist = Jordan Thomas }} '''Icy Cilophyte''' is an uncommon [[Stygian Guard]] [[banner unit]]. She possesses {{IconLink|Sweep}} as well as a {{IconLink|Strike}} trigger that applies {{IconLink|Spell Weakness|1}} to enemies on hit. == Strategy == '''Icy Cilophyte''' was previously regarded by many to be the worst {{IconLink|Sweep}} unit in the game in the original ''Monster Train''. However, in ''Monster Train 2'', she has received significant buffs, both direct and indirect, to keep up. With improved stats (including significantly increased {{Health}}) and a Deployment phase where she can be placed down immediately before the start of combat, '''Icy Cilophyte''' becomes significantly stronger than her original incarnation. The addition of the Deployment Phase and the increased effectiveness of building on lower floors have turned '''Icy Cilophyte''' from perhaps the single least desirable banner unit in the clan to a strong pick that can fit into a variety of strategies. Being able to place all units down before the combat starts allows you to use {{IconLink|Sweep}} units as low-investment, low-opportunity cost waveclear machines that can solve backlines for the run. Because you will no longer need to draw into units to set them up over several turns, there is little remaining opportunity cost in grabbing '''Icy Cilophyte''' to diversify your [[Merchant of Steel]] shops, opening {{IconLink|Speedstone}} and {{IconLink|Largestone}} as valuable major upgrades. You can then drop her on a lower floor to clear waves while fully assembling your main floor at the same time. She fits in wonderfully behind a [[Titan Sentry]] to absorb hits for her while also dealing a little more damage to backliners, especially ones that would otherwise escape being killed like [[Deformed Duo]]s. Her {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} is very useful as long as she is not on the top floor, doubling the damage of the next spell played against the target. Combined with her ability to wipe out backliners on her own, this can set up tanky units to be killed by a spell on the floor above, allowing her to deal massive damage against all enemies. As a sweeper, '''Icy Cilophyte''' appreciates any source of {{IconLink|Quick}}, such as from the aforementioned {{IconLink|Speedstone}} or a [[Swiftsteel Dagger]] from a [[Merchant of Arms]] or Armory. {{IconLink|Multistrike}} is also strong, not only for damage but also to allow '''Icy Cilophyte''' to apply {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} to enemies multiple times. Any equipment with {{IconLink|Strike}} or {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers can also be strong, such as [[Everlasting Light]] or [[Organ Harvester]]. Rooms with these triggers are potent as well, depending on your secondary clan, like [[Bloodsoaked Arena]] and [[Rage Room]]. '''Icy Cilophyte''' can also slot into your main floor as your damage dealer, as her {{IconLink|Sweep}} makes her an excellent recipient of {{Attack}} buffs and {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. However, using her this way without the help of your other clan is generally not viable, as Stygian Guard has no such buffs in its card pool. [[Pyre of Savagery]] and [[Bloodthirsty Blade]] make this a much more appealing option, both allowing her to permanently scale her {{Attack}} whenever she gets a kill. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! She gains {{IconLink|Rage|3}} whenever a spell is played on her floor. == Strategy == '''Nameless Siren''' is the cornerstone offensive {{IconLink|Incant}} unit for the Stygian Guard. With a strong spell-based build, she can quickly accumulate great amounts of {{IconLink|Rage}} and tear through enemy tanks. Compared to her sister, the [[Siren of the Sea]], she is less well-rounded, and far more fragile. '''Nameless Siren''' makes up for this by having significantly greater damage output. Not only does she gain the equivalent of {{Attack|6}} per {{IconLink|Incant}}, compared to Siren of the Sea's {{Attack|3}}, but unlike Siren of the Sea she can also be upgraded with {{IconLink|Dualstone}}, essentially giving her {{Attack|12}} for every spell played. This gives '''Nameless Siren''' a far better shot at taking out high-{{Health}} enemies quickly during the late game. The two units work quite well in concert, with Siren of the Sea protecting the '''Nameless Siren''' behind her. This role can also be served by [[Guard of the Unnamed]], who is the other side of the coin, gaining {{IconLink|Armor|3}} on {{IconLink|Incant}} and being tankier to start; however, Guard of the Unnamed will not scale its damage, and is generally less preferred for this reason. [[Guardian Stone]] and [[Lodestone Totem]] can help protect '''Nameless Siren''', the former by granting a tiny amount of {{IconLink|Armor}}, the latter by applying {{IconLink|Sap}} to enemies. Cards like [[Frenzied Swarm]] can also stop enemies from acting by applying {{IconLink|Dazed}}, giving '''Nameless Siren''' the chance to kill them. [[Drain]] and [[Guardian's Amulet]] can do the same, albeit somewhat less effectively. '''Nameless Siren''' fits well into virtually any {{IconLink|Incant}}-based strategy, providing a huge boost to damage. This includes Champions with {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers, like [[Arduhn]], [[Madame Lionsmane]], and [[Wyldenten]]. Arduhn's '''Hierophant''' path grants {{IconLink|Armor}} to make '''Nameless Siren''' less fragile, while Wyldenten's '''Thornlord''' path gives him enough {{Health}} to tank while adding free triggers, and Madame Lionsmane's '''Everbloom''' path generates [[Funguy]] to block hits. [[Solgard the Martyr]]'s '''Titanchannel''' path can make him an extremely effective tank; however, he enters battle in {{IconLink|Stasis}}, which means enemies will ignore him and directly attack '''Nameless Siren'''. '''Titanchannel''' is generally at its strongest when it can spend several turns in {{IconLink|Stasis}} and building up {{IconLink|Shard}}, but if he is your only means of defending '''Nameless Siren''' you may be forced to activate his '''Resurgence''' sooner than you would prefer. That said, even if you can only get him to, say, {{IconLink|Shard|8}} before bringing him online, that still gives him {{AttackHealth|120|125}} at max level; a Siren of the Sea would require 36 {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers to match those stats. Because {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers affect the whole floor, it is advantageous to fit as many units as possible together. While the Stygian Guard lacks natural access to '''[[Ascend]]''' or '''[[Descend]]''' cards, or means of expanding {{Capacity}} outside of [[Heaven's Light]], the [[Hall of Mirrors]] room will allow you to put down multiple copies of '''Nameless Siren''' without having to duplicate her, so long as you can deal with the reduced {{Capacity}} or replace the room after playing her. When used alongside the [[Hellhorned]], their {{IconLink|Rage}} synergies, such as [[Deranged Brute]], [[Resonant Shard]], and [[Collection of Tails]], can make her even more powerful. Their role was entirely ceremonial until now. |artist = Luke Banke }} '''Titan Sentry''' is an uncommon [[Stygian Guard]] [[banner unit]]. He applies {{IconLink|Frostbite|3}} to ''all'' enemies on the floor each time he takes damage. == Strategy == The main purpose of '''Titan Sentry''' is to wipe out waves of enemies, applying {{IconLink|Frostbite}} to the entire wave each time he takes damage. He can be compared to the [[Prickly Puffball]] from the [[Underlegion]] clan, but their uses are somewhat different. In contrast to Prickly Puffball or units with {{IconLink|Spikes}}, '''Titan Sentry''' kills even backline enemies that don't attack, such as [[Ominous Acolyte]]s and [[Enthralled Ardent]]s. He also applies {{IconLink|Frostbite}} each time he takes damage, regardless of the source, meaning that you can hit him with spells like [[Torch]] to apply {{IconLink|Frostbite}} to all enemies on the floor. Compared to the Puffball, however, his damage against a single target is not very impressive, making him less useful against bosses. He should also not be counted on to take out tankier enemies like [[Avowed Gladiator]], who should instead be dealt with by units like [[Siren of the Sea]]. '''Titan Sentry''' should usually be placed on a floor of his own with your other units higher up, allowing him to wipe out dangerous backliners and soften up tanks before they enter battle with your main floor. With no {{IconLink|Incant}} trigger, there is no real reason why he would have to stay on the same floor as Sirens or other units. If any units are to be placed alongside him, [[Coldcaelia]] and [[Icy Cilophyte]] are the best options, as both are also specialized to take out backline enemies, and can help take out more durable backline enemies that may be out of [[Titan Sentry]]'s reach alone, such as [[Vampiric Cherub]]s and [[Chosen Supplicant]]s. Due to [[Titan Sentry]]'s {{IconLink|Revenge}} trigger, it can actually be preferable for these units not to be upgraded with {{IconLink|Quick}} in order to apply more {{IconLink|Frostbite}} to enemies, although being {{IconLink|Quick}} can help save {{Health}} on '''Titan Sentry'''. It is inadvisable to take this unit when using [[Solgard the Martyr]]'s '''Coldchannel''' path or vice versa, for the simple reason that both units perform effectively the same role. Solgard is much less durable at his baseline, having only {{Health|25}}, and requires more attention due to his {{IconLink|Incant}} trigger, but in exchange can apply far more {{IconLink|Frostbite}}. Equipment with other {{IconLink|Revenge}} triggers, such as [[Shield of Wyngh]], [[Lava Armor]], and [[Spiky Skin]], all work well in conjunction with '''Titan Sentry''', boosting his {{Health}} and making him more efficient at removing backline threats. When used with the Underlegion, [[Loamcoat]] can allow '''Titan Sentry''' to perform effectively the same job as Prickly Puffball, accumulating lots of {{IconLink|Regen}} to keep himself alive. Although he has some flaws, when used well, '''Titan Sentry''' can be a powerful source of both extra damage and indirect defense which requires little investment to be effective. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! {{UnitCard |name = Eel Gorgon |image = PLR_EelGorgon.png |clan = Stygian Guard |rarity = Rare |type = Mage |banner = Yes |cost = 2 |size = 2 |stats = 10/5 |ability = {{IconLink|Incant}}: Gain {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}}.

It is a cycle unlike I've seen elsewhere. |artist = Taylor Bray }} '''Eel Gorgon''' is a rare [[Stygian Guard]] [[banner unit]]. It gains {{IconLink|Multistrike}} after each {{IconLink|Incant}}, but loses all [[Buffs]], [[Debuffs]], and yellow [[Effects]] - including {{IconLink|Multistrike}} - at the end of the turn. == Notes == The game prevents you from applying upgrades to '''Eel Gorgon''' that its {{IconLink|Resolve}} trigger would make obsolete. This includes (but is not limited to) {{IconLink|Speedstone}}, {{IconLink|Frenzystone}}, {{IconLink|Immortalstone}}, {{IconLink|Titanstone}}, {{IconLink|Dualstone}}, and {{IconLink|Runestone}}. == Strategy == If you can support it, the '''Eel Gorgon''' has a very high ceiling and can easily wipe out entire waves on its own due to its numerous strikes. But not every run will be able to take advantage of this potential. '''Eel Gorgon''' can't scale via buffs, so any strategies related to {{IconLink|Rage}} or {{IconLink|Valor}} are out. But it ''can'' scale with {{Attack}} upgrades, [[Equipment]], [[Artifacts]], [[Triggers]], and effects like '''[[Reform]]''' that increase {{Attack}} directly. For '''Eel Gorgon''' to be effective, you will generally want a source of attack scaling that falls into one of these categories. The [[Lazarus League]] has a bevy of options here; [[It's Alive!]], [[Risky Operation]], [[Weaponized Prosthetic]], and [[Scrap for Parts]] can all help scale [[Eel Gorgon]]'s {{Attack}}. [[Brain Transfer]] can also transfer the {{Attack}} of a stronger unit to it. When paired with the [[Banished]], [[Death's Dancer]] is a powerful scaler, but both units are rare and thus are unlikely to be obtained together. With the [[Umbra]], [[Magma Morsel]]s, [[Antumbra Morsel]]s, and [[Morsel Miner]]s are surprisingly strong, particularly with [[Shroud Spike]], and [[Perils of Production]] can be played risk-free on '''Eel Gorgon''' as it will clear {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} (but also the {{IconLink|Rage}}) each turn. With the [[Pyreborne]], [[Soldier of Fortune]] provides a solid {{Attack|+30}}, and while the {{IconLink|Armor|15}} and {{IconLink|Avarice|15}} are largely wasted, '''Eel Gorgon''' can hit so many times per round that you will likely make more {{Gold}} from just a single round of combat than what you spent on the card. [[Primordium]]'s '''Aggressive Edible''' path gives '''Eel Gorgon''' {{Attack|+180}} over three turns, and more if you can replay the unit with [[Retch]]. [[Baron Grael]]'s '''Living Armory''' path grants it and all other units on the floor {{Attack|+24}} whenever he is equipped, scaling '''Eel Gorgon''' rapidly. [[Ekka]]'s '''Lunar Steward''' path gives repeated stat boosts on {{IconLink|Mooncycle}}, shoring up its poor initial statline, and also puts it in prime position to exploit the [[Luna Cyclestaff]]. [[Talos]]'s '''Enchantress''' path will permanently scale [[Eel Gorgon]]'s stats after each battle as long as it survives. {{IconLink|Pyregel}} should also not be underestimated. '''Eel Gorgon''' will frequently output a high number of low-damage hits, and even a little bit of {{IconLink|Pyregel}} can rapidly scale its damage output. The [[Magma Cultist]] and [[Magma Mauler]] units are excellent synergies for this reason; Magma Cultist is even another {{IconLink|Incant}} unit. You will also need a deck capable of consistently triggering {{IconLink|Incant}} many times on ''every'' turn. Be mindful of enemies that punish {{IconLink|Incant}} such as [[Qel the Corruptor]] and [[Enthralled Ardent]], as you'll likely need to {{IconLink|Incant}} several times to get your damage up. Thankfully, the Stygian Guard has the best access to {{IconLink|Mute}} in the game, so the [[Sigiled Seaweed]] artifact or a well-timed [[Unnamed Tome]] can neuter these threats. On the flip side, '''Eel Gorgon''' automatically cleanses debilitating effects, which is a major boon. For example, {{IconLink|Fragile}} from [[Glass Cannon]] will be removed promptly, as will {{IconLink|Burnout}} from [[Wicklash]]. And while [[Adamant Shieldbearer]] does hurt [[Eel Gorgon]]'s damage, the {{IconLink|Sap}} is fortunately removed at the end of the turn along with other debuffs. Equipment is extremely important for '''Eel Gorgon''' as the easiest way to raise its stats. High {{Attack}} equipment like the aforementioned Glass Cannon as well as [[Heph's Hammer]] and [[Bloodthirsty Blade]] are fantastic choices for '''Eel Gorgon''' to hold. [[Overgrowth Carapace]] is perhaps the best, quickly granting '''Eel Gorgon''' massive stats, and if upgraded with {{IconLink|Smidgestone}} only a single {{Capacity}} must be empty on the floor. The [[Combustion Suit]] grants '''Eel Gorgon''' a {{IconLink|Strike}} trigger, which means it can easily apply {{IconLink|Unstable|25}} or more to the whole floor, giving it backline access. The aforementioned Luna Cyclestaff is another piece of equipment that can eventually hit sky-high {{Attack}} levels with enough {{IconLink|Mooncycle}} triggers. One unique strategy involves [[Stoic Platemail]]. {{IconLink|Incant}} as many times as you can, then apply the Platemail to prevent the {{IconLink|Resolve}} trigger from activating. This grants '''Eel Gorgon''' its {{IconLink|Multistrike}} permanently for the rest of combat, though you are prevented from adding any more. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! Lodestone Totem:
{{UnitCard |name = Lodestone Totem |image = PLR_LodestoneTotem.png |clan = Stygian Guard |rarity = Rare |type = Totem |banner = Yes |cost = 3 |size = 1 |stats = 0/1 |ability = {{IconLink|Incant}}: Apply {{IconLink|Sap|1}} to enemy units. |flavor = Of the totems that the founding Guardian built, the Lodestones are possibly the most important. They provide energy for the Stygian Guard by siphoning power from those around them using some ancient technology that's eluded my understanding. |artist = Zihao Luo }} '''Lodestone Totem''' is a rare [[Stygian Guard]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever a spell is played on its floor, it will apply {{IconLink|Sap|1}} to all enemies on the same floor. == Strategy == '''Lodestone Totem''' is arguably more powerful in Monster Train 2 compared to 1, as card upgrades are overall more powerful, allowing for an easier time constructing a deck that can cast many spells in a single turn. For example, {{IconLink|Twinstone}} does not cause the second copy to cost {{Ember|+1}}, so you can cast more copies of the same cheap spell to repeatedly trigger {{IconLink|Incant}}. {{IconLink|Eternalstone}} also does not increase card cost, so powerful spells like [[Deep Offering]] and [[Gifts for a Guard]] are easier to play repeatedly. The introduction of the [[Deployment Phase]] also greatly improves its consistency, as one can place it down before combat begins, allowing for more {{IconLink|Ember}} to be spent on casting spells. If enough spells can be cast in a single turn, you can leave the enemy with so much {{IconLink|Sap}} that they won't be able to attack at all, and you can simply let them stroll up to the Pyre and die. Giving '''Lodestone Totem''' {{IconLink|Dualism}} or finding ways of setting up multiples of it on the floor makes this strategy much easier to pull off. The [[Stygian Guard]] naturally have many {{IconLink|Incant}} synergies that go well with '''Lodestone Totem''', and many appreciate its defensive benefits. [[Siren of the Sea]], [[Nameless Siren]], [[Eel Gorgon]], and [[Solgard the Martyr]] (if he is your champion) are a few to mention. Defensively scaling {{IconLink|Incant}} units should be avoided since defense is not a concern with '''Lodestone Totem'''. Units depending on {{IconLink|Revenge}} should most likely be avoided as well, unless your strategy is to apply enough {{IconLink|Sap}} to lower the enemies' {{Attack}} to just above 0 in order to help the {{IconLink|Revenge}} unit take more hits. While undeniably a powerful unit, it is not an automatic addition to every deck. Much of the strength of '''Lodestone Totem''' depends on your deck's ability to cast many spells in a single turn, potentially making it a liability in the early rings, as its high {{IconLink|Ember}} cost makes it hard to deploy other units during Deployment, and the lack of spell density and spell upgrades makes it potentially difficult to take advantage of its {{IconLink|Sap}}. One should be wary of {{IconLink|Corruption}}, as {{IconLink|Sap}} does not help you against passive damage. [[Qel the Corruptor]] is potentially an early loss if you are unprepared for his floorwide {{IconLink|Corruption}}. Similarly, [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]] can be game-ending if you cannot prevent his {{IconLink|Corruption}} application, although once reduced to {{Attack|0}}, his {{IconLink|Strike}} trigger is at least no longer a concern. [[Seraph Aeternus-The Entropic]] has many anti-spell tactics in his combat waves. The [[Enthralled Ardent]]s are problematic, as they grant {{Attack|5}} on {{IconLink|Incant}}, which is more than a singular '''Lodestone Totem''' can negate, even with {{IconLink|Dualism}}. [[Deafening Herald]]s also appear, and they apply {{IconLink|Silence}} to your units, making '''Lodestone Totem''' unable to apply any {{IconLink|Sap}}. Strong targeting spells are recommended to deal with these threats. Alternatively, and conveniently, both of the above issues can be completely solved with {{IconLink|Mute}}, making [[Sigiled Seaweed]] and [[Unnamed Tome]] extremely important pickups. [[Zone of Silence]] is also a viable option, but since it and '''Lodestone Totem''' both cost {{Ember|3}}, it is difficult to set them both up with your limited {{DeploymentEmber}}. [[Dante's Footstool]], [[Artificial Pyrestone]], [[Ancient Pyretap]], and [[Herzal's Horde]] can all help with this. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! {{UnitCard |name = Offering Monument |image = PLR_OfferingMonument.png |clan = Stygian Guard |rarity = Rare |type = Totem |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 1 |stats = 0/1 |ability = {{IconLink|Incant}}: Draw '''+1''' next turn. |flavor = I created monuments as signposts for the offering sites across the seafloor. But my shoddy work has made them vulnerable to the energy from the Unnamed below, destabilizing them entirely. |artist = Zihao Luo }} '''Offering Monument''' is a rare [[Stygian Guard]] [[banner unit]]. It causes you to draw an additional card next turn on {{IconLink|Incant}}. == Strategy== For almost all {{IconLink|Incant}} decks, the '''Offering Monument''' is incredibly desirable. The importance of the [[Deployment Phase]] and {{DeploymentEmber}} specifically means that [[Hell's Flame]] can be practically mandatory, while the additional {{Capacity}} provided by [[Heaven's Light]] helps fit more {{IconLink|Incant}} units onto a single floor. Unfortunately, this means there is often not much room left to take [[Limbo's Solace]]. But if you are drawing only 5 cards per turn, there's a limit to how much you can {{IconLink|Incant}} per turn, you may not see critical cards by the time you need them, and you can easily be ruined by enemies that shuffle [[Scourge]]s into your deck. For a modest {{Capacity|1}} and {{Ember|1}}, '''Offering Monument''' can allow you to draw 10 cards per turn every turn after the first, an incredible boon for the Stygian Guard. Your scaling {{IconLink|Incant}} units like [[Nameless Siren]] and [[Siren of the Sea]] will build strength much faster, and you will see strong cards like [[Guardian's Amulet]] and [[Crypt Builder]] far more often. It also frees you up to take the other two boss artifacts instead of Limbo's Solace. Having two Hell's Flames and drawing 10 cards per turn can practically assure your victory on its own. Most {{IconLink|Incant}} units are {{Capacity|2}} by default. Even without any {{Capacity}} upgrades, this means '''Offering Monument''' can fit behind two other {{IconLink|Incant}} units, letting you make the most of your {{Capacity}}. This also makes it very easy to squeeze into almost any strategy. Even if you are not leaning into {{IconLink|Incant}} strategies, it can be worth taking, as you will usually play at least a few spells on its floor each turn, netting you additional draw and accelerating your deck. Practically the only time you might not want to take '''Offering Monument''' is if you are already drawing plenty of cards per turn, such as with [[Volatile Gauge]], [[Leaky Pen]], or [[Pyre of Entropy]]. However, even in the former two cases, it can be worth considering. (It is usually not worth it with Pyre of Entropy as you'll eventually draw 10 cards per turn anyway.) Alternatively, in the early game, if you have a weak start, it may be necessary to skip '''Offering Monument''' for a unit more capable of solving immediate problems. Extra draw is only as good as the cards in your deck, and '''Offering Monument''' does not do much in combat, so if your deck is weak, picking this unit over one with better stats or scaling can result in an early loss. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | [[Upgrade]] ! It applies {{IconLink|Spell Weakness|1}} to a single unit. ==Strategy== '''Energy Siphon''' is generally a weak card, and rarely worth taking. By doubling the damage of the next spell used against the target, it can essentially be thought of as a 0-cost copy of that spell. However, it requires that you play a powerful spell next to gain any real benefit, as wasting the {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} on something like [[Frozen Lance]] or [[Icestorm]] will remove the debuff while giving little benefit. It is best used in a very consistent deck which can play powerful damage spells on a regular basis. As a 0-cost spell, it can be moderately useful for {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers. Even if there are no enemies, it can be used to {{IconLink|Incant}} by playing on a friendly unit, as {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} generally isn't a problem on friendly units. It also has no impact at all on spells which deal indirect damage, like [[Forgone Power]]. This can make it completely useless in certain decks. Compared to the similar [[Urchin Spines]], '''Energy Siphon''' comes up far short. Urchin Spines targets the entire floor and applies twice as much {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}}. The only debatable advantage of '''Energy Siphon''' is that it does not have Consume, though this can be fixed with an {{IconLink|Eternalstone}} on Urchin Spines if needed. This card is most useful when going for high [[Score]], such as during Daily Challenges. {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} is useful to stack on flying bosses in order to kill them before they enter {{IconLink|Relentless}}, especially when combined with powerful [[Attuned]] spells like [[Crypt Builder]] or [[Ice and Pyre]]. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! {{SpellCard |name = Offering Token |image = CRD_OfferingToken.png |clan = [[Stygian Guard]] |rarity = Common |cost = 0 |effect = Draw '''1'''. Discard '''1'''. |flavor = Making offerings to the Unnamed Titan has become a religious experience among the Stygian Guard. These offerings are made with such frequency that I helped to create tokens to represent a Guard's offering to the Titan and simplify the process. |artist = Daniel Sarmiento Chuquisengo }} '''Offering Token''' is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It allows the player to draw a card, then discard a card. == Strategy == '''Offering Token''' is one of the strongest cards available to the Stygian Guard, and should almost always be taken if offered. Keep in mind that it does not actually provide any draw: the card you draw by playing it is the same card you would have drawn if you didn't have '''Offering Token''' in your deck, meaning that it essentially makes you discard a card for no immediate benefit. However, it has many indirect benefits. It is one of the best spells for {{IconLink|Incant}} units due to its low cost and ability to draw another card, and it allows expensive [[Offering]] spells to consistently be played for free. At Covenant 5 and above, it can also discard [[Vengeful Shard]] without needing to pay its cost; these [[Blights]] provide an easy discard target, making '''Offering Token''' a better card at high covenants, and even better if using the [[Pyre of Entropy]]. It can also immediately discard the dangerous [[Entropic Crystals]] and [[Savage Shackles]] if drawn, removing them from your current deck cycle without losing any {{Ember}}. [[Dominion's Eye]] can also be discarded this way, but as it increases the cost of Offering Token this will cost the same as playing it normally. It will also destroy [[Ephemeral]] cards such as [[Curse of Entropy]], bypassing the downside of either playing or retaining them. Even if you happen to draw it with no Blights, Scourges, or Offering cards, you can simply discard an unimportant card like [[Forgone Power]], making the downside of drawing it when you don't need it much lower than almost any other card in the game. Given the enormous number of ways to benefit from Offering Token, along with the very minor downside of having it in your deck, it should be taken in almost any situation. The only exception is if you already have [[Volatile Gauge]], as it is not worth using with a randomized cost. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! Instant freezes are now frequent occurrences, much to the dismay of anyone unlucky enough to be caught in their icy grasp. |artist = Luke Banke }} '''Flash Freeze''' is a common [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It deals 3 damage and applies {{IconLink|Frostbite|8}}. ==Strategy== '''Flash Freeze''' is best as an early-game pickup, capable of dealing with low-{{Health}} backliners like the [[Lurking Miscreant]] and [[Savage Spearman]], and also putting a good dent in frontliners like [[Fallen Champion]] and [[Flagellant]] if applied on the bottom floor. It does respectable damage against bosses early as well. It falls off later, however, meaning it isn't worth taking if you're already confident in your ability to handle the first few Rings, and it can be redundant if you already have spells like [[Torch]] or [[Sporetouch]]. It can also be used to instantly kill friendly units like [[Imps]] if you need to remove them to make space. In the late game, '''Flash Freeze''' is usually just strong enough to not be worth removing unless you have already removed your starter cards. However, given the opportunity, it may be worth a removal if you already have a very slim deck. It is one of two [[Stygian Guard]] spells offered by the [[Gremlin Looter]] event. == Strategy == '''Urchin Spines''' applies {{IconLink|Spell Weakness|2}} to an entire floor - with no other sources of {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}}, this will triple the damage that each enemy unit takes to the next spell, allowing spells like [[Crypt Builder]], [[Ice and Pyre]], and others to deal serious damage to each of them. It roughly does double the amount of damage your spells will deal to this floor of enemies, and for {{Ember|0}}. On top of this, it's an easy {{IconLink|Incant}} trigger. It does struggle to realize its full potential in the context of just the [[Stygian Guard]], however, as they don't have any spells that deal heavy damage to an entire floor. In addition, random multi-hit spells like [[Icestorm]] and [[Ice Tornado]] don't work well with {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} unless there's just a single target or you have a lot of [[Magic Power]], as each unit that takes even one hit will have {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} removed from it, often resulting in it being spent rather inefficiently. Even so, it would be a solid spell if it applied its {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} to just a single target; it just can be not too much better than this in practice. At its best, it applies {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} to multiple tanks, and you use powerful spells on each to capitialize. It can be used to build up {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} on a boss in preparation for a deadly strike, though [[Icestorm]], [[Ice Tornado]], and [[Titanstooth]] can ruin this. It can realize its full potential if allied with a clan that has a powerful floorwide damage spell: * The [[Hellhorned]] have [[Inferno]]. * The [[Banished]] have [[Cleave]]. * The [[Pyreborne]] have [[Pyreclasm]] and other [[Explosive]] spells, and {{IconLink|Pyregel}} generally synergizes well with {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} as their effects multiply with each other. This is something the [[Stygian Guard]]'s generally frail units appreciate greatly, especially in the endgame, as all three Seraph forms can otherwise be quite scary to them. It also doesn't work well with anything with the [[Frozen]] keyword, as it will discard any such cards, whether that be cards upgraded with {{IconLink|Freezestone}}, [[Cuttlehex]], or [[Preserve]]. What it certainly '''does''' work well with are cards with the [[Offering]] keyword - any such cards are played right after this card is played. {{SpellCard |name = Harness the Titan |image = CRD_HarnessTheTitan.png |clan = [[Stygian Guard]] |rarity = Rare |cost = 1 |effect = Apply '''+10 [[Magic Power]]''' to spells in hand. |flavor = “When the Titan whose name has been sealed is released again, the Sea shall be illuminated with its awesome power.” - Tethys Titansbane's account of the Titan's return to our defense. |artist = Jordan Thomas }} '''Harness the Titan''' is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It adds 10 [[Magic Power]] to all spells in hand, increasing direct damage or healing by 10. == Strategy == '''Harness the Titan''' is often an awkward spell, as it has no effect on the majority of cards, and is usually not worth it unless it is drawn along with multiple damage spells. Many Stygian Guard spells, such as [[Forgone Power]], only do indirect damage and are unaffected by Magic Power. Drawing '''Harness the Titan''' means you will draw one less other card, making it relatively unlikely that you will draw your important spells alongside it. In a deck not specifically built around spell damage, you will often draw it without any damage spells at all, making it little better than a [[Deadweight]]. However, it can be very useful in a deck which consists mostly of damage spells, especially those with multiple hits, such as [[Icestorm]], or those with '''[[Attuned]]''', such as [[Crypt Builder]]. If you happen to be allied with the [[Luna Coven]] or get either the [[Wreckage Remains]] or [[Gremlin Looter]] event, [[Silver Ink]] can apply Attuned to any spell, increasing the effect of Magic Power by a factor of 5. By playing '''Harness the Titan''' consistently, you can massively increase the damage dealt by these spells and potentially use them to wipe out enemy waves even in the late game. This spell is best used with [[Tethys Titansbane]], mostly because her starter card, [[Frozen Lance]], is affected by Magic Power. Her '''Conduit''' path also decreases the cost of damage spells, making it effective to take more of them and allowing the player to take [[Limbo's Solace]] and other card draw artifacts without worrying about running short on {{Ember}}. Drawing more cards each turn means that '''Harness the Titan''' will affect more spells each time it is played. == Recommended Upgrades== {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! Ice and Pyre:
{{SpellCard |name = Ice and Pyre |image = CRD_IceAndPyre.png |clan = Stygian Guard |rarity = Rare |cost = 1 |effect = '''[[Pyrebound]]'''. '''[[Attuned]]'''.
Deal '''90''' damage to the front enemy unit. |flavor = Having only limited control over the elements, the Stygian have learned to harness the energy of the Pyre and freeze it for even greater impact. Unfortunately, we've only been able to perfect this defense within a limited range. |artist = Daniel Sarmiento Chuquisengo }} '''Ice and Pyre''' is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It deals 90 damage and has [[Attuned]], multiplying any [[Magic Power]] it has by 5, but can only be played on the third floor or in the Pyre Room due to its [[Pyrebound]] keyword. ==Strategy== '''Ice and Pyre''' aims to provide value to an {{IconLink|Incant}} strategy that wants to place units on the top floor, softening up frontline tanks for a unit with high {{Attack}} such as a [[Nameless Siren]] to more easily push through. However, its utility has become much more limited in ''Monster Train 2''. In the original ''Monster Train'', most strategies gravitated towards setting up on the top floor due to the lack of a Deployment Phase, making the first few turns of each combat less consistent. This meant that '''Ice and Pyre''' would usually be live when you needed it, and would at the very least always be playable to power up your floor. With multi-floor setups being more encouraged in ''Monster Train 2'' and several combats punishing the exclusive use of the top floor (such as against [[Cael, Lord of the Cherubs]] or [[Savagery's Final Assault]]), the '''Pyrebound''' downside becomes much more relevant. If you find the need to set up your {{IconLink|Incant}} units away from top floor, '''Ice and Pyre''' becomes significantly worse. If you draw it when no enemies are present on the top floor, it is essentially a [[Deadweight]]. Another factor that makes '''Ice and Pyre''' less of a common choice is that its damage has not been adjusted at all from the original game. 90 damage at baseline was enough to put a sizable dent in any enemy in ''Monster Train 1'', but against new enemies such as the [[Avowed Gladiator]] with {{Health|500}}, it barely leaves a scratch, even with upgrades. This is barely more than [[Crypt Builder]], a Common card that is also Attuned (that has incidentally had its base damage buffed to 80). It requires synergies to muscle through these enemies, though it does become very powerful with them - any source of {{IconLink|Conduit}} on the top floor, or cards like [[Enchanted Chamber]] and [[Harness the Titan]], can very quickly put this card at the high numbers it needs to be at. '''Ice and Pyre''' is overall extremely comparable to Crypt Builder, with a few differences: it deals 10 extra damage, it does not push the target back, it costs {{Ember|1}} rather than {{Ember|3}}, it is not played if discarded, and it is '''Pyrebound'''. Compared to Crypt Builder, it is often a weaker choice, and as a rare card, it has a much higher opportunity cost. Crypt Builder may have a higher upfront cost, but if you have consistent access to discard spells like [[Offering Token]], it is essentially free. In the presence of these synergies, Crypt Builder can weaponize its high cost with {{IconLink|Holystone}}, giving it another niche that '''Ice and Pyre''' lacks. Besides its lower cost, '''Ice and Pyre''' has few other benefits and '''Pyrebound''' is a significant downside. Despite its weaknesses, '''Ice and Pyre''' is a reasonable choice if you have any way to take advantage of its Attuned keyword, and can be a useful addition to a strong spell-based deck. It is effective for builds which can always comfortably set up on top floor, with artifacts such as [[Sigiled Seaweed]] and/or [[Zone of Silence]] protecting them from enemies with {{IconLink|Resolve}} triggers, or a durable tank and/or unit with {{IconLink|Sweep}} and {{IconLink|Quick}} to block or take out these enemies altogether. This makes it work well with artifacts like [[Totem Fragment]] or [[Rootsplit Mask]]. If you do not have a specific way to keep yourself safe while enemies ascend and cannot set up in this way, however, then '''Ice and Pyre''' will be of very limited use. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! So, the Stygian have created shrines all over the seafloor to offer sustenance and other treasures to the sleeping Titan. |artist = John Lee }} '''Deep Offering''' is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It discards all cards in hand, then draws 5 new cards. ==Strategy== '''Deep Offering''' is one of the strongest cards in the game when trying to build [[Infinites]], and is also very powerful even if you don't plan to do so. Once you find it, your main goal should be to find a Magic Shop and add {{IconLink|Eternalstone}} and {{IconLink|Smolderstone}} to it, in that order. This will give you a {{Ember|1}}, non-consuming spell which draws 5 cards, an immensely powerful option in a game where card draw is almost nonexistent. At this point you will usually want to duplicate it. To lower it to {{Ember|0}}, you can use [[Spell Sanctum]] or reduce the cost in another way, such as drawing it with [[Awoken's Rail Spike]] or [[Scrivener]]. If you have [[Lightstone Casing]], you can simply add an {{IconLink|Emberstone}}. If you can whittle down the rest of your deck to a maximum of 4 cards, either through Consume, playing units, or permanent removals, then two copies of this spell can draw each other infinitely. Keep in mind that this means you can only have two other cards at Covenant 5 and above, due to the two [[Vengeful Shard]]s added to your starting deck, unless you have [[Sacrificial Resurrection]] to remove them. This can provide unlimited {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers. It can also allow other spells to be played infinitely, as long as they are either {{Ember|0}} or [[:Category:Offering cards|Offering]] cards like [[Crypt Builder]]. With [[Kinstone Totem]], this infinite can be {{Ember}}-positive, allowing any spell to be used. The Kinstone Totem also allows you to replace {{IconLink|Smolderstone}} with {{IconLink|Twinstone}}, making a duplicate unnecessary. If you are unable to make your deck small enough for an infinite, or if you simply don't want to use one, then '''Deep Offering''' is still a very strong option due to its impressive card draw. However, it absolutely needs a Merchant of Magic as soon as possible; the card is extremely hard to play at {{Ember|3}} without Kinstone Totem, as you will likely have no {{Ember}} to play any of the cards you draw. == Notes == '''Deep Offering''' interacts with [[Split Anvil]] like you'd want it to: after casting '''Deep Offering''', newly drawn spells that cost less are discounted to {{Ember|0}}. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! It's common for a deck to have between 10 and 30 spells, putting this spell's base damage somewhere between 60 and 180, and it generally isn't possible or viable to go much past this. It's hard for it to kill late-game tanks, though {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} or {{IconLink|Conduit}} from the [[Luna Coven]] can get it there, and it is sort of [[Attuned]] by virtue of hitting three times if you can give it [[Magic Power]]. Still, its cost (and lack of [[Offering]] keyword, as compared to [[Crypt Builder]]) makes it fairly hard to justify from an {{Ember}} perspective, especially in a clan that's often looking to spam a large number of spells for {{IconLink|Incant}}, so you often need something to break {{Ember}} economy like [[Boiler Room]] or [[Volatile Gauge]] to justify this. A different life than I would prefer to lead, but most likely much more honorable.'' |artist = Daniel Sarmiento Chuquisengo }} '''Gifts for a Guard''' is a rare spell from the [[Stygian Guard]]. It draws 3 damage spells at random, sets their cost to {{Ember|0}}, applies +30 '''[[Magic Power]]''', and makes them '''[[Consume]]''' when played. Like all "draw a card" spells, it cannot draw cards that are currently in hand. == Strategy == On its own, '''Gifts for a Guard''' is a reasonably useful but dangerous spell. It can draw several cards and, for a significant {{Ember}} cost, allows them to be played for free. Adding '''[[Consume]]''' to the targets can be useful for removing cards like [[Frozen Lance]] from your deck, but the random draw means that you risk losing your strongest and most important spells. This spell is at its strongest when it cannot apply Consume to the spells it draws. Drawing a card with {{IconLink|Eternalstone}} will not reapply Consume, and the upgrades applied by '''Gifts for a Guard''' will apply for the rest of battle. If you can add {{IconLink|Eternalstone}} to both '''Gifts for a Guard''' and the target spell, then you can repeatedly redraw and buff it, consistently adding more Magic Power and even allowing you to play the spell twice in a single turn if you draw them together. Because '''Gifts for a Guard''' reduces the target spell's cost to {{Ember|0}} regardless, it is usually best to add {{IconLink|Surgestone}} rather than {{IconLink|Smolderstone}} to the target spell before adding {{IconLink|Eternalstone}}. The best targets are those with Attuned, multiple hits, or full-floor damage, as well as a high starting cost to take advantage of the cost reduction. [[Crypt Builder]], [[Titanstooth]] and [[Ancient Synergy]] are all excellent in-clan targets. Starting with [[Forgone Power]] means that '''Gifts for a Guard''' cannot be used to clear out your starter spells, but also means that it is much more likely to hit the spell you want. If you start with [[Frozen Lance]], and especially if your other starter card is a damage spell like [[Plink]] or [[Torch]], then it can be difficult to consistently buff the spell you want to target. Cards which already have Consume can be drawn with no downside. Regardless of what this spell draws, it also gives four {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers off of one card. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Upgrade !! {{SpellCard |name = Hoarfrost Effigy |image = CRD_HoarfrostEffigy.png |clan = [[Stygian Guard]] |rarity = Rare |cost = 3 |effect = Transfer all {{IconLink|Frostbite}} on this floor to a unit, then double the amount of {{IconLink|Frostbite}}. |flavor = Even before the freeze, the granite monuments of the Titan dotting the sea were cold structures. Now they've become permanently frozen fixtures of the seascape, ominous presences easily recognizable by their sharp profiles. |artist = Luke Banke }} '''Hoarfrost Effigy''' is a [[Stygian Guard]] spell. It moves all {{IconLink|Frostbite}} from units on the floor to the target, then doubles the amount of Frostbite on that unit. ==Strategy== '''Hoarfrost Effigy''' is generally a useless or even actively harmful card. Its ability to move a large amount of {{IconLink|Frostbite}} to a single unit and double it can make it a tempting choice, especially against flying bosses, but it is ultimately not worth it. Its best case scenario is to take down flying bosses easily in rings 3, 6 and 8. It can transfer larger amounts of {{IconLink|Frostbite}} to them early in the battle, and continue doing so as they fly around. By the time they enter {{IconLink|Relentless}}, they will be much easier to kill as a result. However, this generally makes things harder, due to the non-boss enemies present in the battle. By removing {{IconLink|Frostbite}} from all other units on the floor, it prevents you from using {{IconLink|Frostbite}} to kill backliners, which is generally one of its main uses. This means that, in order to use the spell at all, you must have a build strong enough to take out waves of enemies without using {{IconLink|Frostbite}}. If that is the case, then taking cards which work only on {{IconLink|Frostbite}} is generally not a very good idea. It is arguably at its most useful alongside the [[Frostpiercer]] as a way to slay bosses, effectively forcing the boss to receive the full force of the attacker's damage every turn. Even ignoring its downside, '''Hoarfrost Effigy''' is simply not worth its high cost of {{Ember|3}}. If you happen to have the [[Volatile Gauge]] along with a deck full of more {{IconLink|Frostbite}}-applying cards than you could ever need, then it could theoretically be helpful, but even it that case it is a questionable choice. If you are chasing a high score and are confident you can win either way, '''Hoarfrost Effigy''' becomes much more useful. Its ability to stack enormous amounts of {{IconLink|Frostbite}} on flying bosses allows for early kills, massively increasing your score. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Upgrade !! '''Frostpiercer''' is a rare [[Stygian Guard]] equipment added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It applies {{IconLink|Frostbite}} equal to half the damage dealt by the equipped unit to foes struck.

==Strategy==

When a unit with '''Frostpiercer''' {{IconLink|Strike}}s, once the struck target has taken damage from the {{IconLink|Frostbite}} applied twice, the target has taken a total of double the original damage dealt - something that is guaranteed to happen before the Pyre can be targeted if the unit equipped is on the first or second floor. (This analysis ignores {{IconLink|Frostbite}} decay, but that's negligible compared to the {{IconLink|Frostbite}} this can deal.) This compares quite favorably with {{IconLink|Multistrike}} and can even stack multiplicatively with it. When compared to [[Void Armament]], [[Cursed Twinblade]], and [[Resin Blades]], this is a very good deal, and the damage multiplier is even higher if the damage is dealt on the first floor or against [[Savagery]] and [[Entropy]].

And in {{IconLink|Relentless}} combat, the damage dealt to the boss racks up really fast on a unit with respectable {{Attack}} (quadratically, for the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadratic_function mathematically curious]) in a way similar to [[Tethys Titansbane]]'s '''Chillwind''' path.

There is a less favorable way of looking at this in non-{{IconLink|Relentless}} combat, however - ideally, you'd be equipping this to a unit with high {{Attack}}. And in order for {{IconLink|Frostbite}} to deal any damage, the victim needs to survive combat. But usually your damaging unit doesn't intend on having their victims survive the combat. Another way of saying this - under normal circumstances, if this weapon's {{IconLink|Frostbite}} mattered, the enemies behind the victim survived. This is particularly problematic against waves with two [[Avowed Gladiator]]s that you will see in the lategame. So it can be less effective than you'd think against tanky waves of enemies, though it still performs excellently against {{IconLink|Relentless}} bosses.

There is an in-clan answer to this problem in the form of {{IconLink|Sweep}} units like [[Icy Cilophyte]], [[Coldcaelia]], and [[Tethys Titansbane]]'s '''Handheld Totem''' path, who when equipped with this will ensure the whole floor suffers from {{IconLink|Frostbite}}. [[Glass Cannon]] and especially [[Bloodthirsty Blade]] are excellent choices for merging with this equipment. With a respectable amount of {{Attack}} scaling, a {{IconLink|Sweep}} unit equipped with this can kill backliners, cripple tanks, and leave {{IconLink|Relentless}} bosses in a world of hurt.

The one downside of using this equipment with {{IconLink|Sweep}} units is that {{IconLink|Frostbite}} only deals damage ''after'' battle, so enemies may survive and attack even if your sweeper has {{IconLink|Quick}}. This means that, if you rely on a quick sweeper to wipe out enemies like [[Chosen Assassin]] before they can attack, it may be better to invest in raw {{Attack}} instead.

== Notes ==
* A unit with {{IconLink|Dualism}} will still only apply {{IconLink|Frostbite}} equal to half their damage.

{{RoomCard |name = Siren's Song |image = CRD_Siren's_Song_LA.png |clan = Stygian Guard |rarity = Rare |cost = 2 |effect = '''[[Pyrebound]].'''
At the start of combat, '''[[Ascend]]''' non-boss enemy units on this floor and apply {{IconLink|Dazed|3}}. |flavor = I've heard no song as beautiful or as deadly as that of the Sirens of the Stygian. Their luring voices can disarm even the most hardened of hearts. |artist = Adam Lee }} '''Siren's Song''' is a [[Stygian Guard]] room. Each turn, before combat, it [[Ascend]]s all enemy units on the floor and applies {{IconLink|Dazed|3}} to them. It can only be played in the room just below the Pyre. ==Interactions== * [[Trials#Heaven's Seal|Heaven's Seal]] will heal enemies when this card moves them to the top. * If the enemies are {{IconLink|Rooted}}, such as by the [[Rootsplit Mask]], then they will remain in place and lose a stack of {{IconLink|Rooted}} prior to combat. This will allow them to be attacked by the third floor during combat, though it also means they'll reach the Pyre with one less stack of {{IconLink|Dazed}}. * [[Manifold Mirror]] will not work on this room. ==Strategy== '''Siren's Song''' is an odd room. It moves enemies into your Pyre room - generally something you want to avoid - but also applies an impressive amount of {{IconLink|Dazed}} to the entire floor every turn. This allows the Pyre to attack them 3 times before they can do anything to it. This room essentially lowers the bar for how much damage your units have to deal to waves, as enemies with health less than 3 times the Pyre's {{Attack}} will just die. For much of this game, this encompasses just about every regular enemy. You'll still need to pack an answer for bosses, and in the late game, [[Avowed Gladiator]] and [[Terrifying Amalgam]] will still need to be softened up. This room is especially strong with builds that rely on {{IconLink|Frostbite}} to deal damage, as the enemies will take {{IconLink|Frostbite}} damage three additional times before they can attack the Pyre. This means that even a mediocre source of {{IconLink|Frostbite}} can be enough to take down tanky enemies if your units cannot finish them off. For obvious reasons, it's stronger with high-{{Attack}} [[Pyre Hearts]], like [[Pyre of Savagery]] and [[Proto Heartcage]]. A Pyre with low {{Attack}} like [[Bogwurm's Growth]] or [[Pyre of Dominion]] may still lose significant {{PyreHealth}} to late-game enemies. Keep in mind that your units on the top floor will not be able to attack enemies with this room in play, as they're Ascended before combat begins, so you will need to deal damage on the lower floors instead. This does provide defensive benefit: units on your top floor can only be attacked by bosses, making it a safer place to put units like [[Cuttlehex]] and [[Molluscmage]], though keep in mind that [[Flying Bosses]] can still attack them. There are some notable exceptions to this: * If enemies have {{IconLink|Spikes}}, most notably in [[Cael, Lord of the Cherubs]]'s '''Nourishing Feed''' variant, that will still hurt the Pyre. This room is therefore a much less appealing choice if you're fighting that variant, as that variant more or less requires you to have a way of dealing with tanky enemies early in fights, which this room normally lets you get away with not having. * In the [[The_Great_Abyss#Clash_With_The_Titans|Titans]] fight, letting enemies through gives [[Dominion]] additional opportunities to attack. While this will also make [[Dominion]] take damage, if your build is too passive to kill [[Savagery]] and [[Entropy]], that may not matter. ({{IconLink|Sap}} or {{IconLink|Dazed}} applied to [[Dominion]] can reduce or eliminate damage taken from this, though leaked enemies will make it deplete faster.) As such, [[Siren's Song]] can buy you a lot of time, both in the context of an individual battle and the run in general, to find a good way to scale against bosses - just be sure to remember that you have to find one eventually. ==Sounds== {| ! '''Umbra''' [[File:ClanUmbra.png|20x20px]] is a [[clan]]  in [[Monster Train 2]], returning from [[Monster Train 1]]. It is unlocked after unlocking [[Hellhorned]] first and then increasing {{Capacity}} 20 times.

Umbra features the following mechanics:
* '''[[Morsels]]''' are special units central to Umbra gameplay. They have {{IconLink|Eaten}} triggers which grant {{Attack}}, {{Health}}, and/or buffs to the front friendly unit. As a result, many Umbra units are tanky and designed to sit at the front of a floor, being fed Morsels. Many also have {{IconLink|Gorge}} triggers that activate when eating. For more information, see the [[Morsels]] page.
* Many effects can increase {{Capacity}}, synergizing with the need to place many Morsels on a floor.
* {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} and {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} are common defensive buffs.
* Many powerful spells cause {{IconLink|Emberdrain}}, reducing your {{Ember}} on the next turn. To counteract this, the clan features several ways to generate {{Ember}} mid-turn. The clan also heavily features X-cost spells.

The clan's unique [[Merchant of Steel]] Upgrade is {{IconLink|Shieldstone}}.

{{UnitCard |name = Penumbra |image = PLR_Penumbra.png |clan = Umbra |rarity = Champion |type = Champion |banner = No |cost = 0 |size = 3 |stats = 20/20 |flavor = I have no hard facts on its origin, but it is rumored to be the beginning of the Shroud itself, formed in the long forgotten depths of the Crucible and giving life to the rest of Hell. As the leader of the gluttonous Shroud, they are a champion that usually requires a lot of attention, either in the need for [[Morsels]] or {{Capacity}}. Their starter card is [[Shadesplitter]]. == Light Forge Upgrades == {{ChampionPaths |baseStats=20/20 |baseSize=3 |b1size=4 |b2size=5 |b3size=6 |a=Architect |a1stats=25/20 |a1abilities={{IconLink|Summon}}: {{Capacity|+2}} on this floor. |a2stats=50/30 |a2abilities={{IconLink|Summon}}: {{Capacity|+3}} on this floor. |a3stats=100/40 |a3abilities={{IconLink|Summon}}: {{Capacity|+4}} on this floor. |b=Monstrous |b1stats=50/30 |b1abilities={{IconLink|Trample}}. |b2stats=125/60 |b2abilities={{IconLink|Trample}}. |b3stats=250/120 |b3abilities={{IconLink|Trample}}. |c=Glutton |c1stats=20/20 |c1abilities={{IconLink|Lifesteal|2}}.
{{IconLink|Gorge}}: {{Attack|+4}} and {{Health|+2}}. |c2stats=35/35 |c2abilities={{IconLink|Lifesteal|2}}.
{{IconLink|Gorge}}: {{Attack|+9}} and {{Health|+4}}. |c3stats=50/50 |c3abilities={{IconLink|Lifesteal|2}}.
{{IconLink|Gorge}}: {{Attack|+15}} and {{Health|+6}}. }} == Strategy == '''Penumbra''' is a big, scary champion that hits like a truck, with their '''Monstrous''' path granting some of the highest raw damage of any unit. However, even with these big damage numbers, they won't be able to win the game on their own, and by the endgame they'll rarely be able to kill even a single [[Avowed Gladiator]] without significant support. This means that all of their paths benefit significantly from {{IconLink|Trample}} and {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. Fortunately, Umbra can give them those status effects through [[Umbra Stone]] and [[Furnace Tap]]. If you cannot give '''Penumbra''' their needed support, you're better off dropping them in a random floor you won't use and focusing on other units. ===Architect=== This is '''Penumbra''''s most support oriented path, increasing the size of the floor when they are played. This functionally gives them {{Capacity|1}}, {{Capacity|0}}, or {{Capacity|-1}} depending on how many levels you take. As this is a {{IconLink|Summon}} effect, it can be repeated by killing and [[Reform|reforming]] '''Penumbra''', or by using a [[Transcendimp]]. It lacks either the raw damage output of '''Monstrous''' or the scaling of '''Glutton''', so it is best used as a support unit when you have other damage solutions and just require extra space. This path is better used when you know you will have many units to play, like with alternate [[Lazarus League]], [[Melting Remnant]], alternate [[Hellhorned]], alternate [[Pyreborne]] or with the [[Pyre of Dominion]]. Although '''Architect''' '''Penumbra''' functionally doesn't take up {{Capacity}} at level 2 or 3, it's usually a good idea to remove '''Penumbra''' from the floor after playing them, which will free up an extra {{Capacity|3}}; additionally, they still count towards the 7 unit per floor limit, potentially preventing you from filling the floor with [[Morsels]] or other units. This can be done by [[Ascend]]ing or [[Descend]]ing them off the floor, playing them at the front which will usually have them killed quickly due to '''Architect''''s low {{Health}}, or just killing them yourself with a targeted damage spell. ===Monstrous=== This is the path to the biggest champion in the game, and one of the few ways to get a {{Capacity|6}} unit naturally. This can can help you breeze through the early game with their innate {{IconLink|Trample}}, though their base {{Attack}} is still insufficient to deal with late-game enemies like [[Avowed Gladiator]]. The main problem is that they'll monopolize a floor, and the third level is unplayable without a source of additional space (usually either [[Bogwurm's Growth]] or [[Heaven's Light]]) due to their {{Capacity|6}} requirement. Taking a level in '''Architect''' can help mitigate this, but means you will lose out on the high damage of '''Monstrous III'''. Mixing '''Monstrous''' with '''Glutton''' is generally a bad idea, as their increased size makes it difficult to play Morsels behind them, but can be a method to get {{IconLink|Trample}} on '''Penumbra''' if you cannot find another source. {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} builds centered around [[Perils of Production]] can help power them up further, taking advantage of '''Penumbra''''s high base stats and pushing them even further to create a unit that can, in the best cases, nearly beat the game on its own. If all else fails, leave them alone in one of the upper floors and they will end up killing some stragglers late game. ===Glutton=== This path has the potential to be enormously strong due to the additional stats it gains from each [[Morsels|Morsel]]. This makes them a great contender for {{IconLink|Trample}} from [[Umbra Stone]] and {{IconLink|Multistrike}} from [[Furnace Tap]] if you can scale them correctly. Equipment such as [[Void Armament]] is also powerful, though risky. Unfortunately, this path has two main flaws: it lacks damage output early in the battle, and it requires constant Morsel investment in order to gain any meaningful benefit. To get your money's worth, you need to have enough space to play Morsels, constant Morsel production, and preferably cards like [[Feast]] to speed things up further. '''Glutton''' also works poorly alongside most other Umbra units, which also want to eat as many Morsels as possible. You'll need to choose which {{IconLink|Gorge}} unit to feed, leaving the others ineffective and weak. This makes many of Umbra's best units, such as [[Morsel-Made]] and [[Overgorger]], poor choices when using '''Glutton'''. You will also need to find a way to keep them alive, as their mere {{IconLink|Lifesteal|2}} won't help much, and they're vulnerable to flying bosses early. Using cards which produce uncommon Morsels like [[Morsel Jeweler]] and [[Morsel Excavator]] will help, as will cards like [[Prismal Dust]], [[Grovel]] or [[Gem Trove]]. [[Immortal Trade]] also works if on a good [[Perils of Production]] run. [[Shroud Spike]] is one of the best cards in the game when using this path. '''Primordium''' is the alternate [[Champion]] of the [[Umbra]] clan. It works very differently than any other Champion, as it is intended to be {{IconLink|Eaten}} by other units rather than fighting on its own. Although not considered a [[Morsels|Morsel]], it fulfills a similar purpose, intended as a sacrifice to power up your other units. Its starter card is [[Plink]].
