== Strategy ==
'''Primordium''' is a very unorthodox champion which works different from any other unit. First, you will need a strong front unit to feed off of '''Primordium'''. This can be a strong unit from any clan, or one of the {{IconLink|Gorge}} units from the Umbra clan. Units like [[Animus of Will]] or [[Test Subject Alpha]], with useful effects but low stats, tend to be the best choices. This unit must be strong enough to survive until '''Primordium''' has a chance to buff it. Once '''Primordium''' and the other unit are in place, focus on buffing '''Primordium''' as much as possible. 

Due to being {{IconLink|Eaten}}, '''Primordium''' ''can'' be brought back with [[Retch]]. However, cards like [[Shroud Spike]] which specifically apply only to Morsels do not work on it.

When allied with the [[Lazarus League]], [[Brain Transfer]] can be an incredibly powerful scaling solution. You can pass '''Primordium''''s {{Attack}}, and with Superfood, buffs, to another unit and then back to itself (by having that unit be the front unit without any {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, having Primordium behind it, and then targeting the front unit with Brain Transfer) potentially multiple times, scaling '''Primordium''' (and by extension whoever it's feeding)'s {{Attack}} and buffs to absurd levels.

===Interaction with Equipment and Rooms===
In Monster Train 2, the presence of [[Equipment|equipment]] and [[Room|rooms]] is a major boon for '''Primordium''', because {{Attack}} and {{Health}} granted by equipment and rooms are passed on to the eater. Status effects granted by equipment are also passed on via the '''Superfood''' path. As a result, '''Primordium''' usually wants a strong equipment with '''[[Deployable]]''', ideally a [[Merged Equipment]]. This makes an early {{IconLink|Merchant of Arms|png=MerchantOfArms}} on [[Ring 3]] a high priority.

Nearly all of the Clanless equipment available at the Merchant of Arms is desirable. Highlights include [[Swiftsteel Dagger]], [[Meat Shield]], [[Void Armament]] (note that '''Primordium''' isn't Purged upon being eaten while it's equipped), and especially [[Overgrowth Carapace]]. [[Glass Cannon]] is excellent too, but be mindful that {{IconLink|Fragile}} will be passed on if you have '''Superfood'''. [[Stasis Crystal]] is similarly effective, but only if you are not using '''Superfood''', as otherwise {{IconLink|Stasis}} will be passed on and the eater will be unable to attack and have no means of escape. [[Bloodthirsty Blade]] can also be effective, though its {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers are ideally stacked on a unit other than '''Primordium''' in the early game.

While using '''Superfood''', [[Iron-tongue]] is immensely powerful as it enables you to provide {{IconLink|Sweep}} to any unit without the recipient being locked to {{Attack|30}}. However, be aware that this generally precludes using '''Primordium''' as a means of damage scaling, unless you can replace Iron-tongue after being {{IconLink|Eaten}} once, or you are scaling damage via a buff like {{IconLink|Rage}} rather than raw stat boosts.

The Umbra’s exclusive equipment, [[Glutton's Maw]], is an excellent way to scale '''Primordium''' if you have reliable access to Morsels or other disposable units to use its ability with. This can allow '''Primordium''' to gain at least {{AttackHealth|+15/+15}} each turn, potentially more if devouring a Morsel, which can then be passed onto your frontliner. Unfortunately, Plinks are not very reliable sources of Morsel generation, so it may be more difficult than you would expect to provide fodder for '''Primordium''' to eat.

Equipment from allied clans can also be powerful, though these tend to focus on status effects that are only passed on via '''Superfood'''.

Regarding Rooms, [[Fight Club]] contributes {{Attack|+15}} to the unit in front and {{Attack|+15}} per {{IconLink|Eaten}} trigger, and [[Lazarus League]]'s [[Reanimation Lab]] contributes {{AttackHealth|+7/+7}} each.

===Superfood===
This is generally [[Primordium]]'s most useful path, as it passes on ''all'' of the effects applied to '''Primordium''', which includes {{IconLink|Armor}}, {{IconLink|Titanskin}}, and even {{IconLink|Multistrike}} and {{IconLink|Sweep}}! This makes it a great scaling choice so long as you have the means to apply lots of effects to it. Adding {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}} to '''Primordium''' on turn 1 will grant {{IconLink|Multistrike|3}} to your front unit.

The innate {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} protects '''Primordium''' in the early turns so it doesn't die as easily, as well as stacking multiple times onto your front unit. If you don't need {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} or have better sources of it, it can be a good idea to take one level of '''Superfood''' and two levels of another path.

Be aware that this path passes on ''all'' status effects, including [[Debuffs]]. Be prepared for enormous amounts of {{IconLink|Sap}}, {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}}, or {{IconLink|Corruption}} depending on which version of [[Seraph]] you're going to face; this can be addressed by stacking even more {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} onto '''Primordium''' for the latter two, or aggressive damage scaling (and not playing [[Curse of Entropy]]) for the former. This also means that even a small amount of {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} will completely shut down your {{Ember}} production if you don't have [[Perils of Production]] with {{IconLink|Keepstone}}, or other ways to generate {{Ember}}.

===Stalwart Snack===
'''Stalwart Snack''' makes '''Primordium''' last longer, allowing it to pass its stats to the front unit more times. This is best if you have cards which can increase [[Primordium]]'s stats, which will pay off more times over the course of the battle. It is rarely worth taking all three levels, but it can be a solid pick to extend the effect of '''Superfood'''. '''Superfood I/Stalwart Snack II''' can give your front unit all of [[Primordium]]'s status effects eight times.

[[Feast]] helps eat '''Primordium''' multiple times per turn, taking better advantage of its high {{IconLink|Buffet}}. Feast also makes it much more justifiable to invest fully in this path, as '''Stalwart Snack III''' has {{AttackHealth|10|10}} and will therefore transmit a total of {{AttackHealth|+120|+120}}, but takes a very long time to do so. [[Retch]], meanwhile, makes it less useful, as you can simply bring '''Primordium''' back once eaten.

===Aggressive Edible===
The most straightforward of the paths, this one just gives '''Primordium''' more {{Attack}}. At level III, it will grant a massive {{Attack|+180}} to your front unit over three turns, which can be immensely powerful if combined with {{IconLink|Sweep}}, {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, or both. This is best used when you have no need for greater survivability, and want to focus on putting out as much damage as possible. This is arguably the best path for combining with Retch, as it does not require much investment to perform unlike '''Superfood''' and is eaten fairly quickly.

'''Rubble Morsel''' is a [[Morsel]] of the [[Umbra]] clan. Like all Morsels, its main purpose is to be {{IconLink|Eaten}}. It provides {{AttackHealth|+3/+3}} and {{Ember|1}} upon being eaten.

==Strategy==

This is the most common [[Morsel]] when using the Umbra starting deck, as it appears 50% of the time when [[Shadesplitter]], [[Plink]], or [[Abandoned Antumbra]] generate a Morsel. Typically, it's the least exciting Morsel. It provides a relatively small {{Attack}} and {{Health}} increase, and its {{Ember|+1}} when eaten, while helpful, is granted next turn in most cases, so it's hard for you to rely on having a way to use that, since you usually don't know exactly what you're drawing. In those cases, it should be treated as a minor boost rather than a central part of your strategy. 

That being said, if you have ways of eating it this turn, such as with [[Feast]], [[Morsel-Made]], or [[Shroud Spike]], its {{Ember}} boost becomes much more usable, as you can plan your turn around it much more. [[Shroud Spike]] in particular can use a '''Rubble Morsel''' to double as a [[Kindle]], which opens up powerful self-synergy with {{IconLink|Twinstone}}.

If you don't have ways of eating it this turn, cards like [[Shadesplitter]] and [[Plink]] which frequently create '''Rubble Morsels''' should usually be removed later in the run if possible, as you can only eat so many Morsels in that case - either due to {{Capacity}} or the 7-unit limit. '''Rubble Morsels''' can find themselves unable to be placed on your train to be {{IconLink|Eaten}}, either forcing you to let them be killed by enemies or in the worst case not playing them at all, letting them gum up your deck. When using [[Retch]] to reclaim units that were eaten, it can often be a good idea to intentionally let '''Rubble Morsels''' die to enemies rather than going into your {{IconLink|Eaten}} pile.

'''Rubble Morsels''' are the only common Morsels. Any card which mentions "uncommon or rare" Morsels specifically excludes them.

== Trivia ==
* It is usually impossible to add '''Rubble Morsel''' to your deck. However, if you equip it with [[Mitosis Cap]] and end combat before it can be {{IconLink|Eaten}}, you will gain a permanent copy, and can even upgrade it at the [[Merchant of Steel]].

'''Morsel Excavators''' are best utilized when feeding a bulky and strong tank unit. They serve as one of the better forms of healing within the Umbra clan, while also providing an appreciable {{Attack}} buff. Do note that {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} does not help you if your unit gets killed before it can attack, so make sure your front unit can survive at least one attack from the ring's boss if you plan to rely on this Morsel for survivability.

Like [[Magma Morsel]], its {{Attack|6}} can let it potentially kill a frail backliner in the early rings, but it also makes it susceptible to dying if it attacks an enemy with {{IconLink|Spikes}}. Always keep positioning in mind!

It is somewhat anti-synergistic with [[Morsel Jeweler]]s, as {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} and {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} tend to overlap in purpose.

== Trivia ==
* It is usually impossible to add '''Morsel Excavator''' to your deck. However, if you equip it with [[Mitosis Cap]] and end combat before it can be {{IconLink|Eaten}}, you will gain a permanent copy, and can even upgrade it at the [[Merchant of Steel]].

The [[Lost Arsenal]] update made this unit start with two stacks of {{IconLink|Fuel}}, mitigating its heavy downside of not being able to attack on the first turn and making it a much more reliable unit. That said, it still requires solid Morsel production in order to perform later. It provides you with a constant supply of [[Morsels]] for your units. == Strategy == '''Morselmaker''' makes it so you do not have to rely on Morsel-generating cards to feed your most important units, giving you two (four if paired with [[Morselmaster]]) free Morsels per turn on a single floor. This can let the floor's frontline unit scale for free while you focus on the train's other floors. It is best used with units that have powerful {{IconLink|Gorge}} effects, such as '''Glutton''' [[Penumbra]], [[Alloyed Construct]], [[Morsel-Made]] or [[Overgorger]]. Without a {{IconLink|Gorge}} effect, the Morsels are often underwhelming, giving only the equivalent of a single Morsel Miner per turn. [[Morselmaster]] also doubles its produced Morsels, thus doubling the scaling provided. It can be dangerous to rely on '''Morselmaker''' as your only Morsel source. For example, although pairing it with [[Shadoweater]] makes for solid backline clear, this will allow backline units in the first wave to escape unscathed, as it will not have summoned any Morsels yet. It is effectively a {{Capacity|3}} unit thanks to the two Morsels it summons, but you can overstack the floor if you play another unit before it summons the Morsels or after using [[Feast]]. This does make it slightly awkward with other Morsel generation, however, because it may be difficult to fit more powerful Morsels like [[Morsel Excavator]] on its floor. Its low stats make it vulnerable to anything that targets the backlines, like [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]] or any enemy with {{IconLink|Sweep}}. Always keep this in mind when thinking about adding it or buying upgrades. With {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} (preferably from {{IconLink|Shieldstone}}), this unit has an odd niche during [[Clash with the Titans]]. If placed at the front of a floor, the Morsels it summons are surprisingly efficient protection for vulnerable floors. The combined attacks of [[Dominion]] and [[Entropy]] will only kill one Morsel. [[Savagery]] poses more of an issue due to having {{IconLink|Trample}} and gaining {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, which lets him mow down the Morsels and hit '''Morselmaker''', but he will only be on your floor one out of every three turns, so a solid stack of {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} can ward him off. As long as you can place down a single Morsel or other chump blocker on the first turn to prevent '''Morselmaker''' from gaining {{IconLink|Corruption}}, it can protect your other units or stave off Savagery's {{IconLink|Resolve}} damage for much longer than you would expect. If you have [[Chain of Gems]] or [[Winged Technology]] to automatically put {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} on the Morsels, even Savagery can struggle to kill '''Morselmaker''', especially if you pair it with a Morselmaster for four shielded chump blockers per turn. It creates a copy of any [[Morsel]] units summoned, doubling the scaling of your front units. == Strategy == '''Morselmaster''' can, in the right build, double the output of your [[Morsels]] and {{IconLink|Gorge}} abilities. Put it behind a powerful unit, ideally one with a {{IconLink|Gorge}} ability. You will, however, need {{Capacity}} to make optimal use of this. If you place '''Morselmaster''' behind a {{Capacity|2}} unit on a {{Capacity|5}} floor, such as [[Crucible Warden]], you'll only be able to take advantage of '''Morselmaster''''s ability once per turn, as the first placed Morsel will duplicate, resulting in a full floor ('''Morselmaster'''({{Capacity|1}}) + Morsel (x2) ({{Capacity|2}}) + Crucible Warden ({{Capacity|2}})). If you have {{Capacity|6}}, on the other hand, you can take advantage of this ability twice - the second placed Morsel's copy will overstack the floor. Cards like [[Space Prism]] can be useful to make sure you have an odd number of empty spaces. You'll also want to be selective with the Morsels you duplicate - [[Making of a Morsel]] gives you guaranteed access to high-quality [[Morsel Miner|Morsel Miners]], giving you the maximum benefit for this ability. Alternatively, you can pair '''Morselmaster''' with [[Morselmaker]] to get a flat four Morsels per turn regardless of {{Capacity}}. Just make sure you don't get locked out of playing one of your units by the extra Morsels - high {{DeploymentEmber}} is very helpful here. Once you have this floor set, you're getting 4 Morsels per turn without any extra investment. (It won't be easy to improve on this, though, as your floor will start with 7 units each turn: '''Morselmaster''', Morselmaker, 4 morsels, and whatever unit you place in front.) Even with infinite {{Capacity}}, you won't be able to take advantage of this ability more than twice per turn (assuming you put another unit with Morselmaster) due to the 7 unit limit per floor, unless you have a way of consuming Morsels mid-turn. This makes [[Feast]] and [[Morsel-Made]] ideal partners to really allow '''Morselmaster''''s ability to shine - removing the limit on how many times per turn its ability can activate. With Morsel-Made in particular, it's even worth having two copies of '''Morselmaster''' on the floor, as they will create a total of three Morsels out of one, rapidly accelerating Morsel-Made's scaling. Its low stats makes it weak against anything that targets the backline, and enemies like [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]] or [[Ragewing Assassin]]s are a problem unless you can give it some extra {{Health}}. Cards like [[Void Binding]] can also help keep it alive, but are generally better used on your frontliner. == Recommended Upgrades == {|class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%;" | Upgrade ! Though when I say collect, I really mean eat them whole. |artist = Brian Mutschler }} '''Shadoweater''' is an uncommon [[Umbra]] [[banner unit]]. Instead of attacking, this unit deals damage after eating [[Morsels]]. == Strategy == '''Shadoweater''' is the Umbra clan equivalent of a {{IconLink|Sweep}} unit, getting rid of waves of enemies (or at least the frail backline units) as long as you have the necessary Morsel generation. Feed it well enough and not only will it be very hard to kill, but your other floors will only need to deal with the tanky units. It also heals naturally, leaving you open to give your stacks of {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} or defensive buffs to other units. However, there is a glaring difference between '''Shadoweater''' and true {{IconLink|Sweep}} units: '''Shadoweater''' cannot "attack" before the enemy under normal circumstances. As such, it is very slow and clunky, vulnerable to losing its Morsels to enemy {{IconLink|Sweep}} units or outright dying before it can use its {{IconLink|Gorge}} effect. This makes it almost useless against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]] unless you have a way to {{IconLink|Gorge}} before combat begins. It is also largely helpless against [[Deafening Herald]]s, which disable its {{IconLink|Gorge}} trigger. '''Shadoweater''' is very dependent on having large quantities of Morsels, which can make it difficult to use alongside other {{IconLink|Gorge}} units. Having [[Morselmaker]] and/or [[Morselmaster]] is useful. [[Fossilized Fangs]] also helps a lot, doubling this unit's damage and healing. [[Feast]] is an incredibly important card to seek out if you plan to use '''Shadoweater''' as your backline clear. Upgraded with {{IconLink|Seekstone}} and {{IconLink|Keepstone}}, this card is effectively like granting '''Shadoweater''' {{IconLink|Quick}}, allowing it to destroy enemies before they can attack and potentially kill off its Morsels. It is practically necessary if you are fighting the Savagery variant of Seraph, as otherwise the [[Ragewing Assassin]]s present in every single wave will kill all of your Morsels before they can be eaten, even through [[Winged Technology]]. Even with Feast, you must also be able to consistently produce three Morsels every turn in order to kill the incredibly dangerous [[Chosen Assassin]]s. Though less accessible than Feast, [[Shroud Spike]] is also an option to eat Morsels before combat; however, for this to be consistent, it must be upgraded with {{IconLink|Eternalstone}}, and Shroud Spike is usually stronger as a scaling tool. [[Glutton's Maw]] is insufficient unless you have ways to reduce Cooldown mid-turn like [[Attuned Manacles]]; even with Fossilized Fangs, '''Shadoweater''' cannot deal enough damage by eating a single Morsel to kill a Chosen Assassin. There is one instance where Feast becomes unnecessary: in combination with {{IconLink|Stealth}}. The [[Shadow's Sheath]] artifact grants all units {{IconLink|Stealth|1}} on {{IconLink|Summon}}, which means any Morsels you play will not be targets of attacks. This grants you a ton of breathing room in dealing with these {{IconLink|Sweep}} units. However, this comes at a cost: Morsels can no longer be used as chump blockers against attacks, although they will still absorb {{IconLink|Corruption}} from [[Dominion]] if placed at the front of the floor. Still, if you are fighting Savagery Seraph and you are offered Shadow's Sheath with '''Shadoweater''', it is generally a good choice to take it. Alternatively, if partnered with the [[Melting Remnant]], you can apply {{IconLink|Stealth}} manually through [[Engulfed in Smoke]]. You can also use Glutton's Maw to eat a [[Molten Encasement]] with {{IconLink|Endless}}, as long as you have put down your other Morsels first; they will all receive {{IconLink|Stealth}} and be protected from attacks, letting '''Shadoweater''' eat them in peace. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! It eats any unit with an {{IconLink|Eaten}} ability as soon as that unit is played. == Strategy == '''Morsel-Made''' is a fast scaling unit that circumvents many of Umbra's constraints: * It only needs {{Capacity|1}} to be fed any number of [[Morsels]] as they are consumed instantly * It doesn't need to be in the front of the room, as its {{IconLink|Hunger}} ability makes all Morsels played on the room go directly to it * It does not need to worry about dying or having its Morsels die before its {{IconLink|Gorge}} effect activates As such, it is a unit that offers great value in most Umbra decks as long as you can feed it lots and lots of Morsels. [[Fossilized Fangs]] gives it {{AttackHealth|+8|+8}} per Morsel, while [[Morselmaker]] gives it a constant supply of Morsels. [[Morselmaster]] is perhaps its best partner, doubling its scaling. In fact, you can fit two Morselmasters on its floor by default while still having {{Capacity|1}} left over, which means every Morsel you play will be eaten three times. This rapidly scales the unit even if it's being fed low-quality [[Rubble Morsel]]s. You need very strong Morsel production in order to scale '''Morsel-Made''' fast enough in the later rings - [[Shadesplitter]]s won't cut it. [[Packed Morsels]] upgraded with {{IconLink|Eternalstone}} is a solid choice, particularly if you can then also apply {{IconLink|Twinstone}}. [[Cannibalize]] and [[Gem Trove]] are the next best options, but both have a drawback - needing to '''[[Sacrifice]]''' a unit and costing {{Ember|3}}, respectively. [[Shadelamp]], [[Abandoned Antumbra]], and [[Mask of Penumbra]] are all premium artifact pickups. [[Shadowbox]] is surprisingly worthwhile, as the Morsel output demanded by '''Morsel-Made''' will usually trigger the artifact by turn 3 or so, in order to devastate heavies who managed to sneak past before '''Morsel-Made''' could scale up. After Shadowbox triggers, units leaking is usually not much of a concern, as '''Morsel-Made''' should be destroying anything in its path. Its interaction with [[Primordium]] is usually a plus - while its {{IconLink|Hunger}} ability won't trigger during the deployment phase, it will eat Primordium once per [[Morsel]] placement (in addition to once per turn), letting you eat it quickly. This does mean if you're using Primordium's '''Superfood''' line that you'll need to put status effects on it immediately, but the fast scaling this provides can be amazing. Both of Primordium's other paths are highly desirable; '''Aggressive Edible III''' rapidly grants {{Attack|+180}}, while '''Stalwart Snack III''' will still be fully devoured relatively quick and provide a total of {{AttackHealth|+120|+120}}. Its ability also means you can't use [[Shroud Spike]] or [[Shroud Mitosis]] on its floor at all. [[Retch]] is particularly useful as you can immediately feed '''Morsel-Made''' all the returned Morsels, ignoring capacity limitations imposed by having so many units in your hand at once. This can be extra good with [[Primordium]], letting you completely eat them again instantly. Applying {{IconLink|Trample}} via [[Umbra Stone]] or other sources should be a priority if this unit is your main damage source, as it can easily scale up high enough to leverage the overkill damage. {{IconLink|Multistrike}} can serve this role as well, though outside of upgrades it can be harder to access or comes with drawbacks. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! Each time it eats a [[Morsel]] or [[Primordium]], it gains {{Attack|+2}} permanently. == Strategy == The '''Overgorger''' has the potential to be one of the strongest units in the game in terms of sheer {{Attack}} if obtained early enough and properly scaled. This means that it benefits greatly from {{IconLink|Multistrike}} and {{IconLink|Trample}}, available in-clan from [[Furnace Tap]] and [[Umbra Stone]]. This unit will also need to be in the front to eat Morsels, meaning you will have to protect it until it has time to scale up its {{Health}}. In general, Morsels which provide {{Health}} are more useful than those which provide {{Attack}}; the [[Overgorger]]'s permascaling takes care of all your damage needs, but does not provide defense. You will also need a lot of Morsels to properly scale it, making it generally bad to take any other {{IconLink|Gorge}} units together with '''Overgorger'''. A [[Morselmaker]] and a [[Morselmaster]] will provide four {{IconLink|Gorge}} triggers each turn, leaving you free to give Morsels to other units. [[Packed Morsels]], [[Cannibalize]], [[Gem Trove]], and [[Grovel]] are good Morsel production cards, as are the [[Abandoned Antumbra]] and [[Shadelamp]] artifacts. [[Feast]] allows '''Overgorger''' to eat more Morsels per turn, getting around {{Capacity}} and the 7-unit limit. Once it has scaled sufficiently, you can stop feeding the '''Overgorger''' and place it behind a tank for the last few battles. [[Shroud Spike]] can be used to trigger {{IconLink|Gorge}} multiple times on a single Morsel, potentially providing thousands of {{Attack}} by the endgame. While tricky to line up, casting [[Kindle]] first can skyrocket your scaling. {{IconLink|Freezestone}} can help accomplish this, as can {{IconLink|Twinstone}} on the Shroud Spike if cast first on a [[Rubble Morsel]]. [[Exile's Diadem]] and [[Crucible Extension]] are useful cards for '''Overgorger''', greatly expanding the available {{Capacity}} on its floor and thus allowing you to fit more Morsels onto its floor. [[Glutton's Maw]] lets '''Overgorger''' scale its {{Health}} faster, and it can also give it an extra {{IconLink|Gorge}} trigger every turn, even on a unit that would not normally be {{IconLink|Eaten}}, like an [[Imp]]. [[Fossilized Fangs]] can turn '''Overgorger''' into a true menace, but it is rare to get both, especially since you need to find Fossilized Fangs early on. When used alongside the [[Banished]] clan, [[Cleave]] is an excellent pickup. Since '''Overgorger''' must be placed up front anyway while scaling it, Cleave is effectively like giving the unit {{IconLink|Sweep}} and {{IconLink|Quick}} if it can be safely cast every turn through {{IconLink|Keepstone}}. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! It has the highest base {{Attack}} and {{Health}} of any unit, at the cost of being the biggest individual unit in the game, costing a great amount of {{Ember}}, and possessing inherent {{IconLink|Emberdrain}}. == Strategy== '''Shadowsiege''' is an unwieldy card that is difficult to get into play, requiring a lot of effort to build around. While it has tremendous stats, it provides no utility at all, and requires {{IconLink|Trample}} or {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, such as from [[Umbra Stone]] and [[Furnace Tap]], to make proper use of its stats. It also falls off in later rings, as its impressive {{Attack}} still fails to overcome the frontline tanks of Ring 7 and beyond without support. Playing this unit requires jumping through hoops. First, you will need at least {{Capacity|6}} on a floor. This can be accomplished with [[Heaven's Light]], [[Bogwurm's Growth]], a [[Deployable]] [[Crucible Extension]], or, if played after the Deployment Phase, cards like [[Space Prism]] or [[Renovate]]. Its {{Ember|4}} cost will deplete your entire supply of {{DeploymentEmber}}, unless you have either [[Hell's Flame]], [[Herzal's Horde]], or a {{DeploymentEmber}} artifact like [[Artificial Pyrestone]]. [[Volatile Gauge]] is guaranteed to reduce its initial cost, but its innate {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} can be even more of a burden with this artifact. If playing '''Shadowsiege''' after the Deployment Phase, [[Perils of Production]] with {{IconLink|Twinstone}} will provide enough {{Ember}} to pay for it, and if given {{IconLink|Keepstone}} as well you can ignore its {{IconLink|Emberdrain}}. [[Prism Retrieval]] can draw it and reduce its cost while scaling it slightly, while using [[Kindle]] or casting [[Shroud Spike]] on a [[Rubble Morsel]] can provide plenty of {{Ember}}. [[Ancient Pyretap]] will let you play the card at any time at the cost of {{PyreHealth|4}}, which is typically worth it. Its {{IconLink|Emberdrain|3}} should be managed via [[Perils of Production]], if possible; having this card makes '''Shadowsiege''' much more pickable. Without it, it will effectively cost you a whopping {{Ember|10}} over the first three turns it's in combat. It is possible to bypass its {{Capacity}} limitations with forced deployment effects such as [[Sketches of Salvation]], though you will need to purge units and have no control over the floor this unit is deployed on. Note that Sketches of Salvation always deploys from the bottom floor up, so if your only available unit is '''Shadowsiege''', it will always be played on the bottom floor. You can place '''Shadowsiege''' in a [[Jack in the Box]], and this is generally the best way of playing multiple copies of it, but that requires having multiple copies of '''Shadowsiege''' before you get the event, which is not usually advisable. Also, keep in mind that if you are taking '''Shadowsiege''' because you need to master it for the Logbook, then putting it in a Jack in the Box will '''not''' count as mastering it. Its {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} means you will still have to pay for it partially even when cheating it out. Due to its size, it can be difficult to combo this unit with support and scaling units like [[Primordium]] or units with {{IconLink|Enchant}}, so it is advisable to use spells or equipment-based scaling plans. {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} can act as a tanking solution due to this unit's high {{Attack}} and will often work better than other defensive options; [[Immortal Trade]] can allow it to trade blows with bosses and leverage its high {{Health}} better than most units, and fits well in the {{IconLink|Emberdrain}}-based builds where '''Shadowsiege''' thrives. Alternatively, upgrading it with {{IconLink|Smidgestone}} can allow it to be placed alongside support units with significantly less fuss, and means that only its {{Ember}} cost remains a problem. [[Shield of Wyngh]] is expensive and only available with the [[Banished]], but makes '''Shadowsiege''' significantly more useful, as its tremendous {{Health|250}} can be leveraged to annihilate backliners and put a significant chunk in heavies. This goes double if you can keep its {{Health}} topped up with {{IconLink|Lifesteal}}. [[Cavendish]] is unreliable as it may break right when you require it, but if it happens to stick around, '''Shadowsiege''' gets {{Attack|750}}, enough to slay an [[Avowed Gladiator]] in a single blow and returning it to the glory days of the original game. Overall, '''Shadowsiege''' requires a lot of investment to play and will tend to warp runs around itself. If you can leverage it properly, you can reap the benefits of its gigantic base stats; if not, it will just be a dead draw. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! I can only hope this will not be the case aboard the train. |artist = Andres Olvera }} '''Mine Collapse''' is an [[Umbra]] spell. It deals 3X damage to a single unit, then gives {{Ember|2}} if its target dies. == Strategy == '''Mine Collapse''' provides targeted spot removal of weak backline enemy units and gives an {{Ember}} boost too to let you play some more cards after it. This can be situationally useful and a reasonably helpful card through the early-to-midgame. It will require you to plan your turn around spending {{Ember}} before and after playing it in an efficient way. It's all about the first 3-6 damage with this card - you'll generally want to play it for {{Ember|1-2}} or {{Ember|0}} once it has a damage upgrade, making it {{Ember}}-positive in the best case. It also has utility in killing friendly units that want to die like [[:Category:Imp units|Imps]]. With a damage upgrade, it's reasonably easy to use and useful in a deck that applies {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} to friendly units, such as {{IconLink|Keepstone}} [[Perils of Production]] engines and ones making use of [[Furnace Tap]], [[Immortal Trade]], and [[Void Binding]]. In those decks you can play this at the start of the turn, when you have no {{Ember}} and gain {{Ember|2}} provided you have a suitable victim. In a pinch, this could even be given a {{IconLink|Keepstone}} to make a worse [[Perils of Production]] engine. If you're relying on having an enemy target, however, this is very unreliable, as you may not have a unit you can kill. In particular, in the [[Heaven%27s_Maw#Harbinger of Entropy|Harbinger of Entropy]] fight, only the [[Deafening Herald]]s that occasionally spawn are reasonably going to in this spell's kill range. You'd need your {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} and {{Ember|0}}spells to be strong enough to mostly carry the day, with this spell providing the ability to occasionally have {{Ember}} in a few key situations. You could target a friendly unit in a pinch here, though this would require you to have an expendable unit that either survived from last turn or was played with no {{Ember}} this turn. The [[Abandoned Antumbra]] artifact can provide this, granting a free [[Morsel]] every turn. Other than {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} strategies, this doesn't really play into any grander strategies - it's not a good spell to cast for large values of X, as its damage rate isn't remotely efficient, and since it drains all your {{Ember}} on play, you can't use its {{Ember}} boost to amass tons of {{Ember}} for a different X cost card. It's simply a situationally useful card that becomes less so as the run goes on. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Upgrade !! It provides a large amount of {{Ember}} immediately, and the {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} can be avoided by simply playing it on a [[Morsel]], which will be {{IconLink|Eaten}} before the {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} can do anything. But its true strength only becomes apparent once it is given a {{IconLink|Keepstone}}, allowing it to be drawn every turn. At this point, it can be played on any unit, as the {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} will no longer matter: you can simply start each turn by playing '''Perils of Production''', which will supply all the {{Ember}} you need. {{IconLink|Twinstone}} can be used to double the amount of {{IconLink|Rage}} and {{IconLink|Ember}} it grants. This also frees you to take other cards, such as [[Immortal Trade]], [[Void Binding]] and [[Furnace Tap]], which provide powerful effects at the cost of applying {{IconLink|Emberdrain}}. With all of your {{Ember}} coming from '''Perils of Production''', the downside of these spells becomes irrelevant. By the time the boss arrives, you will often have hundreds of {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} on your units, but it doesn't matter when '''Perils of Production''' still gives you {{Ember|3-6}} each turn. {{IconLink|Slay}}: Add '''2''' uncommon or rare Morsel units to your hand. |flavor = As the first line of defense in the Crucible, Morsels will rocket towards an intruder, often sacrificing themselves in the process. If they succeed in their defense, they live to mine another day. |artist = Ali Hosseinkhan }} '''Antumbra Assault''' is an [[Umbra]] spell. It provides [[Morsels]] when used to kill a target. == Strategy == '''Antumbra Assault''' is a solid spell early on, but falls off later. It is generally a better version of [[Plink]] beyond the first two rings, as it provides two Morsels per {{IconLink|Slay}} and you can choose its target. The Umbra can sometimes struggle with backline clear, and this spell covers most of your needs up until Ring 6. It makes a decent source of Morsels, but should not be relied on for that purpose. It can be used to kill [[Collector]]s throughout all Rings even without upgrades. It will also kill [[Ragewing Assassin]]s, which are dangerous to Umbra due to having {{IconLink|Sweep}}, but it cannot scratch [[Chosen Assassin]]s if you are facing [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]]. It also needs upgrades to kill [[Deafening Herald]]s, [[Enthralled Ardent]]s, and [[Deformed Duo]]s, and is largely helpless against [[Purified Soul]]s, [[Discordant Heretic]]s, [[Cael, Lord of the Cherubs|Cael's Cherubs]], and all Chosen backliners. Aside from killing enemies, it can also be used to kill your own units. For example, it can kill off {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Imps]] and free up space to play the Morsels it generates, or you can use it to kill a weak [[Rubble Morsel]] in order to hopefully get ones of higher quality. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! Draw a unit and apply {{Attack|+5X}} and {{Ember|-X}}. |flavor = Prism stones have the unique ability to refract both light and space, providing protection and creating matter from nothing. I've been able to reverse engineer this power to transport objects and beings across small distances. |artist = Jordan Thomas }} '''Prism Retrieval''' is an [[Umbra]] spell. It spends all of the player's ember and draws a random unit from their deck, reducing its cost by 1 {{Ember}} and increasing its {{Attack}} by 5 for each ember spent. ==Strategy== '''Prism Retrieval''' is essentially a worse version of [[Channelsong]]: it requires {{Ember|4}} just to apply the same amount of {{Attack}} that Channelsong applies with {{Ember|1}}, it doesn't apply {{Health}}, and instead of setting the unit's cost to {{Ember|0}} it decreases it by the amount paid. This means that it essentially gives no discount at all: in order to play a {{Ember|3}} unit, you must pay {{Ember|3}} to draw it using '''Prism Retrieval'''. This is especially bad if you have multiple units with different costs in your deck, as the random unit chosen may either cost less than your current {{Ember}} (in which case the extra {{Ember}} is essentially wasted, only giving {{Attack|5}} per {{Ember}}) or more than your current {{Ember}} (in which case you cannot play the unit until the next shuffle, because you just spent all of your {{Ember}} to draw it). Still, '''Prism Retrieval''''s competition is in other clans (and are Rares). If you have a specific non-banner unit which you want to draw consistently, or a banner unit which you cannot afford to play during the [[Deployment Phase]], then it can be worth taking '''Prism Retrieval''' and adding {{IconLink|Seekstone}} to guarantee that you can play it on the first turn, as well as giving a {{Ember|1}} discount. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Feast:
{{SpellCard |name = Feast |image = CRD_Feast.png |clan = [[Umbra]] |rarity = Uncommon |cost = 0 |effect = Trigger feeding on friendly units with {{IconLink|Eaten}}. |flavor = Gorgers patrol the mines to collect errant Morsels, consuming them to return them back to the Shroud. They take great pleasure in their purpose, often consuming more Morsels than necessary. |artist = Brian Mutschler }} '''Feast''' is an [[Umbra]] spell. It causes all units with {{IconLink|Eaten}} on its floor to be eaten immediately. == Strategy == '''Feast''' allows you to bypass the typical drawback of [[Morsels]], which is that they are only eaten at the end of combat. This card keeps Morsels safe from {{IconLink|Spikes}} and {{IconLink|Sweep}}, and can let you to eat more Morsels than you would otherwise on a standard turn, in which you are limited both by {{Capacity}} and the floor limit of seven units. If you can play this spell reliably and have strong Morsel generation, this can allow Morsels to function as a better lategame scaling option. It will also trigger {{IconLink|Gorge}} effects before combat, which is usually a minor benefit but can still be impactful. For example, it can grant [[Crucible Warden]] stacks of {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} before combat begins, potentially protecting it from death. [[Shadoweater]] is likely the greatest beneficiary; its area of effect damage on {{IconLink|Gorge}} makes casting '''Feast''' essentially like giving the unit {{IconLink|Quick}}, killing off enemy units before combat can begin. If you are using Shadoweater as backline removal against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]], this card is practically a necessity, as it is otherwise extremely difficult to protect Morsels against [[Ragewing Assassin]]s and [[Chosen Assassin]]s, and Umbra does not have many other options for removing these exceptionally dangerous enemies. When using [[Primordium]], this card is generally much better. All three paths can benefit from consuming Primordium faster, but '''Stalwart Snack''' in particular struggles with using all of its {{IconLink|Buffet}} stacks over the course of a normal battle, so the acceleration is extremely useful. With '''Aggressive Edible''', you can bring your damage scaling online much faster (especially if you can bring Primordium back with [[Retch]]). '''Superfood''' requires you to stack your status effects up quickly (perhaps with the use of {{IconLink|Seekstone}}), but if you can manage that then this card can ensure Primordium is fully eaten before too many harmful [[Debuff]]s can be applied, like {{IconLink|Sap}} or {{IconLink|Corruption}}. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! It requires a friendly unit to be killed, but gives you three [[Morsels]] chosen from the uncommon or rare pool. == Strategy == '''Cannibalize''' is very similar to [[Packed Morsels]], with three differences. It costs {{Ember|1}} rather than {{Ember|0}}, it requires a friendly unit to be killed, and it does not '''[[Consume]]'''. Only the third of these is generally beneficial, which means that it is of limited use unless you were unable to find Packed Morsels and desperately need Morsel production. Nevertheless, Packed Morsels, because of its [[Common]] rarity, is unavailable outside of starting with them, Rings 1 or 2, or the occasional [[Gremlin Looter]], so if you're on Ring 3 or later and need Morsels, this is probably the best source you'll find. [[Gem Trove]] provides the same amount of Morsels, but is significantly more expensive. The '''[[Sacrifice]]''' effect can sometimes be useful. It can clear out less useful Morsels to make space, although this requires you to draw this card along with another source of Morsels. It can also kill unwanted units like [[Spear Steward]] to clear up space and your deck, though this is a limited and very situational use. It can be very good with units which want to die but have high {{Health}}, especially a [[Greed Dragon]] with {{IconLink|Endless}}, or which can be awkward to kill off like [[Welder Helper]]. However, the Umbra themselves rarely have units which want to be sacrificed, so this is dependent on your allied clan. == Interactions == * When effects like '''Cannibalize''' try to add more cards to hand than fit into the hand size limit of 10, then those excess cards are not generated. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Ember Cache:
{{SpellCard |name = Ember Cache |image = CRD_EmberCache.png |clan = [[Umbra]] |rarity = Uncommon |cost = 1 |effect = '''[[Consume]]'''.
Add '''3''' '''[[Excavated Ember]]''' cards to your discard pile. |flavor = I created fortified steel boxes to house the dormant Ember mined in the Crucible, increasing its effectiveness through pressure and time. |artist = Zihao Luo }} '''Ember Cache''' is an [[Umbra]] spell. It adds 3 copies of [[Excavated Ember]] to your discard pile. It is one of four [[Umbra]] spells offered by the [[Gremlin Looter]] event. == Strategy == Most of the time, '''Ember Cache''' trades {{Ember|1}} and a card on your first shuffle into a net of {{Ember|6}} on your second. (The [[Excavated Ember]] card created are draw neutral and provide {{Ember|2}}.) For runs that can capitalize on this, this is a strong value trade, and the [[Umbra]] have several ways of taking advantage: * X cost cards like [[Shroud Spike]] * Expensive cards like [[Gem Trove]] * [[Excavated Ember]] allows you to have {{Ember}} on turns where {{IconLink|Emberdrain}} would shut you down It does require a streamlined deck to consistently reach its full potential, both because this lets you reach its payoff faster and so that you're consistently drawing [[Excavated Ember]] with cards that can make use of the extra {{Ember}}. So it'll be at its best in the lategame. It's worth noting you might bottom-deck this card, drawing it and then shuffling your discard into your draw pile. In that case you aren't getting [[Excavated Ember]] until your 3rd cycle through the deck, which is usually too late unless your deck is highly streamlined. It has a lot of value when partnered with the [[Underlegion]], specifically with [[Morel Mistress]] and [[Madame Lionsmane]]'s '''Everbloom''' path. Both cards have {{IconLink|Etch}} triggers, and '''Ember Cache''' will activate those triggers four times total for the cost of a single draft. If you are able to thin your deck down drastically with [[The Great Decay]], you can quickly draw and play all the Excavated Embers. While [[Ember Cache]] can be nice for many non-Umbra runs from [[Gremlin Looter]], it's only one of four things you could get. [[Prismal Dust]] and [[Space Prism]] are two others that can fit in some runs outside [[Umbra]], but [[Packed Morsels]] is also a possibility - a card that generally isn't interesting in a non-Umbra run. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! Cave In:
{{SpellCard |name = Cave In |image = CRD_CaveIn.png |clan = [[Umbra]] |rarity = Uncommon |cost = 2 |effect = '''[[Descend]]''' all units. |flavor = I've only seen the aftermath, but when a level of the Crucible collapses, very few Morsels survive. The Umbra don't even care to check for survivors, choosing instead to spawn new Morsels. |artist = Cameron Archer }} '''Cave In''' is an [[Umbra]] spell. It [[Descend]]s all units on the current floor, including both friendly and enemy units. == Strategy == '''Cave In''' is a somewhat situational card, unlike most Descend or Ascend spells. Because it affects all units, it cannot be used to move flying bosses away from your important floors, and it cannot single out specific targets. It ''can'' be used to overstack a single floor by putting units on both that floor and the floor above, though keep in mind that it will be impossible to play [[Morsels]] there afterwards. Since it is generally more useful to overstack lower floors than higher floors in this game, it can be a very efficient card for this purpose. Clans like the [[Stygian Guard]] and [[Luna Coven]] can especially benefit from this. Alternatively, it can be used to collapse a group of Morsels onto a full floor, or to repeatedly send enemies back down to a kill floor if you are unable to finish them off in a single turn. These strategies, however, are very niche, due to the spell's high cost and the necessity of {{IconLink|Keepstone}} in order to play it consistently. Especially with [[Primordium]], it is often beneficial for the Umbra to set up on higher floors in order to scale up before enemy waves can arrive. However, nearly every miniboss in the game punishes you for playing on upper floors, usually through powerful {{IconLink|Resolve}} effects; [[Rax the Overblessed]] is the quintessential example, being an absolute horror if he is allowed to reach the top floor. '''Cave In''' can save you in this instance by bringing your main floor down to the boss, rather than letting them climb. If you care about score, this can also allow you to kill bosses as soon as they spawn, or to force flying bosses to stay on your main floor for early kills. == Notes == If either side of the floor below the '''Cave In''' already contains too many units, only the frontmost units will descend, up to the maximum of 7 units on the floor below. This can potentially expose more fragile backline enemies, though there will usually not be any units left to kill them. However, once isolated you can take them out with spells like [[Excavation Eruption]] or [[Blazing Bolts]]. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! Grovel:
{{SpellCard |name = Grovel |image = CRD_Grovel.png |clan = [[Umbra]] |rarity = Uncommon |cost = 2 |effect = Apply {{IconLink|Damage Shield|1}}. Add '''2''' uncommon or rare Morsel units to your hand. |flavor = Some errant Morsels, in an effort to please the Wardens, will offer their valuable jewels to try and get in their good graces. This behavior has been noted for future bribes that occur within the Boneshaker. |artist = Cameron Archer }} '''Grovel''' is an [[Umbra]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Damage Shield|1}} to a unit and adds two [[Morsels]] from the "uncommon or rare" pool. See [[Morsels]] for Morsel probabilities. == Strategy == '''Grovel''' is very similar to [[Gem Trove]], with a slightly weaker effect in exchange for costing slightly less. The {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} it applies only goes to a single unit, which makes it worse against effects that threaten the whole floor like {{IconLink|Sweep}} or the {{IconLink|Corruption}} applied by [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]], but is otherwise usually sufficient if your backline is not under threat. It also provides only two Morsels instead of three. If you are purely looking to increase your Morsel density, this is usually a drawback, but if you find yourself lacking the {{Capacity}} to play all three Morsels or if the {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} is more valuable to you, then this may be an advantage instead. Even if you are looking for more Morsels, there are not many spells that can provide Morsels that are available after Ring 2, so this may be the best that you can find. With the [[Abyssal Prism]], '''Grovel''' will produce two Morsels for each unit on the floor, up to your maximum hand size. It deals 25 damage to a random enemy three times, granting {{Ember|2}} for each enemy it kills. == Strategy == '''Excavation Eruption''' can be an effective pick in the early game, often killing one or more low-{{Health}} enemies like [[Savage Spearman]] or [[Ominous Acolyte]] and refunding part of its own cost. With luck, it might even create more {{Ember}} than it costs. Its high damage also means that even if it hits a bulky enemy like [[Fallen Champion]] or [[Flagellant]], it will dent them significantly. In the late game, however, it is almost useless. Its random targeting means that it will often hit tanky enemies like [[Avowed Gladiator]], dealing negligible damage despite its high cost. Even with upgrades, it rarely deals significant damage to such enemies without high {{IconLink|Conduit}} or another way to massively increase its damage. Additionally, even if it does hit the right enemies, many of the low-{{Health}} backliners in the later rings have ways of surviving being struck, such as the {{IconLink|Reanimate}} on [[Deformed Duo]]s or the {{IconLink|Spell Shield}} on [[Purified Soul]]s. It does have a small niche in the lategame with the right upgrades, as it can be played in the Pyre Room to hit [[Dominion]] during [[Clash with the Titans]]. Since it hits three times, it will either clear three stacks of his {{IconLink|Spell Shield|4}}, or if you can clear the {{IconLink|Spell Shield}} beforehand (perhaps by playing [[Plink]]s), it will often deal enough damage to kill him one turn sooner. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! It gives you twice the {{Ember}} you spend on it. == Strategy == This spell can provide massive amounts of {{Ember}}, though it can be hard to leverage the amount of {{Ember}} generated. If your run was built to run with a certain amount of {{Ember}}, it's hard for it to take advantage of twice that amount for one turn, especially down one card, making this card's use not immediately apparent. (It can be semi-reliably good with [[Volatile Gauge]], as you're unlikely to be able to afford your whole hand there too.) This card's main use is to empower other X-cost cards. This card essentially doubles the amount you can spend on another X-cost card you have in hand. Of course, you need to draw it with another X-cost card to be able to do this. You'll need upgrades and/or a small deck to be able to make this consistent. You can add {{IconLink|Twinstone}} and duplicate the card to amass a truly absurd amount of {{Ember}} - just be mindful that 99 is the cap! The Umbra do have a fair number of X-cost cards, but there is one card among them in particular that stands out as a companion to this card - [[Shroud Spike]]. The reason is that this card, more than the rest, is able to capitalize on a very large value of X by making one of your units proportionally large. The rest have an effect that tends to have more sharply diminishing returns with X (though perhaps you could hit a boss with a particularly large [[Forever Consumed]], or make a strong unit with [[Prism Retrieval]]). The other [[:Category:Railspike|Railspikes]] are all potentially good candidates to pair this card with as well, as all of them can be exceptionally strong given enough {{Ember}}, and you'll have access to one other Railspike through your partner clan. It allows your frontmost unit to eat a target [[Morsel]] unit 2X times, triggering {{IconLink|Eaten}} and {{IconLink|Gorge}} that many times. It is the Umbra offering for the [[Railspikes (event)|Railspikes]] event. However, due to its usage being linked to Morsels, it can only be found from this event if you are already playing with the Umbra. == Strategy == '''Shroud Spike''' can be a build-defining card, as it takes one of the [[Umbra]] clan's strengths - namely, generating large amounts of {{IconLink|Ember}} - and uses it to address one of their main weaknesses - namely, the difficulty of finding space for large amounts of Morsels to feed their units, and their slow scaling. With this card, one Morsel can be all it takes to scale your {{IconLink|Gorge}} unit to impressive heights quickly. Any build that creates and uses a respectable amount of Morsels should strongly consider this card when offered. If you have ample access to Morsels, this spell becomes very flexible, too: * [[Rubble Morsel]] makes this double as a [[Kindle]], providing {{Ember|2X}} ** This can be particularly strong if you have another [[Shroud Spike]] in hand, as you'll be able to play it for 2X {{Ember}}! This means that '''Shroud Spike''' can actually have excellent self-synergy if you still have good access to Rubble Morsels, despite being an X-cost card, making it a better duplication candidate than you might initially expect. * [[Morsel Miner]] is the best for raw stats, though [[Antumbra Morsel]] or [[Magma Morsel]] can suffice if you're particularly looking for either {{Health}} or {{Attack}}, respectively * [[Morsel Jeweler]] lets this double as a Doublestacked [[Prismal Dust]], stacking 2X {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} * [[Morsel Excavator]] lets you stack up 2X {{IconLink|Lifesteal}} As with any X-cost card, {{Ember}} generators like [[Perils of Production]], [[Ember Forge]], [[Engine Upgrade]], [[Boiler Room]], and the aforementioned [[Kindle]] pair well with this card. Make it a priority to go to a [[Merchant of Magic]] after picking this card up, as there are many different upgrades it can use well, and it's a great duplication target. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Any units which are {{IconLink|Eaten}}, including both [[Morsels]] and [[Primordium]], are placed in a separate Eaten Pile, and playing '''Retch''' will immediately put as many of these cards as possible back in your hand, up to the hand size limit of 10. Other cards will remain in the Eaten pile. == Strategy == '''Retch''' can take your [[Morsel]] game to another level, giving you potentially tons of high-value morsels in one play for {{Ember|0}}. With mass production of [[Morsels]], this card can easily fill your hand; it is advisable to only use it once you have cleared space in hand to hold and space on your train to play [[Morsels]]. Take care as to what goes into your Eaten pile if you're using this card, as the order of returned Morsels is random: if you have a lot of Morsel generation, you may want to let lesser Morsels, like [[Rubble Morsel]]s or one of [[Morsel Jeweler]] or [[Morsel Excavator]], die as chump blockers rather than eating them. (If you let one through, it's certainly possible to fix that the next time you play '''Retch'''.) You'll need a way of actually placing all these Morsels, of course, so you'll need lots of extra {{Capacity}}, [[Feast]], [[Morsel-Made]], or a combination of any of the above to help with this. [[Primordium]] can benefit massively from this spell, as '''Retch''' is the only in-clan way to return it to the battlefield to be eaten again. This often makes the '''Stalwart Snack''' path redundant, and is likely at its best with the '''Aggressive Edible''' path, which can be eaten quickly and provide its massive {{Attack}} boost again. This new card has all the same upgrades that the original did. This final card does not '''Purge''' but is just played normally. ==Interactions== * If '''Blazing Bolts''' in its first or second stages is generated and played mid-combat (e.g. with [[Large Mystery Box]], {{IconLink|Twinstone}}, [[Emot Tome]], [[Echo Vault]]), the stronger version created is '''NOT''' permanently added to your deck == Strategy == '''Blazing Bolts''' is a strong if somewhat unwieldy damage spell once it has entered its final phase. It is generally not difficult to get it to its final form, and will happen naturally over the course of one or two combats as long as you actually play the card. The randomness of the card's targeting is its biggest downside. 60 damage is enough to take out all backline enemies in one hit short of [[Chosen Sniper]]s and [[Chosen Ardent]]s, including dangerous foes like [[Chosen Assassin]]s and [[Holy Cherub]]s, but you have no guarantee when you play the spell that it will actually hit any of them. If it instead hits a tank or a boss, it will still deal significant damage, but it is virtually guaranteed to not actually kill them. With four hits and only one hit necessary to remove a given backliner, the odds are not terrible, but one unlucky roll can doom your run. As such, it's often better off as a way to carve big chunks out of frontline tanks once the backliners have been removed by some other means (perhaps via [[Shadoweater]] or [[Inferno Room]]). With just one unit on the floor, it's a guaranteed 240 damage, just under half the {{Health}} of an [[Avowed Gladiator]] (and the same amount of damage as casting [[Forever Consumed]] with {{Ember|3}}, barring upgrades). This is more than virtually any other spell can manage, save for [[Attuned]] spells enhanced with {{IconLink|Conduit}}, and greatly reduces pressure on your damage units. Its {{Ember|3}} price tag is hefty, no doubt, but the Umbra have many ways of increasing {{Ember}} available, like [[Ember Forge]], [[Engine Upgrade]], [[Kindle]], or [[Perils of Production]]. In Rings 4-6, it is also much stronger, as the tanks in those rings have {{Health|180}} or less. This means at minimum, in waves with one tank protecting several backliners, you will always take out at least one backliner, and it's possible to kill the tank as well. If your deck is looking weak into the midgame, this may be a necessary pick after the first boss to survive. '''Blazing Bolts''' specifically synergizes very well with the spellcasting clans, the [[Stygian Guard]] and [[Luna Coven]]. The Luna Coven can use {{IconLink|Conduit}} to drastically increase this spell's already solid damage output, letting it demolish tanks just as easily as backliners, and if you make it [[Attuned]] via [[Silver Ink]] it can even shred bosses. The Stygian Guard can instead apply {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} to multiply its output. Two of its best sources, [[Icy Cilophyte]] and '''Handheld Totem''' [[Tethys]], even pull double duty thanks to their {{IconLink|Sweep}}, clearing out backline units while applying {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}} to the tanks to set up a devastating blow. Its utility against the [[Clash with the Titans|Titans]] fluctuates. The presence of [[Entropy]] on every floor means it is very hard to use '''Blazing Bolts''' for waveclear, as you're almost guaranteed to have some of the hits strike Entropy instead of their intended targets. However, it is quite strong against [[Dominion]], whose low {{Health}} and isolation in the Pyre Room makes him uniquely vulnerable to this spell. Although he starts with {{IconLink|Spell Shield|4}}, the first time you cast '''Blazing Bolts''' all four stacks will be removed, and every time after that will damage him badly. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! '''Glutton's Maw''' is an rare [[Umbra]] equipment card added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. Its '''Chomp''' ability lets the equipped unit "eat" any friendly unit in the game, even units without the {{IconLink|Eaten}} keyword.

== Strategy ==
'''Glutton's Maw''' provides decent scaling, so long as you can provide a unit to be eaten every turn. It provides 75% of the {{Attack}} and {{Health}} granted by [[Overgrowth Carapace]] and [[Stasis Crystal]] per turn for the same {{Ember|2}} cost, but in exchange it has a far more forgiving drawback, and one that is often more useful than painful. It is generally better used when your units have strong keywords, such as {{IconLink|Sweep}} and {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, but need help scaling their stats. Units with {{IconLink|Gorge}} also appreciate this equipment greatly. [[Shadoweater]], for example, can immediately trigger its area of effect damage, potentially removing problematic backliners like [[Ragewing Assassin]]s.

Although you can use the equipment to feed exclusively on [[Morsels]], its real strength is letting you kill off other minor units whose deaths are beneficial, such as [[Imps]], [[Tombs]], and [[Assistants]]. For example, you could equip '''Glutton's Maw''' to '''Brawler''' [[Hornbreaker Prince]] alongside an {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Fledgling Imp]], granting him {{Attack|+15}}, {{Health|+15}}, and {{IconLink|Rage|5}} every turn to use alongside his {{IconLink|Multistrike|4}}.

It can also clear out unwanted units to make space, allowing Stewards to be played in order to get them out of your deck without preventing you from playing Morsels afterwards. '''Architect''' [[Penumbra]] can be placed in order to increase {{Capacity}} and then eaten to clear out the {{Capacity|3}} it occupies.

However, without either a steady stream of Morsels for a strong {{IconLink|Gorge}} unit or useful sacrificial units, the scaling provided by this equipment will disappoint. If you are desperate for scaling, you can upgrade a cheap unit with {{IconLink|Immortalstone}} or put {{IconLink|Keepstone}} on a [[Shadesplitter]], guaranteeing at least one {{IconLink|Gorge}} proc per turn.

One interesting use of '''Glutton's Maw''' is on [[Primordium]]. At its baseline, it can be used to scale Primordium's raw {{Attack}} and {{Health}} relatively quickly, which is especially useful on the '''Stalwart Snack''' path. Those stats will then be passed onto whatever unit eats Primordium multiple times. If you can use the equipment three turns in a row, Primordium will have gained {{AttackHealth|+45|+45}}, but the unit eating it will have gained {{AttackHealth|+90|+90}}. Additionally, since these are real stat changes, they will be preserved if you replay Primordium via {{IconLink|Endless}} or [[Retch]]. When eating a Morsel unit, Primoridum will also gain any additional stats and effects granted by its {{IconLink|Eaten}} trigger.

Interestingly, eating a non-Morsel unit with '''Glutton's Maw''' counts as a {{IconLink|Slay}} trigger. This makes it a consistent way to trigger {{IconLink|Slay}} on certain units that can sometimes struggle to do so, such as [[Branded Warrior]], [[Hornbreaker Prince]]'s '''Wrathful''' path, and [[Bolete the Guillotine]]'s '''Headsman''' path. It can also be merged with {{IconLink|Slay}} equipment like [[Heph's Hammer]] and [[Organ Harvester]] for additional procs.

== Strategy ==
'''Crucible Extension''' a way to greatly increase a floor's {{Capacity}} to fit wider units or lines of [[Morsels]]. '''Melting Remnant''' [[File:ClanMeltingRemnant.png|20x20px]] is a [[clan]]  in [[Monster Train 2]], returning from [[Monster Train 1]]. It is unlocked after unlocking [[Hellhorned]] first and then Reanimating or Reforming 50 Units.

The clan is comprised of monsters made entirely from wax. They appear to be candle-like in design, with some having wicks atop their heads.

Melting Remnant features the following mechanics:
* Many units have {{IconLink|Burnout}}, which is a buff that decreases each turn. Once the counter reaches 0, the unit dies. The clan offers many ways to increase {{IconLink|Burnout}}.
* The clan prominently features a unique '''[[Reform]]''' mechanic. Dead units in the consume pile can be reformed, adding their card back into your hand. Reformed units get {{Attack|+5}}, {{Health|+5}}, {{Ember|0}} and {{IconLink|Burnout|1}}. These changes last until the end of battle.
* Some of the clan's units, particularly the '''[[:Category:Tomb_units|Tombs]]''', feature {{IconLink|Extinguish}} triggers and are designed to die. Other units take advantage of these deaths with {{IconLink|Harvest}} triggers.
* The clan features ways of generating {{Gold}}.
* The clan has a few sources of {{IconLink|Stealth}}, a defensive buff that protects your units from attack.

The clan's unique [[Merchant of Steel]] Upgrade is {{IconLink|Wickstone}}.

==Strategy==
Successful Melting Remnant decks tend to make use of the {{IconLink|Burnout}} and Reform mechanics to stack boosts onto their units and exponentially increase their damage and survivability.

It is worth noting that {{IconLink|Eaten}} units do not trigger {{IconLink|Harvest}} and are not added to the consume pile to be reformed if they are eaten.

==Strategy==
It says a lot about the Melting Remnant deck that '''Rector Flicker''' is not its most powerful champion, because he is extraordinarily powerful, quite able to carry a run down all three of his paths with minimal set-up. He can be specced as a support tank or an offensive one, but either way he is capable of taking damage and handing a lot of it back out, taking up only 2 {{Capacity}} as a bonus. All three upgrade paths for '''Rector Flicker''' require specific strategies to take full advantage of their strengths while covering their weaknesses.

===Burn Bright===
The highest priority with '''Burn Bright''' is keeping '''Flicker''' from [[Burnout|burning out]] while allowing his incredible stats to win fights.

'''Burn Bright''' is the most risky of the three choices as a first upgrade. It makes '''Flicker''' powerful enough to take on almost anything you'll encounter early on, but unless you have certain extra starter cards you won't have any way to keep him alive long enough to fight the boss, nor reform him. And unlike in Monster Train 1, on Covenants 1+, even Ring 1 bosses have enough {{Health}} to tank 3 hits from him, so if you don't have any way to help him stay alive you may be in for a short run if you don't have other ways of dealing with the boss. [[Lady of the Reformed]], [[Hallowed Drippings]], and [[Molded]], which either apply additional stacks of {{IconLink|Burnout}} or allow you to Reform, make this line pickable early on. If you only have a few cards that can Reform, try to get a {{IconLink|Freezestone}} or {{IconLink|Keepstone}} for one of them so that it can be saved for immediate use when '''Flicker''' burns out.

In the late game, '''Burn Bright''' is a powerhouse, allowing a properly supported and buffed '''Rector Flicker''' to make an excellent tank while {{IconLink|Burnout}} becomes increasingly easy to manage. The [[Resin Blades]] equipment is practically a must-take for him, as he benefits hugely from its {{IconLink|Multistrike}} and will not die often, so you will not be forced to replay it. Generally speaking, you'll either take all three levels of '''Burn Bright''' or none at all, as the aggressive, sacrifice-focused strategy conflicts with the conservative, buff-focused strategy of the other two builds, and the costs of the path are entirely in the first upgrade.

===Accumulator===
The highest priority if you pick '''Accumulator''' for '''Rector Flicker''' is to create as much death as possible on whatever floor you put him on. {{IconLink|Sweep}} units and glass cannons go great with this path, hiding behind his high {{Health}} while providing kills to make him stronger. Also, pack the front of the floor with quick-dying units that have low health or {{IconLink|Burnout}}. [[Funguy]] are particularly noteworthy in this role, as every stack of {{IconLink|Troop}} lost will trigger {{IconLink|Harvest}}. Consider applying a {{IconLink|Wickstone}} to units without {{IconLink|Burnout}}, especially [[:Category:Tomb units|Tombs]], in order to increase turnover.

If you have enough room or are confident in your ability to protect the Pyre, putting a [[Wickless Tycoon]] on the same floor with '''Flicker''' can allow you to benefit from deaths in the long term as well as the short term by providing {{Gold}} with every death. However, this comes with the drawback of taking up space which could potentially have been spent packing the room with more expendable defenders.

When available, it can be useful to combine '''Accumulator''' with one level of '''Dark Calling''' in order to gain more expendable units which will eventually die from {{IconLink|Burnout}}, as well as creating the offensive capacity to maximize the number of enemy units dying on '''Flicker''''s floor. This will slightly reduce your ability to {{IconLink|Harvest}} heavily compared to another level of '''Accumulator''', but the trade is usually worthwhile given that it largely mitigates the loss of {{IconLink|Harvest}} power while also providing you with a steady supply of increasingly powerful cannon fodder to block hits and deal damage with when the boss arrives.

[[Equalizing Rings]] is an equipment to look out for this line, as he may be the biggest beneficiary of its effect due to his titanic potential {{Health}}. Without Equalizing Rings, his damage output at all levels is worse than [[Wickless Baron]], and he cannot be upgraded with {{IconLink|Multistrike}} or duplicated, so you will need an alternative plan to deal with heavies.

===Dark Calling===
The highest priority with '''Dark Calling''' is keeping your [[Consume]] pile well-stocked with dead units for '''Flicker''' to [[Reform]]. Unlike with most builds for any champion, when using '''Dark Calling''' it is preferable to put units out early and get them into fights even if they will die without dealing damage, because Reforming will get them back into your hand in better than new condition. 

'''Rector Flicker''' should generally be in a safe position, such as near the top back, because if your build relies on his ability to Reform units, the only unit he cannot Reform is himself. Everyone else is expendable; he is not. If you choose to put him on the top, make sure you have a plan to put units in front of him, as otherwise flying bosses and the [[Titans]] can doom your run.

Usually, '''Cryptcall''' has no effect on the first turn of combat, as nothing will have died yet. However, if you can leverage spells like [[Subsuming Blade]] to kill your own units before combat, you can activate '''Cryptcall''' and immediately get them back with bolstered {{Attack}}. Alternatively, the {{IconLink|Worthy Sacrifice}} upgrade from the [[Inscryption]] event allows you to kill a unit, gain {{Ember|3}}, activate '''Cryptcall''' to get it back, and then make full use of the unit every turn. Done this way, '''Dark Calling''' can be a fairly consistent scaling method as long as you keep your Reform pool thin. [[Bloated Whelp]] can do something similar, since it also has an ability that lets it die instantly, but unfortunately its stats are quite low and it lacks other useful traits.

'''Dark Calling''' pairs well with {{IconLink|Extinguish}}, {{IconLink|Harvest}}, and {{IconLink|Burnout}} cards, allowing two more sacrificial creatures to be made available every turn, as well as increasing their power and {{IconLink|Burnout}} time. 

One way to build this route is part of a mass-Reform engine. If you go this route, it is recommended not to remove the [[Dreg|Dregs]] from your deck, because their low health, small size, high base damage, and {{IconLink|Burnout}} make them ideal fodder for Reforming, and by the time a boss arrives even Dregs can be quite dangerous. Consider adding cards that provide even more, such as [[Molded]] or [[Sacred Wicks]] - the former being quite useful for making sure you can always access a particular Reform target as needed. If '''Flicker''' is your only Reform source, you may be at the mercy of the RNG when it comes to finding specific units. [[Memorial Fund]] and [[Wickless Tycoon]] are also extremely valuable for such a deck, since units will be dying constantly and produce vast amounts of money. Putting '''Rector Flicker''' in a [[Hall of Mirrors]] allows you to double his Reform.

It is advisable if using this approach to upgrade a card like [[Hallowed Drippings]] or [[Waxen Spike]] with {{IconLink|Freezestone}}. If your Reform pool is too large, individual units are unlikely to build up significant amounts of {{IconLink|Burnout}}, which can result in them dying after only a turn or two during {{IconLink|Relentless}}. This can cause an otherwise-good run to spiral into a sudden loss. Having a source of floor-wide {{IconLink|Burnout}} extension in hand at all times minimizes the risk of losing this way.

Alternately, you could make a build that plans on having the same two units die over and over, such as with [[Crushing Demise]], to really focus your power on those two particular units. In this case you'll want to remove [[Dreg]]s and other non-essential units so that they don't eat your Reforms.

[[Bounty Stalker|Bounty Stalkers]] and [[Draff]]s are potentially good candidates for this, as they can die repeatedly in each battle and the increasing duration provided by Reform removes the drawback of only being able to attack bosses once if using {{IconLink|Wickstone}}. [[Resin Block]] can allow this to get particularly powerful.

Higher levels of '''Dark Calling''' simply increase the extra {{Attack}} gained by Reformed units. If this is not central to your strategy, it is often valuable to cross-path with '''Accumulator''' as a way to improve '''Rector Flicker''''s survivability.

{{UnitCard |name = Little Fade |image = PLR_LittleFade.png |clan = Melting Remnant |rarity = Champion |type = Champion |banner = No |cost = 0 |size = 1 |stats = 5/1 |flavor = For all that I've learned of these Exiles, it should be no surprise to me that the Exile of the Melting Remnant is a thieving child.
