To help with this, her starter card is [[Primitive Mold]], which '''[[Reform]]s''' a single unit chosen at random. == Light Forge Upgrades == {{ChampionPaths |baseStats=5/1 |a=Fire Light |a1stats=5/1 |a1abilities={{IconLink|Extinguish}}: Add {{AttackHealth|+5|+5}} and {{IconLink|Burnout|2}} to friendly units. |a2stats=5/1 |a2abilities={{IconLink|Extinguish}}: Add {{AttackHealth|+12|+5}} and {{IconLink|Burnout|2}} to friendly units. |a3stats=5/1 |a3abilities={{IconLink|Extinguish}}: Add {{AttackHealth|+20|+5}} and {{IconLink|Burnout|2}} to friendly units. |b=Eternal Flame |b1stats=5/1 |b1abilities={{IconLink|Quick}}. {{IconLink|Endless}}.
{{IconLink|Extinguish}}: {{AttackHealth|+15|+1}}. |b2stats=5/1 |b2abilities={{IconLink|Quick}}. {{IconLink|Endless}}.
{{IconLink|Extinguish}}: {{AttackHealth|+30|+2}}. |b3stats=5/1 |b3abilities={{IconLink|Quick}}. {{IconLink|Endless}}.
{{IconLink|Extinguish}}: {{AttackHealth|+60|+3}}. |c=Little Icarus |c1stats=5/1 |c1abilities={{IconLink|Spikes|7}}.
{{IconLink|Slay}}: Gain {{Attack|+2}} and {{IconLink|Spikes|2}} permanently. |c2stats=5/1 |c2abilities={{IconLink|Spikes|7}}.
{{IconLink|Slay}}: Gain {{Attack|+3}} and {{IconLink|Spikes|3}} permanently. |c3stats=5/1 |c3abilities={{IconLink|Spikes|7}}.
{{IconLink|Slay}}: Gain {{Attack|+4}} and {{IconLink|Spikes|4}} permanently. }} ==Strategy== '''Little Fade''' is probably the most uniquely-played champion in the game, being the only champion which demands frequent deaths. Her starter card, [[Primitive Mold]], draws from the '''[[Reform]]''' pile randomly, so it's typically quite important to ensure the Reform pile is thin so that '''Little Fade''' can be drawn every turn (with the exception of '''[[#Eternal Flame|Eternal Flame]]'''). This makes units such as [[Tombs]] more difficult to play, unless they are made {{IconLink|Endless}}. ===Fire Light=== '''Fire Light''' is [[Little Fade]]'s most straightforward path; play her at the front of your main floor, trying to get her killed every turn. It's notable that she supplies {{IconLink|Burnout}} to the entire floor when she dies, and not just units that already have {{IconLink|Burnout}}. This means she pairs excellently with [[Paraffin Enforcer]], who can now supply full-floor {{IconLink|Rage}} much more effectively. She also pairs well with units who already have {{IconLink|Burnout}}, such as [[Draff]] or [[Lady of the House]], whose incredible statlines are offset by their {{IconLink|Burnout}}. If you happen to be allied with the [[Lazarus League]], then stacking {{IconLink|Reanimate}} on Little Fade can allow her to buff her allies every time she loses a stack. This makes Fire Light a much stronger path, and can make Primitive Mold redundant. '''Fire Light''' can be paired with '''Eternal Flame I''' for {{IconLink|Endless}}, but this can make it hard for her to die repeatedly without {{IconLink|Burnout}}. Given you also forgo additional {{Attack}} scaling from '''Fire Light III''', it is generally better to tailor your deck to be able to consistently Reform her each turn. With a different source of {{IconLink|Endless}} like [[Votive Key]], you ideally want to apply it to '''Little Fade''' when she has exactly {{IconLink|Burnout|1}} to ensure she dies each turn. [[Memorial for the Melted]] can help with this, though if made '''[[Deployable]]''' she must be killed off-floor initially and then Reformed for {{IconLink|Burnout|1}}. The main challenge with this path is that you must kill and Reform '''Fade''' every turn, or at least for two turns in a row and then on most turns after that; the {{IconLink|Burnout}} she applies can kill your other units if she does not continue to apply more of it consistently. This means that you should avoid letting other units die, as doing so will clog up your Reform pile. Avoid playing [[Imps]], Tombs, [[Spear Steward]], [[Bloated Whelp]] or similar cards unless you can keep them alive or give them {{IconLink|Endless}}. As long as '''Little Fade''' is the only unit who is dead, [[Primitive Mold]] will always Reform her. [[Echo of the Time Father]] can also add some security against drawing all your Reform cards at once, as this Pyre can freeze them in hand and prevent them from being discarded, ensuring you can bring her back when necessary. The increased {{Health}} and {{IconLink|Burnout}} she gains with each Reform can also make her harder for enemies to kill, so it may be good to pick up spells which can be used to damage her. [[Subsuming Blade]] is a solid choice for this. It is possible to Reform her, kill her with a spell, and then Reform her again on the same turn. This can scale up your other units much faster. For the same reason she works well with the rare spell [[Hallowed Halls]], as long as you can consistently put her at the front of the floor after the random Reform. As she takes up {{Capacity|1}} but must die each turn before acting, she limits the number of units you can play on her floor. This makes [[Heaven's Light]] or [[Bogwurm's Growth]] very useful, and units with {{IconLink|Smidgestone}} are also a good choice. Overstacking is less helpful, as you will not have room to replay her once you have overstacked the floor. However, if allied with the [[Banished]], [[Rising Rage]] with {{IconLink|Keepstone}} can be used to move her to the front of an overstacked floor each turn. ===Eternal Flame=== '''Eternal Flame''' is likely [[Little Fade]]'s most consistent path; play her at the front of bottom floor in deployment, and then play her wherever she can to get a frontline kill, ensuring that she dies every turn. Her fast damage scaling and {{IconLink|Quick}} status effect make her great at dealing with frontline heavies in later combat rounds, though she does struggle in earlier rounds when her damage output is still low. Once the boss has appeared, try to place her behind a tank so that she can repeatedly hit during {{IconLink|Relentless}} with her highly-scaled attack. '''Eternal Flame''' also allows for more '''[[Reform]]'''-centric runs, since you won't be so dependent on randomly drawing her from [[Primitive Mold]]. As the only path which doesn't require Primitive Mold to work effectively, it is almost always the best choice with the [[Pyre of Dominion]]. [[Resin Blades]] is incredibly useful for this path; {{IconLink|Multistrike}} takes full advantage of her high {{Attack}} and the {{IconLink|Burnout|1}} it applies ensures she will die every turn. However, you will need to replay it every turn, which is difficult to manage due to its {{Ember|2}} cost. Consider combining it with [[Weapons Cache]] if possible, which if used to draw Resin Blades will reduce its {{Ember}} cost to 0. Keep in mind that, because you must draw '''Little Fade''' again every turn, you will only draw 4 other cards each turn. This makes additional draw, such as that from the [[Pyre of Entropy]] or [[Limbo's Solace]], more useful than normal. [[Votivary]]'s +2 draw on {{IconLink|Extinguish}} is also very helpful, essentially making up for [[Little Fade]]'s draw as long as both can die each turn. Similarly to '''Fire Light''', '''Eternal Flame''' can benefit from {{IconLink|Reanimate}} from the [[Lazarus League]], although less so since she's {{IconLink|Quick}} and {{IconLink|Endless}} already; the main benefit of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} here is instead to allow her to die multiple times per turn in order to scale faster, and/or allow her to stay alive between turns, to avoid the draw issue above. ===Little Icarus=== The general strategy with '''Little Icarus''' is the opposite of her other two paths. Here, you want her to remain alive so she can get as many kills as possible. This means buffing her defense with {{Health}} increases, {{IconLink|Armor}}, {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} or even '''[[Reform]]'''. '''Little Fade''' already scales her {{Attack}} on {{IconLink|Slay}} so adding {{IconLink|Multistrike}} or {{IconLink|Trample}} can help get more kills. The rest of your deck should have cards to assist '''Fade''' (such as {{IconLink|Rooted}}, '''[[Descend]]''', or {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}}). You don't want other units stealing kills, so they should only be used to address enemies that '''Fade''' would not be able to hit anyway. Early game is critical for this path to build up sufficient {{IconLink|Spikes}}; if done correctly, she can easily solo entire battles afterwards. In Monster Train 2, '''Little Icarus''' is probably [[Little Fade]]'s most difficult path, especially in the early game. In combats like [[Ring 1#Dominion's Preservation|Dominion's Preservation]], it can be challenging to get even a single {{IconLink|Slay}}, especially if you do not get the [[Trials#Mark of Invasion|Mark of Invasion Trial]]. In general, it is wise to get her killed a couple of times in the early rounds of early combats to build up her {{Health}} and {{Attack}} from '''[[Reform]]'''. Once she has {{IconLink|Spikes}}, she can be played as a backline killer with {{IconLink|Spikes}} damage, then played at the back of a floor in {{IconLink|Relentless}} to take advantage of her {{Attack}}. Due to the risk of taking this path and getting few kills due to bad matchups, it's advisable only to pick it if your starting deck or artifact already contains synergies. Some common cards that make it more pickable overall include [[Divinity]], [[Packed Morsels]], [[Loamcoat]], [[Welder Helper]], [[Echo Infusion]], and [[Fae's Blessing]]. Useful artifacts include [[Martyr's Signet]], [[Life Insurer]], [[Chain of Gems]], and [[Scorched Steel]]. Starting with banner units like [[Awoken Hollow]], [[Steelworker]], [[Morselmaker]], or [[Conductor Steward]] make her more viable as well. Once you have a solid setup for '''Little Icarus''', it's generally advisable to partner her with some {{IconLink|Harvest}} units, who can take advantage of all the waves killing themselves on her {{IconLink|Spikes}}. [[Wickless Baron]] can scale relatively quickly and makes {{IconLink|Relentless}} much easier, while [[Wickless Tycoon]] massively enhances your economy and can allow you to buy a lot of powerful upgrades, artifacts, or card removals to thin down your deck. '''Little Icarus''' should generally not be cross-pathed with '''Eternal Flame''', as the lack of {{Health}} scaling from Reform means that she won't be able to clear waves as effectively. If allied with the [[Awoken]], [[Adaptive Mutation]] can convert her high {{Attack}} to {{Health}}, allowing her to tank damage and kill enemies with her {{IconLink|Spikes}}. However, you must get a reasonable number of kills beforehand. The Awoken also have several other synergies that make '''Little Icarus''' much more takeable, including [[Emblem of the Exiles]], [[Awakening Thicket]], and [[Oldgrowth]] to raise her {{Health}} without needing Reform, and [[Petrified Crucible]], [[Shard Channeler]], and [[Gnarled Root]], which increase the power of {{IconLink|Spikes}}. The [[Lazarus League]] can provide a unique form of survivability in the form of {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, especially useful when you haven't had the chance to build up her {{Health}} yet; at low {{Health}} it acts similarly to {{IconLink|Damage Shield}}, allowing her to take one extra hit per stack, although note that {{IconLink|Unstable}} from the same Clan can steal kills, as it will not trigger her Slay if it explodes on an enemy or '''Fade''' herself and kills something. [[Organ Harvester]] in particular is an incredible equipment for '''Fade''', as her {{IconLink|Spikes}} killing an enemy will trigger its {{IconLink|Slay}} and give her a {{IconLink|Reanimate}} stack. With the [[Railforged]], '''Little Icarus''' is generally much easier to enable. When '''Little Fade''' dies, she can have '''[[Forge Points]]''' applied to her to give her large amounts of {{IconLink|Armor}}, boosting her durability far more than the simple {{Health}} boost from Reforming. If partnered with a unit like [[Salvage Machine]], you can build up ludicrous amounts of Forge Points quickly and turn her into a highly durable wall. She's also a huge beneficiary of the [[Boilerplate]], whose permanent {{IconLink|Armor}} can make her far more immediately bulky without the need to Reform her. The Railforged can be somewhat lacking in backline access as well, making her {{IconLink|Spikes}} even more valuable. == Trivia == [[File:Death_LittleFade.ogg|thumb|right|Little Fade Death Sound Effect]] * On death, Little Fade chuckles softly. * In the [[Lost Arsenal]] update, it was claimed that the '''Little Icarus''' path would be buffed from starting with {{IconLink|Spikes|5}} to {{IconLink|Spikes|7}}. It [[Reform]]s a random unit in the exhaust pool. == Strategy == '''Primitive Mold''' is one of the hardest starter cards to use effectively. If your build has too few units dying, this card is just a dead draw most of the time. If your build has too many units dying, you may not be getting the one you actually need in a given situation. Many non-[[Melting Remnant]] units just aren't great Reform targets as they lack native {{IconLink|Burnout}} and may not fit on the floor they'd need to be. For some decks, you just want to purge these quickly. With a deck that has mostly Melting Remnant units that want to die often and a setup where they can be resummoned flexibly, this can be a very important component to your setup. Still, random reforming won't perform consistently and you'll need a way to make your deck more reliable in the middle-to-lategame. With some care about what goes into your Reform pool, you can keep one or two of these into the lategame as an alternative to [[Molded]]. For decks that contain enough {{IconLink|Burnout}} or [[Reform]] effects, it can be viable to upgrade select non-Remnant units with {{IconLink|Wickstone}}, which makes such units a bit better suited for Reform effects like '''Primitive Mold'''. In the early game, this card can sometimes be helpful during the relentless phase by letting you replay your units as the boss ascends. This is not very reliable as it requires that you draw a '''Primitive Mold''' at the right time and that it hits the correct unit in your Reform pool (the latter can be curated by controlling which units die). But there are times when all you need are a few additional rounds against the boss to prevent early Pyre damage, which '''Primitive Mold''' may be able to provide. This can become a much more effective strategy if you also start the run with {{IconLink|Burnout}} extension cards like [[Hallowed Drippings]] or [[Wicklash]], or find a way to kill and reform one of your units multiple times so it has a good amount of burnout when the boss arrives. If you happen to start with '''Primitive Mold''' and your Champion is [[Lord Fenix]], then his '''Overlord''' path can carry almost the entire game on its own. By having him repeatedly kill and reform himself, you will scale his {{Attack}} permanently, while also stacking {{IconLink|Burnout}} and (once you reach Ring 4) killing whole waves of enemies with his [[Explosive]] damage. In this case, it is best to remove all other units and all non-Reform cards, although you will still need a way to deal with [[Deafening Herald]] and some way to kill enemies in the first three rings. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Its {{IconLink|Burnout|1}} means that it will die after attacking and be available for '''[[Reform]]''' by the next turn, and its built-in {{IconLink|Multistrike}} allows it to benefit twice as much from the {{Attack}} gain each time this happens. It is a solid target for '''Dark Calling''' [[Rector Flicker]], as he can Reform it every time it dies and apply a solid amount of extra {{Attack}}. It can also be used effectively with the '''Fire Light''' path on [[Little Fade]], which can provide it with enormous {{Attack}} scaling and keep it alive by applying more {{IconLink|Burnout}}. Being a {{Capacity|1}} unit also helps it to fit in more easily behind Fade. [[Wicklash]] and [[Waxen Spike]] can boost its {{Attack}} and extend its {{IconLink|Burnout}}. Its explosion damage is unaffected by its stats and is not increased by {{IconLink|Conduit}} or '''[[Magic Power]]''', which makes it difficult to scale into the late game as effectively as other cards. If allied with the [[Underlegion]], {{IconLink|Stealth}} can be [[Propagate]]d to apply even more. If you have enough damage to kill waves already, '''Molten Encasement''' can completely solve your defensive needs. However, it does little or nothing offensively, meaning that your damage output must be strong enough to afford spending energy and space purely on defense. With stacks of {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, '''Molten Encasement''' can continually add {{IconLink|Stealth}} to the floor without needing to be played again or Reformed. It has low stats, but starts with {{IconLink|Endless}} and grants two additional card draws next turn when it dies. ==Strategy== '''Votivary''' is typically a low-value but low-cost card to add to your deck, drawing two cards the turn after it dies to make up for the cost of drawing it in the first place. One turn after initially drawing it and letting it die, you break even ('''Votivary''' has granted two additional card draws, and you have drawn '''Votivary''' twice), and every turn after that accelerates your draw. This makes it a useful chump blocker, as unlike most other {{IconLink|Endless}} units it actually increases your total draw instead of decreasing it, and it can block a single attack and trigger {{IconLink|Harvest}}. With either [[Waxer Snuffer]] or a [[Hall of Mirrors]], you can draw 4 cards next turn for each '''Votivary''' you play, helping draw through your deck much faster as long as you can get them to die consistently. A {{IconLink|Wickstone}} can help guarantee this. Note, however, that with Waxer Snuffer, having more than one '''Votivary''' does not actually increase your draw. A Waxer Snuffer '''Votivary''' draws 9 total cards next turn, one of which will be itself, making 8 "real" draws. Two of them, due to the hand size limit of 10 cards, will draw 10 cards total, but two of those cards will be '''Votivaries''', so you still only have 8 "real" draws. With the {{IconLink|Worthy Sacrifice}} upgrade from the [[Inscryption]] event, the '''Votivary''' can be immediately killed when drawn, not only enhancing your draw but also giving you {{Ember|3}} with which to play your extra cards. The {{IconLink|Many Lives}} upgrade is similarly powerful - not only does it allow '''Votivary''' to trigger {{IconLink|Harvest}} effects four times instead of one, it also practically guarantees you will be drawing 10 cards every turn, as long as '''Votivary''' can fully die. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! {{UnitCard |name = Lady of the House |image = PLR_LadyOfTheHouse.png |clan = Melting Remnant |rarity = Uncommon |type = Waxer |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 25/45 |ability = {{IconLink|Burnout|3}}.

Some of the more generous Remnants decide to fund the Votive Houses scattered throughout the Ring, though I have long suspected that their motives are less than selfless. |artist = Tammy Chang }} '''Lady of the House''' is an uncommon [[Melting Remnant]] [[banner unit]]. She has high stats and gains a extra {{Attack|+5}} for each stack of {{IconLink|Burnout}} she has, but she starts with {{IconLink|Burnout|3}}, meaning that she will die after a few turns if you cannot apply more. == Strategy == '''Lady of the House''' has very respectable stats for a banner unit that only takes {{Ember|1}} and {{Capacity|2}}. By default, she effectively has {{AttackHealth|40|45}}. However, her damage decreases as she burns out, and after three turns she will die. She requires either '''[[Reform]]''' effects or a way to apply additional {{IconLink|Burnout}} in order to perform. Uniquely among {{IconLink|Burnout}} units, she actively benefits from getting her {{IconLink|Burnout}} stacks as high as possible, whereas other units only care about having enough to not die. [[Wicklash]] and [[Purifying Cleanse]] are excellent supporting cards for her, providing {{Attack|+20}} and {{Attack|+15}} respectively while also keeping her alive for longer. [[Hallowed Drippings]] is a particularly good choice if you are using multiple '''Ladies of the House''' on the same floor, granting {{Attack|+30}} to each, and even more if upgraded with {{IconLink|Stackstone}} or {{IconLink|Twinstone}}. [[Waxen Spike]] functions similarly, though as a rare card it is harder to find. [[Hallowed Halls]], another rare, will refresh her {{IconLink|Burnout}} and scale her a little bit faster by killing and [[Reform]]ing her. [[Resin Blades]] is an ideal equipment for her as she wants both {{IconLink|Multistrike}} and {{IconLink|Burnout}}. [[Lady of the Reformed]] is a fantastic partner for '''Lady of the House'''. Applying {{IconLink|Burnout}} on {{IconLink|Revenge}} is usually overkill, as it will often generate more {{IconLink|Burnout}} than can reasonably be used, but that is exactly what '''Lady of the House''' wants in order to scale. This is even more effective if Lady of the Reformed has been upgraded with {{IconLink|Dualstone}}, or with many copies of '''Lady of the House'''. Similarly, [[Little Fade]]'s '''Fire Light''' path will apply both {{IconLink|Burnout|2}} and a healthy dose of stats to the whole floor on {{IconLink|Extinguish}}. [[Combustible Wax]] is usually a fairly weak artifact, but it shines with '''Lady of the House''', rapidly increasing her scaling from most sources of {{IconLink|Burnout}}, including what she naturally starts with. When partnered with the [[Underlegion]], her {{IconLink|Burnout}} can be '''[[Propagate|Propagated]]''' with cards like [[Loamcoat]] and [[Proliferate]]. With the [[Lazarus League]], [[Brain Transfer]] can move all stacks of {{IconLink|Burnout}} from one unit to another while killing the original unit and therefore making it a viable target for [[Reform]]. '''Superfood''' [[Primordium]] is another powerful option for scaling '''Lady of the House'''. The "Reformdium" strategy from the original Monster Train is still plenty viable here, in which Primordium is intentionally allowed to die before being fully {{IconLink|Eaten}} and then [[Reform]]ed with increased stats and {{IconLink|Burnout}}. Alternatively, one can simply stack {{IconLink|Burnout}} directly onto Primordium to be transferred to '''Lady of the House'''. However, be aware that certain cards only apply {{IconLink|Burnout}} to units that already have it, such as Hallowed Drippings. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! I can't say that they are the most welcoming of Hellborne. |artist = Tammy Chang }} '''Lady of the Reformed''' is an uncommon [[Melting Remnant]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever she takes damage, she grants a stack of {{IconLink|Burnout}} to all friendly units on the floor which already have {{IconLink|Burnout}}, including herself. == Strategy == The '''Lady of the Reformed''' is best used for strategies which rely on units with {{IconLink|Burnout}} but which do not want to use [[Reform]]. With her {{IconLink|Revenge}} trigger, she can keep the rest of the floor alive when placed on the front lines, both blocking damage and providing a steady supply of {{IconLink|Burnout}}. As she will usually take damage multiple times per turn, she can stack up {{IconLink|Burnout}} faster than it decreases and make sure your other units have enough to avoid dying to the boss. This makes it viable to put {{IconLink|Wickstone}} on non-{{IconLink|Burnout}} units, as long as you can guarantee that the '''Lady of the Reformed''' will take damage every turn. In turn, this allows the [[Paraffin Enforcer]] to apply {{IconLink|Rage}} to those units without needing to first apply {{IconLink|Burnout}} using a spell like [[Wicklash]]. The [[Waxen Spike]] is very strong with the '''Lady of the Reformed''', providing both additional {{IconLink|Burnout}} in case she cannot take damage often enough and full-floor scaling. Be careful - putting her on a higher floor might lead to your other units dying before enemies arrive. This can be beneficial if you have a consistent source of [[Reform]], but is otherwise risky. Weak damage spells like [[Torch]] or [[Vine Grasp]] can be used to damage her and provide additional {{IconLink|Burnout}}, although the Melting Remnant does not have many good in-clan options for this. Besides Paraffin Enforcer, she also partners exceptionally well with [[Lady of the House]], who scales her {{Attack}} based on how much {{IconLink|Burnout}} she has. Since '''Lady of the Reformed''' will apply far more {{IconLink|Burnout}} than any unit would ever naturally require, she can rapidly scale a whole floor of Ladies of the House. She can also be used with [[Rector Flicker]]'s '''Burn Bright''' path to keep him alive and benefit for longer from his tremendous stats. However, she is quite a weak choice without Paraffin Enforcer or Lady of the House. Unlike the very similar [[Wickless Tycoon]], she does not grant any out-of-battle benefits to justify her inability to scale offensively. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! {{UnitCard |name = Paraffin Enforcer |image = PLR_ParaffinEnforcer.png |clan = Melting Remnant |rarity = Uncommon |type = Wickless |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 15/25 |ability = {{IconLink|Strike}}: Apply {{IconLink|Rage|3}} to friendly {{IconLink|Burnout}} units. |flavor = Once a footsoldier has been promoted to an Enforcer, they are no longer considered the punching bags of the Wickless Remains. But that doesn't mean that they won't haze new recruits the same way they were. |artist = Daniel Sarmiento Chuquisengo }} '''Paraffin Enforcer''' is an uncommon [[Melting Remnant]] [[banner unit]]. Whenever he attacks, he grants {{IconLink|Rage}} to all friendly units on the floor which have {{IconLink|Burnout}}, including himself if he has {{IconLink|Burnout}}. == Strategy == '''Paraffin Enforcer''' is in an odd situation: your units must have {{IconLink|Burnout}} to take advantage of his effect, but [[Reform|Reforming]] them will remove the {{IconLink|Rage}} he applies. This makes him most effective in {{IconLink|Burnout}}-based builds which do not involve Reform. [[Little Fade]], with her '''Fire Light''' path, is the easiest and most effective way to achieve this. Killing her consistently at the front of the floor will provide your other units with a constant supply of {{IconLink|Burnout}}, enough to keep them alive for the entire battle. If using this path, the '''Paraffin Enforcer''' is one of the best units available, able to apply enormous amounts of {{IconLink|Rage}} to the entire floor. A [[Lady of the Reformed]] can fulfill a similar role if not using that path. Spells like [[Wicklash]], [[Hallowed Drippings]], and [[Waxen Spike]] can achieve the same effect if played consistently. However, note that Hallowed Drippings and Lady of the Reformed only apply {{IconLink|Burnout}} to units that already have it, so you will need another way of applying some initial {{IconLink|Burnout}} to '''Paraffin Enforcer'''. In a Reform deck, '''Paraffin Enforcer''' is still a strong choice, though with the downside that {{IconLink|Rage}} will be removed when a unit is Reformed. This limits the amount of {{IconLink|Rage}} he can stack up, but even a small amount applied to the entire floor can go a long way. If he is one of the units being constantly killed and Reformed by [[Hallowed Halls]], he should be given {{IconLink|Quick}}, as he may otherwise not be able to apply {{IconLink|Rage}} before the other units attack. The [[Resin Blades]] equipment is a high-priority pickup with '''Paraffin Enforcer'''. Applying both {{IconLink|Burnout|1}} and {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}} is a huge boon for him, similar in effect to a [[Draff]] infusion from the original game. Of course, this requires you to have an immediate source of {{IconLink|Burnout}} extension available. {{IconLink|Seekstone}} on {{IconLink|Burnout}} applicators is great for keeping him alive. [[Combustible Wax]] also works with his particular playstyle, since he wants to avoid dying to {{IconLink|Burnout}}. [[Draff]]s make for great allies, as long as you can keep them from dying, as they benefit from {{IconLink|Rage}} twice thanks to {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. [[Dreg]]s are okay as well due to their {{Ember|0}} and {{Capacity|1}}. They are especially useful in the early game, if you start with '''Paraffin Enforcer''' and cannot upgrade him yet. If you do not plan to use {{IconLink|Burnout}} at all, '''Paraffin Enforcer''' is not very useful. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Upgrade !! {{UnitCard |name = Wickless Baron |image = PLR_WicklessBaron.png |clan = Melting Remnant |rarity = Uncommon |type = Wickless |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 5/15 |ability = {{IconLink|Harvest}}: {{Attack|+5}} and {{Health|+5}}. |flavor = Some Waxers would prefer to stay in this Ring of Hell, finding their current predicament to be rather comfortable. Even fewer will decide to make that choice more permanent by removing their wicks entirely. |artist = Daniel Sarmiento Chuquisengo }} '''Wickless Baron''' is an uncommon [[Melting Remnant]] [[banner unit]]. He gains {{AttackHealth|+5|+5}} on {{IconLink|Harvest}}. == Strategy== '''Wickless Baron''' is a solid unit. His {{AttackHealth|+5|+5}} on {{IconLink|Harvest}} allows him to scale reasonably fast with any decent {{IconLink|Harvest}} engine. During the last few combats of the run, it is not uncommon for enemy waves to contain five or six enemies, allowing for fast growth. He is best pared with {{IconLink|Extinguish}} units, which provide benefits on death, or low {{Health}} units with {{Capacity|1}} that can be stacked in front of him. Of the Melting Remnant units, [[Votivary]] and [[Remnant Host]] are probably the best partners. Votivary has {{IconLink|Endless}} by default and improves your draw, while Remnant Host effectively provides three {{IconLink|Harvest}} triggers on death. Other clans have strong options as well. [[Imps]] have beneficial {{IconLink|Summon}} effects and are often used as meat shields, and the Melting Remnant has an easier time than usual using them since they can be given {{IconLink|Wickstone}} along with {{IconLink|Immortalstone}} for guaranteed death each turn. [[Bloated Whelp]]s can be placed and killed immediately while potentially killing a few back line enemies in the process, allowing for multiple {{IconLink|Harvest}} triggers while only needing {{Capacity|1}} on the floor. [[:Category:Assistant units|Assistants]] provide useful equipment on death, and {{IconLink|Reanimate}} can let you trigger {{IconLink|Harvest}} repeatedly from a single unit, making [[Nine-Lived Nightmare]] a strong ally. Any units with {{IconLink|Sweep}} or {{IconLink|Spikes}} will rack up {{IconLink|Harvest}} triggers rapidly from backline enemies dying, so units like [[Selene Acolyte]] and [[Thorned Hollow]] are worthwhile companions. Although [[Morsels]] do not activate {{IconLink|Harvest}} when {{IconLink|Eaten}}, they do still count if they are killed normally. The [[Glutton's Maw]] equipment will also kill any non-Morsel unit that it targets, letting you "eat" units like [[Molten Encasement]] for a stat boost and an extra {{IconLink|Harvest}} trigger. [[Funguy]] triggers {{IconLink|Harvest}} for each stack of {{IconLink|Troop}} lost, making for a very potent frontline partner. This also makes [[Green Recruit]] an excellent unit, and again one that benefits heavily from {{IconLink|Wickstone}}. A large Funguy tower can be instantly killed by applying {{IconLink|Burnout}}, which will send any '''Wickless Barons''' on the floor through the roof. Since each stack of {{IconLink|Troop}} provides {{AttackHealth|3|4}}, but '''Wickless Baron''' gets {{AttackHealth|+5|+5}} for each {{IconLink|Troop}} stack lost, you are gaining stats overall even with only a single '''Wickless Baron''', and every additional copy just gets you further ahead. [[Resin Blades]] is the quickest way to kill a Funguy tower, as it applies {{IconLink|Burnout|1}}, but [[Wicklash]] and [[Purifying Cleanse]] will do the job as well; just be sure not to '''[[Propagate]]''' the {{IconLink|Burnout}}, or you will stall its death. If you are using '''Wickless Baron''' and Funguy in tandem, avoid [[Amorous Enoki]], as the extra {{Health}} she applies will make it take longer for enemies to remove {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks. [[Hallowed Halls]] will trigger {{IconLink|Harvest}} for every unit in front of '''Wickless Baron''' and hopefully fill your floor with low-{{Capacity}} fodder units that will die again quickly. Since '''Wickless Baron''' needs a few turns to scale, you will need a plan to deal with early, tanky enemies, especially an early [[Avowed Gladiator]]. [[Crushing Demise]] is ideal for this; it is risky to play on '''Wickless Baron''''s floor since he usually does not want to be [[Reform]]ed, but once it has ascended to a higher floor it is much safer to play, especially if your backline clear was able to eliminate any weak enemies behind it and therefore guarantee that it is the only possible target. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! With any decent {{IconLink|Harvest}} engine, he can provide hundreds of {{Gold}} each battle. He works well with units like [[Votivary]] and [[Remnant Host]] which can easily trigger {{IconLink|Harvest}}, or alongside those like [[Wickless Baron]] or [[Big Sludge]] which can take advantage of it. Even without going out of your way to fuel him, he can provide enough {{Gold}} just from killing enemies on the same floor that it's often worth taking him. This may lead to odd situations, like buffing a boss so that it can kill more of your units, or fighting [[The Undying One]] on the top floor so you can kill him as many times as possible. Safety is not a high priority with this strategy: your goal should be to maximize the number of deaths which occur, even if that means killing your own units. [[Hallowed Halls]] can provide enormous amounts of {{Gold}}, giving you {{Gold|10}} for each unit in front of him whenever it is played. [[Funguy]] triggers {{IconLink|Harvest}} every time {{IconLink|Troop}} is lost, providing enormous amounts of {{Gold}} both in the early and lategame. Whenever another unit dies on its floor, it gathers {{IconLink|Soul}}, which it unleashes in a destructive blast when it is killed. == Strategy== The '''Devourer of Death''' is a relatively niche unit which will not find a use in all decks, but it can be strong in the right circumstances. The simplest way to use it is to put it behind other units on your main kill floor, so that it can stack up {{IconLink|Soul}} as the battle goes on. This way, if your other units die, it will deal massive damage to all enemies on the floor, acting as a backup plan to prevent a total loss. This is best used with decks that can easily take down waves of enemies but struggle against {{IconLink|Relentless}} bosses. In a [[Reform]]-focused deck, the '''Devourer of Death''' can instead be used for backline clear, similar to [[Exploding Candle]]. This is best used with [[Hallowed Halls]], which can provide {{IconLink|Harvest}} triggers before killing the Devourer each time it is played, as long as the Devourer doesn't happen to be Reformed in the front of the room. Keep in mind that {{IconLink|Soul}} is lost when the unit dies and reforms, so this is only useful for dealing small amounts of damage to enemy waves rather than wiping out bosses. It also has some niche interactions with cards from other clans. Any source of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} can allow the Devourer to be killed repeatedly, {{IconLink|Harvest}}ing itself and the enemies it kills and acting similarly to {{IconLink|Unstable}} units like the [[Overworked Assistant]]. With the [[Pyreborne]], because the '''Devourer of Death''' and [[Soulsmelter]] both use {{IconLink|Soul}}, equipping the Soulsmelter to the Devourer will allow you to gain {{IconLink|Soul}} much faster than normal and gain far more [[Dragon's Hoard]] than you could under ordinary circumstances. {{UnitCard |name = Big Sludge |image = PLR_BigSludge.png |clan = Melting Remnant |rarity = Rare |type = Wickless |banner = Yes |cost = 2 |size = 3 |stats = 10/30 |ability = {{IconLink|Harvest}}: Gain {{IconLink|Rage|5}}. |flavor = Even wax dripping has its limits. He gains {{IconLink|Rage|5}} whenever a unit dies on his floor. == Strategy== '''Big Sludge''' is best compared to the [[Wickless Baron]], another unit which becomes stronger on {{IconLink|Harvest}}. There are several important differences between them: * '''Big Sludge''' starts with twice as much {{Attack}} and {{Health}}, one additional {{Capacity}}, and a higher {{Ember}} cost. * '''Big Sludge''' gains {{Attack}} twice as fast as the Baron, and because it is in the form of {{IconLink|Rage}} it can be doubled again with {{IconLink|Dualism}}. * The Wickless Baron gains {{Health}} on {{IconLink|Harvest}}, which '''Big Sludge''' does not. * '''Big Sludge''' loses all of his {{IconLink|Rage}} when '''[[Reform]]ed''', but the Baron keeps his {{Attack}} and {{Health}}. This makes '''Big Sludge''' somewhat more situational than the Baron, but with a much higher potential reward if he can be used effectively. He cannot be Reformed without losing his {{Attack}}, making him significantly less effective with cards like [[Hallowed Halls]]. His lack of defensive scaling requires you to put more resources into keeping him alive. His extra {{Capacity}} also makes it harder to put other units in front of him, either to protect him or as sacrifices to buff his damage. If you can deal with his weaknesses, however, he can deal far more damage than the Wickless Baron, and has the potential to be one of the most effective self-scaling damage units in the entire game. Like the similar [[Nameless Siren]] and [[Siren of the Sea]], the units also work quite well in tandem, with Wickless Baron tanking for '''Big Sludge'''. '''Accumulator''' [[Rector Flicker]] can serve a similar role. His comparatively lower {{Attack}} is made up for by '''Big Sludge''', while his {{Health}} is much higher. Ideally, defensive solutions should involve low-{{Capacity}} units or spells. {{IconLink|Stealth}} is an ideal solve, making '''Big Sludge''' invulnerable for as many turns as you can keep it active with no need for a proper tank. Both [[Engulfed in Smoke]] and [[Molten Encasement]] are excellent picks here; Engulfed in Smoke can be upgraded with {{IconLink|Seekstone}} to ensure you draw it immediately and does not require any empty {{Capacity}} on your floor, but Molten Encasement is cheaper by default and adds an additional {{IconLink|Harvest}} trigger. Multiple copies of '''Big Sludge''' do fare well together on a single floor, as {{IconLink|Harvest}} will scale all of them; however, this is generally a bit unwieldy due to his size and {{Ember|2}} cost. Cards like [[Dripfall]] can overstack the floor to avoid needing {{IconLink|Smidgestone}} or [[Exile's Diadem]], but this will prevent you from playing {{IconLink|Harvest}} fodder like [[Remnant Host]]. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! {{UnitCard |name = Bounty Stalker |image = PLR_BountyStalker.png |clan = Melting Remnant |rarity = Rare |type = Wickless |banner = Yes |cost = 1 |size = 2 |stats = 30/5 |ability = {{IconLink|Burnout|1}}. {{IconLink|Stealth|1}}.

Their incredible prowess in hunting Waxers has made them feared across the entire Ring, from Reformed to Wickless alike. I can't say I much like them myself. |artist = Taylor Bray }} '''Bounty Stalker''' is a rare [[Melting Remnant]] [[banner unit]]. He gains {{Attack|+10}} permanently each time he dies, and enters with both {{IconLink|Stealth}} and {{IconLink|Burnout}}. == Strategy== The main purpose of the '''Bounty Stalker''' is to die and be placed again as many times as possible to rack up absurd amounts of {{Attack}} by endgame. With a strong deck, he can be scaled up to have hundreds or thousands of {{Attack}} by the time you fight the Titans, almost guaranteeing a win. Once you add a '''Bounty Stalker''' to your deck, your whole strategy should generally be based around scaling him as much as possible. As of [[Destiny of the Railforged]], he starts with {{IconLink|Burnout|1}} alongside his {{IconLink|Stealth|1}}, which guarantees that he will be protected from enemy attacks and die at the end of the turn the first time he is sent out onto the field. The main problem with this game plan is that, if '''Reformed''', he will gain extra {{IconLink|Burnout}} stacks, and thus take more than one turn to die. His {{IconLink|Stealth}} will prevent enemies from attacking him as well, so he will almost always take at least two turns to die after being played initially. The solution to this is {{IconLink|Endless}}. An {{IconLink|Endless}} '''Bounty Stalker''' will return to your draw pile on death, letting you play him and have him die every turn. Finding some source of {{IconLink|Endless}} should be your highest priority when using '''Bounty Stalker'''. Usually, that will come in the form of {{IconLink|Immortalstone}} from the shop, but you have other options as well. [[Memorial for the Melted]] will apply {{IconLink|Endless}} to all units on the floor, so if you only need to play '''Bounty Stalker''' on a single floor this works well. [[Remnant Pact]] will apply {{IconLink|Endless}}, though ideally it should be upgraded with {{IconLink|Seekstone}} to ensure it is applied before he dies initially. The [[Votive Key]] artifact, if chosen, is a great choice as well, as long as you don't have any other units that need it. Being {{IconLink|Endless}} does mean that he has a negative impact on your card draw, since you will re-draw him every turn. If possible, try to use him alongside a [[Votivary]] with {{IconLink|Wickstone}}, as its +2 draw on {{IconLink|Extinguish}} will nullify the lost draw from re-drawing itself and '''Bounty Stalker'''. It can be a good idea to upgrade a {{IconLink|Burnout}} extender like [[Hallowed Drippings]] or [[Purifying Cleanse]] with {{IconLink|Freezestone}} when using '''Bounty Stalker'''. This can let him actually participate during {{IconLink|Relentless}} in order to kill the boss, as otherwise he'll make his initial attack and then die after one round. The [[Waxer Snuffer]] artifact is perhaps the single strongest artifact one can find with '''Bounty Stalker''' and should almost always be taken in general. By contrast, [[Combustible Wax]] should basically always be avoided unless you are late enough in the run that you no longer care about scaling; it makes his default {{IconLink|Burnout|1}} instead {{IconLink|Burnout|4}}, drastically slowing down scaling. If partnered with the [[Underlegion]], [[Shroomponics]] should also be avoided unless you can kill '''Bounty Stalker''' yourself with cards like [[Sporetouch]]; it will '''[[Propagate]]''' both his {{IconLink|Burnout}} and his {{IconLink|Stealth}} if he is placed during the Deployment phase, preventing enemies from hitting him and his {{IconLink|Burnout}} from killing him. As with any {{IconLink|Extinguish}} unit, he is highly synergistic with the [[Lazarus League]] for their ability to apply {{IconLink|Reanimate}}. If you are offered something from the Lazarus League at either the [[Railspikes]] or [[Wreckage Remains]] events, they should almost always be taken, as [[Spike of the League]] is a fantastic way to get a bunch of extra scaling on '''Bounty Stalker'''. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! Legion of Wax:
{{Unfinished|Strategy needs updating to account for the fact that as of Destiny of the Railforged, equipment is now inherited by the spawned units.}} {{UnitCard |name = Legion of Wax |image = PLR_LegionOfWax.png |clan = Melting Remnant |rarity = Rare |type = Waxer |banner = Yes |cost = 2 |size = 4 |stats = 16/16 |ability = {{IconLink|Extinguish}}: Summon '''2 Twin of Wax''' and apply this unit's upgrades, equipment, and stat changes. |flavor = When Waxers are reduced to almost nothing, but still cling to what life is left within, they will sometimes band together for protection. This creates a new form that is collectively controlled by this collection of dying Waxers. |artist = Aaron Lovett }} {{UnitCard |name = Twin of Wax |image = PLR_TwinOfWax.png |clan = Melting Remnant |type = Waxer |size = 2 |stats = 8/8 |ability = {{IconLink|Extinguish}}: Summon '''2 Mote of Wax''' and apply this unit's upgrades, equipment, and stat changes. |artist = Aaron Lovett }} {{UnitCard |name = Mote of Wax |image = PLR_MoteOfWax.png |clan = Melting Remnant |type = Waxer |size = 1 |stats = 5/5 |artist = Aaron Lovett }} '''Legion of Wax''' is a rare [[Melting Remnant]] [[banner unit]]. It divides into two '''Twins of Wax''' on {{IconLink|Extinguish}}, who in turn divide into two '''Motes of Wax''' on {{IconLink|Extinguish}}. == Interactions == * '''Twin of Wax''' and '''Mote of Wax''' inherit any effects applied to '''Legion of Wax''''s card. For example, most buffs are not passed down, but the {{Capacity}} change from {{IconLink|Smidgestone}} is, as is {{IconLink|Burnout}} applied to the card from [[Reform]] or {{IconLink|Wickstone}}. When in doubt, look at '''Legion of Wax''' in your deck view to see what will be passed to '''Twin of Wax'''. ** Another way to think of this is that all attributes of a unit that survive a [[Reform]] are passed on. * When '''Legion of Wax''' dies, any [[Equipment]] attached to it simply falls off; neither the equipment nor its stats affect the subsequent spawned units. ** However, if you manage to [[Graft]] equipment onto it, all of its children *will* have a copy of that equipment grafted onto them. This only applies the first time you play '''Legion of Wax'''. ** With {{IconLink|Red Crown}}, the original random equipment is removed, but all of its children gain new random equipment. * The units spawned by '''Legion of Wax''' are {{IconLink|Cardless}}, so they don't enter the [[Reform]] pool, though '''Legion of Wax''' itself will be, even if its children are still alive. * If the {{IconLink|Extinguish}} ability on '''Legion of Wax''' is triggered but it survives (via {{IconLink|Reanimate}} or [[Intent on Death]]), then the '''Twins of Wax''' are spawned in front of the '''Legion of Wax'''. * {{Capacity}} is ignored when their {{IconLink|Extinguish}} ability is triggered, but the 7 unit limit is not. Any excess units simply are not generated. * [[Cavendish]] affects '''Legion of Wax''' additional times on death, multiplicative. Its initial damage output will be increased to {{Attack|48}}, a gain of {{Attack|+32}}; then, when it splits into '''Twin of Wax''', that stat gain will be added onto the unit's base {{Attack|8}} for {{Attack|40}} total, which Cavendish will multiply again into {{Attack|120}}. '''Mote of Wax''' will also have {{Attack|+32}} added to its {{Attack|5}} for {{Attack|37}}, which is multiplied into {{Attack|111}}. == Strategy == Although '''Legion of Wax''' has fallen off from its incarnation in the original ''Monster Train'' due to the lack of unit infusions, it can still be a powerful unit in the right circumstances. Other than upgrades to its card, '''Legion of Wax''' passes on changes to {{Attack}} and {{Health}}, such as from [[Reform]] effects and other cards. Within the Melting Remnant itself, [[Wicklash]], [[Wicked Blaze]], [[Waxen Spike]], and [[Formless Child]] all grant stat increases, as can '''Dark Calling''' [[Rector Flicker]] and '''Fire Light''' [[Little Fade]]. [[Reform]] effects can be difficult to use with '''Legion of Wax''', as it does not free up its {{Capacity|4}} once it dies due to its summons. Thus, it is not easy to replay without {{IconLink|Smidgestone}}. In some ways, '''Legion of Wax''' can be thought of as having an innate {{IconLink|Multistrike|3}}, as it will eventually split into four '''Motes of Wax'''. In practice, however, because the '''Twins of Wax''' will die one at a time, it is rare for all four '''Motes of Wax''' to exist at once. Furthermore, if '''Legion of Wax''' did not receive any {{Health}} upgrades, the '''Motes of Wax''' will be killed off very quickly. {{Health}} upgrades can make '''Legion of Wax''' into a formidable blocker, as they will effectively be multiplied sevenfold. To put this into perspective, {{IconLink|Titanite}} essentially doubles a unit's {{Health}} (including base {{Health}}), healing, and {{IconLink|Armor}}; meanwhile, '''Legion of Wax''' multiplies {{Health}} bonuses (but not base {{Health}} or healing) by 7. The main problem with this strategy is that the {{Capacity|4}} required by '''Legion of Wax''' leaves little room for putting any damage dealers behind it. [[Waxer Snuffer]] is already an incredibly powerful artifact in general, but it makes '''Legion of Wax''' in particular far stronger, as it will summon four '''Twins of Wax''' upon death, and each of them will summon four '''Motes of Wax'''. This means, for example, {{Health}} bonuses will be multiplied by 21 instead of by 7. However, note that if there are any other units on the floor besides '''Legion of Wax''', you will lose some of the summons to the 7 unit limit - three '''Twins of Wax''' plus four '''Motes of Wax''' will max out the capacity. [[Intent on Death]] can trigger its summons while keeping the unit alive, which is useful when giving it upgrades like {{IconLink|Largestone}} that make it harder to kill. '''Twins of Wax''' now inherits equipment from '''Legion of Wax''', a change from previous behavior in the game. [[Glass Cannon]] is primarily useful due to the {{IconLink|Fragile}} it applies, allowing you to kill '''Legion of Wax''' at will. [[Overgrowth Carapace]] and [[Stasis Crystal]] both grant '''Legion of Wax''' {{AttackHealth|+20|+20}} every turn, and these are real stat increases which will be inherited on death. However, Overgrowth Carapace requires a lot of free {{Capacity}} or {{IconLink|Smidgestone}} in order to provide its benefits, while Stasis Crystal prevents '''Legion of Wax''' from attacking or being damaged for the first turn. [[Resin Blades]] are not inherited like other equipment but instead return to hand when '''Legion of Wax''' is killed. With the [[Umbra]], [[Glutton's Maw]] is another excellent way of increasing '''Legion of Wax''''s stats. Though it provides less {{Attack}} and {{Health}} per turn than Overgrowth Carapace or Stasis Crystal, its effect is far less punishing, and it can be used to eat additional [[Morsels]] or [[Primordium]], which will bolster its stats even further. Alternatively, you can use another unit with Glutton's Maw to kill off '''Legion of Wax''' and '''Twin of Wax''' and gain a modest stat boost in the process. [[Cannibalize]] can be used in the same fashion, instantly triggering {{IconLink|Extinguish}}. When partnered with the [[Lazarus League]], '''Legion of Wax''' synergizes well with {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, as it will summon more units whenever {{IconLink|Reanimate}} is triggered. They also have access to [[Sacrifice]] cards like [[Scrap for Parts]] and [[Brain Transfer]] so that you can kill '''Legion of Wax''' whenever you wish. [[Baron Grael]]'s '''Living Armory''' path can rapidly scale its {{Attack}}. {{IconLink|Many Lives}}, obtained from the [[Inscryption]] event, can make '''Legion of Wax''' an obscene tank, especially if you can reduce its size. '''Purifying Cleanse''' is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It heals {{Health|15}} and applies {{IconLink|Burnout|3}}. Like all {{IconLink|Burnout}} spells, it can only be played on friendly units.

==Strategy==

'''Purifying Cleanse''' is most useful for its ability to apply extra {{IconLink|Burnout}} to prevent a unit from running out, as well as providing a reasonable amount of healing. It is somewhat similar to [[Hallowed Drippings]], and can be used in many of the same situations, although it only targets a single unit and does not apply as much {{IconLink|Burnout}}. It is reasonably effective in the early game, but generally a good target for removal later on. It can also be used to buff the {{Attack}} of the [[Lady of the House]], making it more useful if you plan to use her as your main source of damage.

Alternatively, it can be used to kill a friendly unit by applying {{IconLink|Burnout}} and waiting for them to die. This is generally inefficient, since it will take them three turns to die, but it can be useful in a pinch.

It [[Descend]]s a unit and applies {{IconLink|Dazed|1}}. ==Strategy== '''Dripfall''' can slow down an enemy and put them out of commission for a turn, giving you several ways of disrupting enemy waves and pulling enemies that managed to escape back to your kill floor. It's also solid at disrupting [[Flying Bosses]], like [[Arkion]]. Its [[Descend]] means that it isn't a way to feed enemies to your Pyre, unlike other {{IconLink|Dazed}} effects, and its {{IconLink|Dazed}} makes it awkward to use for floor overstacking in the same way [[Restoring Retreat]], [[Rising Rage]], and others can - if used on friendly units, that friendly unit won't be able to act against two floors of enemies: its current floor, and the floor it's descended to. The [[Melting Remnant]] also don't tend to use floor overstacking as often as other clans anyway, as it doesn't work with [[Reform]] or {{IconLink|Endless}} - units that die can't be replayed on a full floor. However, if you can upgrade this card with {{IconLink|Keepstone}} so you have it every turn, Reformed units can be replayed on a higher floor and then descended, and if you have '''[[Advance]]''' effects (or {{IconLink|Wickstone}}/[[Melting Spout]]), you can also use {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Tombs]]. {{SpellCard |name = Resin Removal |image = CRD_ResinRemoval1_2.png |clan = [[Melting Remnant]] |rarity = Uncommon |cost = 2 |effect = Remove all '''[[Debuff]]''' effects from friendly units and all '''[[Buff]]''' effects from enemy units. |flavor = When wax hardens into resin, it is possible to chip away the crystallized exterior to expose the soft wax underneath. The process does not come without risks, though. |artist = Aaron Lovett }} '''Resin Removal''' is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It removes all [[Debuff]]s (red status effects) from friendly units on a given floor, and removes all [[Buff]]s (green status effects) from all enemies on that floor. ==Strategy== '''Resin Removal''' is one of the strongest cards in the game, and worth using in essentially any situation. It provides an easy way to strip buffs from enemies, which can trivialize many of them, even bosses like [[The Undying One]]. It also removes all debuffs from your own units, which is immensely helpful in many situations. Most importantly, it trivializes all three versions of Seraph: It removes the {{IconLink|Corruption}} applied by [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]] and prevents it from stacking up over time. It immediately removes the {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} on spawn against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]], as well as removing the {{IconLink|Rage}} he enchants his units with. It can cancel out the {{IconLink|Sap}} applied both by [[Seraph Aeternus-The Entropic]] directly and by his [[Curse of Entropy]] cards. Ironically, it is actually better when ''not'' using many other Melting Remnant cards and focusing on the allied clan. [[Reform]] strategies can already deal with debuffs by simply dying, which resets all debuffs (except for the {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} on summon when fighting Seraph's Savagery form). That said, even in a completely Reform-focused strategy which relies on constantly spamming [[Hallowed Halls]] to kill your own units over and over, '''Resin Removal''' can still be an excellent choice. ==Recommended Upgrades== {| class="wikitable" ! style="width:10%" | Upgrade ! A Fatal Melting:
{{SpellCard |name = A Fatal Melting |image = CRD_AFatalMelting.png |clan = Melting Remnant |rarity = Uncommon |cost = 2 |effect = Deal damage to enemy units equal to '''3x''' the number of friendly unit deaths this battle. |flavor = Charged with both the extension of life and the acceleration of melting, the Reformed tend to large flames at each Votive House, allowing for Waxers to congregate and melt more quickly than they would on their own. |artist = Brian Mutschler }} '''A Fatal Melting''' is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It deals damage to all enemies on the floor equal to '''3x''' the number of friendly unit deaths this battle. == Strategy == '''A Fatal Melting''' starts out the combat as a 0 damage spell, making it not a card you want to draw on turn 1. It doesn't get much better as combat progresses. With one or two friendly deaths, it can kill smaller backliners, and with seven it can kill [[Discordant Heretic]]. Killing [[Chosen Supplicant]] is 12, and [[Chosen Assassin]] is 17. You can (and probably should) upgrade this with a [[Magic Power]] upgrade to allow it to hit these benchmarks sooner - notably letting it do something even on turn 1. It also doesn't have any way to get through tricks that backliners have to survive removal - [[Purified Soul]] and [[Deformed Duo]] will survive this. The card does have some upside later in fights, and later in your run in general when you're able to kill and [[Reform]] lots of units. If you have 10 friendly deaths per turn (optimistic, but possible and even beatable with [[Hallowed Halls]] and/or [[Legion of Wax]]), it will deal around 240 damage by the end of endgame fights, which can help trim down tanky later waves. It could also hypothetically be your payoff for an [[Infinite]] involving killing a unit, letting it scale to arbitrarily high damage, though there are many other ways to accomplish this. Probably its best selling point, however, is that it is the only area-of-effect damage spell the [[Melting Remnant]] have, meaning it could be your only option to answer problems like [[Profane Supplicant]] or [[Chosen Supplicant]]. This can make it worth picking up despite its clumsiness and {{Ember|2}} cost. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Upgrade !! {{SpellCard |name = Engulfed in Smoke |image = CRD_EngulfedInSmoke.png |clan = [[Melting Remnant]] |rarity = Uncommon |cost = 2 |effect = Apply {{IconLink|Stealth|2}} to friendly units. |flavor = In the dangerous depths of Hell, it's important to have the means for quick concealment. If needed, I've found that wicks bundled together will burn slowly and create large quantities of smoke. |artist = Tammy Chang }} '''Engulfed in Smoke''' is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It applies {{IconLink|Stealth}} to all friendly units on the floor, protecting them from being targeted by enemy attacks. == Strategy == '''Engulfed in Smoke''' is a strong defensive technique. No matter how strong the enemies are, it will buy you two turns where your units simply cannot be hit. It is most useful against enemies that threaten you with extreme damage, like in the [[Cael, Lord of the Cherubs#Vampiric Feed|Vampiric Feed]] variant of Cael or against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Savage]]. Compared to [[Molten Encasement]], it has upsides and downsides: * Molten Encasement costs {{Ember|1}}. '''Engulfed in Smoke''' costs {{Ember|2}} by default, but can have its cost reduced to {{Ember|0}} with the right upgrades. * Molten Encasement triggers {{IconLink|Harvest}} when it dies, but requires {{Capacity}} on the floor to be placed down. '''Engulfed in Smoke''' is usable even if the floor is overstacked. * Molten Encasement is a common card, which means you are likely to see it early in the run and can therefore build around it, but you cannot see it past Ring 2. '''Engulfed in Smoke''' is harder to find early, but can still be obtained from Ring 3 onwards. * Both cards can be replayed every turn, either with {{IconLink|Immortalstone}} or {{IconLink|Keepstone}}. * Both cards can be upgraded to apply twice as much {{IconLink|Stealth}}, with {{IconLink|Dualstone}} and {{IconLink|Stackstone}} respectively. * Molten Encasement can have its effect triggered multiple times with effects like [[Waxer Snuffer]], [[Intent on Death]], and {{IconLink|Reanimate}}. * '''Engulfed in Smoke''' can be upgraded with {{IconLink|Seekstone}}, which is a huge boon for consistency, ensuring you will draw the card immediately. * Molten Encasement is disabled by {{IconLink|Silence}}, and it will not protect your units from the first hit of {{IconLink|Sweep}} attacks. '''Engulfed in Smoke''' is punished by {{IconLink|Incant}} enemies. Either way, both cards are very strong defensive options, and they will both serve you well if that's what you need. If you can play them repeatedly throughout the combat, you can build up a lot of {{IconLink|Stealth}} for {{IconLink|Relentless}}, giving you several free rounds to beat up the boss before you need to worry about taking hits. Although {{IconLink|Stealth}} protects your units from being attacked, it is not always a perfect defensive solution. It will not protect your units from {{IconLink|Spikes}} from [[Legion]], [[Penitent Prayerstone]]s, or [[Athane, Last to Fall]]. It will also not guard you from certain {{IconLink|Corruption}} effects. [[Misshapen Fiend]]s and [[Dominion]] both apply {{IconLink|Corruption}} to your front unit, and [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]] and [[Qel the Corruptor]] will apply it to a certain area. Both of these effects occur regardless of {{IconLink|Stealth}}. However, it does prevent {{IconLink|Corruption}} application on {{IconLink|Strike}}, as from [[Blightbound Guardian]]s, [[Deformed Duo]]s, and Seraph's {{IconLink|Corruption}}-doubling effect. Units with {{IconLink|Stealth}} will be safe against [[Terrifying Amalgam]]s and [[Savagery]], and will also count as a unit on the floor for the purposes of their {{IconLink|Resolve}} triggers, protecting your Pyre from damage. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Reluctantly, I created it with the Wickless when Hell was invaded to defend against the advancing Winged. |artist = Luke Banke }} '''Subsuming Blade''' is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It starts by dealing 5 '''[[Piercing]]''' damage and permanently adds 3 to its damage on {{IconLink|Slay}}. ==Strategy== '''Subsuming Blade''' is an effective targeted backline removal spell when drafted, being able to kill a decent number of enemies off the bat. Its Piercing effect cuts through [[Purified Soul]]'s protection as well as enemies protected by {{IconLink|Titanskin}} and {{IconLink|Armor}}. You'll often want to look for '''[[Holdover]]''' with this card, as it will let you use it consistently and scale it. Its ability to scale allows it to expand its list of potential victims: you can kill [[Discordant Heretic]], Chosen variants of enemies, enemies that rely on {{IconLink|Armor}} to block like [[Celestial Bastion]] and [[Chosen Bastion]], and [[Cael, Lord of the Cherubs]]'s Cherubs. It's never going to be an answer to heavy enemies like [[Avowed Gladiator]] or bosses, even in the best case. While it's stronger if picked up early, scaling it beyond 50 or so isn't that impactful. Notably, it's fine to pick up as late as the midgame, as it doesn't need to be scaled that much to fulfill its role. In the context of Melting Remnant, it has another less obvious but important role - killing your own units so you can [[Reform]] them. Thanks to its metascaling, it can become quite consistent at doing this even once your units have accumulated some {{Health}} from Reforming, letting your Reform engine not skip a beat. This is very useful for [[Tombs]], [[Little Fade]], and [[Bounty Stalker]] in particular. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Upgrade !! It gains 10 damage each time a friendly unit dies, meaning that it will be at its strongest only late in the battle, and is often a wasted draw early on. Even once the boss shows up, however, its damage output is generally rather pathetic, especially considering its high cost; few strategies are capable of killing enough friendly units to scale up its damage to reasonable levels. If this is the case, however, you won't need '''Memento Mori''', because you are already going to win the game. It deals 25 damage, gains 5 extra damage for each point of '''[[Magic Power]]''', and applies {{IconLink|Dazed|3}}. However, it can only be used on units which are not at full {{Health}}. ==Strategy== '''Mortal Entrapment''' is an extremely powerful spell, but often an awkward one. You need to deal damage to the target before using it, but at {{Ember|3}} it uses all of your starting {{Ember}}, making it difficult to play another damaging spell beforehand. Upgrades like {{IconLink|Emberstone}} can help with this, as can cheap damage spells like [[Sting]] or [[Flicker]]. The best use for this spell is against flying bosses, which will usually take damage on the first turn and remain damaged for the rest of the battle. [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]] and [[Seraph Aeternus-The Entropic]] are particularly good targets, as is [[Savagery]] in the [[Clash with the Titans|Titans]] fight. [[Dominion]] can also be a good target if you are capable of killing him faster than the other Titans. Applying {{IconLink|Dazed}} to these bosses is also very helpful, and it can be worth adding {{IconLink|Stackstone}} to keep them locked down for most of the battle. Its '''Attuned''' keyword is rarely relevant, as its ability to apply {{IconLink|Dazed}} is this card's main selling point, but it can be incidentally valuable if you have {{IconLink|Conduit}}. Damage upgrades are rarely worth using up a slot, as even 75 damage isn't worth {{Ember|3}} in the late game. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Upgrade !! To seal their pact, they created a Railspike from their collective wax and drove it into our Rail. |artist = Brian Mutschler }} '''Waxen Spike''' is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It boosts the {{Attack}} of friendly units and gives them {{IconLink|Burnout|4}}. It is the Melting Remnant offering for the [[Railspikes (event)|Railspikes]] event. ==Notes== '''Waxen Spike''' is unique among the [[Railspikes]] cards in that it still has an effect even if played for {{Ember|0}}: namely, it still applies {{IconLink|Burnout|4}} to friendly units. == Strategy == '''Waxen Spike''' is somewhat similar to [[Hallowed Drippings]], and is generally less efficient per {{Ember}} spent, giving {{Attack|+4}} and {{IconLink|Burnout|4}} instead of {{Attack|+5}} and {{IconLink|Burnout|5}}. However, Hallowed Drippings only applies {{IconLink|Burnout}} to units that already have it, while '''Waxen Spike''' applies it to ''all'' units on the floor. Normally, you want to avoid adding {{IconLink|Burnout}} to units that don't already have it, but it has a key niche with [[Paraffin Enforcer]], which applies {{IconLink|Rage}} to {{IconLink|Burnout}} units whenever it attacks. Since Paraffin Enforcer does not naturally have {{IconLink|Burnout}}, for it to scale its own damage you need to apply {{IconLink|Burnout}} through other means. There are very few ways to apply {{IconLink|Burnout}} to units that do not already have it outside of the common cards [[Wicklash]] and [[Purifying Cleanse]], and you cannot be offered these cards past Ring 2. As such, if you don't have one of these cards, you may be forced to waste a precious upgrade slot on {{IconLink|Wickstone}} instead of {{IconLink|Dualstone}}, {{IconLink|Frenzystone}}, {{IconLink|Speedstone}}, or {{IconLink|Smidgestone}}, or you may have to get Paraffin Enforcer killed and '''[[Reform]]''' him. '''Waxen Spike''' can save you from this, applying a respectable amount of {{IconLink|Burnout}} such that dying is not an immediate concern, and also ensuring that Paraffin Enforcer can scale your entire floor, even if you use him with other units that lack innate {{IconLink|Burnout}}. It also works quite well with [[Lady of the House]] in the same way that Hallowed Drippings does, with the upside of being available after [[Arkion]]. If for some reason you decide you want to get rid of {{IconLink|Burnout}} from a unit affected by this spell, you can use [[Wickless Recruitment]]. The {{Attack}}-boosting effect is generally of secondary importance compared to the {{IconLink|Burnout}} application, as it is hard to improve upon, and with either Lady of the House or Paraffin Enforcer it will quickly be made irrelevant due to the natural scaling of those units. However, since the {{IconLink|Burnout}} application is not tied to the amount of {{Ember}} spent on the card, you can play '''Waxen Spike''' even when you are out of {{Ember}} and still apply {{IconLink|Burnout|4}}. It is a lot less useful from the [[Railspikes (event)|Railspikes]] event unless you happen to be playing Melting Remnant, as you will not have any way of extending the {{IconLink|Burnout}} applied and will thus doom your floor to die in a few turns. This can occasionally be helpful for units which want to die like [[Assistants]] or an {{IconLink|Endless}} [[Greed Dragon]], but is usually not a good choice. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Sacrificial Resurrection:
{{SpellCard |name = Sacrificial Resurrection |image = CRD_SacrificialResurrection.png |clan = Melting Remnant |rarity = Rare |cost = 0 |effect = '''[[Consume]]''' cards in hand. Add a '''[[Draff]]''' unit to your hand and apply {{Attack|+10}} for each card consumed. |flavor = When new wax is unavailable to reform a fallen Waxer, the more selfless Reformed choose to donate a portion of their own form to the resurrection. |artist = Anita Tung }} '''Sacrificial Resurrection''' is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It sends ''all'' other cards in hand to the Consume pile, including those which cannot ordinarily be consumed. It then adds a [[Draff]] to the player's hand, and adds {{Attack|+10}} for each card consumed. ==Strategy== '''Sacrificial Resurrection''''s main purpose is to remove unwanted cards from your deck. It is one of the only ways (besides '''[[Smelt]]ing''') to send {{IconLink|Endless}} units, [[Blights]], [[Scourges]], or spells with {{IconLink|Eternalstone}} to the Consume pile. This can act as a pseudo-remove, taking all but a few cards out of your deck to allow for a consistent set of cards played each turn. It can remove [[Vengeful Shard]] from the deck, even just for the current battle, which makes it very useful above Covenant 5 and even more so with the [[Pyre of Entropy]]. [[Dante the Dependable]] also benefits, due to the ability to remove [[Dante's Candle]], and because he still gains {{IconLink|Multistrike}} for Blights in the Consume pile. Note that any units consumed will be considered dead, which may fill up your '''[[Reform]]''' pool with undesirable units when using random Reform cards like [[Primitive Mold]]. However, this also allows you to send {{IconLink|Endless}} units to the Consume pile, then Reform them with one stack of {{IconLink|Burnout}}, which can act as a substitute for a {{IconLink|Wickstone}} on units which you want to have die every turn. It can be extremely useful if your units have {{IconLink|Etch}} triggers. {{IconLink|Etch}} will trigger for every card Consumed by '''Sacrificial Resurrection''', potentially giving you a tremendous number of simultaneous triggers if you can draw a lot of cards every turn. You will likely run out of cards eventually if you keep playing it, but the '''Draff''' created each time it is played can be used as material for the next time it is played, as can cards like [[Curse of Entropy]] and [[Discordant Toll]] which will be added to your deck by enemies. You can also play other cards first in order to keep them in your deck, if they're worth more than an Etch trigger. Although removing cards is usually the main purpose, the Draff can also be useful, dealing a large amount of damage immediately and acting as a potential Reform target later on. Keep in mind that this card doesn't [[Consume]] itself, which can allow it to churn through large decks. It's also slightly annoying, as once you're out of things worth [[Consume|Consuming]] it's an almost dead card itself, merely adding an unbuffed [[Draff]] unit to your hand. Uniquely, it is able to Consume [[Infusion]] cards, which is the only way to remove them from your hand besides playing them. If you then use a spell that returns cards from the Consume pile to your hand, like [[Unearth Treasure]], you can have two Infusion cards simultaneously. This isn't really useful for anything. '''[[Mix]]ing''' while you have two Infusion cards in hand will only upgrade the leftmost one. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Upgrade !! It also means you don't have to spend a draw re-drawing this card once you've [[Consume]]d everything you intend to. |- | style="text-align:center;" | [[file:KeepStone.png|50x50px]]

Wickless Recruitment:
{{SpellCard |name = Wickless Recruitment |image = CRD_WicklessRecruitment.png |clan = [[Melting Remnant]] |rarity = Rare |cost = 0 |effect = Remove all {{IconLink|Burnout}} and '''[[Debuff]]''' effects on a unit. |flavor = ''Initiation into the Wickless Remains is a rite performed in the underbelly of the Waxen Arches, involving the sacrifice of a Waxer's wick to forever tie them to their hellish homeland. Even after the many I've witnessed, the ritual still gives me pause.'' |artist = Daniel Sarmiento Chuquisengo }} '''Wickless Recruitment''' is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It removes all [[Debuff]]s from a given unit, along with all {{IconLink|Burnout}}. ==Strategy== '''Wickless Recruitment''' has two separate uses. The first and most obvious is to instantly remove all stacks of {{IconLink|Burnout}} from a unit, preventing it from dying once it runs out of {{IconLink|Burnout}} normally. This can be helpful, but as this card is rare, it is likely that you will already have another way to deal with {{IconLink|Burnout}} effectively by the time you find it. Its second use is to remove Debuffs from a unit. This can be very useful, but is generally outclassed by [[Resin Removal]], an uncommon spell from the same clan which not only removes debuffs from all friendly units on the floor, but also removes all buffs from enemy units. Still, Resin Removal is one of the strongest cards in the game, and even if you only use '''Wickless Recruitment''' as a weaker substitute it is still a very useful card. Its lower price can also come in handy. It has a specific niche with [[Fade's First Blade]], which grants {{IconLink|Rage|3}} whenever you lose a stack of {{IconLink|Burnout}}. Removing all {{IconLink|Burnout}} with this card will immediately grant {{IconLink|Rage|3}} for every stack removed. If you find this combination early, you can exploit it through, for example, having a [[Lady of the Reformed]] with {{IconLink|Dualism}} apply a lot of {{IconLink|Burnout}} to a unit, then casting [[Wickless Recruitment]] for a massive {{IconLink|Rage}} spike. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! Intent on Death:
{{SpellCard |name = Intent on Death |image = CRD_IntentOnDeath.png |clan = [[Melting Remnant]] |rarity = Rare |cost = 1 |effect = '''[[Consume]]'''.
Trigger a unit's {{IconLink|Extinguish}} ability without killing it. |flavor = Votive Houses can become crowded and melting away is a long process. To avoid the wait, I've seen some Waxers increase the intensity of their flame through extreme focus, though they typically lose consciousness briefly after doing it. |artist = Tammy Chang }} '''Intent on Death''' is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It activates a unit's {{IconLink|Extinguish}} ability while keeping the unit alive. ==Notes== It will also trigger {{IconLink|Harvest}} and {{IconLink|Siphon}} / {{IconLink|Hellborne Harvest}} (depending on which unit you target) on the floor when played, even when targeting a unit without an {{IconLink|Extinguish}} ability. == Strategy == When using builds that rely on {{IconLink|Extinguish}} effects, this card is typically quite desirable, as it functionally allows a unit's {{IconLink|Extinguish}} trigger to happen twice - once immediately and then again when it dies properly. Thus, the strength of this card depends largely on the strength of your deck's {{IconLink|Extinguish}} triggers. For example, casting it on an [[Entombed Explosive]] to deal 65 damage to the front enemy unit is a rather weak effect, more or less equivalent to [[Titan's Gratitude]], whereas casting it on a [[Molten Encasement]] to apply {{IconLink|Stealth|2}} to the floor compares favourably in terms of {{Ember}} cost to [[Engulfed in Smoke]]. Using it on [[Green Recruit]] '''[[Spawn]]s 4''' for {{Ember|1}}, which is cheaper than [[Spawning Pods]] for the same effect, whereas on [[Gildmonger]] it provides half the value of [[Alchemy]] for a third of the price. Likely its best usage is on units with powerful {{IconLink|Extinguish}} triggers that can be difficult to actually kill. [[Legion of Wax]] with {{IconLink|Largestone}}, [[Bounty Stalker]], and [[Balmabello]] come to mind. This card allows Legion of Wax to take {{Health}}-increasing upgrades while still letting it split up into Twins and Motes of Wax promptly, increasing its potential tremendously. Casting it on Bounty Stalker permanently scales its {{Attack}}. On Balmabello, it immediately allows you to transfer all of its Buff stacks to all other units on your floor, and two Balmabellos on a single floor can scale each other multiplicatively with enough copies of '''Intent on Death'''. With [[Little Fade]]'s '''Eternal Flame''' and '''Fire Light''' paths, this card is quite powerful. It can either scale her {{Attack}} even further, or scale and apply {{IconLink|Burnout}} to your entire floor. If she is your champion and you are using either of these paths, this card should be a high priority if offered. This card has a niche with [[Devourer of Death]] if you can remove '''[[Consume]]''', allowing the unit to preemptively blast all enemies with the {{IconLink|Soul}} built up on {{IconLink|Harvest}}. Since this does not kill the unit, it can be placed safely at the back to build up lots of {{IconLink|Soul}}, dealing tremendous damage to all enemies whenever you draw this card. However, this combination is somewhat difficult to execute as it requires two different Rare cards and the {{IconLink|Eternalstone}} upgrade. The card can also target enemies, including bosses. Notably, it can target [[Collector]]s to provide some free {{Gold}}, and it can also trigger {{IconLink|Relentless}} early on [[Stryx]] & [[Hallow]]. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" !
