Hallowed Halls:
{{SpellCard |name = Hallowed Halls |image = CRD_HallowedHalls1_2.png |clan = [[Melting Remnant]] |rarity = Rare |cost = 3 |effect = Kill friendly units.
'''[[Reform]]''' random units to this floor until it exceeds its {{Capacity}}. |flavor = ''Wurmkin stoneform speaks of passageways deep below those controlled by the Wickless, further even than the caverns of the Reformed. These halls of stone sleep in the dark, their floors covered in the wicks of lost Waxers. Should Wax ever fall from the Ring above, and flame come to the wicks that lay there, a soul is said to live again for a brief moment of time. In my darkest nightmares, I rest in these wicked halls forever flickering between life and death.'' |artist = Brian Mutschler }} '''Hallowed Halls''' is a [[Melting Remnant]] spell. It instantly kills all friendly units on the floor, then [[Reform]]s units at random until either there are none left to Reform, or the floor is overstacked. It can Reform the same units which it just killed. Units are killed from right to left, which can be important when considering {{IconLink|Extinguish}} or {{IconLink|Harvest}} triggers. Note that it only stops once the floor is overfilled. If the units summoned fill the floor exactly, such as a [[Shield Steward]] and [[Spear Steward]] on a {{Capacity|5}} floor, then one more unit will be summoned. == Strategy == '''Hallowed Halls''' is one of the strongest cards available to the Melting Remnant, and can be the main engine for a very powerful deck. If you have a small group of units which can fit on a single floor, then it can repeatedly kill and reform them, gradually buffing their stats, providing {{IconLink|Harvest}} and {{IconLink|Extinguish}} triggers, repeatedly triggering {{IconLink|Summon}} effects, and stacking up more and more {{IconLink|Burnout}}. It also acts as a full heal for the entire floor, a kind of substitute for [[Unleash the Wildwood]] which also removes debuffs. It is best used with {{IconLink|Keepstone}} so that you can play it every turn, or even multiple times per turn. This allows it to buff your units more and make sure that they never run out of {{IconLink|Burnout}}. The biggest issue with this spell is its {{Ember|3}} cost, which makes it difficult to spam even with upgrades. The fact that it uses up all your {{Ember}} is not necessarily a problem, as in a strong deck '''Hallowed Halls''' can easily be the only spell you want to cast; the biggest problem is that it makes it difficult to play it more than once per turn (such as via {{IconLink|Twinstone}}), as it is often too slow a scaling method otherwise. [[Boiler Room]] is the easiest way around this problem, as it is virtually guaranteed to produce more {{Ember}} than you spent to play the card. [[Encased Ember]] is another option as long as you can keep at least one [[Tomb]] unit in your Reform pool for this spell to kill and bring back; [[Pyre Chomper]] provides a similar effect if you happen to be partnered with the [[Hellhorned]]. [[Volatile Gauge]] has a 75% chance to make this card cheaper, and it also gives you additional card draw, letting you draw more copies of it. [[Spell Sanctum]] is expensive but will save a lot of {{Ember}} in the long run if you play this card frequently. Killing and Reforming units with [[Ability|Abilities]] resets their cooldown, enabling multiple activations in one turn. The {{IconLink|Wrath}} upgrade is especially powerful, allowing a unit to attack every time '''Hallowed Halls''' is played. [[Spiritbreaker's Charge]] also allows you to scale {{Attack}} on the Reformed units even more rapidly. If you have a unit with the {{IconLink|Worthy Sacrifice}} upgrade, you can kill it before playing '''Hallowed Halls''' and then have it be reformed to immediately refund the spell's cost. The usefulness of '''Hallowed Halls''' varies with different Melting Remnant units. It is enormously effective with [[Wickless Baron]] or [[Wickless Tycoon]], providing a {{IconLink|Harvest}} trigger for every friendly unit in front of them each time it is played. Wickless Tycoon is weak on his own, but with an otherwise strong set of banner units, his extra {{Gold}} can help pay for the removals and upgrades needed to put together a deck capable of beating late-game bosses. [[Lady of the House]] appreciates having her {{IconLink|Burnout}} refreshed to maximum and increased, but note that soft {{IconLink|Burnout}} application like from [[Lady of the Reformed]], [[Hallowed Drippings]], or [[Waxen Spike]] will be lost, so her {{Attack}} may actually go down. Both Champions interact favorably with the card, especially the '''Fire Light''' path on [[Little Fade]] (as long as you can move her back to the front of the floor once she's reformed) and either '''Accumulator''' or '''Burn Bright''' on [[Rector Flicker]]. Units which rely on buffs or status effects applied during battle are less effective, as these will be reset when they are Reformed. [[Big Sludge]], for example, will lose his {{IconLink|Rage}}. [[Devourer of Death]] will lose his {{IconLink|Soul}}s, preventing him from stacking them up for an enormous hit at the end of the battle. However, he can deal constant damage with each use of '''Hallowed Halls''' to wipe out enemy backliners. If you happen to have a way to stack up enormous amounts of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} on him, he can gain more and more {{IconLink|Soul}}s and damage all enemies each time '''Hallowed Halls''' is played. [[Paraffin Enforcer]] is a mixed bag with this spell: '''Hallowed Halls''' guarantees that all units on the floor will have {{IconLink|Burnout}}, but also resets the {{IconLink|Rage}} he applies between turns. It can also randomly place him in the back, so that he only applies {{IconLink|Rage}} to the other units after they have already attacked. Giving him {{IconLink|Quick}} can help guarantee that he applies {{IconLink|Rage}} before the other units can act. '''Hallowed Halls''' is immensely powerful with [[Dante the Dependable]], granting boosts to his otherwise unimpressive {{Attack}} and {{Health}} and constantly resummoning him to add more [[Dante's Candle]]s into your deck. However, this requires both {{IconLink|Seekstone}} and {{IconLink|Keepstone}} to prevent the spell itself from being buried under an enormous deck of [[Blights]]. Units with {{IconLink|Endless}} will not be reformed, instead being placed on top of the deck. Units with {{IconLink|Reanimate}} will simply lose a stack of it and survive at {{Health|1}} in front of your newly Reformed units. This can make both of these status effects harmful to a '''Hallowed Halls''' build. One important note is that '''Hallowed Halls''' chooses units randomly, meaning that any unwanted units will clog up your [[Reform]] pool. This makes it a high priority to remove units like [[:Category:Steward units|Stewards]], or weak starter units like [[Dreg]]s, [[Queen's Impling]]s, or [[Bloated Whelp]]s. If you have not yet removed them, avoid playing them even if you have the {{Ember}} and {{Capacity}} to do so, unless you are certain you can keep them alive. They're a much bigger problem in your [[Consume]] pile than in your discard pile. ==Interactions== * Assuming you [[Reform]] at least one unit, this counts as both a spell and a unit for [[Versatile Emberstaff]], even though you technically didn't play any unit cards. * The units summoned by '''Hallowed Halls''' will not decrease the cost of your cards if you have [[Flicker's Liquor]]. ==Recommended Upgrades== {| class="wikitable" ! Resin Blades:
{{EquipmentCard |image = CRD Resin Blades.png |clan = Melting Remnant |rarity = Rare |cost = 2 |effect = {{IconLink|Burnout|1}}.
{{IconLink|Multistrike|1}}.
Return to hand when equipped unit is destroyed. |flavor = It is because of blades such as these that the Reformed lament the process of molding the remains of their brethren into new weapons. They understand that each time the steel reforms itself, the trapped soul within the wax is struggling to be free. |artist = Loy Bouttamy }} '''Resin Blades''' is a rare [[Melting Remnant]] equipment added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It grants a unit {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}} and {{IconLink|Burnout|1}}. Additionally, unlike other equipment, it is immediately returned to your hand when the equipped unit dies. == Strategy == '''Resin Blades''' provides {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, a difficult-to-get commodity, especially for [[Champion]]s. This comes with {{IconLink|Burnout|1}}, however, meaning if you equip it on a unit without {{IconLink|Burnout}}, they'll just die at the end of the turn. There are a couple of ways of addressing this. One way is to simply apply additional {{IconLink|Burnout}} to the unit, ignoring the return-to-hand property and enjoying the {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. [[Rector Flicker]]'s '''Burn Bright''' variant is an exceptional user of this equipment, and any run using [[Lady of the Reformed]] to keep a floor of {{IconLink|Burnout}} units alive will have no trouble finding a good recipient of this, such as [[Paraffin Enforcer]]. Another way is to recur the unit with [[Reform]] effects or {{IconLink|Endless}} and re-equip it every time, using its return-to-hand property. This can be hard to do, because you'll need to spend {{Ember|2}} each time you play '''Resin Blades'''. Exceptional users of this include: * [[Little Fade]]'s '''Eternal Flame''' path, using {{IconLink|Endless}} to recur and {{IconLink|Quick}} to make the most of her one turn; this equipment doubles her hit-and-run potential while also guaranteeing she dies each turn * [[Hornbreaker Prince]]'s '''Reaper''' path combined with a source of {{IconLink|Endless}} like [[Memorial for the Melted]] or [[Remnant Pact]]; this allows him to use '''Culling''' every turn before reaching '''Reaper III''', grants him an extra hit, and can allow him to multiclass into '''Brawler''' for extra {{IconLink|Multistrike}} * [[Animus of Speed]] with {{IconLink|Immortalstone}} or another {{IconLink|Endless}} source; dying to {{IconLink|Burnout}} and being replayed lets her immediately use '''Swiftshot''' again, and the {{IconLink|Multistrike}} doubles both her standard and '''Swiftshot''' attacks One way to defray this card's {{Ember}} cost if you're recurring it is using [[Weapons Cache]] to draw it, as once discounted it will remain at {{Ember|0}} for the rest of the fight. Another is to use [[Boiler Room]] which triggers when its equipped unit dies. [[Attuned Whetstone]] will also nullify its price tag, and can even allow you to merge it with another piece of equipment while remaining at {{Ember|0}}. It is not affected by changes in cost induced by [[Volatile Gauge]], and will be returned to hand at its normal, unmodified cost. Since this card's "Return to hand" property persists when merged, merging this with other equipment can allow recurring units to enjoy the benefits of any other equipment, such as [[Glass Cannon]] or [[Bloodthirsty Blade]], which they normally cannot. '''Memorial for the Melted''' is an uncommon [[Melting Remnant]] room added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update, replacing [[Memories of the Melted]]. It grants friendly units {{IconLink|Endless}}.

== Strategy ==
{{IconLink|Endless}} is a useful property in general, but it is not always synergistic with the Melting Remnant. It prevents units from being '''[[Reform]]ed''', and when a unit dies it will take up draw next turn, which can be disadvantageous as it will slow down the process of drawing through your deck.

Its best utility is granting {{IconLink|Endless}} to units that want to die repeatedly without needing to hunt for {{IconLink|Immortalstone}} at the [[Merchant of Steel]], including [[Imps]], [[Tombs]], [[Gildmonger]], and [[Green Recruit]]. Not only does this save you from bad luck at the shops, it also saves you {{Gold}}, which you can use on a different major upgrade for one of your main units instead. [[Shardtail Queen]] appreciates this room quite a bit for her Imps, especially on her '''Imperialist''' path, where finding a good {{IconLink|Endless}} Imp is crucial.

It's also useful for [[banner unit]]s that want {{IconLink|Endless}}, as those units often have two other upgrades that they would also really like to have as well:
* [[Greed Dragon]] with {{IconLink|Frenzystone}} and {{IconLink|Smidgestone}}
* [[Titan Sentry]] and [[Prickly Puffball]] with some combination of {{IconLink|Dualstone}}, {{IconLink|Titanstone}}, and {{IconLink|Largestone}}
* Any [[Railforged]] units, who can have '''[[Forge Points]]''' applied to them when replayed
'''Memorial for the Melted''' lets you essentially have [[Pyrestone Housing]] on these units, with the upside of not needing to go to as many Merchants of Steel.

It's one of very few ways to apply {{IconLink|Endless}} to [[Champion]]s, which is sometimes useful depending on who your Champion is. [[Little Fade]]'s '''Fire Light''' path appreciates it quite a bit, as it prevents her from gaining too much {{Health}} through '''[[Reform]]''' and makes it easier for her to die each turn. [[The Sentient]]'s '''Bristling''' path can sometimes crumble against a barrage of high damage, so bringing her back without any {{IconLink|Burnout}} is great. When [[Primordium]] is fully {{IconLink|Eaten}}, it will be returned to the top of your draw pile, which is extremely strong with its '''Aggressive Edible''' path in the same way that [[Retch]] is. (However, be aware that any [[Morsels]] eaten in this room will also be returned to the top of your draw pile, which is usually not ideal.)

It is useful against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]], whose mounting {{IconLink|Corruption}} will kill even the sturdiest tanks unless you can kill him first or otherwise prevent him from attacking. Replaying your units with {{IconLink|Endless}} will clear {{IconLink|Corruption}}, drastically lessening the threat he poses. However, [[Resin Removal]] can accomplish more or less the same goal but does so more effectively, and is available from the same clan.

After each battle, the Bone Dog permanently adds {{PyreHealth|10}} to the Pyre, as long as it remains alive. == Notes == Bone Dog increases both current and maximum {{PyreHealth}} by 10. For the purposes of the [[Score]], this counts as {{PyreHealth|10}} restored, and thus effectively reduces the "damage taken" score penalty by 10 damage. == Strategy == '''Bone Dog''' is mostly along for the ride, and ideally can be placed behind other units, and ideally above where most combat is happening. Used this way, he can give {{PyreHealth|10}} per fight with his {{IconLink|Celebrate}} trigger, and also makes future [[Pyre Remains]] nodes on the map heal you for about {{PyreHealth|3}} more per time his ability triggers. Assuming you can accommodate him, you can roughly figure out how much total {{PyreHealth}} this is. It's a non-banner unit, but that mostly doesn't matter since he just needs to be on the train by the end, though he will cost you one card draw per fight. That said, there are a couple of pitfalls to consider - [[Qel the Corruptor]], on [[Covenant]] 4+, will kill an unboosted [[Bone Dog]] no matter where he is on the train, and trials that add [[Penitent Prayerstone]]s require you to clear them before placing '''Bone Dog'''. You will need to keep him safe against [[Flying Bosses]] to benefit in those fights. Also, if you have effects that draw/summon random units like [[Sketches of Salvation]], {{IconLink|Dominating Authority}}, or [[Channelsong]], '''Bone Dog''' probably isn't the ideal target for such effects. In general, it's quite hard to keep him alive in the endgame and his benefit is mostly spent, making him often a good candidate for removal in Ring 8. If you have ways of duplicating '''Bone Dog''', such as [[Hall of Mirrors]], it is possible to multiply the {{PyreHealth}} gained, though in many cases it is better to spend such resources on units that affect the outcome of the battle. The main argument against '''Bone Dog''' is the opportunity cost - the [[Bone Dog (event)|Bone Dog event]] also offers [[Bone Dog's Pendant]], which provides 1/4 of your endgame {{PyreHealth}} in many cases, and doesn't cost a card nor require you to be able to protect it. If the [[Bone Dog (event)|Bone Dog event]] shows up later in the game, [[Bone Dog's Pendant]] should just about always be taken over this, as it may just be more {{PyreHealth}} then. But '''Bone Dog''' can be considered if found early with a bottom-row build, especially on Pyres with lower base {{PyreHealth}} like [[Pyre of Savagery]]. == Recommended Upgrades == {| class="wikitable" ! '''Jack in the Box''' is an uncommon [[Clanless]] unit. It can be obtained from the [[Wondrous Boxes]] event. It has a {{IconLink|Resolve}} ability that summons one of the 3 units used to create it to the floor just in front of it.

==Notes==
* Multistrike on Jack in the Box is not inherited by the units that it spawns.

* Its {{IconLink|Resolve}} ability randomly chooses one of its remaining units to summon. You can see which units it still has by mousing over it.
** When the box is re-played, either through [[Endless]] or [[Reform]]ing it, it will have its full roster of 3 units again.

* If the box is copied (either permanently or temporarily) or replayed, the units inside aren't completely separate units in certain ways:
** For {{IconLink|Graft}} units, if a unit pops out of one box, dies, and gives you their [[Equipment]], that unit will not have their Grafted equipment when they pop out of a different box.  But if the unit is still alive with equipment when a second copy pops out of a different box, it will have the Grafted equipment.
** For permanent scaling units like [[Kinhost Carapace]] bonuses accrue across both permanent copies from duplicating the [[Jack in the Box]] as well as cardless copies from an [[Endless]] '''Jack in the Box'''.
** A unit with a soul attached will duplicate the soul when it pops out of a different box.

<!-- TODO add more about how this behaves with e.g. permascaling -->

*{{Capacity}} is ignored when its {{IconLink|Resolve}} ability goes off, but the 7 unit limit is not.
** If 7 units are already on the floor, its '''Resolve''' ability does nothing, but it retains its remaining units, so it could summon them later.

* The units put in the box are [[Cardless]], but they are not put in the [[Consume]] pile when they die, and [[Endless]] does not work on them.
** As such, they cannot themselves be [[Reform]]ed, though the box itself can be. This means it's a poor choice to put units in the box that you intend to [[Reform]].

* The units put in the box cannot be purged using [[Void Armament]].

* A unit with [[Purified Essence]] upgrade will regain card text if summoned out of a '''Jack in the Box'''.

* Temporary or permanent buffs applied to the *cards* of such units are just as persistent as they usually are. E.g. if you have [[Talos]]'s '''Enchantress''' path, her buffs can be applied to the units inside and the changes will persist to the next combat.


==Trivia==
* This unit is a reference to the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack-in-the-box Jack-in-the-box] toy.
* When Jack in the Box summons a unit, a unique text pop-up appears that reads, "[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_Goes_the_Weasel Pop goes the weasel!]"

{{UnitCard |name = Dante the Dependable |image = DanteTheDependable.png |clan = Clanless |rarity = Rare |type = Dante |banner = Yes |cost = 2 |size = 2 |stats = 3/10 |ability = {{IconLink|Summon}}: Add a permanent '''[[Dante's Candle]]''' to your deck. Heaven and Hell are just stops on his cultural itinerary, each with its own charms to savor. |artist = Loy Bouttamy }} '''Dante the Dependable''' is a rare [[Clanless]] unit. He is obtainable only from the [[Dante Returns|Celestial Alcove event]]. Once you have played '''Dante''' twice, you will get a follow-up event during which you are offered a choice between [[Dante's Inferno]] and [[Dante's Candelabra]]. Each time he is summoned, '''Dante''' adds a copy of [[Dante's Candle]] to your deck. These [[Blights]] will fill up your deck and damage your Pyre if not played, but each one grants '''Dante''' an additional stack of {{IconLink|Multistrike}} and increases the damage of '''Dante's Inferno'''. == Strategy == '''Dante the Dependable''' is a game-warpingly strong unit, and it is very rare that it is wrong to take him from his event. The earlier you see him, the better, but even in Ring 5 - the last opportunity to add him to your deck - he is still usually strong enough to be worth taking. '''Dante''' is the ultimate payoff for whatever form of damage scaling you are using to win the run. Whether that involves {{IconLink|Rage}}, {{IconLink|Valor}}, {{IconLink|Mageblade}}, {{IconLink|Pyregel}}, [[Morsels]], or even just raw {{Attack}} boosts, '''Dante''' can make better use out of it than almost any other unit, simply due to the huge amount of {{IconLink|Multistrike}} he will build up. With targeted effort - and clever use of [[Empyrean Well]]s - it isn't hard to give '''Dante''' {{IconLink|Multistrike|10}}, {{IconLink|Multistrike|15}}, or even more. He is almost always strong enough to be worth the cost of clogging up your deck with [[Dante's Candle]], especially if you take [[Dante's Candelabra]], which grants {{IconLink|Titanskin|2}} to your Pyre. This makes [[Vengeful Shard]]s harmless, and reduces the damage from Dante's Candles, [[Curse of Entropy|Curses of Entropy]], and [[Dominion]] from 3 to 1. This artifact is so strong if you intend to fight the [[Clash with the Titans|Titans]] that it can be worth taking '''Dante''' even if you plan to just throw him away, playing him twice to trigger his followup event and then removing him from your deck. He is a lot more powerful at [[Covenant Rank]] 5 and above, as you will start with two copies of [[Vengeful Shard]] in your deck, so the first time you play '''Dante''' he will already have {{IconLink|Multistrike|3}}. Above Covenant Rank 6, one card per draft will also come with a [[Calcified Ember]]; it can be worth taking these cards intentionally to grant '''Dante''' even more {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, especially as Calcified Ember is not harmful outside of costing a draw. The [[Pyre of Entropy]] will add a Vengeful Shard to your deck after each battle and grant extra draw each turn for every Blight in your deck, letting you scale '''Dante''' very quickly. [[Sinner's Salve]] reduces the cost of all Blights to {{Ember|0}}, so you will never have to take Pyre damage from the Candles. [[Looming Darkshard]] offsets both the cost and the lost card draw by granting {{Ember|1}} and drawing a non-Blight card. '''Dante''' benefits massively from equipment and rooms. At minimum, uncommon cards like [[Swiftsteel Dagger]], [[Glass Cannon]], and [[Fight Club]] can bolster his {{Attack}}, making him significantly more powerful. But this is only the tip of the iceberg. [[Stasis Crystal]] and [[Overgrowth Carapace]] both allow him to gain {{AttackHealth|+20|+20}} per turn, albeit with a drawback; still, with enough {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, it can be well worth the costs. [[Bloodthirsty Blade]] permanently scales every time '''Dante''' gets a kill, which he will very often ([[Pyre of Savagery]] also grants this effect). [[Moonlit Glaive]] and [[Luna Cyclestaff]] both have the potential for very high damage output, which will be multiplied by '''Dante''''s {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. [[Glutton's Maw]] grants {{AttackHealth|+15|+15}} per turn while also allowing him to instantly eat a Morsel or another sacrificial unit (and really, in a '''Dante''' run, all units other than him are sacrificial). [[Organ Harvester]] can provide some defense by letting '''Dante''' gain {{IconLink|Reanimate|1}} any time he gets a kill. Cards that grant {{IconLink|Strike}} triggers can turn '''Dante''' into a true monster, activating their effects 10+ times a round. [[Everlasting Light]] is the gold standard, as the {{IconLink|Valor}} it applies will scale the whole floor's damage output and grant a huge amount of {{IconLink|Armor}} on top of that. [[Rage Room]] does not provide defense and only applies to '''Dante''' himself, but scales his damage output twice as fast as Everlasting Light. [[Twisted Back]] grants {{IconLink|Trample}} and the same amount of {{IconLink|Rage}} per hit as Rage Room, while [[Combustion Suit]] applies ungodly amounts of {{IconLink|Unstable}} to all enemies. The only {{IconLink|Strike}} equipment that should be avoided is [[Cursed Twinblade]], as its {{Attack}}-lowering effect will quickly run '''Dante''''s damage into the ground, and he has more than enough {{IconLink|Multistrike}} already. Copying '''Dante''' at an [[Empyrean Well]] is a great idea, as you will scale his {{IconLink|Multistrike}} twice as fast, and also you will now have two '''Dantes'''. But if you do not think you can afford to play two '''Dantes''', it can instead be wise to copy a Blight card. If you took [[Dante's Candelabra]], copy a Vengeful Shard or Calcified Ember, as they are harmless but still increase his {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. But if you took [[Dante's Inferno]], you are better off copying a Dante's Candle, since that will scale both him and the spell. With the [[Melting Remnant]], it can be smart to intentionally allow '''Dante''' to die so that you can '''[[Reform]]''' him. Not only does this boost his stats further, but it also adds another Candle to your deck. You can get a head start on scaling him this way, even if you found him relatively late. A similar effect can be achieved by any clan if you make him {{IconLink|Endless}}. His {{IconLink|Summon}} trigger will be doubled by [[Ashes of the Fallen]] and repeated by [[Transcendimp]], making the [[Hellhorned]] one of his strongest potential allies. Ashes of the Fallen will cause him to add two Dante's Candles to your deck, and then gain {{IconLink|Multistrike}} equal to twice the number of Blights in your deck. '''Dante''' is one of the most reliable ways to reach high levels in [[Endless Mode]]. You will usually need some very strong synergies, like the aforementioned Everlasting Light or Ashes of the Fallen, or a source of permanent scaling. '''Bloodthirsty Blade''' is an uncommon [[Clanless]] equipment. Its {{Attack}} increases by 1 whenever the unit carrying it kills another unit.

==Strategy==
'''Bloodthirsty Blade''' can be thought of as a [[Pyre of Savagery]] that applies only to a single unit. It is best used on a unit which will kill all or most enemies on its own, such as [[Test Subject Alpha]], [[Wyldenten]] with '''Strangler''' and '''Predator''', or another {{IconLink|Sweep}} unit with {{IconLink|Speedstone}}. Though weak early on, it can easily scale up to more than {{Attack|100}} in the late game. It's significantly stronger if you pick it up early, as the later you find it the fewer enemies will be available for kills. However, if you are using a {{IconLink|Sweep}} unit (especially with {{IconLink|Multistrike}}), it may still be worth picking up late if you are trying to hit a specific damage breakpoint, such as against [[Chosen Supplicant]]s or [[Chosen Assassin]]s.

It is possible to scale up '''Bloodthirsty Blade''' on one unit and then use it on a different unit, but if one unit is killing most enemies on its own then it is generally best to keep it on that unit. If duplicated in the late game, it can provide massive {{Attack}} boosts to multiple units.

If you plan to get a lot of kills with spells or status effects, or if you have multiple damage dealers, then '''Bloodthirsty Blade''' is much less useful.

'''Exile's Diadem''' is an uncommon [[Clanless]] equipment added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It grants a unit {{Capacity|-2}}.

==Strategy==

'''Exile's Diadem''', given a suitable {{Capacity|3+}} unit to equip it to and assuming you have one dedicated kill floor, is a [[Heaven's Light]] in one equipment, though it will need to be made [[Deployable]] and cost {{DeploymentEmber|1}} to allow you to set up more units then. It's particularly good for clans that are {{Capacity}}-needy - for example, the [[Underlegion]], where [[Bolete the Guillotine]] and [[Spore Launcher]], assuming you didn't get {{IconLink|Smidgestone}} applied, are excellent candidates for it.

Even when not placed on a {{Capacity|3}} unit, it can be valuable, as it allows you to fit three {{Capacity|2}} units rather than two on a single floor with no {{Capacity}} upgrades. Large [[Champion]]s like [[Lady Gilda]] and [[Wyldenten]] particularly benefit from it, as they cannot receive the {{IconLink|Smidgestone}} upgrade. However, it cannot substitute for a {{Capacity}} boost for '''Monstrous III''' [[Penumbra]] or [[Shadowsiege]], since you cannot play the unit in the first place on a {{Capacity|5}} floor.

It can be merged with most equipment well. [[Overgrowth Carapace]] in particular can be useful, granting two additional triggers before running out of {{Capacity}}, but note that unlike {{IconLink|Smidgestone}} '''Exile's Diadem''' will not prevent the unit from growing to {{Capacity|6}} eventually.

'''Glass Cannon''' is an uncommon [[Clanless]] equipment. It grants {{Attack|50}}, but also applies {{IconLink|Fragile}}, causing the equipped unit to die instantly on losing {{Health}}.

== Strategy ==

It might be tempting to see '''Glass Cannon''' as a quick way to boost a backline unit's up-front damage - a backline unit with {{IconLink|Fragile}} can be kept alive in many combats simply by keeping the unit in front of it alive. But there are several exceptions to this, and unless you understand each one and have a reliable answer to them all, you'll need additional support to keep them alive. You can at least opt not to play this equipment in fights where it could be problematic.

{{IconLink|Armor}}, {{IconLink|Damage Shield}}, and {{IconLink|Reanimate}} are buffs you can apply that mitigate this, making '''Glass Cannon''' easier to take in runs that can apply them.

{{IconLink|Spikes}} are particularly dangerous, and are most commonly seen either from the [[Trials#Thorn Guard|Thorn Guard Trial]] or from [[Athane, Last to Fall]]. In the former case, you can avoid equipping [[Glass Cannon]] until the [[Penitent Prayerstone]] has been destroyed, but the latter is much harder to circumvent without one of the aforementioned defensive options.

This card does have a notable use on Covenant 10 - if you have a unit with {{IconLink|Sweep}}, applying this to that unit lets it kill [[Chosen Assassin]] and [[Chosen Supplicant]], two important late-game threats. 

* In [[Heaven's Maw#Chosen of Dominion|Chosen of Dominion]], you'll need a defense against the {{IconLink|Corruption}} that [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]] applies to all units with his {{IconLink|Action}} trigger. Besides the effects mentioned above, this can be prevented through applying {{IconLink|Mute}} or {{IconLink|Dazed}} to Seraph, or consistently [[Ascend]]ing or [[Descend]]ing him off your primary floor until {{IconLink|Relentless}}.
* In [[Heaven's Maw#Champion of Savagery|Champion of Savagery]], if your {{IconLink|Sweep}} unit has {{IconLink|Quick}}, this equipment allows you to kill [[Chosen Assassin]] before they can do anything, meaning all you need to do to keep your sweeper alive is ensure your frontline unit survives - no need for any other support to your sweeper. You may need a tiny bit of additional {{Attack}} to kill Chosen Assassins with {{IconLink|Titanskin}} from [[Harpist Protector]]s, but since all {{IconLink|Sweep}} units naturally have at least {{Attack|3}}, this should not be difficult to accomplish, and the {{IconLink|Speedstone}} upgrade in the shop or a merged [[Swiftsteel Dagger]] will more than suffice.
* In [[Clash with the Titans]], the only threat to your backline is [[Ragewing Assassin]] and [[Chosen Assassin]], again addressed by a {{IconLink|Sweep}} unit with {{IconLink|Quick}} having this equipment.

In [[Heaven's Maw#Harbinger of Entropy|Harbinger of Entropy]], you can apply this to any backline unit safely as nothing in that fight directly threatens your backline. It doesn't have any notable targets there but it's a nice offensive boost regardless.

It can be merged with [[Bloodthirsty Blade]] to add lategame scaling to complement its up-front offense. [[Stoic Platemail]] mitigates the {{IconLink|Fragile}} downside with {{IconLink|Armor}}, and there are some {{IconLink|Sweep}} units that don't mind being {{IconLink|Silence}}d, like [[Test Subject Alpha]].

It synergizes with [[Eel Gorgon]], who benefits tremendously from its high {{Attack}} due to the many {{IconLink|Multistrike}} stacks the unit can build up, and {{IconLink|Fragile}} will be removed upon {{IconLink|Resolve}}.

'''Meat Shield''' is an uncommon [[Clanless]] equipment. It grants {{Health|15}}, and heals {{Health|10}} at the end of each round of combat.

==Strategy==

'''Meat Shield''' is reasonably strong equipment for a tanky frontliner in the early game, but falls off later on. Healing {{Health|10}} each turn can help keep a frontliner alive effectively through the first few rings, but in the late game this effect is not nearly enough to have a meaningful impact.

Because a [[Merchant of Arms]] will not appear until Ring 3, the '''Meat Shield''' cannot be acquired until just before the battle against [[Arkion]] or [[Fleshweaver]], at which point it is already of limited use. It can be worth picking up if you desperately need survivability going into that battle, but other equipment is often a better choice. It's somewhat more useful against Fleshweaver than Arkion due to Fleshweaver's tremendous frontloaded damage; the extra {{Health}} and healing can be critical in keeping a tank unit alive against this combat.

If merged with [[Oldgrowth]], it can provide an extra {{IconLink|Rejuvenate}} trigger each turn, making it an effective choice if the [[Equalizing Rings]] are not available.

'''Meat Shield''' can be used to keep your backline units alive in certain situations. For example, it can help them survive {{IconLink|Spikes}}, an enemy unit with {{IconLink|Sweep}}, or minor amounts of {{IconLink|Corruption}}. It is particularly helpful against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]], as he will need 5 {{IconLink|Action}} (3 with the Titan Trial) triggers before the {{IconLink|Corruption}} starts to outscale the healing.

|artist = Leonardo Dionisi
}}

'''Stoic Platemail''' is an uncommon [[Clanless]] equipment. It applies a significant amount of {{Health}} and {{Armor}}, but also applies {{IconLink|Silence}} to the user.

==Strategy==

'''Stoic Platemail''' provides a ton of survivability for a {{Ember|1}} card (just compare it to [[Hellhorned]] {{IconLink|Armor}} spells like [[Fortified Pauldrons]] or [[Alloy of the Ancients]]), with the drawback of {{IconLink|Silence}} disabling much of what makes a unit good. {{IconLink|Silence}} disables [[Abilities]], {{IconLink|Enchant}}, and [[Triggers]], but not [[Buffs]], [[Debuffs]], or [[Status Effects]]. See the page on {{IconLink|Silence}} for a comprehensive explanation of which effects and units are (not) affected by '''Stoic Platemail'''.

While most frontline blockers have useful triggers or abilities that are disabled by {{IconLink|Silence}}, this is not always the case. For example, [[Funguy]] is unaffected by {{IconLink|Silence}}, and '''Stoic Platemail''' can even protect Funguy's {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks from damage.

Or maybe your blocker unit does have a decent ability, but you primarily need it to protect your own backline units. In that case, '''Stoic Platemail''' can once again be worthwhile.

It can be merged with [[Void Armament]] to disable that equipment's {{IconLink|Extinguish}} trigger, if the intended recipient is not otherwise affected by {{IconLink|Silence}}.

==Good Recipients for Stoic Platemail==

* Units without card text, like [[Shield Steward]] or [[Funguy]].
* Units whose primary value comes from status effects or buffs rather than triggers, like [[Miser]], [[Animus of Will]], [[Test Subject Alpha]], or [[Demon Fiend]].
* Squishy units played at the frontline as chump blockers (e.g. {{IconLink|Summon}} units like [[Imps]]) become proper blockers via '''Stoic Platemail'''.
* High-{{Health}} units with card text that's (mostly) not deactivated by {{IconLink|Silence}}, like '''Bristling''' [[Sentient]], [[Ember Forge]], or [[Greed Dragon]] (which only has a {{IconLink|Summon}} effect).
* Low-{{Health}} backline units with card text that's not deactivated by {{IconLink|Silence}}, if there's no better way to protect them from enemies with {{IconLink|Sweep}}, or from [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]]'s {{IconLink|Corruption}}. One good target is '''Conduit''' [[Tethys Titansbane]].
* [[Eel Gorgon]] can be equipped with '''Stoic Platemail''' after building up several {{IconLink|Incant}} triggers during a turn. This will prevent it from losing {{IconLink|Multistrike}} stacks on {{IconLink|Resolve}}, though it will also be unable to gain more. This can be useful against minibosses that punish active {{IconLink|Incant}}ing on their floor, such as [[Qel the Corruptor]] and [[Athane, Last to Fall]]. This can be easier to achieve with a source of '''[[Frozen]]''' like [[Preserve]], to keep '''Stoic Platemail''' in hand until you are ready to equip it.

'''Swiftsteel Dagger''' is an uncommon [[Clanless]] equipment. It grants {{Attack|+15}} and {{IconLink|Quick}}.

==Strategy==
'''Swiftsteel Dagger''' with the [[Deployable]] keyword can give any {{IconLink|Sweep}} unit in the game {{IconLink|Quick}} and enough {{Attack}} to kill most backliners. This is useful if you are not offered {{IconLink|Speedstone}} in the shop, and allows you to take two other upgrades, such as {{IconLink|Frenzystone}} and {{IconLink|Largestone}}. Merging it with [[Bloodthirsty Blade]] allows the equipment to naturally scale with kills, eventually providing enough power to take out dangerous enemies like [[Chosen Assassin]]s and deal significant damage to frontline enemies like [[Avowed Gladiator]]s.

'''Swiftsteel Dagger''' is the only Clanless method of giving [[Champion]]s the {{IconLink|Quick}} keyword, and is as such very useful with high {{Attack}} Champions like '''Monstrous''' [[Penumbra]]. '''Brawler''' [[Hornbreaker Prince]] also benefits due to his massive damage potential, which can allow him to wipe out whole waves of enemies before they attack. The {{Attack}} gain from this equipment, usually only a minor factor, is multiplied by 5 by his {{IconLink|Multistrike}}.

It can be merged with the [[Iron-tongue]] to give any unit both {{IconLink|Quick}} and {{IconLink|Sweep}}, though because this will lock their {{Attack}} to 30, they will fail to kill important backliners like [[Chosen Supplicant]]s and [[Chosen Assassin]]s without {{IconLink|Multistrike}} or {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}}.

* Because '''Equalizing Rings''' overrides effects that would change a unit's {{Attack}}, it also essentially makes the unit it's equipped to immune to {{IconLink|Sap}}.

If one buys '''Equalizing Rings''' at a [[Merchant of Arms]] and directly upgrades it to be Deployable, for a total of {{Gold|165}}, it essentially constitutes a permanent unit upgrade that now costs neither {{Ember}} nor a card.

'''Equalizing Rings''' is also a way for low-{{Attack}} units with crucial {{IconLink|Strike}} triggers to avoid being brought down to {{Attack|0}} by [[Seraph Aeternus-The Entropic]]'s {{IconLink|Sap}} application. This includes [[Icy Cilophyte]] or {{IconLink|Sweep}} units with {{IconLink|Dominating Power}} or {{IconLink|Dominating Control}}.

It is especially effective when merged with [[Oldgrowth]], which will give the unit {{Attack|+10}} whenever they are healed.

Heph's Hammer:
{{EquipmentCard                
|name = Heph's Hammer
|image = CRD_HephsHammer.png
|clan = Clanless
|rarity = Rare
|cost = 1
|stats = {{Attack|20}}
|effect = {{IconLink|Slay}}: {{Capacity|+1}} on this floor.
|flavor = What was once Herzal's hammer, it has now passed down to his daughter Heph. Over the years, it forged the Rail and the trains that ride it, yet it shows no signs of wear.
|artist = Loy Bouttamy
}}

'''Heph's Hammer''' is a rare [[Clanless]] equipment obtained in the [[Heph's Blueprints (event)|Heph's Blueprints]] event. It gives its wielder {{Attack|+20}}, and gives them a {{IconLink|Slay}} trigger that adds {{Capacity|+1}} to the floor.

== Strategy ==

'''Heph's Hammer''' adds a respectable amount of {{Attack}} to the unit it's equipped to. Its {{IconLink|Slay}} trigger expands the size of the floor, which seems interesting but is difficult to put into practice. 

It's hard to build a consistent strategy based on the {{IconLink|Slay}} trigger as it may or may not come, depending on the enemies you face. Like many {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers, it's more consistent with {{IconLink|Sweep}} and {{IconLink|Spikes}} to trigger against the weaker backline enemies. In e.g. [[The Great Abyss|Clash with the Titans]] it's not going to trigger on turn 1 unless you have a way of triggering {{IconLink|Slay}} on your own units. And even if you do, it won't trigger during the [[Deployment Phase]], meaning you won't be able to use it to expand your initial setup.

So it's at its best in builds that can be flexible in how many units are on the floor at a time - they're strong enough to {{IconLink|Slay}} and hold off early waves with relatively few units, but can scale by adding more units. One example of this include [[Imp]] builds with e.g. [[Imp-cicle]] or [[Imp-in-a-Box]]. [[Shardtail Queen]], especially on her '''Imperialist''' path, is a particularly good wielder of '''Heph's Hammer''', as her ability can rack up {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers quickly, including on the [[Imp]]s themselves. Other examples include {{IconLink|Endless}} units with {{IconLink|Fecundity}} who can accumulate on a floor as its {{Capacity}} increases (though of course a different unit will need to be actually wielding the '''Heph's Hammer''' here, lest it be lost when its wielder dies).

It can be useful for the [[Umbra]] in order to fit more [[Morsels]] on the floor, and can be merged with [[Glutton's Maw]] to trigger {{IconLink|Slay}} by killing a non-Morsel unit; however, this clan also has natural access to {{Capacity}} increases, like [[Space Prism]], [[Crucible Extension]], and [[Mine Jacks]], making it less valuable.

Even in the best possible setup, this can only scale so much. While it can increase your {{Capacity}} to the point where you can place whatever units on the floor you want, the 7 unit limit will still prevent you from going too crazy with this.

'''Heph's Hammer''' is also a difficult-to-justify pick because of its opportunity cost - [[Heph's Blueprints]] also offers [[Boiler Room Mod]] and [[Spell Sanctum Mod]], and the former is often strong in the same runs that '''Heph's Hammer''' is. And this is the only option in that event that takes up a card in your deck, and has to be given [[Deployable]] to be available from the start. Its {{Attack}} bonus is solid in the early-game but becomes less meaningful later. So this might be skippable even if none of the room options are helpful to your run. Still, in certain runs, '''Heph's Hammer''' can be the right pick.

==Notes==

* In Monster Train 1, the hammer was called [https://monster-train.fandom.com/wiki/Railforger%27s_Hammer Railforger's Hammer] and could be found in a Concealed Cavern event. True to its flavour text, it can be seen wielded by [[Heph]] in both games.

{{EquipmentCard
|name= Overgrowth Carapace
|image = CRD_OvergrowthCarapace.png
|clan= [[Clanless]]
|cost= 2
|rarity= Rare
|effect= {{IconLink|Resolve}}: Gain {{Capacity|+1}}, {{Attack|+20}}, and {{Health|+20}} if there is {{Capacity}} available.
|flavor= Don't think too hard about what is in this supplement. Just know that it will certainly make you FEEL stronger.
|artist= Merilliza Chan
}}
'''Overgrowth Carapace''' is a rare [[Clanless]] equipment card that is primarily obtained at the [[Merchants#Merchant of Arms|Merchant of Arms]]. On [[Resolve]], a unit with this equipment will attempt to grow in size, gaining {{AttackHealth|+20|+20}} and {{Capacity|+1}} if the floor has empty {{Capacity}}.

Note that the effect is only conditional on the floor having empty {{Capacity}}, not whether the unit actually gains {{Capacity}}. This is relevant for {{Capacity|6}} units, and for units with {{IconLink|Smidgestone}}.

==Strategy==

'''Overgrowth Carapace''' is on first glance a hard-to-use equipment, providing a good but ultimately finite amount of stats while requiring you to leave a lot of empty space, in all likelihood consigning your unit to be alone. In most situations, having a partner unit take that space instead is higher-impact.

But it does have some interactions that make it easier to use than it seems. For one, a unit's {{Capacity}} can never go higher than 6, but this equipment will continue to provide its benefits as long as space is open. This can make it work with effects that provide {{Capacity}} over time, like [[Heph's Hammer]], or certain setups where you have {{Capacity|7}} on your floor and your unit ends up being alone.

It also works excellently with any units that have a {{IconLink|Smidgestone}}, as that locks them to {{Capacity|1}}. They will still benefit from this equipment as long as {{Capacity|1}} is available, while not actually increasing in size. This lets your unit have friends while also growing.

While losing {{Capacity}} is not great for the [[Umbra]], this equipment nonetheless works better with [[Morsels]] than one might expect: because {{IconLink|Eaten}} triggers before {{IconLink|Resolve}}, you can fill any spare {{Capacity}} on the floor with Morsels and still have '''Overgrowth Carapace''' grow at end of turn. The same applies to other effects that kill friendly units before the end of the turn, like '''Imperialist''' [[Shardtail Queen]], or [[Melting Remnant]]'s {{IconLink|Burnout}}.

== Notes ==
The {{Capacity}}, {{Attack}}, and {{Health}} gained are attached to the unit, not the equipment, and are not lost if the equipment is replaced. They also persist if the unit becomes a card again, e.g. if they die with {{IconLink|Endless}} or are [[Reform]]ed.

==Trivia==
* The name is most likely a reference to [[Kinhost Carapace]], a [[Wurmkin]] unit which was originally only available in Monster Train 1 but was later added to the sequel. In Monster Train 1, the Kinhost Carapace grew larger and gained stats when played.

It places the target unit in {{IconLink|Stasis}}, during which the unit gains {{AttackHealth|+20|+20}} per turn. Although they cannot attack, units in {{IconLink|Stasis}} can still activate any triggers that don't rely on being targeted, including {{IconLink|Incant}}, {{IconLink|Resolve}}, and {{IconLink|Enchant}}. This provides invincibility to the unit while still gaining their benefits, and means that once the battle reaches its end you will have a useful stat stick to face the boss with. Good units for this approach include [[Magma Cultist]], [[Morselmaker]], [[Moon Pixie]], and [[Morel Mistress]]. It is a strong option for the '''Aggressive Edible''' and '''Stalwart Snack''' paths on [[Primordium]], keeping the unit safe from dying while bolstering its stats, but should '''not''' be taken with '''Superfood''', as this will pass {{IconLink|Stasis}} onto the eater with no way of removing it. ==History== ''See [[Version History]]'' {| class="wikitable" |- ! '''Void Armament''' is a rare [[Clanless]] equipment. It grants {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, but will purge any unit that dies with it equipped. Note that '''Void Armament''' itself will not be purged, only the unit holding it.

== Notes ==
This weapon will purge ''any'' unit it is equipped on, including [[Champion]]s. This is the only way to remove a Champion from your deck besides the [[Soulforge]] event. Note that a unit has to ''die'' to be purged, whereas '''Superfood''' [[Primordium]] can safely be {{IconLink|Eaten}} without being purged.

A unit which has {{IconLink|Reanimate}} or {{IconLink|Endless}} will still be purged on death, even if it would normally survive being "killed." In the case of {{IconLink|Endless}}, you won't draw the unit again. You won't be able to [[Reform]] the unit either, as they don't enter the [[Consume]] pile. {{IconLink|Reanimate}} will keep the unit alive until the end of the battle, but after combat is complete they will be gone.

== Strategy ==

In the early game, '''Void Armament''' can be used to easily Purge undesired units like [[Spear Steward]], [[Shield Steward]], and more. For runs that start with many such units, this can be taken early with the idea of using it to Purge unwanted units, and later equipping it to a powerful unit you don't expect to die. 

Its {{IconLink|Multistrike}} is powerful when applied to a more valuable unit, such as your [[Champion]], but equipping it to such a unit is risky - your run can be dead in the water if a key unit you've invested in gets Purged. Clans which embrace death such as the [[Melting Remnant]] and [[Lazarus League]] should be especially wary, as {{IconLink|Endless}} won't save the unit, and you won't be able to [[Reform]] purged units. Most counterintuitively, if a unit with {{IconLink|Reanimate}} loses a stack with this equipped, they '''will''' be purged, despite remaining on the battlefield for the duration of the fight, and won't be available in future fights. Use extreme caution with this equipment.

That being said, if a unit's death would realistically mean game over to your run, they're a good candidate for this equipment - the unit being purged doesn't matter if your run is over anyway, and you'll often have such a unit by the lategame.

Its high cost makes [[Attuned Whetstone]] a good pickup if you have it, and that lets you merge it with other expensive equipment freely.

{{RoomCard                
|name = Boiler Room
|image = CRD_BoilerRoom.png

|effect = Gain {{Ember|1}} when a unit dies.

|artist = Samuel Lim

'''Boiler Room''' is an uncommon [[Clanless]] room. All units that die in that room give you {{Ember|1}}.

==Notes==

'''Boiler Room''' behaves like a {{IconLink|Harvest}} trigger:
* It triggers off of unit deaths of friendly units, too.
* For [[Funguy]], it triggers for every [[Troop]] stack lost.

== Strategy ==

'''Boiler Room''' can be one of the strongest sources of {{Ember}} in the game as long as you are able to consistently kill enemies within a specific room. With damaging spells, you can play them at what amounts to a discount. For all other ways of killing enemes, such as with your units, you'll get the {{Ember}} next turn.

It can be somewhat inconsistent if you are completely reliant on it for {{Ember}}, as the {{Ember}} it produces is dependent on the number of enemies present each turn. Still, at an average of {{Ember|~3}} each turn it is extremely useful.

Its main problem is that it incentivizes you to take [[Limbo's Solace]] over [[Hell's Flame]], as the extra draw will make sure you have cards to spend all of that {{Ember}} on, and a single extra {{Ember}} on top of what '''Boiler Room''' gives you is not worth giving up the extra draw. However, it should usually be made Deployable, and that leaves you only {{DeploymentEmber|3}} to spend on other cards. This is rarely a reason to not take it, however, as the '''Boiler Room''' is very strong; it is just something to keep in mind.

Keep in mind that '''Boiler Room''' can be powered by your own units as well. This means that units like [[:Category:Imp units|Imps]], [[:Category:Assistant units|Assistants]], units that [[Reform]] or {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, and so on can make great use of this. [[Hallowed Halls]] can more than pay for itself, and units like [[Overworked Assistant]] which die constantly will provide consistent extra {{Ember}}. [[Funguy]] can generate a ton of {{Ember}} this way when losing {{IconLink|Troop}} stacks.

You do have to have a deck that can capitalize on large amounts of {{Ember}} mid-fight while being able to set up without that {{Ember}}, but [[Boiler Room]]'s output is considerable, and it often justifies the investment.

Be wary of leaning too hard into this room against [[Clash with the Titans]], as unless you are killing off your units to fuel it, every third wave will provide no {{Ember}} due to only containing [[Savagery]].

'''Enchanted Chamber''' is an uncommon [[Clanless]] room. It grants +15 [[Magic Power]] to all spells played in that room.

== Strategy ==

'''Enchanted Chamber''' empowers your spells in a given room. This can be used with spells like [[Vent]], [[Ice Tornado]], [[Make It Rain]], [[Celestial Storm]], [[Surgical Strike]], and so on to amplify their power without having to spend an upgrade spot on them. Some of the above mentioned can kill Chosen variants of enemies with this room's help, which is relevant on Covenant 10.

If you happen to start with [[Plink]], '''Enchanted Chamber''' is particularly good. It can be played on an otherwise empty floor where you are unlikely to need a different room, and it allows Plink to take out backliners throughout almost the entire game. This can turn a generally underwhelming starter card into a very powerful one, as the Magic Power will apply to each hit.

It can be played on lower floors without a need for your units unlike {{IconLink|Conduit}}, though in that role it somewhat suffers by comparison to [[Inferno Room]], as that also clears most backliners without need for investment, albeit at a slightly higher price. Unlike that, it can be played on floors with your units. When playing [[Luna Coven]], it's very similar to [[Planetarium]] when played on a floor with units - [[Planetarium]] is better with 4+ units on floor and worse with 2 or fewer - but it's available when not playing the [[Luna Coven]], and for many purposes does the same job anyway.

'''Fight Club''' is an uncommon [[Clanless]] room. It grants {{Attack|+15}} to all friendly units.

==Strategy==
'''Fight Club''' is mainly of interest for clans and strategies which have lots of units and enough {{Capacity}} to play many of them on one floor. This particularly concerns unit [[starter cards]] like [[Queen's Impling]]s, [[Dreg]]s, or [[Erratic Assistant]]s, as well as [[Umbra]]'s [[Morsel]]s. Units with {{IconLink|Multistrike}} or {{IconLink|Sweep}} can also make good use of it.

'''Fight Club''' is almost always useful, while many other rooms are more situational but also stronger if used properly. If you don't need a specific room, '''Fight Club''' is a solid option for almost any build.

It does have a few synergies with specific cards. [[Primordium]] can pass the {{Attack}} to another unit every turn. [[Baron Grael]] can '''Devour''' [[Assistants]] in this room to gain additional {{Attack}}. [[Adaptive Mutation]] can use the extra {{Attack}} in the same way that it uses buffs like {{IconLink|Rage}} to massively increase a unit's stats.

'''Steward's Quarters''' is an uncommon [[Clanless]] room. It gives {{Attack|+20}} and {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}} to [[:Category:Steward units|Train Stewards]] (but '''not''' to [[Railforged]] Automaton units with "Steward" in their names), and increases the room's {{Capacity}} by 1 when played.

==Notes==

When a different room is played on the floor, overwriting '''Steward's Quarters''', the extra {{Capacity|1}} is lost.

==Strategy==

'''Steward's Quarters''' turns [[Spear Steward]] into a {{Attack|34x2}} attacker, and [[Shield Steward]] isn't far behind at {{Attack|28x2}}. This is quite powerful in the midgame, and with upgrades and investment, these can become powerful attackers in their own right! While you've often already built a plan that doesn't involve Stewards by the time you see this, it's worth considering if you still have them and see it early enough.

Even with '''Steward's Quarters''', one practical obstacle to actually using Stewards into the late game is their lack of durability (which this room doesn't help with), and upgrades can only do so much here. You also need ways to scale and diversify against several different threats the game can throw at you. Floor overstacking is a great way to both get lots of Stewards to enjoy the benefits of this room while also allowing other units to support them. The [[Hellhorned]] and [[Banished]] clans in particular are good at overstacking floors and scaling units that don't have specific interactions with them.

Finally, you don't actually need to be using Train Stewards at all to benefit from this room! Keep in mind that it costs {{Ember|0}} and grants {{Capacity|1}}. If you make it [[Deployable]], you can use it to fill a room with {{Capacity|1}} more than you otherwise could in the Deployment Phase, all without needing more {{DeploymentEmber}}. You can then even play a different room! As long as you don't intend on playing other units, losing {{Capacity|1}} doesn't matter at this point.

You could perhaps use it to boost Stewards in the middle game and pivot towards just using it for {{Capacity}} late.

{{RoomCard |name = Weapons Cache |image = CRD Weapons Cache.png |clan = Clanless |rarity = Uncommon |cost = 2 |effect = When you summon a friendly unit, draw an [[Equipment]] and apply {{Ember|-2}}. |flavor = "Although I do not know who forged these weapons, I do know the Skull Crusher's armory always seemed to know when I needed them most."
—Tales of the Inferno |artist = Genevieve Bega }} '''Weapons Cache''' is an uncommon [[Clanless]] room added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. When you summon a friendly unit in the room, you draw a random [[Equipment]] card from your deck and apply {{Ember|-2}}. ==Notes== * The effect also applies when friendly units are summoned in unconventional ways, such as via [[Sketches of Salvation]] or {{IconLink|Dominating Authority}}, or when [[Spawn]]ing. * Its effect is implemented as a {{IconLink|Summon}} trigger on each unit (though it cannot be {{IconLink|Mute}}d or {{IconLink|Silence}}d). With [[Ashes of the Fallen]], each unit will draw two pieces of equipment, and [[Transcendimp]] played in the future will copy it. * Equipment drawn by '''Weapons Cache''' but not played will be discarded, and can be drawn again on later turns. If this happens, the {{Ember}} reduction will stack. This is contrary to the effect of [[Attuned Whetstone]], whose cost reduction does not persist when discarded. If you are playing with clans that can reliably trigger {{IconLink|Summon}} outside of Deployment, this can be a good way to defray the {{Ember}} cost of expensive [[Merged Equipment]]. ** If '''Weapons Cache''' draws [[Resin Blades]], its price will remain reduced for the rest of the battle, including when returned to hand, making it much easier to replay when the equipped unit dies to {{IconLink|Burnout}}. ==Strategy== '''Weapons Cache''' is a powerful card under the right circumstances, but needs a bit of effort to reach its maximum potential. The card's ideal use case is putting it down during the [[Deployment Phase]], then placing your units and having each of them draw out their equipment, letting you start battle with a fully-equipped floor of units. It serves both as a de facto source of {{DeploymentEmber}}, letting you play out a more expensive hand of cards than you could normally afford, and a way to get a lot of equipment out during the Deployment Phase without repeatedly visiting the [[Merchant of Arms]] for the [[Deployable]] upgrade. As such, for obvious reasons, '''Weapons Cache''' really needs to be made Deployable. Its utility diminishes drastically if not, as you may not be able to draw or play it until you have already drawn past all your equipment, or when your floor is already at full {{Capacity}} and thus you cannot place any more units down. While some clans can trigger {{IconLink|Summon}} efficiently outside of Deployment, like the [[Underlegion]] with [[Funguy]] or the [[Umbra]] with [[Morsels]], most cannot. If you have [[Dante's Footstool]], this will let you play '''Weapons Cache''' during Deployment for {{Ember|0}}, which is a significant power spike and one of the better uses of that artifact. Since it costs {{Ember|2}} and provides a discount of {{Ember|-2}}, you must draw at least two pieces of equipment to actually save {{Ember}} overall compared to simply making the desired equipment Deployable. Additionally, equipment that already is Deployable cannot be drawn or have its cost reduced during the [[Deployment Phase]], only after it has been reshuffled. This makes '''Weapons Cache''' a weaker choice if you already have important Deployable equipment. If you have the choice between applying Deployable to '''Weapons Cache''' or a piece of equipment that costs at least {{Ember|2}}, it is often better to put it on '''Weapons Cache'''. Units with {{IconLink|Equipped}} or {{IconLink|Artificer}} triggers, including [[Pincushion]], [[Swordmaiden]], and [[Hydra Armed Horror]], become far, far stronger with '''Weapons Cache'''. It allows these units to trigger their effects immediately and repeatedly before combat even begins, for less {{Ember}} than they would otherwise require. In certain cases, it can even enable you to buy or draft every piece of equipment you see, since drawing them through '''Weapons Cache''' prevents them from taking up normal card draw and cheapens them, effectively making them "free" cards. It is relatively easy to replace with another room after the Deployment Phase, since you are unlikely to trigger its effect much more. ==History== ''See [[Version History]]'' {| class="wikitable" |- ! Version !! |artist = Genevieve Bega

'''Echo Vault''' is a rare [[Clanless]] room added in the [[Lost Arsenal]] update. It causes the last spell played on its floor to be played again at the end of the turn.

==Notes==
* Drawn cards and generated {{Ember}} will be available for the next turn.
* Targeted spells are played in the same ''position'', not necessarily on the same unit. As such, if a unit is moved (for example with [[Just Cause]]) or removed (for example with [[Dripfall]]), the unit that is next in the same position will be targeted.
* X cost cards will be played for the same {{Ember}} cost.
* The last played spell only refers to the same turn. (this may be a bug)
* The Moon phase will be displayed incorrectly as the phase the moon will be in after Turn End.
* [[Infusion]] cards are ignored by '''Echo Vault''', since they cannot be copied in any way.
* [[Extract]] is part of the casting cost, so cards with this mechanic can be copied even if you no longer have sufficient {{Echo}} at end of turn.
* If a card with [[Offering]] (e.g. [[Crypt Builder]]) is played with a discard effect from cards like [[Offering Token]], then [[Offering Token]] will be considered the last spell played.

==Strategy==
'''Echo Vault''' is expensive, but generally worth picking up. Broadly speaking, it provides as much value as the most valuable spell in your hand on any given turn. If you have high-quality spells, it can be one of the most powerful rooms in the game. If you are using unupgraded starter cards, it will often not be worth {{Ember|2}}.

Good options for duplicating in an '''Echo Vault''' include:
* Cards with out-of-combat benefits like [[Alchemy]], [[Pay Off]], and expensive cards with the {{IconLink|Holystone}} upgrade
* Cards with powerful effects that '''[[Consume]]''' like [[Spawning Pods]], [[Furnace Tap]], and [[Adaptive Mutation]]
* Expensive or X-cost cards like [[Mix-a-Lot]], [[Heavenfall]], and the [[:Category:Railspike|Railspikes]]
* Doubling cards like [[Superheated]], [[Hoarfrost Effigy]], and [[Last Stand]]
* Cards whose upsides stack but their downsides do not, like [[Onehorn's Tome]], [[Faulty Body]], and [[The Great Decay]]

Its value rises dramatically if you intend to take on [[Clash with the Titans]], as long as you don't intend to play a different Room card on all three floors. It allows you to play [[Pyre Light]] twice each turn, which rapidly accelerates your progress against [[Dominion]]. Since Dominion tends to be the bottleneck for decks strong enough to make it to the Titans, taking '''Echo Vault''' can let you win two or three turns sooner than you would otherwise, and save a decent amount of Pyre health.

Normally, it's pretty easy to play your spells in the right order to make sure the spell you want copied is targeted, but there are certain situations where it can be difficult. X-cost cards can be powerful targets since the copy will use the original version's {{Ember}} cost, but if you need to use an X-cost card like [[Vent]] to clear out backline enemies or [[Prismal Dust]] to ensure a key unit survives, you will not be able to use '''Echo Vault''' to repeat a spell that costs {{Ember|1}} or more. Another issue is with discard cards found with the [[Stygian Guard]]; a card like [[Frenzied Swarm]], which discards your hand, must always be the last card played on a turn, which means unless your '''Echo Vault''' is off the floor where you're casting Frenzied Swarm, it will always be the spell copied.

The discard interaction can be particularly harmful against the Titans. If you play a discard card in an '''Echo Vault''', the Pyre Light generated by Dominion will be added to your hand ''before'' the card is replayed, and will then be discarded (and thus immediately destroyed, since it is '''[[Ephemeral]]''').

—Heph |artist = Hannah Lim }} '''Hall of Mirrors''' is a rare [[Clanless]] room. It decreases the floor's {{Capacity}} by 2 when played but creates a copy of any units played. ==Notes== * {{Capacity}} is ignored when copying - you only need to have space for the original unit to play it. * The copy is {{IconLink|Cardless}}. * When this room is replaced, the floor gets {{Capacity|+2}}. ==Strategy== '''Hall of Mirrors''' can be an incredibly strong room with the right setup. At worst, it can be used to create a second copy of your strongest unit or [[Champion]], though note that the {{Capacity|-2}} means you may not be able to play other units behind or in front without some means of increasing {{Capacity}} like [[Heaven's Light]] or [[Bogwurm's Growth]]. However, '''Hall of Mirrors''' has a number of powerful synergies beyond this, generally revolving around effects that double-dip on the room's benefits. The [[Deployable]] upgrade is vital for this room, as otherwise you may not be able to play the '''Hall of Mirrors''' before playing the units you want to duplicate. * Any {{IconLink|Summon}} [[Status_Effects#Triggers|triggers]] are doubled on this floor, while {{IconLink|Rally}} triggers have +1 added to them. This can be used to great effect by the [[Underlegion]], who can set up trigger chains that are increased at each step of the chain. For example, placing [[Madame Lionsmane]] with '''Everbloom''' in a '''Hall of Mirrors''' will cause each {{IconLink|Incant}} and {{IconLink|Etch}} trigger to activate once for each copy of [[Madame Lionsmane]], then each {{IconLink|Spawn}} effect will increase by 1, for a total of up to 14 [[Troop]] stacks if consuming a spell and thus benefitting from both {{IconLink|Incant}} and {{IconLink|Etch}}. If you have enough {{Capacity}} to add a unit with a {{IconLink|Rally}} trigger such as [[Amorous Enoki]] or [[Spore Launcher]] to this, then both copies of that unit will trigger {{IconLink|Rally}} for each troop stack, resulting in up to 28 activations just from consuming one spell. Be prepared to increase the game speed! * [[:Category:Assistant_units|Assistants]] can be played on this floor to drop a second copy of their [[Equipment]] once killed. * '''Gildmother''' [[Lady Gilda]] becomes quite lucrative in a '''Hall of Mirrors''', as each copy summons a [[Lady Gilda#Gilded Eggs|Gilded Egg]] that also gets duplicated, resulting in four eggs for the price of one. This means even one level of '''Gildmother''' can provide {{DragonsHoard|8}} per battle, or alternately, three levels of '''Gildmother''' can provide an absurd {{Gold|1600}} (for the one battle before Seraph where you have access to this) in addition to maxing out [[Pyreborne#Dragon's_Hoard|Dragon's Hoard]]. So unless summoned units are moved elsewhere or killed to make room for new ones, there's no guarantee of summoning several copies of any particular boxed unit, let alone one. * In general, as one of the few ways to duplicate [[Champions]], '''Hall of Mirrors''' works very well with many of them as they're usually balanced around only having one copy, although {{Capacity}} can often become an issue: ** Champions that can metascale other units e.g. '''Pyresmith''' [[Herzal]] or '''Learning Limb''' [[Baron Grael]] will provide double the scaling ** Two '''Battleborne''' [[Arduhn]]s will boost each other's {{IconLink|Mageblade}} with their {{IconLink|Conduit}} resulting in nearly quadruple the damage of a single '''Arduhn''' ** Two '''Weaponsmith''' [[Heph]]s means double the {{Attack}} and {{Armor}}, and they can alternate using '''Weaponcraft''' to generate [[Crafted Equipment]], allowing them to trigger their {{IconLink|Artificer}} every turn ** All '''[[Talos]]''' paths benefit very strongly, doubling the (meta) scaling on '''Enchantress''' and '''Battle Cleric''' while '''Celestial Radiance''' can alternate using '''Flight''' to swap positions with each other and apply massive amounts of {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} constantly ** Similarly all [[Echowright]] paths benefit strongly, returning double the amount of spells with '''The Repeater''', doubling {{IconLink|Armor}} on '''The Shellsmith''', or filling up the entire floor with massive amounts of hatched units with '''The Marshlord''' * [[Morsel]] units played will be duplicated, which is an easy way to trigger a large number of {{IconLink|Gorge}} activations on the front unit. [[Morselmaker]] will definitely run into the 7-unit limit, as each [[Morselmaker]] will attempt to summon 4 [[Morsels]] each round. As such, if trying to stack {{IconLink|Gorge}}, it may be best to play your [[Morselmaker]] or [[Morselmaster]] '''before''' playing the '''Hall of Mirrors''' to leave more room for all the spawned morsels. * A good way to work around both the {{Capacity}} limits of this room and the 7-unit limit per floor is to play a unit into the '''Hall of Mirrors''', then use [[Ascend]] or [[Descend]] effects to move one or both copies to another floor. This method can be used to duplicate many more units over the course of a battle than would normally be possible. {{RoomCard                
|name = Inferno Room
|image = CRD_InfernoRoom.png
|clan = [[Clanless]]
|rarity = Rare
|cost = 2
|effect = Deal '''50''' damage to all units at the start of combat.
|flavor = Let's just say that if you spray Pyregel everywhere, things tend to get a bit... ‘fiery'.
|artist = Leonardo Dionisi
}}

'''Inferno Room''' is a rare [[Clanless]] room. It deals 50 damage to all units, friendly and enemy, at the start of combat. This damage is not [[Piercing]], but it is not considered magic damage and so it ignores {{IconLink|Spell Shield}}.

==Strategy==

'''Inferno Room''' is a great set-and-forget solution to backline enemies, particularly [[Scourge]]-adding ones. Simply play it on the bottom floor and watch them die - no further setup required! You won't want to play your units in that room unless you want them to die, such as stray [[Spear Steward]]s or [[Shield Steward]]s you haven't purged yet. This room is one you'll generally want to make Deployable so that you don't leak the first wave.

It isn't a complete answer to backline enemies, as [[Deformed Duo]]s, [[Holy Cherub]]s, and [[Chosen Ardent]]s can get through, but it usually suffices. In particular, 50 damage is good enough to kill most Chosen enemies you really need dead early, like [[Chosen Supplicant]] and [[Chosen Assassin]] (though one of the latter barely survives in the [[Heaven's_Maw#Champion_of_Savagery|Champion of Savagery]] fight because it has {{IconLink|Titanskin|5}} from a [[Harpist Protector]]). Your upper floors can focus on being able to take out the bosses and tanky enemies that will shrug off this damage.

[[Terrifying Amalgam]]s and [[Savagery]] are hard to stop from hitting your Pyre if they show up on the floor with '''Inferno Room''', though, so unless you have specific answers to them, you'll have to account for taking a decent amount of Pyre damage in fights featuring them. Specifically, on [[Covenant Rank]] 10, there are 7 Terrifying Amalgams in [[The_Observatory#Savagery's_Final_Assault|Savagery's Final Assault]] on [[Ring 7]], which will deal a total of 35 Pyre damage unless blocked on the bottom floor. And in the [[Heaven's_Maw#Champion_of_Savagery|Champion of Savagery]] fight, there are another 7 Terrifying Amalgams. Finally, in the [[Titans]] fight, [[Savagery]] deals another 5 Pyre damage on turns 1, 4, 7, and so on.

Units in {{IconLink|Stasis}} will prevent damage from these enemies while being immune to [[Inferno Room]]'s damage, so [[Stasis Crystal]] is a good pairing if you can afford it to prevent unnecessary Pyre damage.

== Notes ==
[[Inferno Room]]'s damage does not count as spell damage and is not blocked by {{IconLink|Spell Shield}} on units like [[Purified Soul]].

'''Zone of Silence''' is a rare [[Clanless]] room. It applies {{IconLink|Silence}} to non-boss enemy units on the floor.

==Strategy==

{{IconLink|Silence}} disables [[Status Effects|Triggers]] on enemies, as well as their {{IconLink|Enchant}} effects. 

There's a fair number of lategame threats this counters, should one of them look threatening to your run:
* {{IconLink|Corruption}} applicators, like [[Misshapen Fiend]], [[Blightbound Guardian]], and [[Deformed Duo]]
** This makes the [[Heaven's Maw#Chosen of Dominion|Chosen of Dominion]] fight more manageable, leaving only [[Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant]] able to apply {{IconLink|Corruption}} on the floor this is added.
* [[Scourge]] shufflers, like [[Discordant Heretic]] and [[Chosen Supplicant]]
* {{IconLink|Incant}} punishers, like [[Enthralled Ardent]] and [[Adamant Shieldbearer]]
* [[Deafening Herald]]s {{IconLink|Enchant}}ing your units with {{IconLink|Silence}}
* Enemies that punish you for setting up top floor, like [[Terrifying Amalgam]] and [[Nourishing Cherub]], by putting it on lower floors
** This application also lets you play a different room on your main floor.
and more.

Awkwardly, it also disables gaining {{Gold}} from a [[Collector]].

The opportunity cost for this is quite high, however, as it replaces a [[Room]] that actively helps your main floor (with the exception being setups that apply it to lower floors), and it costs {{Ember|3}}. It generally should be played at the start of the fight, often necessitating making it [[Deployable]].

It's a great candidate for a room to be drawn with [[Dante's Footstool]], by making all other rooms in your deck [[Deployable]].

At [[Covenant Ranks|Covenant 6]] and higher, each set of card rewards will randomly choose one card to add a '''Calcified Ember''' to the deck if chosen. It is also generated by [[Perkeo]]. Curse of Entropy:
{{SpellCard |name = Curse of Entropy |image = CRD_CurseOfEntropy.png |clan = Clanless |cost = 0 |effect = '''[[Ephemeral]]'''.
Apply {{IconLink|Sap|4}} to friendly units on all floors.
'''[[Reserve]]''': Your Pyre takes '''3''' damage. |flavor = The Titans, within their nature, each worked towards their own twisted form of peace. For Entropy, eternal peace can only be achieved through the stasis of all things. |artist = Lauren Russo }} '''Curse of Entropy''' is a playable [[Scourges|Scourge]]. It can either be played at the cost of applying significant {{IconLink|Sap}} to '''all''' your units, or if left unplayed at turn end, it will damage your Pyre and remove itself. It is obtained from [[Seraph Aeternus-The Entropic]] or [[Entropy]] in [[Clash with the Titans]]. Both bosses shuffle '''Curse of Entropy''' into your draw pile on {{IconLink|Resolve}}. This trigger can be blocked by {{IconLink|Mute}}. == Strategy == * If you have a great amount of {{PyreHealth}}, it can be worthwhile to let '''Curse of Entropy''' hit your Pyre, as {{IconLink|Sap|4}} is a significant setback to all units. Playing too many copies can reduce units to {{Attack|0}}, which can disable {{IconLink|Strike}} and {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers. If your {{PyreHealth}} is low, playing them may be necessary, especially in drawn-out combats against the Titans. * Against [[Seraph Aeternus-The Entropic]], strong offensive scaling is highly important to offset the effect of the {{IconLink|Sap}}. The better your scaling is, the more {{PyreHealth}} you can save by playing out some copies of the card, which can be important against the Titans. * As the card is '''Ephemeral''', it will be purged if discarded, meaning Stygian Guard cards such as [[Offering Token]], [[Forgone Power]], [[Titan's Gratitude]], and [[Deep Offering]] can remove the Scourge from your deck without suffering the {{IconLink|Sap}} effect on play. * [[Resin Removal]] or [[Wickless Recruitment]] can remove the {{IconLink|Sap}} gained from playing the card immediately. * Having sources of additional draw is important as well, as this card is shuffled directly into your draw pile every turn. Essentially, during these combats, you have -1 draw per turn. If you have '''[[Holdover]]''' cards as well, you might be drawing as few as two or three cards per turn. This severely slows down the rate at which you get through your draw pile, and in the worst case might result in you drawing a full hand of '''Curses of Entropy'''. As such, sources of card draw should be prioritized. [[Limbo's Solace]] is the most common, but options like [[Deep Offering]], [[Awoken's Rail Spike]], [[Votivary]], [[Everchurning Soil]], and [[Versatile Emberstaff]] are highly valuable to ensure you can find important cards when you need them. Applying {{IconLink|Mute}} to Seraph or Entropy (only if you can do so on all three floors) also prevents them from polluting your draw. ==History== ''See [[Version History]]'' {| class="wikitable" |- ! Discordant Toll:
{{SpellCard |name = Discordant Toll |image = CRD_DiscordantToll.png |clan = Clanless |cost = 1 |effect = '''Purge'''.
'''[[Reserve]]''': Your Pyre takes '''3''' damage. |flavor = As Dominion arrived upon Heaven its acolytes began to ring the bells, their hands bloodied until they could ring no more. |artist = Lauren Russo }} '''Discordant Toll''' is a playable [[Scourges|Scourge]]. It is obtained from [[Profane Supplicant|Profane Supplicants]] and [[Chosen Supplicant|Chosen Supplicants]] ([[Covenant Ranks|Covenant 10]] only). == Strategy == It is critical to have early backline clear in combats featuring the Supplicants, as later waves can often have two Supplicants each, almost completely taking up the player's draw or {{Ember}} for the next turn. [[Chosen Supplicant]]s are particularly threatening variants that appear in [[Heaven's Maw#Chosen of Dominion|Chosen of Dominion]] and [[High Heaven#Nourishing Feed|Nourishing Feed]] on Covenant 10, who add two copies of '''Discordant Toll''' to your deck. They will appear in most waves - be sure to have a plan to kill them on the bottom floor if you are facing these combats, or else you'll mostly just be drawing this. == Trivia == * The card art is [[Dominion]] themed by the distinctive green and red eye pattern. ==History== ''See [[Version History]]'' {| class="wikitable" |- ! It tolls for you, and the sweet embrace of madness. |artist = Lauren Russo }} '''Resonant Ruin''' is a playable [[Scourges|Scourge]]. It is obtained from [[Discordant Heretic|Discordant Heretics]]. == Strategy == '''Resonant Ruin''' should almost always be played, as it deals significant damage to the Pyre and goes into your discard pile if not played. After a shuffle, you will redraw all of the Scourges you chose not to play on the previous shuffle, along with any new ones which have been added to your deck. [[Sinner's Salve]] and [[Looming Darkshard]] can both help mitigate the effect of Scourges. == Trivia == * The card art is [[Dominion]] themed by the distinctive green and red eye pattern ==History== ''See [[Version History]]'' {| class="wikitable" |- !
